an2ano02.dialogue: Mother Mystra, you are remembered!  Even now, your token is known.
an2ano02.speaker: anorrwyn

an2ano03.dialogue: This medallion is a welcome sight to me. I had feared that the spinning centuries had put an end to our Lady's worship in this land.
an2ano03.speaker: anorrwyn

an2ano04.dialogue: But none of you are strangers to the Mother of Mystery. The touch of Mystra is upon you.
an2ano04.speaker: anorrwyn
an2ano04.desc: spoken to the party, with glad surprise

an2ano05.dialogue: For her sake and for yours, let me give what aid I can. But speak swiftly children, for without the place-binding of my bones, my foothold in your time is light. The past summons me back to face my death again.
an2ano05.speaker: anorrwyn

an2ano06.dialogue: The priest sees clearly. Our Lady mourns the corruption of that which was her delight, the greatest spell ever to be raised in Faerun: the Mythal.
an2ano06.speaker: anorrwyn

an2ano07.dialogue: The new foe. Yes, I feel them, even through the years: there is a shadow spitting flame and a soft voice. Know this: their strength is stolen from the strength of the Mythal.
an2ano07.speaker: anorrwyn

an2ano08.dialogue: They have raised an abomination under the very seat of the Coronal. An abomination that cracks stone and earth in its hunger, reaching ever outward to feed. But as I look forward I see only back...
an2ano08.speaker: anorrwyn

an2ano10.dialogue: The Armies of Darkness cleft its strength asunder in the Weeping Wars, foiling the magical gates that could have been our escape. But the Mythal's weave is deep.
an2ano10.speaker: anorrwyn

an2ano11.dialogue: It sings yet in the air around you, though the tune is off. Some corruption warps the Mythal to its will. Can you not find Miroden to tune it?  Whose voice? Who calls?
an2ano11.speaker: anorrwyn

an2ano12.dialogue: Ah, the beauty of those times... the Serpentspires, the Glim-gardens... We floated on the air!  But then the wars. The blood. The keening flameswords...
an2ano12.speaker: anorrwyn

an2ano13.dialogue: Miroden Silverblade. I know him well. A master of lore and the keeper of our hopes. Before he relinquished his mortal life, he was a great mage, an elven lord. Now he is a Baelnorn. An undead guardian.
an2ano13.speaker: anorrwyn

an2ano14.dialogue: His existence is bound to the Sapphire of the Weave, through which he can tune and repair the Mythal.
an2ano14.speaker: anorrwyn

an2ano15.dialogue: He guards it deep within the catacombs, in a lair sealed with the Glyph of Safekeeping. This Word will allow you to pass...
an2ano15.speaker: anorrwyn

an2DM00.dialogue: Anorrweyn's spell teaches you Kehelben, the Word of Necessity.
an2DM00.speaker: DM

an2ano16.dialogue: Use it, children!  Find Miroden and restore the Mythal, before the Armies of Darkness beat down our gates. No... no... those armies have come and gone...
an2ano16.speaker: anorrwyn

an2ano17.dialogue: I am little help here, trapped between now and gone. Since the desecration of my grave, my spirit only flickers in this time. I beat my fists against the centuries, but still the past recalls me and I die again...
an2ano17.speaker: anorrwyn

an2ano19.dialogue: For centuries, my bones bound me to this plane. My spirit moved freely in this city and I fought darkness where I could. But such work draws enemies. A lich I battled sent his minions to disturb my grave and break my bond with this sacred shrine.
an2ano19.speaker: anorrwyn

an2ano20.dialogue: They undid the charms that bound my tomb and stole back to the catacombs with my skull for trophy. Without it, I am a feeble shade. Ah. I can hear their laughter...
an2ano20.speaker: anorrwyn

an2ano21.dialogue: Miroden's Sapphire is tuned to the Mythal. With it, he can restore the fraying weave of old Mythanthor's spell.
an2ano21.speaker: anorrwyn

an2ano22.dialogue: He is bound to the gem as its Communicant: a vessel for its cleansing fire. Find him!  My time grows short...
an2ano22.speaker: anorrwyn

an2ano23.dialogue: Her intentions for you, I know not, but you are known to her. It is she that weaves your path: her will is the loom, your deeds, the thread. But hark: trumpets...
an2ano23.speaker: anorrwyn

an2ano24.dialogue: Miroden Silverblade. He is the Mythal's Protector. Before he relinquished his mortal life, he was a great mage, an elven lord. Now he is a Baelnorn. An undead guardian.
an2ano24.speaker: anorrwyn

an2ano25.dialogue: Restore it? That magic is beyond the living. Seek out the baelnorn Miroden. His bond serves to tune the Mythal. His strength can aid you. In time past, his wisdom was a beacon to us all...
an2ano25.speaker: anorrwyn

an2ano26.dialogue: Elminster Aumar lives yet?  Time, your hand crushes some but never all.
an2ano26.speaker: anorrwyn

an2ano27.dialogue: How can I help the friends of the Chosen of Mystra?  We of Myth Drannor do not forget our debts. We do not forget...
an2ano27.speaker: anorrwyn

an2ano28.dialogue: Forgive me, children, in my ears, the din of Myth Drannor's fall drowns out your voices. Ah, the thunder!  I will strive to hear you. Speak again.
an2ano28.speaker: anorrwyn

an2ano30.dialogue: The tide moves back again... Eltargrim, oh Coronal, where are you?  Are the Tel'Quessir to be uncaptained in this dark sea? We must fortify the Mythal. Trasaal... Ailos... summon the armathors!
an2ano30.speaker: anorrwyn

an2ano31.dialogue: No, that time is gone!  The Towers of Song have crumbled. I must face the living moment...
an2ano31.speaker: anorrwyn

an2ano34.dialogue: Night falls again on the eve of my destruction. The spellfire comes... Who will shield us?
an2ano34.speaker: anorrwyn

an2ano35.dialogue: Children, my death revisits me. Speak quickly now before I am caught up in its blaze again.
an2ano35.speaker: anorrwyn

an2ano36.dialogue: The clouds burn!  Flee, priestesses, we are undone!  Mother Mystra, hear me - so long as my bones rest in your temple, let my spirit walk this plane to do your will!  I...
an2ano36.speaker: anorrwyn

an2ano39.dialogue: No!  Do not leave me to the past. The future is in need!
an2ano39.speaker: anorrwyn

an2ano40.dialogue: The Mythal is black with corruption. The Protector must tune its weave. Seek out Miroden Silverblade, baelnorn of the Gem.
an2ano40.speaker: anorrwyn

an2ano41.dialogue: His lair is deep within the catacombs, sealed with the Glyph of Safekeeping. This Word will allow you to pass...
an2ano41.speaker: anorrwyn

an2DM01.dialogue: Anorrweyn's spell teaches you Kehelben, the Word of Necessity.
an2DM01.speaker: DM

an2ano42.dialogue: My time is done... Hear me!
an2ano42.speaker: anorrwyn

an2ano43.dialogue: Mystra's will is with you, but my hold on this plane fails me.
an2ano43.speaker: anorrwyn

an2ano44.dialogue: Base creatures have stolen my skull into the catacombs. Without it here on my altar, I slip...
an2ano44.speaker: anorrwyn

an2ano46.dialogue: My grip fails, this time slips from my grasp...
an2ano46.speaker: anorrwyn

an2ano47.dialogue: Elminster was an armathor of Myth Drannor, a favorite of the Coronal. But that was long before the Weeping Wars, when the streets were lit by elven laughter and our city was the jewel of great Cormanthyr's crown.
an2ano47.speaker: anorrwyn

an2ano48.dialogue: Ah, how the nobles would have shuddered that any human, even the Chosen of Mystra, could outlive all our glory...
an2ano48.speaker: anorrwyn

an2pro00.dialogue: Ask what Mystra has to do with you
an2pro00.speaker: Protagonist

an2pro01.dialogue: Tell her you were sent by Elminster
an2pro01.speaker: Protagonist

an2pro04.dialogue: Ask her what you can do to restore the Mythal
an2pro04.speaker: Protagonist

an2pro05.dialogue: Ask her what she knows about the Cult
an2pro05.speaker: Protagonist

an2pro06.dialogue: Tell her about Beriand's vision of Mystra
an2pro06.speaker: Protagonist

an2pro07.dialogue: Ask for her help against the Cult
an2pro07.speaker: Protagonist

an2pro08.dialogue: Ask her about Myth Drannor before the fall
an2pro08.speaker: Protagonist

an2pro10.dialogue: Ask who Miroden is, and where he can be found
an2pro10.speaker: Protagonist

an2pro11.dialogue: Ask about the Sapphire of the Weave
an2pro11.speaker: Protagonist

an2pro12.dialogue: Ask how you can ground her in this time
an2pro12.speaker: Protagonist

an2pro13.dialogue: Leave the apparition to her memories
an2pro13.speaker: Protagonist

an6ano02.dialogue: Speak swiftly, children... Have you not found Miroden Silverblade?
an6ano02.speaker: anorrwyn
an6ano02.desc: spoken, splice of an2ano05 and an3ano23, (Text Change) added KE 6-2-01

an6dmaYA.dialogue: You tell Anorrweyn that you overheard a Cult Mage Captain talking, deep in the Catacombs...
an6dmaYA.speaker: DM

an6dmaYB.dialogue: Through the keyhole of a Cult stronghold, you saw him tell Kya Mordrayn that he had the Baelnorn as his prisoner.
an6dmaYB.speaker: DM

an6ano04.dialogue: Ill tidings indeed! You must free him, children. But beware! For anyone with the power to imprison Miroden Silverblade is a formidable opponent indeed... but hark...
an6ano04.speaker: anorrwyn

an6ano05.dialogue: Again my fate calls me... I slip away! Farewell!
an6ano05.speaker: anorrwyn

an6dmaYC.dialogue: You tell Anorrweyn about the many drow you defeated, deep within the Catacombs...
an6dmaYC.speaker: DM

an6ano07.dialogue: But still the drow hold my skull - I know this to be true. But harken, children! I have only moments left...
an6ano07.speaker: anorrwyn

an6ano08.dialogue: Remember what I told you! You must free the baelnorn Miroden Silverblade... or the Mythal's corruption will overwhelm us again, in living fire...
an6ano08.speaker: anorrwyn

an6ano09.dialogue: It is in the Catacombs, I can feel it... not deep, but surrounded by evil. But first you must find Miroden Silverblade!
an6ano09.speaker: anorrwyn

an6ano10.dialogue: Goodbye... I implore you... stop the corruption of the Mythal... find Miroden Silverblade!
an6ano10.speaker: anorrwyn

an6ano11.dialogue: You return with eyes dark from battle... Have you not found Miroden Silverblade?
an6ano11.speaker: anorrwyn
an6ano11.desc: spoken, splice of an2ano20 and an3ano23, (Text Change) added KE 6-2-01

an6dmaYD.dialogue: You tell Anorrweyn that you overheard a Cult Mage Captain talking, deep in the Catacombs...
an6dmaYD.speaker: DM

an6dmaYE.dialogue: Through the keyhole of a Cult stronghold, you saw him tell Kya Mordrayn that he had the Baelnorn as his prisoner.
an6dmaYE.speaker: DM

an6ano13.dialogue: Then run swiftly, children, to release him! The Baelnorn can do nothing to restore the Mythal while he is a prisoner.
an6ano13.speaker: anorrwyn

an6ano14.dialogue: But take care! For anyone with the power to imprison Miroden Silverblade is a formidable opponent indeed.
an6ano14.speaker: anorrwyn

an6ano15.dialogue: Go now. May Mystra keep you - and bring you here to me again when the Baelnorn is free.
an6ano15.speaker: anorrwyn

an6dmaYF.dialogue: You tell Anorrweyn you saw Kya Mordrayn deep in the Catacombs, through the keyhole of the Cult stronghold...
an6dmaYF.speaker: DM

an6dmaYG.dialogue: You say that the Mage Captain told Kya that the Baelnorn was being held prisoner within the stronghold.
an6dmaYG.speaker: DM

an6ano17.dialogue: Worry not about Kya Mordrayn. I will hold her attention, for the moment. You must set yourselves to the great task of freeing the Baelnorn, Miroden Silverblade.
an6ano17.speaker: anorrwyn

an6ano18.dialogue: Come back here when you have talked with him, and I will meet with you again. Until then, may Mystra guide you...
an6ano18.speaker: anorrwyn

an6ano19.dialogue: In this you have done well, but I ask again: what have you learned about the baelnorn, Miroden Silverblade?
an6ano19.speaker: anorrwyn

an6ano20.dialogue: He has the power to restore the corrupted Mythal. Have you no news of him?
an6ano20.speaker: anorrwyn

an6ano21.dialogue: Continue to seek the Baelnorn! I will search for him also, on paths that only the dead may walk.
an6ano21.speaker: anorrwyn

an6ano22.dialogue: We will meet here again, when you have learned of his fate. Farewell.
an6ano22.speaker: anorrwyn

an6ano23.dialogue: Oh Lady... the Servants of Mystery... are they here?
an6ano23.speaker: anorrwyn
an6ano23.desc: spoken, edited version of ng1ano00 (text change)KE 6-4-01

an6dmaYH.dialogue: Anorrweyn's ghost gestures toward the sarcophagus.
an6dmaYH.speaker: DM

an6pro00.dialogue: Tell her the Cult captured Miroden
an6pro00.speaker: Protagonist

an6pro01.dialogue: Tell her you've slain many drow
an6pro01.speaker: Protagonist

an6pro02.dialogue: Say you still seek her skull
an6pro02.speaker: Protagonist

an6pro04.dialogue: Tell her the Cult captured Miroden
an6pro04.speaker: Protagonist

an6pro05.dialogue: Tell her you've seen Kya Mordrayn
an6pro05.speaker: Protagonist

an6pro06.dialogue: Tell her you've defeated the drow forces
an6pro06.speaker: Protagonist

an3dmaYA.dialogue: As soon as you place the skull, you feel a ghostly presence.
an3dmaYA.speaker: DM

an3ano02.dialogue: The place-binding is sealed. My spirit stands firm in the present moment once again.
an3ano02.speaker: anorrwyn

an3ano03.dialogue: You have striven much to restore me. Let Mystra's blessings comfort you.
an3ano03.speaker: anorrwyn
an3ano03.desc: Spoken, generous, she heals & resurrects the party

an3DM01.dialogue: Anorrweyn's spell cures your wounds and restores life to the dead.
an3DM01.speaker: DM

an3ano06.dialogue: Your deeds have brought hope, but the corruption within the Mythal grows.
an3ano06.speaker: anorrwyn

an3ano07.dialogue: You must find the baelnorn Miroden Silverblade. He can tune the Mythal and bend its strength to guardianship again.
an3ano07.speaker: anorrwyn

an3ano08.dialogue: It lies deep within the catacombs. Deeper than your path has taken you. Look beyond the Glyph of Safekeeping. The way is open to you.
an3ano08.speaker: anorrwyn

an3ano09.dialogue: Such valor! The dark Children of Lloth are pitiless foes. Their presence here is ill news indeed.
an3ano09.speaker: anorrwyn

an3ano11.dialogue: Then you must free him!  Without his aid, we cannot cleanse the Mythal of its corruption.
an3ano11.speaker: anorrwyn

an3ano12.dialogue: Even now the darkness is spreading. The evil under Castle Cormanthor reaches out across Faerun. Its hunger will not be slaked until we wrench the Mythal from its grip.
an3ano12.speaker: anorrwyn

an3ano13.dialogue: There are dark paths here in the city, where none but the dead may walk. I will walk them. Thus may the minds of our enemies be distracted away from you.
an3ano13.speaker: anorrwyn

an3ano14.dialogue: Return to my shrine when you have news from the baelnorn, and I will come forth again to meet you.
an3ano14.speaker: anorrwyn

an3ano15.dialogue: Move quickly, children. The Mythal is once again a shield about the city, but one that weakens good and shelters evil.
an3ano15.speaker: anorrwyn

an3ano16.dialogue: Its spell was woven by faith. And faith can redeem it. But if it is lost to hatred and despair, then so are we all.
an3ano16.speaker: anorrwyn

an3ano17.dialogue: Find Miroden. With him lies our salvation.
an3ano17.speaker: anorrwyn

an3ano18.dialogue: Rescue Miroden. With him lies our salvation.
an3ano18.speaker: anorrwyn

an3ano20.dialogue: You return with eyes dark from battle. May the Goddess refresh you.
an3ano20.speaker: anorrwyn

an3DM02.dialogue: Anorrweyn's spell cures your wounds and restores life to the dead.
an3DM02.speaker: DM

an3ano21.dialogue: You return with eyes dark from battle. May the Goddess refresh you.
an3ano21.speaker: anorrwyn

an3ano22.dialogue: You return with eyes dark from battle. May you find ease in Mystra's holy shrine.
an3ano22.speaker: anorrwyn

an3ano23.dialogue: The air about us still reeks of the Mythal's corruption. Have you not found Miroden Silverblade?
an3ano23.speaker: anorrwyn

an3ano24.dialogue: You carry a Gem of the Weave - but it is not the Sapphire. What has happened?  And what has become of Miroden Silverblade?
an3ano24.speaker: anorrwyn

an3ano25.dialogue: No one in this time, I fear. Its ways are deep. The intricacies of its web would overpower mortal minds. Why do you ask this?  What has happened?
an3ano25.speaker: anorrwyn

an3ano26.dialogue: How can this be?  Miroden's wards and traps have made his lair impregnable for centuries. No mortal could enter that labyrinth uninvited.
an3ano26.speaker: anorrwyn

an3ano27.dialogue: Your service will not be forgotten. But why has he not restored the Mythal?  The darkness is about us yet...
an3ano27.speaker: anorrwyn

an3ano28.dialogue: Madness!  Can he have done such a thing?  Without a Gem of the Weave, the Mythal cannot be tuned.
an3ano28.speaker: anorrwyn

an3ano29.dialogue: But why?  Why would he?  And how?  For surely his own existence is bound to the Gem. Can he have destroyed it and survived?
an3ano29.speaker: anorrwyn

an3ano30.dialogue: Better that, I suppose, than letting the Gem fall into the hands of his captors.
an3ano30.speaker: anorrwyn

an3ano31.dialogue: Yes... His bond would demand such a sacrifice. And yet he survived to tell this tale. I wonder...
an3ano31.speaker: anorrwyn

an3ano32.dialogue: So he destroyed the Gem to prevent it falling into the hands of this Cult.
an3ano32.speaker: anorrwyn

an3ano33.dialogue: Your service will not be forgotten.
an3ano33.speaker: anorrwyn

an3ano34.dialogue: But surely his own existence is bound to the Gem. He must have destroyed it rather than let it fall into the hands of his captors.
an3ano34.speaker: anorrwyn

an3ano35.dialogue: The Mythal holds Myth Drannor's hope... and its doom.
an3ano35.speaker: anorrwyn

an3ano36.dialogue: Corrupted, it feeds evil as surely as it once nurtured good. Until it is restored, the darkness under Castle Cormanthor will reach ever further.
an3ano36.speaker: anorrwyn

an3ano37.dialogue: So Miroden is powerless?  Then I must step forward, and dare the fire of the Mythal.
an3ano37.speaker: anorrwyn

an3ano38.dialogue: If Miroden is powerless then how can we proceed? The Mythal must be cleansed.
an3ano38.speaker: anorrwyn

an3ano39.dialogue: I remember when this city rose like a song of joy into the sky. What would I not sacrifice to hear even a strain of that song again?  But to enter the heart of the Mythal?
an3ano39.speaker: anorrwyn

an3ano40.dialogue: Do you know what it is you demand?  The power of the weave is great, greater perhaps than strength left in my spirit.
an3ano40.speaker: anorrwyn

an3ano43.dialogue: But how can I refuse?  For the sake of hope, you have braved the depths of the catacombs and beaten back the abominations that defiled our holy places. I will do what I can.
an3ano43.speaker: anorrwyn

an3ano44.dialogue: So you hope I will become its Communicant, and brave the Mythal's fire?
an3ano44.speaker: anorrwyn

an3ano45.dialogue: What you ask may be beyond me. The power of the weave is great, greater perhaps than the strength left in my spirit.
an3ano45.speaker: anorrwyn

an3ano46.dialogue: But how can I not try, when you've already risked life and limb all for the sake of hope?  I will do what I can.
an3ano46.speaker: anorrwyn

an3ano47.dialogue: No!  The fire of the weave would consume you. You have fought bravely and well. This last sacrifice is not yours to make.
an3ano47.speaker: anorrwyn

an3ano48.dialogue: I shall speak the incantation, and offer myself as the new Communicant. It may be that communing with the Mythal requires more power than I have left in my spirit.
an3ano48.speaker: anorrwyn

an3ano49.dialogue: But if you can brave the depths of the catacombs, all for the sake of hope, then I can gather hope to brave the Mythal's fiery web.
an3ano49.speaker: anorrwyn

an3ano50.dialogue: Long ago, the Coronal entrusted the Onaglym dwarves with the Gems of the Weave. Their fortress hides one yet. I will seek out the dwarf spirit Harldain Ironbar and tell him of our need.
an3ano50.speaker: anorrwyn

an3ano51.dialogue: Fetch the Gem from him to the Speculum and scale the dragon's back. Antarn's gate will open to you now.
an3ano51.speaker: anorrwyn
an3ano51.desc: she casts a spell to enable this

an3DM04.dialogue: Anorrweyn's spell marks you with the fire tattoo, which enables you to pass through Antarn's gate.
an3DM04.speaker: DM

an3ano52.dialogue: Bring the Gem to the Speculum and scale the dragon's back. Antarn's gate will open to you now.
an3ano52.speaker: anorrwyn
an3ano52.desc: she casts a spell to enable this

an3DM05.dialogue: Anorrweyn's spell marks you with the fire tattoo, which enables you to pass through Antarn's gate.
an3DM05.speaker: DM

an3ano53.dialogue: When you've placed the Gem upon the dragon's spines, I will take my place beneath it and speak the Incantation of the Weave. With Mystra's aid, what strength I have will serve.
an3ano53.speaker: anorrwyn

an3ano54.dialogue: Be mindful, though: the forces of your enemies will move with determination now. Your rescue of the baelnorn marks you as a threat to them. Mystra's blessings go with you.
an3ano54.speaker: anorrwyn

an3pro00.speaker: Protagonist

an3pro01.speaker: Protagonist

an3pro02.dialogue: Tell her you retrieved her skull from the drow
an3pro02.speaker: Protagonist

an3pro03.dialogue: Ask what she will do now
an3pro03.speaker: Protagonist

an3pro05.dialogue: Ask her who else can restore the Mythal
an3pro05.speaker: Protagonist

an3pro06.dialogue: Ask what happens if the Mythal cannot be restored
an3pro06.speaker: Protagonist

an3pro07.dialogue: Tell her the Cult held the baelnorn prisoner
an3pro07.speaker: Protagonist

an3pro08.dialogue: Tell her you rescued the baelnorn from the Cult
an3pro08.speaker: Protagonist

an3pro09.dialogue: Tell her Miroden destroyed the Sapphire
an3pro09.speaker: Protagonist

an3pro10.dialogue: Explain he destroyed the Gem to keep it from the Cult
an3pro10.speaker: Protagonist

an3pro11.dialogue: Tell her she must be the Communicant now
an3pro11.speaker: Protagonist

an3pro12.dialogue: Ask what sacrifice she will make for Myth Drannor
an3pro12.speaker: Protagonist

an3pro13.dialogue: Tell her she must become a Communicant of the Weave
an3pro13.speaker: Protagonist

an3pro14.dialogue: Tell her one of you will become the Communicant
an3pro14.speaker: Protagonist

an3pro15.dialogue: Tell her she must use the Gem of the Weave
an3pro15.speaker: Protagonist

An1Ano03.dialogue: Are they no more?...the faithful of the Goddess of the Weave.
An1Ano03.speaker: Anorrwyn

An1Ano04.dialogue: So long, the temple languishes. Are we unremembered?
An1Ano04.speaker: Anorrwyn

An1Ano05.dialogue: Where are the Servants of Mystery?
An1Ano05.speaker: Anorrwyn

An1Ano06.dialogue: Can no one bring me the token of our Lady?  Do none attend her?
An1Ano06.speaker: Anorrwyn

An1Ano07.dialogue: Oh Mystra, I have failed you. The People are gone astray.
An1Ano07.speaker: Anorrwyn

an4ano02.dialogue: The Mythal is cleansed and I shall take my place as its new Communicant. You have restored hope to this land and peace to the soul of Miroden Silverblade. Myth Drannor is grateful.
an4ano02.speaker: Anorrwyn
an4ano02.desc: spoken, calm but joyous, with gratitude

an4ano03.dialogue: The Lady bless you and keep you. Her temple will always welcome you.
an4ano03.speaker: Anorrwyn
an4ano03.desc: spoken, administering a blessing, then a goodbye

an4ano04.dialogue: The blessings of Mystra go with you. Her temple will always welcome you.
an4ano04.speaker: Anorrwyn

at1DMa00.dialogue: The man in the cell is near to death. His body bears the marks of torture.
at1DMa00.speaker: DM

at1ath03.dialogue: You're no illusion? Then New Phlan did send heroes after us... The gatecall was not in vain.
at1ath03.speaker: Athan
at1ath03.desc: spoken, halting as if near to death

at1ath04.dialogue: I am Athan. And my breath is short. Hear me.
at1ath04.speaker: Athan

at1ath05.dialogue: The Cult of the Dragon has possession of Castle Cormanthor. They have raised a Pool of Radiance beneath it.
at1ath05.speaker: Athan

at1ath06.dialogue: The Pool sucks life from New Phlan, Mulmaster, all the port cities. With it, the Cult can put all of Faerun under their thrall.
at1ath06.speaker: Athan

at1ath07.dialogue: The Gauntlets of Moander. Elminster entrusted them to my band, but the Cult overpowered us and captured them. The Gauntlets can destroy the Pool. They must be regained.
at1ath07.speaker: Athan

at1ath08.dialogue: She carries them with her, always. Kya Mordrayn.
at1ath08.speaker: Athan

at1ath09.dialogue: The most powerful of their fighters and mages guard the castle. Dragonkin aid them, as well as drow and orog made mindless slaves by the touch of the Pool of Radiance.
at1ath09.speaker: Athan

at1ath10.dialogue: Kya Mordrayn leads them, with her creature Pelendralaar. He is a dracolich. Vicious and immense in power. Their minions mark themselves with the dragon scars.
at1ath10.speaker: Athan

at1ath11.dialogue: She has taken command of the Mythal. She controls it, and the Pool of Radiance, from a cavern deep beneath the castle.
at1ath11.speaker: Athan

at1ath12.dialogue: Pelendralaar is the master of Mordrayn's army. It was he who drove the most powerful of Myth Drannor's monsters from the city Heights so Mordrayn could make her nest.
at1ath12.speaker: Athan

at1ath13.dialogue: Devils. Alhoon. Phaerrim. They all scattered before him. Mordrayn bends the Mythal around him like a shield. While she controls it he is invulnerable.
at1ath13.speaker: Athan

at1ath14.dialogue: Mordrayn's mages have been hard at work sealing even the most secret entrances from within. I saw only one flaw in their defense.
at1ath14.speaker: Athan

at1ath15.dialogue: The dragonkin have made an aerie of the throne room of the Coronal, which is open to the sky. If you can find a way to climb the battlements, you may be able to gain entrance there.
at1ath15.speaker: Athan

at1ath16.dialogue: I saw such a gem in the Pool cavern when they brought me before Mordrayn. When she stood beneath it, the Mythal's magic enveloped her and she was heedless of all else.
at1ath16.speaker: Athan

at1ath17.dialogue: Healing?  Let me join you, and your healing spells will not be wasted! But if you cannot take me in your party, save your benisons. You will need them yourselves soon enough.
at1ath17.speaker: Athan

at1ath19.dialogue: Yes! If you can heal me, then give me the chance! My friends in ashes... The weeks of agony... Through all this shame, only the hope of justice kept me sane. Vengeance! Let us strike at them together.
at1ath19.speaker: Athan

at1ath20.dialogue: If you can heal me, then give me the chance! You bear your slain, which is noble, but the deeds before you call for the might of the living.
at1ath20.speaker: Athan

at1ath21.dialogue: Only give me the chance!  If any of your band would step aside, I will join you to rip vengeance from the Cult.
at1ath21.speaker: Athan

at1ath24.dialogue: Lay the dead to rest and I'll avenge them with you. Elsewise I'll make my way to the Nightingale Court and, once mended, find a way to strike at the Cult myself.
at1ath24.speaker: Athan

at1ath25.dialogue: Elsewise I'll make my way to the Nightingale Court and, once mended, find my own path to strike at them.
at1ath25.speaker: Athan

at1ath27.dialogue: Listen. All through the Cult's torture, they pried into my mind. Your deeds came to me through their fear of you. The destruction of the spawn pools, the freeing of the baelnorn...You have struck them to the core.
at1ath27.speaker: Athan

at1ath28.dialogue: You have the strength and the cunning to destroy them. Here, I am nothing. With you, I can be my comrades' avenging wrath. Let me join you. Let us rip this power from their grasp together.
at1ath28.speaker: Athan

at1ath29.dialogue: Their games have left my body a ruin, but heal me and my fury will be a weapon in your hands. If any of your company will step aside, take me with you that we may tear vengeance from the Cult together.
at1ath29.speaker: Athan

at1ath30.dialogue: You have the strength and the cunning to destroy them. If you can heal me, let me join you on your quest. Bury your dead. Together we can be their avenging wrath.
at1ath30.speaker: Athan

at1ath31.dialogue: Elsewise I'll make my way to the Nightingale Court and, once mended, find my own path to strike against the foe.
at1ath31.speaker: Athan

at1ath32.dialogue: Go with the gods. I will find my way out to the Nightingale Court, and heal upon the blueglow moss. Healed, I will make my own way against the Cult.
at1ath32.speaker: Athan

at1ath33.dialogue: Come, time is short. Let us be off. Our enemies and our destinies await us.
at1ath33.speaker: Athan

at1ath34.dialogue: Enough, time is short. The Cult's hold on Faerun tightens by the hour. If you will have me, my strength is yours. Otherwise, my prayers go with you.
at1ath34.speaker: Athan

at1ath35.dialogue: Then let us be off. Mordrayn and Pelendralaar await.
at1ath35.speaker: Athan

at1pro04.dialogue: Ask where they keep the Sapphire of the Weave
at1pro04.speaker: Protagonist

at1pro05.dialogue: Ask where the Gauntlets can be found
at1pro05.speaker: Protagonist

at1pro06.dialogue: Ask how you can destroy the Pool of Radiance
at1pro06.speaker: Protagonist

at1pro08.dialogue: Ask if he would join you in your quest
at1pro08.speaker: Protagonist

at1pro11.dialogue: Agree to take Athan into the party
at1pro11.speaker: Protagonist

at2ath02.dialogue: Dracolich slayers! All of New Phlan thanks you for your deeds.  The Pool is dead, and for now, its evil is beaten back to hell.
at2ath02.speaker: Athan

at2ath03.dialogue: Your deeds are sung up and down Faerun, my friends. They say the crack of Pelendralaar's bones was heard in the Far Reaches. All of New Phlan thanks you.
at2ath03.speaker: Athan

at2ath04.dialogue: Dracolich slayers! All of New Phlan thanks you for your deeds.  The Pool is dead, and for now, its evil is beaten back to the dark place it came from.
at2ath04.speaker: Athan

at2ath05.dialogue: Friends! My blade sings all the sweeter since we sent Mordrayn to Hell. But never so keenly as when I walked with you. Let us join company again, and cleanse the darkness from this place together.
at2ath05.speaker: Athan

at2ath06.dialogue: Friends! My blade sings all the sweeter since we sent Mordrayn to meet her masters. But never so keenly as when I walked with you. Let us join company again, and cleanse the darkness from this place together.
at2ath06.speaker: Athan

at2ath07.dialogue: Let me take up arms with you, if you would have another companion. I would be honored to walk by your side.
at2ath07.speaker: Athan

at2ath08.dialogue: If you will have another companion, let me take up arms with you again. Together, we can overcome any foe!
at2ath08.speaker: Athan

ba1mir01.dialogue: Freedom, at last. All is not lost.
ba1mir01.speaker: Miroden

ba1mir02.dialogue: Whoever you be, your valor has freed me from a terrible enemy. Let us be quick.
ba1mir02.speaker: Miroden

ba2mir02.dialogue: We are safe here. For a time.
ba2mir02.speaker: Miroden

ba2mir03.dialogue: I am Miroden Silverblade. Protector. Baelnorn.
ba2mir03.speaker: Miroden

ba2mir04.dialogue: Centuries ago, I was an armathor of the realm. A confidant to the Coronal, and a mage of the high court.
ba2mir04.speaker: Miroden

ba2mir05.dialogue: When Myth Drannor fell, I sacrificed all that was my life to bind myself to the Mythal. To tend it through the Sapphire of the Weave.
ba2mir05.speaker: Miroden

ba2mir06.dialogue: I have lain undisturbed in these lairs since, communing with the Mythal, knitting together its fraying weave as the years fell away.
ba2mir06.speaker: Miroden

ba2mir07.dialogue: Myth Drannor crumbled. All that I knew withered and died. Rivals, enemies, lovers, even the trees that held our towers to the sky. But I remained. Tending the Mythal. Protecting what was left of our majesty, our hope.
ba2mir07.speaker: Miroden

ba2mir08.dialogue: Until now. They came. The Cult of the Dragon. I had... grown weak in my solitude. I succumbed where I should have stood fast...
ba2mir08.speaker: Miroden

ba2mir09.dialogue: But you have freed me. There is hope yet.
ba2mir09.speaker: Miroden

ba2mir10.dialogue: Anorrweyn survives?  I thought the years had claimed her spirit. She would come to me, not so many decades ago. She knew her visits lightened the burden of my time.
ba2mir10.speaker: Miroden

ba2mir11.dialogue: We would speak of the old days, the golden days before the Weeping Wars. The fashions, and the intrigues, the arrogant and the beautiful...
ba2mir11.speaker: Miroden

ba2mir12.dialogue: No. My time is done. Another must lift the burden now. I am Protector no more.
ba2mir12.speaker: Miroden

ba2mir13.dialogue: My time is done. Another must lift the burden I have carried. The Mythal needs a new Protector.
ba2mir13.speaker: Miroden

ba2mir14.dialogue: Live? I have not lived since the Year of Doom!  No breath. No blood. What life could they take from me?
ba2mir14.speaker: Miroden

ba2mir15.dialogue: Pain is their delight. Bondage. And humiliation.
ba2mir15.speaker: Miroden

ba2mir18.dialogue: They came to me. They wanted the Sapphire. They pried into my mind.
ba2mir18.speaker: Miroden

ba2mir21.dialogue: Do you think I would let them have it?  Do you think I would betray centuries of trust?
ba2mir21.speaker: Miroden

ba2mir22.dialogue: I have destroyed it!  It is no more!
ba2mir22.speaker: Miroden

ba2mir23.dialogue: I cannot... I cannot... Do you not see?
ba2mir23.speaker: Miroden

ba2mir24.dialogue: Forgive my outburst. I am... unsteady.
ba2mir24.speaker: Miroden

ba2mir25.dialogue: I have destroyed that which I swore to protect.
ba2mir25.speaker: Miroden

ba2mir26.dialogue: But the Mythal must be restored. A new Communicant must be found. A new Gem dedicated to the Weave. I have failed, but you can succeed.
ba2mir26.speaker: Miroden

ba2mir27.dialogue: The Gems were a gift from the dwarf lords.
ba2mir27.speaker: Miroden

ba2mir28.dialogue: They mined the deepest reaches of the Far Hills to find them. A Ruby, a Sapphire, and an Emerald.
ba2mir28.speaker: Miroden

ba2mir29.dialogue: The Ruby was destroyed by the nycaloth, when the Armies of Darkness besieged the city. But if the House of Gems still stands, the Emerald survives. It was hidden for safe-keeping in the hoard of the Onaglym dwarves.
ba2mir29.speaker: Miroden

ba2mir30.dialogue: Ha!  Arrogant younglings!  Do you think you could withstand the Mythal's fire?
ba2mir30.speaker: Miroden

ba2mir31.dialogue: The incantation alone would wither your tongues. No, the Communicant must be versed in the ancient ways.
ba2mir31.speaker: Miroden

ba2mir32.dialogue: It is a dire role, but Anorrweyn Evensong will rise to the task. She is as bound to the dying dream of this city as I am. Beg her in my name to be the Communicant of the Weave.
ba2mir32.speaker: Miroden

ba2mir33.dialogue: There is a spirit, frail in appearance, iron strong in heart... Anorrweyn Evensong. She would come to me in years long past and ease my loneliness. If she survives, she would take up the task.
ba2mir33.speaker: Miroden

ba2mir34.dialogue: Do you question me?  What can you know of my regrets?  My hopes?  You who have walked on this earth mere moments to my centuries?
ba2mir34.speaker: Miroden

ba2mir35.dialogue: How can you know what strength it takes to destroy that which you gave all to preserve?
ba2mir35.speaker: Miroden

ba2mir36.dialogue: You are young. You cannot know. The centuries have exhausted me. But Myth Drannor has need of you.
ba2mir36.speaker: Miroden

ba2mir37.dialogue: They are cunning. And she most cunning of all. Soft words... Promises...
ba2mir37.speaker: Miroden

ba2mir38.dialogue: But it is done. And the cost is too high to repay.
ba2mir38.speaker: Miroden

ba2mir39.dialogue: The Cult grows stronger by the day. Their mistress whips them into a frenzy of destruction. She calls up drow from the Underdark to further her ends, and under Castle Cormanthor...
ba2mir39.speaker: Miroden

ba2mir40.dialogue: They speak of a terrible Pool of Radiance that shreds the soul from flesh. It draws life from its hungry mouths throughout Faerun. Without the Mythal's strength, we cannot hope to stop them.
ba2mir40.speaker: Miroden

ba2mir41.dialogue: Claim the Gem. Find it a Communicant.
ba2mir41.speaker: Miroden

ba2mir42.dialogue: My treasure I give you, to aid you in this cause. Weapons and armor the likes of which have not been worn by flesh since the empire's fall.
ba2mir42.speaker: Miroden

ba2mir43.dialogue: Take them, for my work in this world is finished. When you have restored the Mythal I will sleep at last....At long last.
ba2mir43.speaker: Miroden

ba2mir45.dialogue: The hoard of the Onaglym dwarves holds the last remaining Gem of the Weave. An Emerald which can be tuned to the Mythal.
ba2mir45.speaker: Miroden

ba2mir46.dialogue: A new Communicant must take on the role I left behind. No mortal, but one as untouched by life as I.
ba2mir46.speaker: Miroden

ba2pro01.dialogue: Ask him how you can help
ba2pro01.speaker: Protagonist

ba2pro02.dialogue: Ask him to tune the Mythal
ba2pro02.speaker: Protagonist

ba2pro03.dialogue: Ask him why the Cult let him live
ba2pro03.speaker: Protagonist

ba2pro04.dialogue: Tell him to use the Sapphire now
ba2pro04.speaker: Protagonist

ba2pro05.dialogue: Ask him why he is no longer the Protector
ba2pro05.speaker: Protagonist

ba2pro06.dialogue: Tell him to use the Sapphire now
ba2pro06.speaker: Protagonist

ba2pro07.dialogue: Ask him why he won't use the Sapphire
ba2pro07.speaker: Protagonist

ba2pro08.dialogue: Tell him the Mythal is corrupted, he must tune it
ba2pro08.speaker: Protagonist

ba2pro09.dialogue: Tell him you have no time for excuses
ba2pro09.speaker: Protagonist

ba2pro10.dialogue: Ask him where a new Gem can be found
ba2pro10.speaker: Protagonist

ba2pro11.dialogue: Tell him one of you will volunteer to be the Communicant
ba2pro11.speaker: Protagonist

ba2pro12.dialogue: Ask him who can serve as Communicant
ba2pro12.speaker: Protagonist

ba2pro13.dialogue: Ask him why he destroyed the Gem
ba2pro13.speaker: Protagonist

ba2pro14.dialogue: Ask him how the Cult defeated him
ba2pro14.speaker: Protagonist

ba2pro15.dialogue: Tell him you will find a new Gem
ba2pro15.speaker: Protagonist

ba2pro16.dialogue: Leave the baelnorn to his misery
ba2pro16.speaker: Protagonist

ba3ano00.dialogue: Miroden Silverblade. Where is the Sapphire of the Weave?
ba3ano00.speaker: Anorweyn
ba3ano00.desc: spoken, infinite sadness, she suspects the truth

ba3mir03.dialogue: Anorrweyn - Do you remember the silvertrees in the courtyard of the Maerdrym?  How the Windsong Towers brushed against the stars?
ba3mir03.speaker: Miroden

ba3ano01.dialogue: Speak plainly now, Miroden. Your lies have cost these children dearly.
ba3ano01.speaker: Anorweyn

ba3mir04.dialogue: She... came to me. She begged me to use the Gem, to raise a Pool of Radiance under Castle Cormanthor. She swore the Pool would bring life to Myth Drannor, to the Mythal.
ba3mir04.speaker: Miroden

ba3mir05.dialogue: Kya Mordrayn.  The glory you knew will come again, she said. The Windsong Towers will rise again...I believed her.  I taught her the incantation.
ba3mir05.speaker: Miroden
ba3mir05.desc: spoken, defeated, despairing, explaining, feebly, finally confessing

ba3mir06.dialogue: The Pool brought life, yes,  stolen life. From Phlan, from everywhere...  I have destroyed our hopes.
ba3mir06.speaker: Miroden
ba3mir06.desc: spoken, doggedly continues his confession, grieved, somber

ba3ano04.dialogue: Hope lives. We have created a new Gem of the Weave.
ba3ano04.speaker: Anorweyn

ba3mir07.dialogue: Then I can be redeemed.  You must break her link with the Mythal. Find the Sapphire I gave her. Destroy it with this Word...
ba3mir07.speaker: Miroden

ba3DM00.dialogue: The Baelnorn's spell teaches you Ethgonil, the Word of Redemption.
ba3DM00.speaker: DM

ba3ano05.dialogue: Children, your place in this weave is clear: enter the Castle and find the Gem. Speak the Word, and when the Sapphire is destroyed, I will turn the Mythal's power against our enemies.
ba3ano05.speaker: Anorweyn

ba3ano06.dialogue: What we ask is not easy. Only your strength stands between us and despair. Mystra's blessing go with you, children, as do all our hopes.
ba3ano06.speaker: Anorweyn

ba3mir09.dialogue: The time I knew is past. It will not come again. But the future... That you can still save. Go!
ba3mir09.speaker: Miroden
ba3mir09.desc: spoken, almost to himself, to the party, intensely

ba3DM01.dialogue: The baelnorn opens a Gate to take you into Castle Cormanthor. Now the fate of Myth Drannor and all Faerun rests in your hands.
ba3DM01.speaker: DM
ba3DM01.desc: (text change)MAB, 07-02-01: made this spoken: localizers: SPOKEN, to the party

be5fae00.dialogue: Beriand! Tell them what we learned.
be5fae00.speaker: Faeril

be5ber05.dialogue: Travellers, I have heard a rumor from Nottle, concerning the scarred mages.
be5ber05.speaker: Beriand

be5ber06.dialogue: We have been waiting patiently for you to return.
be5ber06.speaker: Beriand

be5fae01.dialogue: Beriand had been patient, maybe. But I have not! Come, come, tell us your news.
be5fae01.speaker: Faeril

be5ber07.dialogue: It has been quiet here, perhaps too quiet.
be5ber07.speaker: Beriand

be5fae02.dialogue: I tire of looking at these walls, and pacing this floor, and swinging my mace only at the air!
be5fae02.speaker: Faeril

be5ber08.dialogue: Travelers - while you were out, we have been gathering tales about places in the dungeons.
be5ber08.speaker: Beriand

be5fae03.dialogue: Beriand! Tell them what I saw.
be5fae03.speaker: Faeril

be5ber10.dialogue: Oh no, Faeril, if they want to hear it they must hear it from you.
be5ber10.speaker: Beriand

be5ber11.dialogue: I am glad you have come. The shelter has been under attack.
be5ber11.speaker: Beriand

be5fae04.dialogue: By orogs I think, and behind those ugly beasts, some dark hand urging them on.
be5fae04.speaker: Faeril

be5fae05.dialogue: I wished to slay them! But Beriand said nay, and eventually they moved on, to batter at other doors.
be5fae05.speaker: Faeril

be5ber13.dialogue: Friends - I must tell you - we have had a narrow escape.
be5ber13.speaker: Beriand

be5fae06.dialogue: By the Lady! Death was close to us.
be5fae06.speaker: Faeril

be5ber14.dialogue: But once again Faeril's great heart saved us.
be5ber14.speaker: Beriand

be5ber17.dialogue: Tell us, travelers, what has happened to you.
be5ber17.speaker: Beriand

be5fae07.dialogue: And you bear dead. If only the staff Deathbane was back in Beriand's hand!
be5fae07.speaker: Faeril

be5ber18.dialogue: Friends - we are worried - Nottle seems to be missing.
be5ber18.speaker: Beriand

be5fae08.dialogue: Orcs took it, and fled down the Main Halls. If Beriand had Deathbane back, once again he might raise the dead - if the Lady Mystra wills it.
be5fae08.speaker: Faeril

be5ber26.dialogue: He thinks they belong to some kind of secret brotherhood. Some power is behind them - a deep and dark power indeed, he says.
be5ber26.speaker: Beriand

be5fae09.dialogue: Of course, that does not prevent him from trading with them, the scurrilous sandwag!
be5fae09.speaker: Faeril

be5ber27.dialogue: Not so harshly, Faeril! He gives them trinkets, yes, but he takes their secrets. Not every hero wields a sword, or wears shining armor.
be5ber27.speaker: Beriand

be5fae10.dialogue: I do not know what to think! I was outside, near Nottle's wagon, and I saw... I saw... I do not know what I saw.
be5fae10.speaker: Faeril

be5fae11.dialogue: She was a serpent, a great serpent, all shimmery in silver, gold and green. She smelled of flowers!
be5fae11.speaker: Faeril

be5fae12.dialogue: She looked right at me - how her eyes flashed! But then she was gone, into a cleft in the rocks. I wonder who she was.
be5fae12.speaker: Faeril

be5ber29.dialogue: I opened the door to the outside - it was foolish, but all seemed quiet, and I wanted to smell the air and hear the wind in the trees.
be5ber29.speaker: Beriand

be5ber30.dialogue: There were three of the lizardfolk there - who came fast for me. But Faeril stepped forward and fetched one of them such a blow...
be5ber30.speaker: Beriand

be5fae13.dialogue: The Lady guided my hand, and strengthened my arm! I am sure of it!
be5fae13.speaker: Faeril

be5ber31.dialogue: It was enough for them, and they ran. Beware the lizardfolk, my friends, they too walk with a dark purpose these days, darker even than their usual love for human flesh to eat.
be5ber31.speaker: Beriand

be5ber32.dialogue: He did not say. But he had recently returned from the Deep Halls of the dungeon, and he said he had met some of the scarred mages there, and talked about trading.
be5ber32.speaker: Beriand

be5ber33.dialogue: There is not much to tell about the small area we're in, a place we call Stillwater.
be5ber33.speaker: Beriand

be5ber34.dialogue: This is a quiet area, overlooked by everyone except the orcs and undead. But there are very few places indeed that those swarming creatures overlook.
be5ber34.speaker: Beriand

be5ber36.dialogue: As we told you, the Ring of Calling was on the Skeletal Arm, which the scarred mages took from Athan's band...
be5ber36.speaker: Beriand

be5ber37.dialogue: Nottle says there are many scarred mages in the Halls of Light, the upper halls of the dungeons. One of those mages may have the Arm.
be5ber37.speaker: Beriand

be5ber38.dialogue: Ah yes, and the Ring is bound fast to the bones. Athan could not get the Ring off, no matter how hard he tried...
be5ber38.speaker: Beriand

be5fae14.dialogue: It will take great magic to release that Ring. Maybe you should go to the Hall of Wizards!
be5fae14.speaker: Faeril

be5ber39.dialogue: But how to get there? I believe all the normal routes were blocked up centuries ago. But maybe there is a magical path that remains - Athan thought so, and so does Nottle.
be5ber39.speaker: Beriand

be5fae15.dialogue: Then you must use it to escape the foul dungeons!
be5fae15.speaker: Faeril

be5ber41.dialogue: Yes, it is said that the Ring will open the Seal of Mythanthor, which is somewhere in the Halls of Light, I believe.
be5ber41.speaker: Beriand

be5ber42.dialogue: And through the Circle, you may at last reach the City Heights, and walk through the glorious ruin of Myth Drannor.
be5ber42.speaker: Beriand

be5ber46.dialogue: We have news for you! We have had a visitor.
be5ber46.speaker: Beriand

be5fae16.dialogue: Yes. Some fast-talking friend of Nottle's.
be5fae16.speaker: Faeril

be5ber47.dialogue: I have news for you! I have had a visitor - a friend of Nottle's.
be5ber47.speaker: Beriand

be5ber48.dialogue: Travellers! You told us earlier that our adversary is the Cult of the Dragon....
be5ber48.speaker: Beriand

be5fae17.dialogue: We have learned something about that fell company.
be5fae17.speaker: Faeril

be5jar00.dialogue: Tymora help me, if I could crawl back into my boulder, I would!
be5jar00.speaker: Jarial

be5ber50.dialogue: Travellers, I have heard some dire news - about the Cult of the Dragon.
be5ber50.speaker: Beriand

be5ber51.dialogue: Good news! There may be friends nearby who could aid you.
be5ber51.speaker: Beriand

be5jar01.dialogue: I have felt the presence of the Silver Fire!
be5jar01.speaker: Jarial

be5jar02.dialogue: Have you seen Nottle? He seems to have disappeared!
be5jar02.speaker: Jarial

be5ber53.dialogue: I am concerned about Nottle. He has been gone a long time.
be5ber53.speaker: Beriand

be5ber55.dialogue: I hope you are able to help Anorrweyn Evensong - she is much beloved by Mystra.
be5ber55.speaker: Beriand

be5ber56.dialogue: It has been quiet here. I crave your news.
be5ber56.speaker: Beriand

be5jar03.dialogue: Quiet, yes. But I sense great magics in the air, spells laid with deadly skill.
be5jar03.speaker: Jarial

be5ber57.dialogue: Travelers - enemies have been battering at our door!
be5ber57.speaker: Beriand

be5jar04.dialogue: Until I cast a spell! And raised such a stinking cloud that many of them were overcome!
be5jar04.speaker: Jarial

be5ber58.dialogue: Friends - I must tell you - we have been hard pressed here.
be5ber58.speaker: Beriand

be5jar05.dialogue: I was sure our time had ended.
be5jar05.speaker: Jarial

be5ber61.dialogue: Welcome back, friends. You have a question?
be5ber61.speaker: Beriand

be5fae18.dialogue: His name was Tudo, and I like him not at all!
be5fae18.speaker: Faeril

be5ber65.dialogue: He is a rogue, I gather, of no small ability - and quite comfortable plying his trade, picking at the bones of old Myth Drannor.
be5ber65.speaker: Beriand

be5ber67.dialogue: The Cult is a very secretive organization, as you may know - usually divided by factions and infighting and backstabbing. This keeps them from ever strking out with their full power.
be5ber67.speaker: Beriand

be5ber68.dialogue: A Pool of Radiance is a mighty thing, however! Faced with its power, all the Cult seems to have come to an agreement - to protect the Pool and nurture it.
be5ber68.speaker: Beriand

be5ber69.dialogue: I am afraid the Cult forces here are going to grow in strength very rapidly. Soon, no one will be able to stand against them.
be5ber69.speaker: Beriand

be5ber70.dialogue: He did not say. But he had recently returned from the Deep Halls of the dungeon, and he said he had met some of the scarred mages there, and talked about trading.
be5ber70.speaker: Beriand

be5ber71.dialogue: I think they were orogs, but they seemed strange to me. They seemed dull, as if the souls had been ripped from them.
be5ber71.speaker: Beriand

be5ber72.dialogue: Undead, dozens of them. Perhaps hundreds.
be5ber72.speaker: Beriand

be5ber74.dialogue: You seek a spirit? Myth Drannor is overrun with the ghostly remnants of the dead.
be5ber74.speaker: Beriand

be5ber75.dialogue: But since it is a dwarf lord you seek, I suggest you look in the great dwarven halls of old - the Halls of Light, and the Onaglym, the House of Gems.
be5ber75.speaker: Beriand

be5ber77.dialogue: Something is preventing the dwarf lord's spirit from communicating with you. Some evil thing, probably.
be5ber77.speaker: Beriand

be5fae19.dialogue: You must find it - and destroy it!
be5fae19.speaker: Faeril

be5ber79.dialogue: A torc is a neckpiece, is it not? A rare one, certainly. Almost any creature might hold a treasure like that in its lair. I do not know any more about it than that.
be5ber79.speaker: Beriand

be5fae20.dialogue: I never saw anything like it on our travels.
be5fae20.speaker: Faeril

be5ber81.dialogue: Ah, the sorrow must be almost unbearable, to be dead yet still tied to your dusty bones. What you propose to do for the Lady Anorrweyn must be a great comfort to her.
be5ber81.speaker: Beriand

be5fae21.dialogue: By the Mother! How I wish I could assist you!
be5fae21.speaker: Faeril

be5ber83.dialogue: It will be a difficult task - her enemies will have taken the skull deep into the dark, hoping it will never again be found.
be5ber83.speaker: Beriand

be5ber84.dialogue: If Anorrweyn's skull is in the Catacombs, you must find a way to get into that fell place.
be5ber84.speaker: Beriand

be5ber88.dialogue: I am glad to see you again.
be5ber88.speaker: Beriand

be5ber89.dialogue: Welcome, travellers. I have at least one new tale to tell you, thanks to Nottle.
be5ber89.speaker: Beriand

be5ber90.dialogue: By the Hand of Mystery, that was a narrow escape! I am much indebted to you for your aid against the Cult.
be5ber90.speaker: Beriand

be5ber91.dialogue: Ask - and I will tell you what I know.
be5ber91.speaker: Beriand

be5ber95.dialogue: As I said, I heard this tale from Nottle, so you can judge for yourself what truth may be in it.
be5ber95.speaker: Beriand

be5fae22.dialogue: He would not tell us how he came to learn such a tale!
be5fae22.speaker: Faeril

be5ber96.dialogue: A great wizard has arrived in Myth Drannor - Azmark Duathel, from the Zulkir's Court in Thay. When I heard this, I was overjoyed - here is powerful help, indeed!
be5ber96.speaker: Beriand

be5fae23.dialogue: He is renowned for his bravery in opposing the Red Wizards.
be5fae23.speaker: Faeril

be5ber97.dialogue: But what Nottle has learned is this - Azmark Duathel is secretly a member of the Cult of the Dragon. He has come to help defend the Pool of Radiance.
be5ber97.speaker: Beriand

be5ber98.dialogue: So what seemed to be our great hope has turned instead to great dismay.
be5ber98.speaker: Beriand

be5bera0.dialogue: A creature like that would be far underground, and his holdings well-protected and not easy to find.
be5bera0.speaker: Beriand

be5bera2.dialogue: Surely you do not mean me? If so, I am honored, but must tell you, such a thing would be far beyond my power, or indeed that of almost any mortal.
be5bera2.speaker: Beriand

be5bera3.dialogue: What of the Lady Anorrweyn, beloved of Mystra? She could wield the power, if she would.
be5bera3.speaker: Beriand

be5bera5.dialogue: Surely the dwarf lord Harldain Ironbar is your only hope to obtain such a thing.
be5bera5.speaker: Beriand

be5bera6.dialogue: Then your long task is nearly done. Mystra be praised!
be5bera6.speaker: Beriand

be5bera8.dialogue: Greetings, my friends. I will tell you where evil lurks, if I may.
be5bera8.speaker: Beriand

be5bera9.dialogue: I welcome you once again, in the name of Mystra.
be5bera9.speaker: Beriand

be5berb0.dialogue: You have been busy, or so I have heard.
be5berb0.speaker: Beriand

be5berb4.dialogue: What part of the city are you interested in?
be5berb4.speaker: Beriand

be5berb5.dialogue: Perhaps I can help you find treasures to aid you against the Cult.
be5berb5.speaker: Beriand

be5berb6.dialogue: Greetings, and the blessing of Mystra upon you all.
be5berb6.speaker: Beriand

be5berb8.dialogue: Have you looked in our book? It will teach you the Word of Power that unseals the Tumbledown Door.
be5berb8.speaker: Beriand

be5berb9.dialogue: That door is sealed with the Glyph of Mystra. Learn the Word, and the Glyph will unseal for you.
be5berb9.speaker: Beriand

be5berc0.dialogue: You have learned the Word of Mystra! Now try to open the sealed door. It leads into the dungeons.
be5berc0.speaker: Beriand

be5berc5.dialogue: Well, here is a story. When we were wandering down in the Main Halls, Faeril did a very clever thing.
be5berc5.speaker: Beriand

be5faeYB.dialogue: Clever! Do not think so! We were desperate.
be5faeYB.speaker: Faeril

be5berc6.dialogue: So we were. We had hidden ourselves from a large group of orcs, but they were on the verge of finding us...
be5berc6.speaker: Beriand

be5faeYC.dialogue: ...so I threw a stone at the head of Mol, their captain.
be5faeYC.speaker: Faeril

be5berc7.dialogue: It struck his forehead with a sound I shall never forget! He was furious! And while the brute was whacking off heads with his great lead mace, we crept away, forgotten.
be5berc7.speaker: Beriand

be5berc8.dialogue: Nottle told us that evil mages have taken over the stairs that lead from the Main Halls to the Upper Halls. They have undead servants with them.
be5berc8.speaker: Beriand

be5fae24.dialogue: I remember those stairs! They are far away to the east. You pass through endless halls, and the stairs are in a room at the end.
be5fae24.speaker: Faeril

be5berc9.dialogue: But take care, if what Nottle said is true. For he also said that the scarred ones scare him - and our friend Nottle does not scare easily.
be5berc9.speaker: Beriand

be5berd1.dialogue: Here is a tale - a strange one. When Faeril and I were lost in the dungeons, we came across a most helpful fellow.
be5berd1.speaker: Beriand

be5berd2.dialogue: He was locked away in a cell, but we could hear his voice. He gave us advice on how to stay alive.
be5berd2.speaker: Beriand

be5fae26.dialogue: He hates orcs more than I do! If such a thing be possible.
be5fae26.speaker: Faeril

be5berd3.dialogue: Up far to the northeast his cell was. I remember him mentioning necklaces, amulets and torcs. He seemed to treasure them.
be5berd3.speaker: Beriand

be5berd5.dialogue: Well, Nottle once told Faeril and me the tale of the Crazy Laughing Man.
be5berd5.speaker: Beriand

be5fae27.dialogue: Surely you did not believe him, Beriand! It is clearly a tall tale.
be5fae27.speaker: Faeril

be5berd6.dialogue: Somewhere in the Main Halls it was, that Nottle saw this man, trading jokes with a dark naga. Do you know of these nagas? Big serpent creatures, with powerful magics and a thirst for fresh blood.
be5berd6.speaker: Beriand

be5berd7.dialogue: How a man could befriend one is beyond my ken. But Nottle swears the story is true.
be5berd7.speaker: Beriand

be5bere0.dialogue: Have you ever met an Ormyrr? Fearsome they look, and fearsome they are indeed in battle - but they are not evil creatures.
be5bere0.speaker: Beriand

be5bere1.dialogue: We came upon the tracks of a group of them, when we were down in the dungeons.
be5bere1.speaker: Beriand

be5fae28.dialogue: And heard them, too, from a distance. How they made the stone shake!
be5fae28.speaker: Faeril

be5bere2.dialogue: It is unusual for them to go underground. But we never talked with them, to learn what their story may be.
be5bere2.speaker: Beriand

be5fae29.dialogue: Beriand! Tell them the tale of the Ways of Mythanthor!
be5fae29.speaker: Faeril

be5bere6.dialogue: This tale is quite old. It is said that Mythanthor himself created portals throughout the city, great gateways of magic that the people were glad to use.
be5bere6.speaker: Beriand

be5bere7.dialogue: He put upon these gateways his great Seal. In days of old, the Ways were open to all. But when the Wars came, many of the Ways were sealed, and have been sealed ever since.
be5bere7.speaker: Beriand

be5fae30.dialogue: Well, I heard a tale once about the sorceress they called Borea.
be5fae30.speaker: Faeril

be5fae31.dialogue: She was from the deep North, and what power flowed in her veins! One drop of her blood could freeze a dozen men.
be5fae31.speaker: Faeril

be5fae32.dialogue: But woe for her! Her power was no match for the evils of this city. She came here in glory, and was never seen again.
be5fae32.speaker: Faeril

be5fae33.dialogue: How I wish I could understand the speech of orcs! For often I heard them muttering as we crept by them in the dungeon halls...
be5fae33.speaker: Faeril

be5fae34.dialogue: ...but all I know is, they are deathly afraid of their leader, some brute named Zud, and he dwells in a great hall somewhere in the northwest section of the Main Halls.
be5fae34.speaker: Faeril

be5berf4.dialogue: Now here is a thing. When we were in the dungeons, Faeril and I often crept by groups of orcs...
be5berf4.speaker: Beriand

be5berf5.dialogue: ...I could not make out all they said, but they often talked of their leader, Zud, and of the great hall of orcs. It is in the northwestern part of the dungeons, I am almost sure.
be5berf5.speaker: Beriand

be5berg0.dialogue: Here is a thing that Athan told us - something he heard when he passed through the south part of the Main Halls of the Dungeons...
be5berg0.speaker: Beriand

be5berg1.dialogue: He could sense an unearthly creature moving beyond a wall. It jingled and jangled, he said, as if it carried hundreds of keys.
be5berg1.speaker: Beriand

be5berg2.dialogue: But he could not figure out how to reach the creature. He heard it go down stairs, and then it disappeared.
be5berg2.speaker: Beriand

be5berg5.dialogue: One of Myth Drannor's treasures is the Wizard's Torc, a great neckpiece. Supposedly it was last worn by Ualair the Silent, the city's last Grand Mage.
be5berg5.speaker: Beriand

be5berg6.dialogue: The Wizard's Torc was lost when Myth Drannor was overrun, and has never been seen again, although rumors about it abounded in the Elven Court.
be5berg6.speaker: Beriand

be5fae35.dialogue: Here is a strange tale! When I was down in the dungeon, I heard three orcs speaking in the common tongue. One of them mentioned the Talking Room.
be5fae35.speaker: Faeril

be5fae36.dialogue: It seemed to be high upstairs and off to the east. There was something in the Talking Room, something they wanted...
be5fae36.speaker: Faeril

be5fae37.dialogue: ...but I did not learn what it was, because then I stepped out and killed them, alas.
be5fae37.speaker: Faeril

be5berh2.dialogue: Nottle has told us a tale, but I am not sure I am ready to believe it.
be5berh2.speaker: Beriand

be5berh3.dialogue: He said he came across a magical Gate. And undead beings were coming through it! More and more of them!
be5berh3.speaker: Beriand

be5fae38.dialogue: An abomination! Who would create such a thing?
be5fae38.speaker: Faeril

be5berh4.dialogue: Nottle said the Gate was near the center of the Halls of Stone. And he swears that that it was not there a fortnight ago.
be5berh4.speaker: Beriand

be5berh6.dialogue: It is said that of all the great books that once graced the libraries of Myth Drannor, only the evil ones remain.
be5berh6.speaker: Beriand

be5berh7.dialogue: These are dangerous books, but the guardians of Myth Drannor banded them with protective spells, so that none could look at them who were not powerful enough to stand against their evil.
be5berh7.speaker: Beriand

be5berh8.dialogue: But woe to us if these books should fall in the hands of evil! For if they somehow learn how to remove the protective spells, they could wield terrible instruments of evil against us.
be5berh8.speaker: Beriand

be5fae39.dialogue: Tell them of the waters I found!
be5fae39.speaker: Faeril

be5beri1.dialogue: Travelers, Faeril has saved my life many times, but never so skilfully as when she brought me the healing Waters of Life.
be5beri1.speaker: Beriand

be5beri2.dialogue: I was at the point of death - I could not heal myself. But she found a source of healing waters, somewhere in the Upper Halls of the Dungeons.
be5beri2.speaker: Beriand

be5fae40.dialogue: The Lady guided me, I am sure. And strengthened my arm when I battled with the lizardfolk guarding the well! And there were many of them.
be5fae40.speaker: Faeril

be5beri3.dialogue: And with Mystra's help she defeated the lizardfolk there. Maybe the well can aid you as well, in your travels.
be5beri3.speaker: Beriand

be5beri6.dialogue: Now this is a slight tale. But when we were in the Dungeons, Faeril and I once camped near a fountain. The waters ran clear and sweet then, not foul as they are now.
be5beri6.speaker: Beriand

be5beri7.dialogue: And in the dark I awoke once to hear a woman singing a beautiful song. Very faint it was, echoing up out of the splashing fountain.
be5beri7.speaker: Beriand

be5beri8.dialogue: That is all there is to my tale - except that the song lifted my heart, and gave me courage to go on.
be5beri8.speaker: Beriand

be5berj1.dialogue: Faeril, you have a good memory for places. Tell them what we learned about the Dungeons, as we wandered through.
be5berj1.speaker: Beriand

be5fae41.dialogue: We found four floors in the Dungeons. When you go through the Tumbledown Door, you enter the Main Halls. From there, there are two upper floors and one lower floor.
be5fae41.speaker: Faeril

be5fae42.dialogue: There are many orcs in the Main Halls. In the Upper Halls, we found many undead, as well as bands of lizardfolk who seem to be searching for something.
be5fae42.speaker: Faeril

be5fae43.dialogue: We spent as little time as possible in the Deep Halls. That was a nasty place! And we saw orogs there, who trooped about according to some dark plan.
be5fae43.speaker: Faeril

be5berj2.dialogue: In the Dungeons, I remember that there were four floors - two in the Upper Halls, one floor called the Main Halls, and one called the Deep Halls.
be5berj2.speaker: Beriand

be5berj3.dialogue: The Tumbledown Door leads you to the Main Halls. I remember there were many orcs there, when we traveled through.
be5berj3.speaker: Beriand

be5berk1.dialogue: Well now, as you know, Athan was looking for a way to get to the City Heights.
be5berk1.speaker: Beriand

be5berk2.dialogue: He told me a story about old Myth Drannor - that the city held magical devices that could whisk you from deepest pit to highest tower, all in a blink.
be5berk2.speaker: Beriand

be5berk3.dialogue: He was looking for one in particular - it moved within a circle of stones, and travelled from floor to floor. It went all the way up to a building on the City Heights.
be5berk3.speaker: Beriand

be5fae44.dialogue: He said he was following a trail of ice! But I did not understand what he meant.
be5fae44.speaker: Faeril

be5berk6.dialogue: Now, Nottle once told me a tale he heard from an orc.
be5berk6.speaker: Beriand

be5berk7.dialogue: The orc said that deep in the Dungeons, big spiderlike creatures hunt everything that moves, and take anything that glitters back to line their nests.
be5berk7.speaker: Beriand

be5berk8.dialogue: Many times the orcs had tried to win back these treasures, but each attempt met with disaster.
be5berk8.speaker: Beriand

be5berl1.dialogue: Surely you have heard already of the Mountain Fist? A great club, or perhaps it is a mace. The legends vary.
be5berl1.speaker: Beriand

be5berl2.dialogue: It is a mighty weapon, but not powerful enough to save its master from the chill touch of spirits. Legends say that he was turned to shadow, and went to stalk the deep underground, taking the Mountain Fist with him.
be5berl2.speaker: Beriand

be5berl5.dialogue: I do not know if this tale should be believed. It came to me in a dream.
be5berl5.speaker: Beriand

be5berl6.dialogue: In my dream I held something in my hand - I dared not look at it, but it was bright - so bright my whole hand glowed red as blood.
be5berl6.speaker: Beriand

be5berl7.dialogue: Before me there was an abyss in the shape of a grave. I closed my eyes - yes, in my dreams I can still see - and opened my hand, letting the bright object fall into the depths.
be5berl7.speaker: Beriand

be5berl8.dialogue: In only a moment a great wind sprung up, such that I was borne up, away from the abyss and into the bright sky, like a bird. Then I awoke.
be5berl8.speaker: Beriand

be5berm0.dialogue: When we were in the Deep Halls, we met a ghost of an elven woman - a cleric of Hanali Celanil. She did not speak, but it was clear she wished to show us something up in the Main Halls.
be5berm0.speaker: Beriand

be5fae45.dialogue: Alas! We could not go with her, and at last she disappeared.
be5fae45.speaker: Faeril

be5berm1.dialogue: But alas! We could not go with her, and at last she disappeared.
be5berm1.speaker: Beriand

be5berm2.dialogue: I do not know what she wanted, but it sorrowed her greatly. As you walk the Dungeons, watch for her.
be5berm2.speaker: Beriand

be5berm5.dialogue: I remember coming across several doors that were sealed with Glyphs, placed in the floor before them.
be5berm5.speaker: Beriand

be5fae46.dialogue: Yes! The Glyph of Water, and another foul Glyph I did not recognize.
be5fae46.speaker: Faeril

be5berm6.dialogue: These doors are sealed with strong magic. You cannot break into them - do not even try! For some of these Glyphs will destroy those who attempt to unwrite them.
be5berm6.speaker: Beriand

be5berm7.dialogue: To open these doors, learn the Word of Power that unseals the Glyph. Words can be found in books or on scrolls, or they can be learned from one who knows them.
be5berm7.speaker: Beriand

be5berm8.dialogue: Once learned, merely approach the Glyph. The Word will speak itself, the Glyph will open, and you may pass in safety.
be5berm8.speaker: Beriand

be5bern2.dialogue: An Ormyrr came by, and we talked. She said that drow had taken up residence in the Catacombs. Unusual for those creatures of darkness to dwell so close to the sunlight.
be5bern2.speaker: Beriand

be5bern3.dialogue: According to the Ormyrr, the drow have been raiding everywhere in the underground, seizing treasures wherever they may find them. Myth Drannor's sacred relics, in drow hands - it is horrible to imagine.
be5bern3.speaker: Beriand

be5bern5.dialogue: Here is a strange thing. I heard a creature shuffling about outside our shelter. I believe it was an orog, and he was fishing in our stream!
be5bern5.speaker: Beriand

be5bern6.dialogue: After much splashing and thrashing, I believe he caught something. He met with another of his kind, and they agreed to go back down to their master's chambers in the Catacombs.
be5bern6.speaker: Beriand

be5bern8.dialogue: I have never been to the Catacombs, so there is little I can tell you. In days of old, it was connected only to Castle Cormanthor, and so was considered the safest place in all of Myth Drannor.
be5bern8.speaker: Beriand

be5bern9.dialogue: The Catacombs were a stronghold where the elves laid up the city stores, studied their most dangerous magics, and buried their dead. And the dwarves had tombs there also, for there was friendship between them in those days.
be5bern9.speaker: Beriand

be5bero0.dialogue: I have heard tell that people were imprisoned there as well - the most incorrigible enemies of the city, of course, but also ones guilty only of embarrassing the Court. But that is just rumor.
be5bero0.speaker: Beriand

be5berp2.dialogue: I am reminded of a tale I heard years ago, when I lived in the Elven Court.
be5berp2.speaker: Beriand

be5berp3.dialogue: The tale concerned an eternal guardian of Myth Drannor, an undead elf. This baelnorn had a lair deep, deep underground - or so the tale said.
be5berp3.speaker: Beriand

be5berp5.dialogue: When I was young, there was an elf-woman who lived near me, of the great House of Ammath. - Don't worry, this tale does pertain to you!
be5berp5.speaker: Beriand

be5berp6.dialogue: She wore a magnificent cloak which was said to have come from Myth Drannor, from the Catacombs deep underneath the Castle.
be5berp6.speaker: Beriand

be5berp7.dialogue: When I touched it, I could tell it was once the cloak of Thyaast Ammath, a mage of great power - but who is said to have died by her own magic. And I tell you true, tragedy is woven into that cloak, as much as thread.
be5berp7.speaker: Beriand

be5berr3.dialogue: Of all the great buildings that existed on the City Heights of Myth Drannor, only three still exist: the House of Gems, the Speculum, and magnificent Castle Cormanthor.
be5berr3.speaker: Beriand

be5berr4.dialogue: The House of Gems is east of the center of the Heights, above the eastern end of the Dungeons. The Speculum is south of the center, and the Castle is to the northwest.
be5berr4.speaker: Beriand

be5berr5.dialogue: In its glory there were many more buildings - the Noble House of Ammath, and of course a beautiful shrine to the Lady of Mysteries. But they were utterly destroyed during the Fall, and now little if anything remains.
be5berr5.speaker: Beriand

be5berr6.dialogue: Travelers, did you know that in Myth Drannor, the buildings themselves can be ghosts? It is true - I have felt their presence myself.
be5berr6.speaker: Beriand

be5berr7.dialogue: The buildings slide back into being for a moment or an hour, then fade again into the whispering shadows of time.
be5berr7.speaker: Beriand

be5berr8.dialogue: I have heard the city's Shrine of Mystra is such a building, but that it has not been seen by mortals for well on a hundred years.
be5berr8.speaker: Beriand

be5bert2.dialogue: Ah, Castle Cormanthor, my thoughts often go there. It is a cesspool of evil! And many evil things prowl its once-stately halls.
be5bert2.speaker: Beriand

be5bert3.dialogue: But the castle itself seeks to resist these invaders, as best it can. Ancient defenses watch and wait - I can feel them. They wait for the small stone that will begin the cleansing landslide.
be5bert3.speaker: Beriand

be5bert5.dialogue: Alas, friends, I have some bad news about Castle Cormanthor. I have been casting cantrips of divination, and learned something dire indeed!
be5bert5.speaker: Beriand

be5bert6.dialogue: You know that Myth Drannor has a very old, very powerful protective spell cast over it - the Mythal. One of the fundamental powers of the Mythal is to block any who attempt to invade by magical portal.
be5bert6.speaker: Beriand

be5bert7.dialogue: But the Mythal has been corrupted! And portals are being opened into the Castle from all over Faerun. The Cult's greatest wizards are coming here to pay homage to Kya Mordrayn and Pelendralaar.
be5bert7.speaker: Beriand

be5berv2.dialogue: I am remembering that a traveler told me about the Great Pump of the House of Gems... Do you know the House of Gems, atop the City Heights, off to the east?
be5berv2.speaker: Beriand

be5berv3.dialogue: When this traveller was there, a year ago, it made a happy thump, like a heartbeat.
be5berv3.speaker: Beriand

be5berv4.dialogue: But when Faeril and I passed by a fortnight ago, the heartbeat could barely be heard! And many of the waters here have grown foul. I wonder what has happened there.
be5berv4.speaker: Beriand

be5berv7.dialogue: The House of Gems... that reminds me. An orog came and shouted a message through our door. I think the message was for you!
be5berv7.speaker: Beriand

be5berv8.dialogue: It said that the orogs wish to parley with you in the Round Tower of the House of Gems. They will wait for you there.
be5berv8.speaker: Beriand

be5fae47.dialogue: Surely you will not do it? It's clearly a trap!
be5fae47.speaker: Faeril

be5berv9.dialogue: It may be a trap, so if you go, go cautiously.
be5berv9.speaker: Beriand

be5berx2.dialogue: Athan told us that if we were ever in danger, to make our way as best we could to the central part of the City Heights.
be5berx2.speaker: Beriand

be5berx3.dialogue: He said there was a sanctuary there, a shrine to the god of travelers, Shaundakul.
be5berx3.speaker: Beriand

be5berx6.dialogue: I have heard a tale, but do not whether to believe it, because it came from an orc.
be5berx6.speaker: Beriand

be5berx7.dialogue: The beast was telling another of a sword that was to be left alone at all costs. For any who took the sword would be turned into a statue of stone, adorning the coldest of tombs.
be5berx7.speaker: Beriand

be5berx8.dialogue: This sword was off in the ruins to the east, or so they seemed to say. I do not know what the truth of this tale may be.
be5berx8.speaker: Beriand

be5bery0.dialogue: When I was in the Elven Court, I heard tell of a mysterious place in Myth Drannor, the Garden they say was planted by Fiona Casilltenirra.
be5bery0.speaker: Beriand

be5bery1.dialogue: Have you heard tell of Fiona? She is that rare creature, an elf vampire, very beautiful and very dangerous.
be5bery1.speaker: Beriand

be5bery2.dialogue: I do not know much about her garden, if it even exists. But the shadows whisper that it should only be visited by those who welcome the darkest of bargains.
be5bery2.speaker: Beriand

be5bery4.dialogue: Oh, travelers, don't you wish we could see the old Myth Drannor, if only for a moment? It was indeed the most marvelous of places!
be5bery4.speaker: Beriand

be5bery5.dialogue: I am blind, so maybe I am better able to imagine what it was like. Do you know that there was a place you could go, if you had lost something, and it would tell you where it was?
be5bery5.speaker: Beriand

be5bery6.dialogue: The Column of the Whispering Wind is what they called it. Oh, what glorious ruins they are, that surround us on every side.
be5bery6.speaker: Beriand

be5berz6.dialogue: It is good you ask about such places, because it reminds me of a tale that I heard long ago.
be5berz6.speaker: Beriand

be5berz7.dialogue: It was said that in the Hall of Wizards, which some call the Speculum, there was a device of great magic, a wizard's Scrying Mirror.
be5berz7.speaker: Beriand

be5berz8.dialogue: In the Mirror, one could see things far away. But this was no simple stargazing ball, oh no! For it could show images to satisfy the deepest desires of the heart.
be5berz8.speaker: Beriand

be5ber{1.dialogue: Athan told Faeril and me that under no circumstances were we to venture into the ruins away to the southwest.
be5ber{1.speaker: Beriand

be5ber{2.dialogue: There was great peril there, he said, for a sorcerer he hates dwells in the ruins, among the lizardfolk.
be5ber{2.speaker: Beriand

be5ber{3.dialogue: It seems incredible that a man should live among lizards, who relish human flesh above all things. But Athan said this was no ordinary man - indeed, not hardly a man anymore at all.
be5ber{3.speaker: Beriand

be5ber{4.dialogue: What was the name he said? -Malgi Hi. You may want to stay clear of the ruins to the southwest, or risk falling victim to the greed and wrath of Malgi Hi.
be5ber{4.speaker: Beriand

be5ber{7.dialogue: I was talking with an Ormyrr - do not be amazed, for despite their ferocious appearance, some of the Ormyrr can be friends to our kind.
be5ber{7.speaker: Beriand

be5ber{8.dialogue: This Ormyrr said that his friend Pujik had recently become King of the Ormyrr, and invited us to visit. He said they lived in the marshes away to the southeast.
be5ber{8.speaker: Beriand

be5ber{9.dialogue: I also learned that the Ormyrr are traders, and buy and sell goods from many creatures in the area. If you earn their trust, maybe they will trade with you.
be5ber{9.speaker: Beriand

be5ber|2.dialogue: In that area, as in all areas, you must take care. Stay away from creatures that are too strong for you right now.
be5ber|2.speaker: Beriand

be5ber|3.dialogue: Come back later, when you are stronger, and maybe have found allies to aid you. Then may the evil things fall to your sword and your spell.
be5ber|3.speaker: Beriand

be5ber|5.dialogue: A word about resting in that area. When Faeril and I grew tired, we sought out safe places to rest -  rooms that were off the main paths, with doors we could shut against spying eyes.
be5ber|5.speaker: Beriand

be5ber|6.dialogue: And Faeril made quite sure there were no monsters dwelling nearby, before we settled down to sleep.
be5ber|6.speaker: Beriand

be5fae48.dialogue: I will tell you something I noticed, as we made our way through the Dungeons... Maybe it will be useful to you.
be5fae48.speaker: Faeril

be5fae49.dialogue: The old areas were haunted with undead creatures, and shunned by living things.
be5fae49.speaker: Faeril

be5fae50.dialogue: If you see obelisks or spires or worst yet, coffins - beware! That is an old area, where ghouls, shadows and wraiths might be found.
be5fae50.speaker: Faeril

be5ber|9.dialogue: I will tell you something Faeril noticed, as we made our way through the Dungeons...
be5ber|9.speaker: Beriand

be5ber}0.dialogue: ...the old areas were haunted with undead creatures, and shunned by living things.
be5ber}0.speaker: Beriand

be5ber}1.dialogue: Whenever she would see obelisks or spires or worst yet, coffins - we would watch out for ghouls, shadows and wraiths, and other things darker still.
be5ber}1.speaker: Beriand

be5ber~1.dialogue: I cannot tell you any more tales now. Talk to me later, after you have gone down into the Dungeons and seen for yourself.
be5ber~1.speaker: Beriand

be5ber~2.dialogue: I am afraid I have no more tales to tell you about the Main Halls of the Dungeons.
be5ber~2.speaker: Beriand

be5ber~3.dialogue: That is all the dungeon tales I know right now, relating to the Upper Halls.
be5ber~3.speaker: Beriand

be5ber~4.dialogue: We do not know any more tales about the Deep Halls of the dungeon.
be5ber~4.speaker: Beriand

be5ber~5.dialogue: I have already told you all the dungeon tales I know.
be5ber~5.speaker: Beriand

be5ber~6.dialogue: You've heard every tale I know about them.
be5ber~6.speaker: Beriand

be5ber~7.dialogue: I have told you every tale I know about the buildings of Myth Drannor.
be5ber~7.speaker: Beriand

be5ber~8.dialogue: I've now told you all the Catacomb tales I know.
be5ber~8.speaker: Beriand

be5ber~9.dialogue: I do not know any more tales about the upper floors of the Catacombs.
be5ber~9.speaker: Beriand

be5ber0.speaker: Beriand

be5ber1.speaker: Beriand

be5ber2.speaker: Beriand

be5ber4.speaker: Beriand
