be5ber5.speaker: Beriand

be5ber6.dialogue: You've heard every tale I know about them.
be5ber6.speaker: Beriand

be5berYF.dialogue: You need not say it - my heart knows it already. Faeril is dead.
be5berYF.speaker: Beriand

be5berYG.dialogue: So young, so full of life - it is truly a cruel and terrible world.
be5berYG.speaker: Beriand

be5ber7.dialogue: Goodbye. May the blessings of Mystra go with you.
be5ber7.speaker: Beriand

be5ber8.dialogue: Farewell. Return to me, if ever you need healing.
be5ber8.speaker: Beriand

be5berÄ1.dialogue: Walk in Mystra's sight, until we meet again.
be5berÄ1.speaker: Beriand

be5berÄ2.dialogue: Goodbye. Return here if you would hear more tales, or if you require blessed healing from our Lady of Mystery.
be5berÄ2.speaker: Beriand

Be1fae00.dialogue: Stand ready, Beriand! They are not of Athan's band. And I do not like their look.
Be1fae00.speaker: Faeril

Be1Ber03.dialogue: Calm, Faeril. Mystra has touched them, can you not feel it?
Be1Ber03.speaker: Beriand

Be1Ber04.speaker: Beriand
Be1Ber04.desc: spoken, with sadness and infinite concern

Be1Ber05.dialogue: And they are badly hurt by the foul ones.
Be1Ber05.speaker: Beriand
Be1Ber05.desc: spoken, with sadness and infinite concern

Be1Ber06.dialogue: And they bear their dead, and loss weighs heavy upon them.
Be1Ber06.speaker: Beriand
Be1Ber06.desc: spoken, with sadness and infinite concern

Be1Ber07.dialogue: Friend or foe, I will heal them.
Be1Ber07.speaker: Beriand

Be1Ber08.dialogue: Rest easy here, strangers, and tell us your news.
Be1Ber08.speaker: Beriand

Be1Ber09.dialogue: Bide a moment, and give an old blind elf a chance to speak.
Be1Ber09.speaker: Beriand

Be1Ber10.dialogue: Athan is dead, you tell us, and all his band. So Athan's quest becomes your quest - is this not so? To do as Elminster asked - to find out what is twisting the Mythal to evil.
Be1Ber10.speaker: Beriand

Be1Ber11.dialogue: We have already guessed some of your news. Athan and his band are dead.
Be1Ber11.speaker: Beriand

Be1Ber12.dialogue: So Athan's quest becomes your quest. Is this not so? To do as Elminster asked - to find out what is twisting the Mythal to evil?
Be1Ber12.speaker: Beriand

Be1Ber13.dialogue: The Mythal is an ancient spell of protection, laid upon this city long, long ago.
Be1Ber13.speaker: Beriand

Be1Ber14.dialogue: It is one of the greatest spells ever cast in Faerun, and is thus much beloved of Mystra, the Mother of All Magic.
Be1Ber14.speaker: Beriand

Be1fae01.dialogue: We are humble followers of the Mother.
Be1fae01.speaker: Faeril

Be1Ber15.dialogue: You will want to get to the Heights of the city, just as Athan did. He had the Ring of Calling - a gold ring, with a silver Starstone...
Be1Ber15.speaker: Beriand

Be1fae02.dialogue: ...stuck fast on the fingerbone of a skeleton's arm. He was searching for a Word of Power that would release the Ring...
Be1fae02.speaker: Faeril

Be1Ber16.dialogue: ...the Word of Oblivion. He heard tell of a place called the Room of Words. But he never found it.
Be1Ber16.speaker: Beriand

Be1fae03.dialogue: Nottle says there are many red-robed mages in the Halls of Light, the upper halls of the Dungeons. One of them may have the Arm.
Be1fae03.speaker: Faeril

Be1Ber17.dialogue: You would know it if you saw it. The Ring is magically bound onto the finger of its former owner.
Be1Ber17.speaker: Beriand

Be1fae04.dialogue: Athan tried everything to get it off! How he cursed as he struggled! But none of them knew how to speak the Word of Oblivion.
Be1fae04.speaker: Faeril

Be1Ber18.dialogue: If you did not find the Ring on Athan's body, then his enemies must have taken it. And they too may be searching for the Room of Words.
Be1Ber18.speaker: Beriand

Be1Ber19.dialogue: They are Words that command magic, in a language all but lost to mortals.
Be1Ber19.speaker: Beriand

Be1fae05.dialogue: Magical words, which Mystra rejoices to hear.
Be1fae05.speaker: Faeril

Be1Ber20.dialogue: Learn them to unleash Mystra's power - to wield a magical object or unseal a glyph-held door.
Be1Ber20.speaker: Beriand

Be1Ber21.dialogue: Right now the way is sealed.
Be1Ber21.speaker: Beriand

Be1fae06.dialogue: We were in the dungeons below, when orcs came upon us. They seized Beriand's mighty staff, Deathbane...
Be1fae06.speaker: Faeril

Be1faeYA.dialogue: ...so we fled up and out, and Beriand sealed the door behind us with the Glyph of Mystra.
Be1faeYA.speaker: Faeril

Be1Ber22.dialogue: You can learn the Word of Power that will unseal the way to the Room of Words. I wrote it here in our book.
Be1Ber22.speaker: Beriand

Be1Ber25.dialogue: If you are indeed to shoulder Athan's burden, you must take up where he left off - seek the Ring of Calling, and the Word of Oblivion that releases it. They will unseal the way to the City Heights.
Be1Ber25.speaker: Beriand

Be1fae07.dialogue: To begin that quest, look in our book. It will teach you the Word of Power that unseals the Tumbledown Door.
Be1fae07.speaker: Faeril

Be1fae08.dialogue: Beware of orcs. They are many, and they are greedy! They seized Beriand's staff, Deathbane, right out of his hands!
Be1fae08.speaker: Faeril

Be1Ber28.dialogue: But beware! They who killed Athan have also corrupted the Mythal, this city's ancient and beautiful spell...
Be1Ber28.speaker: Beriand

Be1fae09.dialogue: ...so there will be much evil afoot, and the city itself may seem hostile.
Be1fae09.speaker: Faeril

Be1fae10.dialogue: Heed what Athan said! Search for the Room of Words.
Be1fae10.speaker: Faeril

Be1fae11.dialogue: East of here you will find the Tumbledown Door, which we sealed with the Glyph of Mystra.
Be1fae11.speaker: Faeril

Be1fae12.dialogue: Speak the Word of Power that is written in our book, and the door will open for you.
Be1fae12.speaker: Faeril

Be1Ber31.dialogue: Mystra guide you. To hear our tales, or to get healing, come talk to me again.
Be1Ber31.speaker: Beriand

Be1Ber32.dialogue: You may rest here without fear. To hear our tales, or to get healing, come talk to me again.
Be1Ber32.speaker: Beriand

Be1Ber33.dialogue: Little good will its healing do them. It will not raise up their kind!
Be1Ber33.speaker: Beriand

Be1Ber34.dialogue: Take heed! Nottle can be friendly, but he is not your friend!
Be1Ber34.speaker: Beriand

Be1fae13.dialogue: Sly scavenger! Loyal only to himself and his purse.
Be1fae13.speaker: Faeril

Be1Ber35.dialogue: Still, we are thankful he sent you to us.
Be1Ber35.speaker: Beriand

Be1fae14.dialogue: We will pay for it somehow, mark my words!
Be1fae14.speaker: Faeril

Be1Ber36.dialogue: So Athan and his companions are dead. What we feared has come to be. Greatly we rue their passing.
Be1Ber36.speaker: Beriand

Be1fae15.dialogue: He was a great warrior! How he sent the orcs a-flying!
Be1fae15.speaker: Faeril

Be1Ber37.dialogue: Athan told us the great Mythal of Myth Drannor was corrupt, and that he sought to make it whole. What will become of his quest, now that he is no more?
Be1Ber37.speaker: Beriand

Be1Ber38.dialogue: We can shed some light on that story. Athan told us his band would try to open a Gate back to Phlan.
Be1Ber38.speaker: Beriand

Be1fae16.dialogue: He knew evil was rising here, but he did not know what it was. Or if he knew, he did not say.
Be1fae16.speaker: Faeril

Be1Ber39.dialogue: A Pool of Radiance... you think there is one here, in Myth Drannor? This city has a Mythal, a great protective spell. It would prevent such a thing...
Be1Ber39.speaker: Beriand

Be1fae17.dialogue: ...unless the Mythal is corrupt! Just as Athan told us!
Be1fae17.speaker: Faeril

Be1Ber40.dialogue: Woe to Mystra and her servants, then! And a double curse upon us, now that Athan is dead! For he swore to restore the Mythal.
Be1Ber40.speaker: Beriand

Be1Ber41.dialogue: If you seek a Pool of Radiance, his quest seems now to fall upon you. For one terrible hand seems to be at work here - bringing the Mythal low in order to raise the Pool.
Be1Ber41.speaker: Beriand

Be1BerYB.dialogue: Woe to Mystra and her servants, then! And a double curse upon us! For Nottle told us Athan is dead, and Athan was sworn to restore the Mythal.
Be1BerYB.speaker: Beriand

Be1fae18.dialogue: He did not know his enemy. 'Scarred mages,' he called them, and spat.
Be1fae18.speaker: Faeril

Be1Ber43.dialogue: But it seems clear they are the evil ones who have bent the Mythal to their own ends. Or in league with them, at least.
Be1Ber43.speaker: Beriand

Be1fae19.dialogue: Why else would they come howling after Athan?
Be1fae19.speaker: Faeril

Be1fae20.dialogue: Mystra! Why, she is the goddess of magic, the lady of possibilities. Do you not know of her? She tends the Weave, which all mortals use to cast spells.
Be1fae20.speaker: Faeril

Be1Ber45.dialogue: Gently, Faeril. Many honor the Mother of Magic, even if they know her not by name.
Be1Ber45.speaker: Beriand

Be1Ber46.dialogue: Both Faeril and I are humble servants of Mystra.
Be1Ber46.speaker: Beriand

Be1Ber47.dialogue: Athan vowed to destroy whatever was corrupting the Mythal. To do that, he knew he must reach the City Heights. He had the Ring of Calling...
Be1Ber47.speaker: Beriand

Be1fae21.dialogue: ...a gold ring with a silver Starstone, stuck fast on the fingerbone of a skeleton's arm. He needed the Word of Power that releases the Ring...
Be1fae21.speaker: Faeril

Be1Ber48.dialogue: ...the Word of Oblivion. He heard tell of a place called the Room of Words. But he never found it.
Be1Ber48.speaker: Beriand

Be1faeZA.dialogue: Nottle says there are many red-robed mages in the Halls of Light, the upper halls of the Dungeons. One of them may have the Arm.
Be1faeZA.speaker: Faeril

Be1Ber50.dialogue: I sealed the way myself. When we came up from the dungeons, orcs were after us, so I laid the Glyph of Mystra upon the Tumbledown Door.
Be1Ber50.speaker: Beriand

Be1fae22.dialogue: You may pass through that door, if you learn the Word of Mystra. It is written here in our book.
Be1fae22.speaker: Faeril

Be1fae23.dialogue: The Word of Mystra is written in our book.
Be1fae23.speaker: Faeril

Be1Ber52.dialogue: Once you learn the Word of Mystra, you can enter the dungeons. With the Word, you can pass the Glyph of Mystra that seals the Tumbledown Door.
Be1Ber52.speaker: Beriand

Be1fae24.dialogue: Blame the orcs! For your dead would be back with us already, if the cursed orc rabble hadn't seized Beriand's staff.
Be1fae24.speaker: Faeril

Be1Ber54.dialogue: Ah, it is true, Mystra willing. I named my staff Morathil - that is, Deathbane. I cut it myself, guided by Mystra's hand. And I put much of my healing power into it.
Be1Ber54.speaker: Beriand

Be1fae25.dialogue: I went to take it back, but alas! Too many orcs infest the dungeons for one alone...
Be1fae25.speaker: Faeril

Be1Ber55.dialogue: ...although that did not stop you from trying, valiant Faeril, and nearly perishing in the attempt!
Be1Ber55.speaker: Beriand

Be1fae26.dialogue: Athan believed he could reach the Room of Words from the dungeons below. He looked in our book, and learned the Word of Mystra to unseal the way...
Be1fae26.speaker: Faeril

Be1Ber57.dialogue: But he did not live to use it. If you would take up after him, you must begin with the Word.
Be1Ber57.speaker: Beriand

Be1Ber58.dialogue: Mystra sent me a vision! I saw her wrapped in magic amid the ruin of Myth Drannor. So I joined a band of travelers bound for this city.
Be1Ber58.speaker: Beriand

Be1fae27.dialogue: And I came along, to protect my good master from harm.
Be1fae27.speaker: Faeril

Be1Ber59.dialogue: But our group came to a bad end. We fled underground, where we were hunted by drow. We escaped them, only to be hounded by orcs. They forced us up from the dungeons...
Be1Ber59.speaker: Beriand

Be1fae28.dialogue: ...where we met Nottle, generous Nottle, who sold us the password to this ancient elven shelter.
Be1fae28.speaker: Faeril

Be1Ber60.dialogue: Considering our need, the price was not unreasonable - almost every coin and gem we had.
Be1Ber60.speaker: Beriand

Be1Ber61.dialogue: The Mythal is an ancient spell of protection, laid upon this city long, long ago.
Be1Ber61.speaker: Beriand

Be1fae29.dialogue: Some say it is the greatest spell ever cast by mortals!
Be1fae29.speaker: Faeril

Be1Ber62.dialogue: Under its powerful weave, Myth Drannor became a city unmatched in its grace and grandeur.
Be1Ber62.speaker: Beriand

Be1fae30.dialogue: Legends tell of a golden city, beloved of elves, full of peace and song. How far has it fallen!
Be1fae30.speaker: Faeril

Be1Ber63.dialogue: As long as the Mythal remains, hope remains - hope that one day, Myth Drannor will rise from ruin and once again be the most sacred of cities.
Be1Ber63.speaker: Beriand

Be1Ber64.dialogue: But if the Mythal should be turned - it is a horrible thought, all that ancient power set to evil.
Be1Ber64.speaker: Beriand

Be1Ber65.dialogue: There is little to tell. They were wounded - I healed them as best I could. I lost my staff, you see, to orcs. Without Deathbane, my healing power is small.
Be1Ber65.speaker: Beriand

Be1fae31.dialogue: Athan told us Elminster sent him here, because some ill had struck the great Mythal of Myth Drannor.
Be1fae31.speaker: Faeril

Be1Ber66.dialogue: They did not stay long. Athan did not want to bring doom upon us. The mage with him said she would try to open a Gate back to Phlan.
Be1Ber66.speaker: Beriand

Be1fae32.dialogue: By the Goddess! The Weave was like silk in her hands!
Be1fae32.speaker: Faeril

Be1Ber67.dialogue: Athan was determined to return to the City Heights. In our book, he read the Word of Mystra that unseals the Tumbledown Door. But he never used it.
Be1Ber67.speaker: Beriand

Be1Ber68.dialogue: Of course. Exhaustion is written in your voice. Forgive us for keeping you.
Be1Ber68.speaker: Beriand

Be1fae33.dialogue: Rest here, and rest well! Then look in our book for the Word of Mystra, and use the Word to pass through the Tumbledown Door.
Be1fae33.speaker: Faeril

Be1Ber70.dialogue: I know, I know - I am rattling on and on. Forgive me for keeping you. Now you must be about your quest.
Be1Ber70.speaker: Beriand

Be1fae35.dialogue: Beware of orcs. They are many, and they are greedy! They seized Beriand's staff, Deathbane, right out of his hands!
Be1fae35.speaker: Faeril

Be1fae36.dialogue: To begin that quest, look in our book. It will teach you the Word of Power that unseals the Tumbledown Door.
Be1fae36.speaker: Faeril

Be1Ber73.dialogue: But beware! They who killed Athan have also corrupted the Mythal, this city's ancient and beautiful spell...
Be1Ber73.speaker: Beriand

Be1fae37.dialogue: ...so there will be much evil afoot, and the city itself may seem hostile.
Be1fae37.speaker: Faeril

Be1fae38.dialogue: Heed what Athan said! Search for the Room of Words.
Be1fae38.speaker: Faeril

Be1Ber75.dialogue: May Mystra guide you. To hear our tales, or to get healing, talk to me again at any time.
Be1Ber75.speaker: Beriand

Be1BerYC.dialogue: And talk to us again, anytime, to hear our tales and tell us your progress.
Be1BerYC.speaker: Beriand

Be1faeYF.dialogue: ...so we fled up and out, and Beriand sealed the door behind us with the Glyph of Mystra.
Be1faeYF.speaker: Faeril

Be1faeYK.dialogue: Athan told us Elminster sent him here, because some ill had struck the great Mythal of Myth Drannor.
Be1faeYK.speaker: Faeril

Be1pro03.speaker: Protagonist

Be1pro05.speaker: Protagonist

Be1pro08.speaker: Protagonist

Be1pro09.speaker: Protagonist

Be1pro10.dialogue: Tell them a Gate brought you to Myth Drannor
Be1pro10.speaker: Protagonist

Be1pro11.dialogue: Tell about the dead adventurers you found
Be1pro11.speaker: Protagonist

Be1pro13.dialogue: Ask them about a Pool of Radiance here
Be1pro13.speaker: Protagonist

Be1pro15.dialogue: Ask them about their dealings with Athan
Be1pro15.speaker: Protagonist

Be1pro16.dialogue: Ask them about the 'Mythal of Myth Drannor'
Be1pro16.speaker: Protagonist

Be1pro17.dialogue: Tell of your quest for the Pool of Radiance
Be1pro17.speaker: Protagonist

Be1pro22.dialogue: Ask them how to take up Athan's quest
Be1pro22.speaker: Protagonist

Be1pro24.dialogue: Tell them how you met Nottle
Be1pro24.speaker: Protagonist

Be1pro25.dialogue: Ask for the Word of Mystra
Be1pro25.speaker: Protagonist

Be1pro26.speaker: Protagonist

Be1pro27.dialogue: Ask them why the way is sealed
Be1pro27.speaker: Protagonist

Be1pro28.dialogue: Ask them how they met Athan
Be1pro28.speaker: Protagonist

Be1pro29.dialogue: Ask them how they came to be here
Be1pro29.speaker: Protagonist

Be1pro30.dialogue: Ask how your dead might live again
Be1pro30.speaker: Protagonist

Be1pro31.dialogue: Ask if you can rest here
Be1pro31.speaker: Protagonist

Be2dmaYA.dialogue: You give the staff Deathbane back to Beriand, its rightful owner.
Be2dmaYA.speaker: DM

Be2Ber02.dialogue: Why, what is this? I know it at once. Look, Faeril! It is Deathbane. They have brought my staff back to my hand.
Be2Ber02.speaker: Beriand

Be2fae00.dialogue: Yes! I saw them bring it forth, and how my heart leapt!
Be2fae00.speaker: Faeril

Be2Ber03.dialogue: Haha! The Lady is smiling, Faeril, at last! By the Weave, it is good to feel her warmth again.
Be2Ber03.speaker: Beriand

Be2Ber04.dialogue: If you feel pain, or if one among you hears the icy whisper of death, come to me! With Deathbane in my hand and Mystra's favor in my heart, there is little I cannot heal.
Be2Ber04.speaker: Beriand

Be2Ber06.dialogue: Behold! With Deathbane in my hand, even for those who have died, hope blazes anew!
Be2Ber06.speaker: Beriand

Be2fae01.dialogue: Oho! I bet you made them pay for their greed.
Be2fae01.speaker: Faeril

Be2Ber08.dialogue: The orcs have grown greatly in numbers, it seems, and in strength. Thank the Goddess you opposed them, and not Faeril alone!
Be2Ber08.speaker: Beriand

Be2Ber09.dialogue: One may only do so much against so many, even one as valiant as she.
Be2Ber09.speaker: Beriand

Be2Ber10.dialogue: For us, no. You have already helped us beyond all accounting. Now you must think to your own quest.
Be2Ber10.speaker: Beriand

Be2Ber11.dialogue: I hope my own need has not made you stray from your pursuit of the Pool of Radiance...
Be2Ber11.speaker: Beriand

Be2Ber12.dialogue: I hope my own need has not made you stray from your pursuit of the Ring of Calling...
Be2Ber12.speaker: Beriand

Be2Ber13.dialogue: I hope my own need has not made you stray from your path to reach the city Heights...
Be2Ber13.speaker: Beriand

Be2Ber14.dialogue: I hope my own need has not made you stray from your search for the Baelnorn...
Be2Ber14.speaker: Beriand

Be2Ber15.dialogue: I hope my own need has not made you stray from your quest to return Anorrweyn Evensong her skull...
Be2Ber15.speaker: Beriand

Be2fae02.dialogue: Yet even so, I do not regret it!
Be2fae02.speaker: Faeril

Be2Ber19.dialogue: Nor I! For the Lady Mystra is glad, and that is good for all of us.
Be2Ber19.speaker: Beriand

Be2Ber20.dialogue: Well... I had not expected this. There is nothing of value I have, nothing I can give you. Unless...
Be2Ber20.speaker: Beriand

Be2Ber21.dialogue: ...I can offer you the service of my protector and friend, Faeril, if she would consent to it.
Be2Ber21.speaker: Beriand

Be2fae03.dialogue: I will not! Consent to serve such greed? Never!
Be2fae03.speaker: Faeril

Be2Ber22.dialogue: Then I am afraid I have no way to pay for the return of my staff, except to use it in your benefit when I may.
Be2Ber22.speaker: Beriand

Be2fae04.dialogue: And that should suffice, and more than suffice, even if you be more grasping than Nottle!
Be2fae04.speaker: Faeril

Be2Ber24.dialogue: Speak no more of it. We are all caught up in Mystery, and do what we can, not to solve it, but to help others appreciate its beauty.
Be2Ber24.speaker: Beriand

Be2Ber25.dialogue: But I talk too much, as usual.
Be2Ber25.speaker: Beriand

Be2Ber27.dialogue: You need rest - and you are welcome to rest here, in our haven.
Be2Ber27.speaker: Beriand

Be2Ber28.dialogue: You must be on your way. May Mystra walk with you.
Be2Ber28.speaker: Beriand

Be2Ber30.dialogue: Goodbye. If you need rest - you are welcome to rest here, in our haven.
Be2Ber30.speaker: Beriand

Be2Ber31.dialogue: You must be on your way. May Mystra walk with you.
Be2Ber31.speaker: Beriand

Be2pro00.dialogue: Tell how you fought many orcs for the staff
Be2pro00.speaker: Protagonist

Be2pro01.dialogue: Ask him if there's anything else you can do
Be2pro01.speaker: Protagonist

Be2pro02.dialogue: Ask him to pay for the staff
Be2pro02.speaker: Protagonist

Be2pro03.dialogue: Thank him for his healing gifts
Be2pro03.speaker: Protagonist

Be3fae00.dialogue: Stay a moment! Beriand craves your news, and so do I.
Be3fae00.speaker: Faeril

Be3fae01.dialogue: Yes! Tell us what you've seen.
Be3fae01.speaker: Faeril

Be3Ber04.dialogue: I am wondering - have you seen or heard anything of the Goddess of the Weave, Mystra?
Be3Ber04.speaker: Beriand

Be3fae02.dialogue: We are waiting for a sign from our Lady.
Be3fae02.speaker: Faeril

Be3fae03.dialogue: Travelers! Mystra has sent us a sign!
Be3fae03.speaker: Faeril

Be3Ber06.dialogue: Tell us, travelers, tell us what you've seen.
Be3Ber06.speaker: Beriand

Be3Ber08.dialogue: Yes - I have had a vision. There were ruins, and a voice crying the name of our Lady... one who is lost in the past, who believes that all of the followers of Mystra are gone.
Be3Ber08.speaker: Beriand

Be3fae04.dialogue: You must take a token to her!
Be3fae04.speaker: Faeril

Be3fae05.dialogue: Better than that - can you not take me with you? For I am a Servant of Mystery, and more proof than any token that the Lady of Spells has not been forgotten!
Be3fae05.speaker: Faeril

Be3fae06.dialogue: Ugh - to understand what gargoyles say - that is magic I have no use for!
Be3fae06.speaker: Faeril

Be3fae07.dialogue: Still, the Elves of Harrowdale had a saying, 'To understand an enemy is to defeat him.'
Be3fae07.speaker: Faeril

Be3Ber12.dialogue: Ah, a follower of Shaundakul, the Wind Rider! That was a fortuitous meeting for you.
Be3Ber12.speaker: Beriand

Be3fae08.dialogue: For you - and for the naga you name Odelinde. But not for the orcs, haha!
Be3fae08.speaker: Faeril

Be3Ber13.dialogue: The Wind Rider is a powerful ally - no god is as keen to restore Myth Drannor. For it was here that his worshippers came, and when the city fell, so did they.
Be3Ber13.speaker: Beriand

Be3Ber14.dialogue: So you toppled the great Malgi Hi! Ah, that is quite a feat, and no mistake. Perhaps Faeril could make a song of it.
Be3Ber14.speaker: Beriand

Be3fae09.dialogue: The Bard of Kara-Tur, maybe, but not me!
Be3fae09.speaker: Faeril

Be3fae10.dialogue: I know I should not envy you - all that blood, and fear, and pain - and yet, to smite down such evil! Glorious!
Be3fae10.speaker: Faeril

Be3Ber15.dialogue: Nottle told us of such a horrible place, but we did not believe him.
Be3Ber15.speaker: Beriand

Be3Ber16.dialogue: I would be careful about going there too often, lest its thirst become yours.
Be3Ber16.speaker: Beriand

Be3Ber18.dialogue: This is very strange! Dwarves do not often become ghosts. It is not in their nature.
Be3Ber18.speaker: Beriand

Be3fae11.dialogue: They loathe spirits, that is commonly known.
Be3fae11.speaker: Faeril

Be3fae12.dialogue: Still, you did well to free him. Even ghosts have their uses.
Be3fae12.speaker: Faeril

Be3fae13.dialogue: I had forgotten about the gargoyles! Even now, their cruelty fills me with rage.
Be3fae13.speaker: Faeril

Be3Ber20.dialogue: It is hard not to envy the Old Ones - while we struggle against evil, she worries only about the music of splashing water.
Be3Ber20.speaker: Beriand

Be3Ber22.dialogue: That is the hand of the Cult at work, or I am a fool. And we will see more of that - more of our friends will become our enemies - as their power grows stronger.
Be3Ber22.speaker: Beriand

Be3Ber23.dialogue: A strange circumstance. I wonder who he is, and how he came to be caught in such a cold and empty trap.
Be3Ber23.speaker: Beriand

Be3fae14.dialogue: When he is released, what stories he may tell!
Be3fae14.speaker: Faeril

Be3fae15.dialogue: We encountered such a naga, deep in the dungeons. We barely escaped with our lives!
Be3fae15.speaker: Faeril

Be3Ber25.dialogue: It spared us - I do not know why. They are deep creatures, I have heard, and do things willfully and for reasons none can fathom. Their gods are mysterious gods.
Be3Ber25.speaker: Beriand

Be3Ber27.dialogue: Preybelish? I have not heard that name.
Be3Ber27.speaker: Beriand

Be3fae16.dialogue: But if he has been dwelling in the dungeons long, he is probably not your friend!
Be3fae16.speaker: Faeril

Be3Ber28.dialogue: Perhaps you should bring him a gift of some kind. Once he knows you mean him no harm, he may open the door.
Be3Ber28.speaker: Beriand

Be3fae17.dialogue: I've heard it said that the nagas came here as servants to far more evil powers. That must have been a dark time indeed!
Be3fae17.speaker: Faeril

Be3fae18.dialogue: You were wise not to redeem him! Thieves make me nervous.
Be3fae18.speaker: Faeril

Be3fae19.dialogue: Ah, present company excepted, of course!
Be3fae19.speaker: Faeril

Be3Ber32.dialogue: Nervous! I have never known you to be nervous, Faeril, and you've had better cause than thieves.
Be3Ber32.speaker: Beriand

Be3Ber33.dialogue: Thieves are not dear to the Mother of Magic, but all creatures have their place in the Weave. You should consider well whether this thief Tudo may be of use to you.
Be3Ber33.speaker: Beriand

Be3Ber34.dialogue: Dear Faeril - do not worry - see, they take no offense.
Be3Ber34.speaker: Beriand

Be3Ber35.dialogue: Thieves are not dear to the Mother of Magic, but all creatures have their place in the Weave. You should consider well whether another thief will aid you in your cause.
Be3Ber35.speaker: Beriand

Be3Ber36.dialogue: It sounds like the drow have arrived in force.
Be3Ber36.speaker: Beriand

Be3fae20.dialogue: They were only scattered bands when we were down there.
Be3fae20.speaker: Faeril

Be3fae21.dialogue: They are fierce, and cunning, and relentless! Expect no quarter from them.
Be3fae21.speaker: Faeril

Be3Ber37.dialogue: The Mythal! Perhaps the greatest spell ever cast by mortals. Under the protection of its powerful weave, Myth Drannor became a city unmatched in its grace and grandeur.
Be3Ber37.speaker: Beriand

Be3fae22.dialogue: Legends tell of a golden city, beloved of elves, full of peace and song. How far has it fallen!
Be3fae22.speaker: Faeril

Be3Ber38.dialogue: As long as the Mythal remains, hope remains - hope that one day, Myth Drannor will rise from ruin and once again be the most sacred of cities.
Be3Ber38.speaker: Beriand

Be3Ber39.dialogue: The Mythal - the Mythal is fading. Tell them, Faeril.
Be3Ber39.speaker: Beriand

Be3fae23.dialogue: Yes. Have you seen the blueglow moss? There are patches of it here and there in the city.
Be3fae23.speaker: Faeril

Be3fae24.dialogue: In the old days it glowed strong - and healed those who touched it, because the power of the Mythal was behind it.
Be3fae24.speaker: Faeril

Be3fae25.dialogue: But when we arrived the moss hardly glows at all. So...
Be3fae25.speaker: Faeril

Be3Ber40.dialogue: ...so we think some ill has overtaken the Mythal.
Be3Ber40.speaker: Beriand

Be3fae26.dialogue: And we believe the Mother of Magic wants it restored.
Be3fae26.speaker: Faeril

Be3Ber41.dialogue: But that - that was in my vision, the one that brought me to Myth Drannor.
Be3Ber41.speaker: Beriand

Be3Ber42.dialogue: I dreamed that such a cry wafted up from the ruins, and Mystra herself appeared, wrapped in magic, and walking lightly under crumbled archway and over toppled stone, to answer it.
Be3Ber42.speaker: Beriand

Be3Ber43.dialogue: Can you find your way back to that place? And take with you a token of Mystra? For someone must answer that call!
Be3Ber43.speaker: Beriand

Be3fae27.dialogue: Better than that - can you not take me with you? For I am a Servant of Mystery, and more proof than any token that the Lady of Spells has not been forgotten!
Be3fae27.speaker: Faeril

Be3fae28.dialogue: One thing only I ask. Someone should stay here with Beriand, to guard him, else I will not go.
Be3fae28.speaker: Faeril

Be3fae29.dialogue: - but it is wise. I will leave you, Beriand, if Mystra wills, but I will not leave you alone!
Be3fae29.speaker: Faeril

Be3fae30.dialogue: You must decide who will stay behind. I will join you when that is settled.
Be3fae30.speaker: Faeril

Be3fae31.dialogue: But first, I give you the token - our Lady's Medallion. Give it to the one who cries out for Mystra, if I do not make the journey with you.
Be3fae31.speaker: Faeril

Be3fae32.dialogue: First, I give you the token - our Lady's Medallion. Give it to the one who cries out for Mystra, if I do not survive the journey.
Be3fae32.speaker: Faeril

Be3Ber52.dialogue: The vision came to me some weeks ago.
Be3Ber52.speaker: Beriand

Be3Ber53.dialogue: As I told you, I saw Mystra walking through the ruins. There was magic streaming all around her - the air was alive with possibility.
Be3Ber53.speaker: Beriand

Be3Ber54.dialogue: Ahead was a place where her shrine once stood. And a woman's voice cried out, despairing - 'where are the followers of Mystra?'
Be3Ber54.speaker: Beriand

Be3Ber55.dialogue: And our Lady grieved, or so it seemed to me. She bowed her head and look! There were bones on the ground, all of them missing their heads; but a path went through them and into the ruin of the shrine.
Be3Ber55.speaker: Beriand

Be3Ber56.dialogue: That is all. Somehow I knew that the ruins were Myth Drannor - I recognized them, although I have never been here and am blind besides.
Be3Ber56.speaker: Beriand

Be3fae33.dialogue: So he decided to come here, and I could not convince him otherwise.
Be3fae33.speaker: Faeril

Be3fae34.dialogue: Why, I am a cleric of Mystra, with some small skill in healing. But I also am a fighter who wields staff, mace and maul, and such hurtful spells as the Lady has taught me.
Be3fae34.speaker: Faeril

Be3Ber59.dialogue: And I may add that she has the heart of a lion, she is shrewd in the melee, and a glad soul and a healing hand at the campfire. Full of song is my Faeril, and I will miss her, if she goes with you.
Be3Ber59.speaker: Beriand

Be3Ber60.dialogue: Not much has happened. Nottle came by, and asked about you, but that was some time ago.
Be3Ber60.speaker: Beriand

Be3fae35.dialogue: He wondered if you were rich with plunder. I told him no!
Be3fae35.speaker: Faeril

Be3Ber61.dialogue: He sold us a medallion of Mystra. He said that he bought it from a lizard-man who had found it 'at the foot of a cloud-house.'
Be3Ber61.speaker: Beriand

Be3fae36.dialogue: By which he meant 'ghost building.' Nottle says Myth Drannor has many.
Be3fae36.speaker: Faeril

Be3Ber62.dialogue: The medallion is a relic of the old years, when Myth Drannor was a dream city and many, many followers of Mystra dwelt here.
Be3Ber62.speaker: Beriand

Be3fae37.dialogue: Farewell. Watch for Morathil, Beriand's staff, will you? Orcs stole it from us - they may still have it.
Be3fae37.speaker: Faeril

Be3fae38.dialogue: Farewell. Watch for Morathil, Beriand's staff, will you? His heart sinks without it, and even I cannot cheer him up.
Be3fae38.speaker: Faeril

Be3fae39.dialogue: Farewell. Watch for Morathil, Beriand's staff, will you? His healing gift would be great again if he could get it back.
Be3fae39.speaker: Faeril

Be3pro00.dialogue: Say you found the gargoyle Stone Mouth
Be3pro00.speaker: Protagonist
