Be3pro03.speaker: Protagonist

Be3pro04.dialogue: Tell about woman crying for Mystra
Be3pro04.speaker: Protagonist

Be3pro08.dialogue: Tell how the Ormyrr king opposed you
Be3pro08.speaker: Protagonist

Be3pro09.dialogue: Say you found a knight in a tomb
Be3pro09.speaker: Protagonist

Be3pro10.dialogue: Describe the dark naga trio you killed
Be3pro10.speaker: Protagonist

Be3pro11.dialogue: Tell about your talk with Preybelish
Be3pro11.speaker: Protagonist

Be3pro12.dialogue: Tell about meeting Nottle and Tudo
Be3pro12.speaker: Protagonist

Be3pro13.dialogue: Tell about drow in the Catacombs
Be3pro13.speaker: Protagonist

Be3pro17.dialogue: Ask about taking Faeril into your party
Be3pro17.speaker: Protagonist

Be3pro18.dialogue: Agree to take Faeril into your party
Be3pro18.speaker: Protagonist

Be3pro19.dialogue: Agree to take Faeril into your party
Be3pro19.speaker: Protagonist

Be3pro20.dialogue: Ask to hear more about Beriand's vision
Be3pro20.speaker: Protagonist

Be3pro21.dialogue: Ask about Faeril's strengths and qualities
Be3pro21.speaker: Protagonist

Be3pro22.dialogue: Take only the token of Mystra
Be3pro22.speaker: Protagonist

Be3fae41.dialogue: Here is the token - our Lady's Medallion. Take it, one of you, and bring it to she who cries out for Mystra, with our thanks.
Be3fae41.speaker: Faeril

be9ber02.dialogue: In Mystra's name, stand!...aah, aaaah, it is you. Ah, well met, friends!
be9ber02.speaker: Beriand
be9ber02.desc: spoken, fierce menace gives way to relief

be9ber03.dialogue: Forgive me - I am shaken - I expected doom to greet me. It is still very near, I can feel it.
be9ber03.speaker: Beriand
be9ber03.desc: spoken, relieved, wavering because he's just had a very close call

be9ber04.dialogue: The Cult - you have made them very angry. They are searching for you everywhere. They found my shelter instead. I must go back there... hide it again...
be9ber04.speaker: Beriand

be9ber05.dialogue: No, I will not talk of it. My Lady is telling me to leave this place at once.
be9ber05.speaker: Beriand

be9ber06.dialogue: Yes, an old blind elf will only bring you trouble. I will go back to my shelter...
be9ber06.speaker: Beriand

be9ber08.dialogue: But first, you need the healing touch of Mystra.
be9ber08.speaker: Beriand

be9ber09.dialogue: Look for me back in my place of refuge, in the tree stump.
be9ber09.speaker: Beriand

be9ber10.dialogue: But I leave the blessing of Mystra upon you, and commend your hearts to the Lady of Possibilities.
be9ber10.speaker: Beriand

be9fae00.dialogue: Praise her name, Beriand! It is the heroes!
be9fae00.speaker: Faeril

be9ber12.dialogue: Why, you are right. Mystra smiles yet again.
be9ber12.speaker: Beriand

be9fae01.dialogue: It seems you have angered the Cult! And so they took us captive, and set a trap for you.
be9fae01.speaker: Faeril

be9fae02.dialogue: They made the mistake many have made - thinking that Beriand is blind and defenseless!
be9fae02.speaker: Faeril

be9ber14.dialogue: They did not say. But it was clear you have come too close to whatever they wish to remain hidden.
be9ber14.speaker: Beriand

be9fae03.dialogue: Their leader's face was gray with fear. And his eyes darted like a mouse before a cat!
be9fae03.speaker: Faeril

be9ber15.dialogue: Come, Faeril. No more stories. Let us return to our shelter...
be9ber15.speaker: Beriand

be9fae04.dialogue: ...and fix it so that the Cult never finds it again!
be9fae04.speaker: Faeril

be9ber16.dialogue: Come, Faeril. Let us return to our shelter. We will fix it so that the Cult never finds it again.
be9ber16.speaker: Beriand

be9ber17.dialogue: But first, you need the healing touch of Mystra, I deem.
be9ber17.speaker: Beriand

be9ber18.dialogue: Look for us back in our place of refuge, in the tree stump.
be9ber18.speaker: Beriand

be9ber19.dialogue: But before we go, I leave the blessing of Mystra upon you, and commend your hearts to the Lady of Possibilities.
be9ber19.speaker: Beriand

be9pro01.dialogue: Ask about his feeling of doom
be9pro01.speaker: Protagonist

be9pro05.dialogue: Ask why the Cult is angry
be9pro05.speaker: Protagonist

be8ber03.speaker: Beriand
be8ber03.desc: spoken, with great concern, calling forth gentle healing

be8ber05.dialogue: We welcome you back into the embrace of Mystery...
be8ber05.speaker: Beriand
be8ber05.desc: spoken, with great concern, calling forth gentle healing

be8ber06.dialogue: ...if ever you need healing, or a place to rest, you are welcome here.
be8ber06.speaker: Beriand
be8ber06.desc: spoken, with great concern, calling forth gentle healing

be8ber07.dialogue: ...and watch! By the Lady's grace, your hurts are no more.
be8ber07.speaker: Beriand
be8ber07.desc: spoken,  kindly but strong, full of the god's beneficent power

be8ber08.dialogue: ...and see! Your terrible wounds vanish, as if they never were.
be8ber08.speaker: Beriand
be8ber08.desc: spoken,  kindly but strong, full of the god's beneficent power

be8ber09.dialogue: Welcome back to our humble shelter, under the gentle cloak of the Lady of Mystery.
be8ber09.speaker: Beriand
be8ber09.desc: spoken, kindly but strong, full of the god's beneficent power

be8ber10.dialogue: Now travellers, be healed by the touch of her hand.
be8ber10.speaker: Beriand

be8ber11.dialogue: Rest easy here, under her protection.
be8ber11.speaker: Beriand

be8ber14.dialogue: They are hurt. -Mystra, show them your face.
be8ber14.speaker: Beriand
be8ber14.desc: spoken, with great concern, calling forth gentle healing

be8ber16.dialogue: Behold - your troubles vanish in the gaze of the Lady.
be8ber16.speaker: Beriand
be8ber16.desc: spoken, with great concern, calling forth gentle healing

be8ber19.dialogue: Again, O Mistress of Mysteries, we humbly ask for your healing.
be8ber19.speaker: Beriand
be8ber19.desc: spoken, with great concern, calling forth gentle healing

be8ber22.dialogue: Mother of Magic, smile once again upon your children.
be8ber22.speaker: Beriand
be8ber22.desc: spoken, with great concern, calling forth gentle healing

be8berXA.dialogue: Alas, without my staff Deathbane, I cannot raise your dead.
be8berXA.speaker: Beriand

be4ber02.dialogue: Travelers! Faeril has told me everything. The fall of Kya Mordrayn, how the dracolich perished, the destruction of the Pool.
be4ber02.speaker: Beriand

be4fae00.dialogue: I feel the Lady was with us.
be4fae00.speaker: Faeril

be4ber03.dialogue: We who follow the Lady Mystra honor you for this great deed.
be4ber03.speaker: Beriand

be4ber04.dialogue: Travelers! I have heard that Kya Mordrayn has fallen by your hand, and the Pool of Radiance is no more.
be4ber04.speaker: Beriand

be4ber05.dialogue: All who follow the Lady Mystra honor you for this great deed.
be4ber05.speaker: Beriand

be4ber06.dialogue: Travelers! We welcome you most warmly.
be4ber06.speaker: Beriand

be4fae01.dialogue: Beriand has seen it all! The death of Kya Mordrayn, the great fall of Pelendralaar, the destruction of the Pool. Oh! it was glorious!
be4fae01.speaker: Faeril

be4ber07.dialogue: The Lady blessed me with a vision. We who follow Mystra honor you for this great deed.
be4ber07.speaker: Beriand

be4fae02.dialogue: How I wish I could be venturing with you, a humble warrior in the hushed service of the Lady.
be4fae02.speaker: Faeril

be4ber08.dialogue: But we should not detain you. Rest here, if you are tired, for here no darkness will enter.
be4ber08.speaker: Beriand

be4ber09.dialogue: But I am forgetting my duty. You have suffered loss and pain - let me ask the Lady to remove it all, every trace.
be4ber09.speaker: Beriand

be4ber11.dialogue: Rest here, if you are tired, for here no darkness will enter.
be4ber11.speaker: Beriand

be4ber12.dialogue: Rest here, if you are tired, for here no darkness will enter.
be4ber12.speaker: Beriand

br4bro03.dialogue: Travelers, we have heard the great news. Thanks to you, Pelendralaar is destroyed, and we have fulfilled our quest. The Silver Fire is ever in your debt.
br4bro03.speaker: Bronwyn

br4bro04.dialogue: Kellan is dead. Much though I miss my sister-in-arms, I also rejoice - for she died as she would have liked, in brave company, smashing a foe who deserved to be brought low.
br4bro04.speaker: Bronwyn

br4bro05.dialogue: Rest easy here, under our protection. And if ever you seek a comrade, consider me. You were Kellan's companions, and I would be honored to call you my own.
br4bro05.speaker: Bronwyn

br4bro07.dialogue: Travelers, I have heard the great news - Pelendralaar is destroyed, and Kya Mordrayn as well, and all the Cult dismayed and afraid!
br4bro07.speaker: Bronwyn
br4bro07.desc: spoken, with decorum, with great joy underneath

br4bro08.dialogue: Thanks to you, the Silver Fire has fulfilled our quest. We will ever be in your debt.
br4bro08.speaker: Bronwyn
br4bro08.desc: spoken, with decorum, with great joy underneath

br4bro09.dialogue: And for my part, you have kept my sister-in-arms Kellan alive! This is no small feat, and from my deepest heart, I thank you.
br4bro09.speaker: Bronwyn

br4bro11.dialogue: Travelers, I have heard the great news - Pelendralaar is destroyed, and Kya Mordrayn as well, and all the Cult dismayed and afraid!
br4bro11.speaker: Bronwyn
br4bro11.desc: spoken, with decorum, with great joy underneath

br4bro12.dialogue: Thanks to you, the Silver Fire has fulfilled its quest. Rest easy here, under our protection, for as long as you like.
br4bro12.speaker: Bronwyn

br4bro13.dialogue: Ah, dear companions, how good to see you again!
br4bro13.speaker: Bronwyn

br4bro14.dialogue: I am of the woodland, and lack skill with words, but I treasure the time we spent together, and the memory of the great deeds we did.
br4bro14.speaker: Bronwyn

br4bro15.dialogue: Kellan is dead. Much though I miss my sister-in-arms, I also rejoice - for she died as she would have liked, in brave company, smashing a foe who deserved to be brought low.
br4bro15.speaker: Bronwyn

br4bro16.dialogue: Rest easy here, dear companions, for as long as you like.
br4bro16.speaker: Bronwyn

br4bro18.dialogue: Greatly do I envy my sister in arms, for she walks with true heroes of Faerun.
br4bro18.speaker: Bronwyn

br4bro19.dialogue: Thanks to you, the quest of the Silver Fire is ended, and the Cult is dismayed and afraid! We will be long in your debt.
br4bro19.speaker: Bronwyn

selections: Sneak a peek into the bowl
Ask who Malgi Hi might be
Tell them you will avoid Malgi Hi
Say you already defeated Malgi Hi
Ask them about the Backwards Key
Ask them to tell their story

caldmaYA.dialogue: Try as you might, you cannot get Caalenfaire and Volun to even realize you are here.
caldmaYA.speaker: DM

caldmaYB.dialogue: You have become so talibund, so unpredictable, they can no longer sense you at all.
caldmaYB.speaker: DM

caldmaYD.dialogue: The diviner and his assistant do not notice you. They are engrossed in the images of past and future that flicker and float in the scrying bowl.
caldmaYD.speaker: DM

caldmaYE.dialogue: Caalenfaire and Volun are studying the scrying bowl, and take no notice of you.
caldmaYE.speaker: DM

caldmaYF.dialogue: Rapt in their divining, the two ghosts do not notice your approach.
caldmaYF.speaker: DM

caldmaYG.dialogue: The diviner and his assistant will not speak to you until you have successfully made your way out of the Dungeons.
caldmaYG.speaker: DM

calvolYH.dialogue: Hush now! Or you will bother my master.
calvolYH.speaker: Volun

calvolYI.dialogue: Next time, just wait until we notice you. Otherwise some very delicate spells may go completely awry! And your future may suffer for it.
calvolYI.speaker: Volun

calvolYJ.dialogue: Now, let me announce you... Caalenfaire my sweet, the Veiled Ones are here again.
calvolYJ.speaker: Volun

calcaa08.dialogue: Aaaaah! Aaaah! It is coming apart, it is slipping away! What on Faerun is happening?
calcaa08.speaker: caalenfa

calvolYK.dialogue: Master, it is the Veiled Ones. They are here, and they spoke to you.
calvolYK.speaker: Volun

calcaa09.dialogue: It is torn, Volun, will we ever be able to mend it? -Bid them begone, Volun! Before the rest of their fortunes end up in tatters!
calcaa09.speaker: caalenfa

calvolYL.dialogue: You had best leave, and come back to us later.
calvolYL.speaker: Volun

calvolYM.dialogue: Eeeeeeek! By the grace of Tymora!
calvolYM.speaker: Volun

calcaa11.dialogue: What - what is it, Volun? I see nothing!
calcaa11.speaker: caalenfa

calvolYN.dialogue: Pardon, master, and do not fear. I saw a shadow - I thought - I thought it was the Emissary of the Lady Shar! But now I see it is only the Veiled Ones.
calvolYN.speaker: Volun

calcaa12.dialogue: They must learn not to creep up upon us that way! So for now, Veiled Ones, begone!
calcaa12.speaker: caalenfa

calcaa14.dialogue: What? What is that? The thread, Volun! I have lost it. -No, no, here it is.
calcaa14.speaker: caalenfa

calvolYO.dialogue: Again the Veiled Ones have interrupted us, my master. Their need must be very great.
calvolYO.speaker: Volun

calcaa15.dialogue: Aaaiiieee! The thread! The thread, Volun! It is broken.
calcaa15.speaker: caalenfa

calvolYP.dialogue: What? Who is there? Oh, I see. Master, it is the Veiled Ones.
calvolYP.speaker: Volun

calvolYQ.dialogue: What? What is it? Ah, yes. Master, the Veiled Ones stand before you.
calvolYQ.speaker: Volun

calvolYR.dialogue: Eh? -Master, it is the Veiled Ones. They seek another audience with you.
calvolYR.speaker: Volun

calcaa20.dialogue: What is that? Who is here?
calcaa20.speaker: caalenfa

calvolYT.dialogue: Calm yourself, my love. It is only the Veiled Ones, come to us once again.
calvolYT.speaker: Volun

calvolYU.dialogue: Yes, master, the Veiled Ones have returned.
calvolYU.speaker: Volun

calvolYV.dialogue: Hold, master! Hold your spellweaving! For the Veiled Ones stand before us once more.
calvolYV.speaker: Volun

caldmaYW.dialogue: You wait only a few minutes. Then Caalenfaire speaks up.
caldmaYW.speaker: DM

calcaa24.dialogue: But wait, Volun. Something is amiss... The bowl is clouding...
calcaa24.speaker: caalenfa

calvolYX.dialogue: Let me look... Ah, my dear, I see the problem.
calvolYX.speaker: Volun

calcaa25.dialogue: Have I poured too much krakatoac into it?
calcaa25.speaker: caalenfa

calvolYY.dialogue: No, no my love, it is the Veiled Ones. They are here again.
calvolYY.speaker: Volun

caldmaY[.dialogue: You wait. They do not acknowledge you.
caldmaY[.speaker: DM

caldmaY\\.dialogue: Your feet hurt. They are still intently studying the scrying bowl.
caldmaY\\.speaker: DM

caldmaY].dialogue: Your arms are getting heavy. They do not acknowledge your presence.
caldmaY].speaker: DM

caldmaY^.dialogue: You scuff the ground with your toe. They do not look up.
caldmaY^.speaker: DM

caldmaY_.dialogue: You clear your throat, loudly, several times. There is no reaction.
caldmaY_.speaker: DM

caldmaY`.dialogue: You say 'Pardon, good sir' about twoscore times. Nothing happens.
caldmaY`.speaker: DM

caldmaYa.dialogue: You announce your name in a loud and important tone. They do not acknowledge your presence.
caldmaYa.speaker: DM

caldmaYb.dialogue: You tug gently at Caalenfaire's sleeve. He does not respond.
caldmaYb.speaker: DM

caldmaYc.dialogue: You wave a hand inches from the diviner's face. His eyelids do not even flicker.
caldmaYc.speaker: DM

caldmaYd.dialogue: Your tired bodies are beginning to exude an unpleasant odor. But Caalenfaire and Volun do not seem to notice it.
caldmaYd.speaker: DM

caldmaYe.dialogue: Faeril emphatically scuffs the ground with her toe. They do not look up.
caldmaYe.speaker: DM

caldmaYf.dialogue: Jarial clears his throat, loudly, several times. There is no reaction.
caldmaYf.speaker: DM

caldmaYg.dialogue: Emmeric says 'Pardon, lady, and good sir' about twoscore times, until his throat is hoarse. Nothing happens.
caldmaYg.speaker: DM

caldmaYh.dialogue: Eadred announces his name in a loud and important tone. They do not acknowledge him at all.
caldmaYh.speaker: DM

caldmaYi.dialogue: Bronwyn tugs gently at Caalenfaire's ghostly sleeve - or tries to. He does not respond.
caldmaYi.speaker: DM

caldmaYj.dialogue: Kellan waves her weapon inches from the diviner's face. His eyelids do not even flicker.
caldmaYj.speaker: DM

caldmaYk.dialogue: Your dead are beginning to exude an unpleasant odor. But Caalenfaire and Volun do not seem to notice it.
caldmaYk.speaker: DM

calvolYl.dialogue: Wait, Master. I sense a shadow... across our path... Ah. Of course. The Veiled Ones have returned.
calvolYl.speaker: Volun

calcaa56.dialogue: The vision is fading, Volun. Maybe more efreet ash will - why, what is it? There is concern writ large upon your face, Volun!
calcaa56.speaker: caalenfa

calvolYm.dialogue: Because I see what you cannot, Caalenfaire my love. The talibund warriors are here again.
calvolYm.speaker: Volun

calvolYn.dialogue: Ah, there you are. -Caalenfaire, the Veiled Ones have come, just as you thought they would.
calvolYn.speaker: Volun

calvolYo.dialogue: Ah, there you are. Have you been waiting long? -Caalenfaire, the Veiled Ones are here for you.
calvolYo.speaker: Volun

calvolYp.dialogue: Ah, here they are, Caalenfaire - the Veiled Ones. We did not expect you so soon.
calvolYp.speaker: Volun

calvolYq.dialogue: Who is that? It's getting hard to - ah, yes. Dearheart, the Veiled Ones are here.
calvolYq.speaker: Volun

calcaa66.dialogue: What, Volun! Hand of Beshaba, what is wrong with them?
calcaa66.speaker: caalenfa

calcaa67.dialogue: The Dungeons! They must get out of the Dungeons! Send them away, send them away at once.
calcaa67.speaker: caalenfa

calvolYr.dialogue: You heard the Master! You best be on your way.
calvolYr.speaker: Volun

calvolYs.dialogue: Once you leave the Dungeons, then we can tell you about the amazing visions we are seeing.
calvolYs.speaker: Volun

calcaa70.dialogue: Never mind them, Volun. Look, look here at the self-anointed Priestess of Mystra, Anorrweyn Evensong.
calcaa70.speaker: caalenfa

calcaa71.dialogue: She was so imperious in court - do you remember? So full of advice for everyone. But look - look at her now, Volun.
calcaa71.speaker: caalenfa

calvolYt.dialogue: Ah, but Caalenfaire, the Veiled Ones are waiting -
calvolYt.speaker: Volun

calcaa72.dialogue: Let them wait. See, she wails for her followers - she believes them all dead - not knowing that two of them are right nearby, right here in the city! Too bad the blind healer will never live to meet her.
calcaa72.speaker: caalenfa

calcaa75.dialogue: Ahhh. Good. Ask them, Volun. Ask them about Plinshree.
calcaa75.speaker: caalenfa

calcaa77.dialogue: Good. Tell them what I told you - that they should stay away from the one called Malgi Hi.
calcaa77.speaker: caalenfa

calvolYu.dialogue: You heard my master! We have seen the lizardfolk dining merrily on one of his victims.
calvolYu.speaker: Volun

calcaa78.dialogue: What? Unpredictability settles over them, Volun. Soon we may not be able to see the talibund ones at all.
calcaa78.speaker: caalenfa

calcaa79.dialogue: Well, what brings them here this time? Tell me what they say, if you can still hear it!
calcaa79.speaker: caalenfa

calvolYv.dialogue: Oh, but my love, look in the bowl, look what is happening in the bowl!
calvolYv.speaker: Volun

calvolYw.dialogue: We have said enough to them, maybe more than we should.
calvolYw.speaker: Volun

calvolYx.dialogue: Now it is time for them to go on, to continue on their path. -Farewell, Veiled Travelers. May your path be ever your own.
calvolYx.speaker: Volun

calvolYy.dialogue: O Veiled Ones, did you have another question for my master? Ask wisely, now - his time is precious.
calvolYy.speaker: Volun

calvolYz.dialogue: Master, they do not know of the naiad!
calvolYz.speaker: Volun

calvolY{.dialogue: Master, they returned the waterbells to the naiad!
calvolY{.speaker: Volun

calvolY|.dialogue: Master, they wish to know who Malgi Hi is.
calvolY|.speaker: Volun

calvolY}.dialogue: Master, they said they would avoid the evil sorcerer.
calvolY}.speaker: Volun

calvolY~.dialogue: Master, they refuse to take your advice!
calvolY~.speaker: Volun

calvolY.dialogue: Master, woe to you! They have already met Malgi Hi - and killed him!
calvolY.speaker: Volun

calvolYÄ.dialogue: Master, the Veiled Ones inquire about the goddess Shar.
calvolYÄ.speaker: Volun

calvolYÅ.dialogue: Master, the Veiled Ones inquire about Anorrweyn Evensong!
calvolYÅ.speaker: Volun

calvolYÇ.dialogue: Master, the Veiled Ones want to know more about the dwarf-lord, Harldain Ironbar.
calvolYÇ.speaker: Volun

calvolYÉ.dialogue: My love, the Veiled Ones are asking about the Golden Serpent, the Shrinekeeper of Shaundakul.
calvolYÉ.speaker: Volun

caldmaYÑ.dialogue: There is a shocked silence. Then Volun whispers to Caalenfaire something you cannot hear.
caldmaYÑ.speaker: DM

calcaa83.dialogue: Volun and I knew her, of course, back in the days before Myth Drannor fell. I did not have a high regard for her...
calcaa83.speaker: caalenfa

calcaa84.dialogue: She was good at predicting the future, very good, but not clever enough to avoid it.
calcaa84.speaker: caalenfa

calcaa85.dialogue: She thought her goddess would save her. And maybe the Lady will. But the ways of Mystra are notoriously inscrutable.
calcaa85.speaker: caalenfa

calcaa86.dialogue: Now she languishes in the ruins of her shrine, too defeated even to call out for her followers, believing them all dead. A sorry end, but not entirely undeserved.
calcaa86.speaker: caalenfa

calcaa87.dialogue: At least her spirit is grounded in the present once again. The Veiled Ones have seen to that.
calcaa87.speaker: caalenfa

calvolYÖ.dialogue: No, my love, that was the future you saw, not the present.
calvolYÖ.speaker: Volun

calcaa89.dialogue: Oh, I cannot be bothered right now with that - you tell them, Volun.
calcaa89.speaker: caalenfa

calvolYÜ.dialogue: Harldain Ironbar was lord of the dwarves during the glory days of Myth Drannor.
calvolYÜ.speaker: Volun

calvolYá.dialogue: Under his direction, the city's dwarves built some great marvels - an ingenious system of 'liquid fire' for illumination, waterworks that fed refreshing fountains and pools - and of course the Orrery that powered the Spinning Spires for transportation.
calvolYá.speaker: Volun

calvolYà.dialogue: Now, these wonders lie in ruins or have been turned to evil, and his spirit haunts the House of Gems, hoping for the day when the corruption ends.
calvolYà.speaker: Volun

calvolYâ.dialogue: We knew that day would never come for him - until you came. And set  our hoard of knowledge aflame, and reduced all our old predictions to ashes!
calvolYâ.speaker: Volun

calvolYä.dialogue: Now I think that his ghost will see a turn in the tide of corruption, and his ghost will find peace at last in the halls of his fathers. But that is not a soothsaying - just a guess.
calvolYä.speaker: Volun

calcaa91.dialogue: Odelinde? She is fiercer by far than her mother, and even her mother's mother, all of whom were guardians of the Wind Rider's shrine.
calcaa91.speaker: caalenfa

calvolYã.dialogue: And her daughter will be fiercer still - as great as the Shrinekeepers of old...
calvolYã.speaker: Volun

calcaa92.dialogue: Yes! It was exciting to see that new future emerge in the scrying bowl.
calcaa92.speaker: caalenfa

calcaa93.dialogue: Assuming she has a daughter - that outcome is in doubt, now that orcs are in her Shrine.
calcaa93.speaker: caalenfa

calcaa94.dialogue: You ask for too much. What I know was well-protected and dearly bought.
calcaa94.speaker: caalenfa

calcaa95.dialogue: But nevertheless I will tell you the tale - what I know of it, anyway.
calcaa95.speaker: caalenfa

calcaa96.dialogue: Of Kya Mordrayn herself I know very little. Honored as a hero, she was secretly rising quickly in stature within the Cult of the Dragon. When Pelendralaar the Dragon disappeared, she was thought to have helped defeat him...
calcaa96.speaker: caalenfa

calcaa97.dialogue: ...but in reality she was the archmage who persuaded him to transform into a dracolich. And since that day they have been as one.
calcaa97.speaker: caalenfa

calcaa98.dialogue: The utter destruction of Mocthrinul, and the great tower he resided in, was done by them - but blamed on others; so was the ransack of the Far Holes. And of course they have been ruthless in seizing this city for their own, for purposes that are hidden even from me.
calcaa98.speaker: caalenfa

calvolYå.dialogue: There is not much to tell. Back in the glory days of Myth Drannor, we were rivals, enemies even, in those days when power at court was everything.
calvolYå.speaker: Volun

calvolYç.dialogue: Caalenfaire pursued his art without mercy, and I did not - so eventually he defeated me, and I became a skull upon his writing desk.
calvolYç.speaker: Volun

calvolYé.dialogue: And when Myth Drannor fell, Caalenfaire died and became a ghost, just as he had foreseen. And by my choice I became his familiar, and only companion.
calvolYé.speaker: Volun

calvolYè.dialogue: And so the centuries have passed. He still pursues his art without mercy, as you have seen, but it has come to pass that we love each other, an outcome that despite our arts neither of us had foreseen.
calvolYè.speaker: Volun

calvolYê.dialogue: Master! They have spoken with the naiad!
calvolYê.speaker: Volun

calcaaa4.dialogue: What is this? Plinshree usually has no patience for mortals - and little regard for them, either.
calcaaa4.speaker: caalenfa

calvolYë.dialogue: She looks on them the way we looked upon mayflies, once upon a time. Her thoughts and concerns are like the water she swims in, ever flowing and ever changing.
calvolYë.speaker: Volun

calcaaa5.dialogue: Have you found the Glyphs of Water? Have you learned the Splashing Word? Once we saw great treasures come to one who unlocked their secret...
calcaaa5.speaker: caalenfa

calvolYí.dialogue: ...but that is a future which now will not come to pass, unless you fulfill it.
calvolYí.speaker: Volun

calcaaa6.dialogue: Ah. Of course. That is in the future - if it exists at all.
calcaaa6.speaker: caalenfa

calcaaa7.dialogue: Curse them, Volun! By the forelock of Beshaba, they have astounded me yet again.
calcaaa7.speaker: caalenfa

calcaaa8.dialogue: This is one more thing I had not foreseen - and it changes everything. Now the phaerrim will have their hands full - now the alhoon may stay away, in the dark holes to which they fled...
calcaaa8.speaker: caalenfa

calvolYì.dialogue: Now you will have to recast all your soothsaying incantations, and recalculate all the possibilities. And I know how much you HATE doing that, Caalenfaire my love.
calvolYì.speaker: Volun

calcaab0.dialogue: Ah - you have felt the touch of the Lady of Loss, have you? No mortal is ever free from her embrace...
calcaab0.speaker: caalenfa

calcaab1.dialogue: ...when a beloved companion dies, Shar is there. Pain or forgetfulness is what she offers you, and either choice suits her dark whims very well.
calcaab1.speaker: caalenfa

calcaab3.dialogue: Do not tell them! It is better if they do not know.
calcaab3.speaker: caalenfa

calcaab4.dialogue: That is wise. He is human, but he abhors humankind, for reasons I will not divulge. For decades he has gathered dark spells from creatures that shun the light of day...
calcaab4.speaker: caalenfa

calcaab5.dialogue: ...and now he moves like the breath of pestilence through villages and towns.
calcaab5.speaker: caalenfa

calvolYî.dialogue: His will to destroy is ironwrought, and now his form echoes it. A mask of iron hides a face from which all kinship and mercy have fled.
calvolYî.speaker: Volun

calcaab6.dialogue: Then they are fools, because Malgi Hi eats up his enemies as an elf-child savors dreamberries. The lizardfolk obey him absolutely, and his spells can turn his fanatic troops into warriors with skins of stone.
calcaab6.speaker: caalenfa

calcaab7.dialogue: But I waste my breath, laying wisdom before the talibund. You will go your own way, come what may. I wash my hands of it.
calcaab7.speaker: caalenfa

calcaab9.dialogue: Then you were right, curse you, Volun! The human the lizardfolk were eating...
calcaab9.speaker: caalenfa

calvolYï.dialogue: ...that was Malgi Hi himself, just as I told you.
calvolYï.speaker: Volun

calcaac3.dialogue: That is enough, Volun! We have given them guidance. Now they must go.
calcaac3.speaker: caalenfa

calvolYñ.dialogue: Now, Veiled Ones, you must depart. My master is eager to return to his spellweaving.
calvolYñ.speaker: Volun

calvolYó.dialogue: That is all we will say for now.
calvolYó.speaker: Volun

calcaac6.dialogue: Achh! Now my bowl is all cloudy. Send them away, Volun, send the Veiled Ones away!
calcaac6.speaker: caalenfa

calvolYò.dialogue: What it all means, I do not know. But that is all we can tell you right now.
calvolYò.speaker: Volun

caldmaYô.dialogue: Images twist and writhe deep in the sloshing fluid of the conjuring bowl. But you cannot make any sense of them at all.
caldmaYô.speaker: DM

caldmaYö.dialogue: Images flicker in the scrying bowl. You glimpse howling undead mobbing a hapless orog, predatory lizardfolk running through the darkness - and all the while, a Cult Mage stands next to an evil-looking Gate, laughing hysterically.
caldmaYö.speaker: DM

caldmaYõ.dialogue: Images flicker in the scrying bowl. You glimpse predatory lizardfolk running through the darkness, a troop of orogs herding some howling undead down a corridor - under the watchful eyes of two Cult Mages.
caldmaYõ.speaker: DM

caldmaYú.dialogue: Images dance in the scrying bowl, and the sound of footsteps wells up from its oily surface. You see Beriand offering up a simple prayer to Mystra, while Faeril paces impatiently in front of him, swinging her weapon.
caldmaYú.speaker: DM

caldmaYù.dialogue: The bowl seems to be entirely dark.
caldmaYù.speaker: DM

caldmaYû.dialogue: But then you dimly see a figure - she is swimming - you catch your breath - she is indescribably beautiful.
caldmaYû.speaker: DM

caldmaYü.dialogue: But then Volun screams at you, and you jump back!
caldmaYü.speaker: DM

calvolY†.dialogue: Fools! Imbeciles! That vision of loveliness you see is the naiad Plinshree. And one good look at her would take your breath away forever.
calvolY†.speaker: Volun

caldmaY°.dialogue: You only catch a glimpse - of reptilian jaws snapping rapturously at animal meat. Then the vision flickers away.
caldmaY°.speaker: DM

caldmaY¢.dialogue: You see vague shapes moving in the bowl's depths - a gargoyle? A dragon? You hear something - a spell being cast? Everything seems dim and distorted.
caldmaY¢.speaker: DM

caldmaY£.dialogue: Caalenfaire and Volun return their attention to the scrying bowl.
caldmaY£.speaker: DM

caldmaY§.dialogue: Caalenfaire and Volun attend once again to the scrying bowl.
caldmaY§.speaker: DM

calvolY•.dialogue: Oh yes. And next time, do not stand there so quietly! Let us know as soon as you approach.
calvolY•.speaker: Volun

caldmaY¶.dialogue: With that, the diviners turn their attention once again to the shifting scenes in the scrying bowl.
caldmaY¶.speaker: DM

calcaae1.dialogue: Well, Volun, it has happened, just as I feared.
calcaae1.speaker: caalenfa

calvolYß.dialogue: The Veiled Ones - they have disappeared entirely?
calvolYß.speaker: Volun

calcaae2.dialogue: Yes. And I fear it may be forever.
calcaae2.speaker: caalenfa

calvolY®.dialogue: Veiled Ones - if you can hear me - my master says you must walk your own way. Unless the pall on this city is lifted, we can help you no longer.
calvolY®.speaker: Volun

caldma00.dialogue: Volun takes something away from you - it is the Backwards Key!
caldma00.speaker: DM

calvol00.dialogue: You for is this, Ones Veiled, here. Master, yes.
calvol00.speaker: Volun

caldma01.dialogue: Now Caalenfaire seems to answer her. He also is talking backwards.
caldma01.speaker: DM

calcaae4.dialogue: Volun, them to it give, ahead, go! Wizards of House the into, here leads that door magical the unlocks it.
calcaae4.speaker: caalenfa

calcaae5.dialogue: Way unusual an in operates it. Obsidian and adamant of tendrils vein-like with inlaid and bone of out sculpted cunningly, key ornate an - it see they when it know will they. Course of.
calcaae5.speaker: caalenfa

calvol01.dialogue: Ritual the begin I should? Key Backwards the about you asking are they - Ones Veiled the, Master.
calvol01.speaker: Volun

calvol02.dialogue: There. Now that the Backwards Ritual is done, Veiled Ones, is there something else you wish to ask my master about?
calvol02.speaker: Volun

calpro03.dialogue: Sneak a peek into the bowl
calpro03.speaker: Protagonist

caldmaY©.dialogue: The images in the bowl are dazzling and incoherent. You cannot even begin to understand them.
caldmaY©.speaker: DM

calpro08.dialogue: Ask who Malgi Hi might be
calpro08.speaker: Protagonist

calpro09.dialogue: Tell them you will avoid Malgi Hi
calpro09.speaker: Protagonist

calpro11.dialogue: Say you already defeated Malgi Hi
calpro11.speaker: Protagonist

calproXA.dialogue: Ask them about the Backwards Key
calproXA.speaker: Protagonist

calpro17.dialogue: Ask them to tell their story
calpro17.speaker: Protagonist

ca1caa02.dialogue: And now orc-arrows pierce the Golden Serpent.
ca1caa02.speaker: caalenfa

ca1vol00.dialogue: Do not disturb the Master. Here is the wise counsel you seek. Your coming has been foreseen.
ca1vol00.speaker: Volun

ca1vol01.dialogue: Seek out Odelinde, the golden serpent. Seek out the spirit of the Dwarf Lord, Harldain Ironbar. You will find them beyond the Circle of Mythan -But hold a moment!
ca1vol01.speaker: Volun

ca1vol02.dialogue: You do not have the Ring of Calling!
ca1vol02.speaker: Volun

ca1vol03.dialogue: You already have the Ring of Calling!
ca1vol03.speaker: Volun

ca1vol04.dialogue: And there is a man among you, one of Athan's companions!
ca1vol04.speaker: Volun

ca1vol05.dialogue: And that sorcerer, Jarial, has joined you!
ca1vol05.speaker: Volun

ca1vol06.dialogue: And you haven't yet looked into the Scrying Mirror!
ca1vol06.speaker: Volun

ca1vol07.dialogue: Master! Despair and woe! Your prediction has gone awry.
ca1vol07.speaker: Volun
ca1vol07.desc: spoken, calling to her master, excited and intrigued

ca1caa13.dialogue: What? What? Hand of Beshaba, where are they? I cannot see them. I cannot hear them. The fools!
ca1caa13.speaker: caalenfa
ca1caa13.desc: spoken, coming briefly out of his trance, irritated

ca1vol08.dialogue: They are talibund, I tell you! They have left the Path.
ca1vol08.speaker: Volun

ca1caa16.dialogue: Volun! They know all they should. Give them guidance, and let them go.
ca1caa16.speaker: caalenfa
ca1caa16.desc: This line is no longer spoken, brisk

ca1vol09.dialogue: Master! They seek the Ring of Calling. Is that not according to the Path?
ca1vol09.speaker: Volun

ca1caa18.dialogue: I will look into the bowl.
ca1caa18.speaker: caalenfa

ca1caa19.dialogue: I am looking... It is unclear. They are Veiled Ones now, and their shadow darkens anything they might touch or anyplace they might go.
ca1caa19.speaker: caalenfa

ca1caa20.dialogue: There are many possibilities... the Tulun Wall... the Corridor of Salg... but... first they should go to the House of Gems, in the Room of Words. Yes. But look!
ca1caa20.speaker: caalenfa

ca1DM00.dialogue: Caalenfaire's spell teaches you Rhesheshannen, the Word of Oblivion.
ca1DM00.speaker: DM

ca1caa22.dialogue: I have taught them the Word of Oblivion, so that when they find the Ring, its once-proud bones will release it.
ca1caa22.speaker: caalenfa

ca1vol10.dialogue: The Master knows much that is hidden. Remember that.
ca1vol10.speaker: Volun

ca1vol12.dialogue: Now, Veiled Ones, it is time for you to go.
ca1vol12.speaker: Volun

ca1vol13.dialogue: Now, Veiled Ones, it is time for you to go. Here is the Ring of Calling.
ca1vol13.speaker: Volun

ca1vol14.dialogue: Master! They have the Ring of Calling. But behold! Its owner clings to it, even after death. They seek the Word of Oblivion.
ca1vol14.speaker: Volun

ca1caa28.dialogue: Yes, Volun. I will speak the Word of Oblivion, and give these bones peace.
ca1caa28.speaker: caalenfa

ca1caa29.dialogue: There - I have freed the Ring. Bring it before the Seal of Mythanthor, to open up the way to the City Heights.
ca1caa29.speaker: caalenfa

ca1vol15.dialogue: Return? You cannot. Do not even try.
ca1vol15.speaker: Volun

ca1vol16.dialogue: We will peer ahead as far as we can, and give you such help as we can.
ca1vol16.speaker: Volun

ca1vol17.dialogue: But if Caalenfaire could see you, maybe others could also. People of power. Maybe it is better for you to walk alone in the dark...
ca1vol17.speaker: Volun

ca1caa33.dialogue: And yet - not quite alone, Volun. For there is a hand over them... whose hand, and for good or ill, I cannot tell.
ca1caa33.speaker: caalenfa

ca1vol18.dialogue: Master, the Veiled Ones seek your guidance.
ca1vol18.speaker: Volun

ca1caa35.dialogue: I will look into the bowl. Let me see...
ca1caa35.speaker: caalenfa

ca1caa36.dialogue: The Path is dimming now... it twists. Still, the signs are clear. You must get to the Heights of the city. If you remain in the dungeons, you will die.
ca1caa36.speaker: caalenfa

ca1caa37.dialogue: To get to the Heights, there are two paths... no, now there is only one. You must wear the Ring of Calling, and stand before the great Seal of Mythanthor.
ca1caa37.speaker: caalenfa

ca1caa38.dialogue: Beyond the Seal... Odelinde... Harldain. These are your allies. Befriend them or die. But wait, who is this? Ancient... trapped... The Veil of Mystra descends. I cannot see more.
ca1caa38.speaker: caalenfa

ca1vol19.dialogue: Augh! I hate it when that happens.
ca1vol19.speaker: Volun

ca1vol20.dialogue: I will not tell you. No mortal should glimpse their future. It is never happy enough, or long enough.
ca1vol20.speaker: Volun

ca1vol21.dialogue: Take a look at my master! Would you become like him? Do not seek out the future! It will find you soon enough.
ca1vol21.speaker: Volun

ca1vol22.dialogue: Talibund. The Veiled Ones. What soothsayers call those whose destinies cannot be foretold.
ca1vol22.speaker: Volun

ca1vol23.dialogue: How one becomes talibund, I do not know. My master says it has something to do with foolishness. I believe it has more to do with courage.
ca1vol23.speaker: Volun

ca1vol24.dialogue: My master Caalenfaire had worked out a destiny for you - a path you should walk. For the eventual good of Myth Drannor, if not your own.
ca1vol24.speaker: Volun

ca1vol25.dialogue: But instead you have become talibund. Now you walk your own path, which none can see. May Tymora help us! This is an unsettling turn.
ca1vol25.speaker: Volun

ca1caa46.dialogue: Hoho, Volun! What do I see now, in my bowl? The Veiled Ones will be writ into the Song of Faerun!
ca1caa46.speaker: caalenfa

ca1vol26.dialogue: Why, it is the great tale of this world, sung by the Bard of Kara-Tur. Master! Tell us more about the Song!
ca1vol26.speaker: Volun

ca1bar00.dialogue: In Cormanthor did mage Mordrayn / speak spells of greed in Words of flame; / with poison troth she soon unmade / proud treasure of the Silver Blade; / and by her side, Pelendralaar, / their minds as one, come from afar; / dark creatures drown the city bright, the dragon's kin, the elf of night; / The Pool! The Pool! It grows, and yet, / one small band against it set.
ca1bar00.speaker: Bard
ca1bar00.desc: spoken: LOCALIZERS:  plays Song of Faerun Stanza 1 which should be saved as faerun1.wav

ca1vol27.dialogue: Yes, yes! I am amazed. This is not what we had foreseen! It gives me hope.
ca1vol27.speaker: Volun

ca1vol28.dialogue: Yes, yes! I give you guidance now. Then you can go.
ca1vol28.speaker: Volun

ca1vol29.dialogue: Seek, as I said, the serpent Odelinde and the dwarf spirit Harldain. They are your natural allies. Heed well their counsel!
ca1vol29.speaker: Volun

ca1vol30.dialogue: To reach them on the Heights, you must go to the Seal of Mythanthor. Do you know where that is? Look for a purple crescent arc on the wall, in the uppermost part of the dungeons.
ca1vol30.speaker: Volun

ca1vol31.dialogue: To reach them on the Heights, you open the Seal of Mythanthor. You have seen it - a purple crescent arc on the wall, in the uppermost part of the dungeons.
ca1vol31.speaker: Volun

ca1vol32.dialogue: To open the Seal, you must find the Ring of Calling. -Master, look into your bowl. Can it tell you where the Ring of Calling might be?
ca1vol32.speaker: Volun

ca1vol33.dialogue: To open the Seal, you must find the Ring of Calling. My master says it may be in the House of Gems, which is east of here.
ca1vol33.speaker: Volun

ca1vol34.dialogue: To open the Seal, you must wear the Ring of Calling. My master has released it from its bones for you.
ca1vol34.speaker: Volun

ca1vol35.dialogue: To open the Seal, you must wear the Ring of Calling. My master will speak the Word of Oblivion, and release it from its bones for you.
ca1vol35.speaker: Volun

ca1pro00.dialogue: Ask them about the Song of Faerun
ca1pro00.speaker: Protagonist

ca1pro01.dialogue: Tell them you seek the Ring of Calling
ca1pro01.speaker: Protagonist

ca1pro02.dialogue: Tell them you seek the Word of Oblivion
ca1pro02.speaker: Protagonist

ca1pro04.dialogue: Ask them what the Path is
ca1pro04.speaker: Protagonist

ca1pro05.dialogue: Ask how you return to the Path
ca1pro05.speaker: Protagonist

ca1pro06.dialogue: Ask them what your future holds
ca1pro06.speaker: Protagonist

ca1pro07.dialogue: Ask them to finish their wise counsel
ca1pro07.speaker: Protagonist

caxcaa01.dialogue: Now watch, the omens change. Watch them, Volun; they pirouette.
caxcaa01.speaker: caalenfa

caxvol00.dialogue: I tell you, something is happening!
caxvol00.speaker: Volun

caxcaa03.dialogue: And the Ring of Calling... what of the Ring? It enters the Room of Words!
caxcaa03.speaker: caalenfa

caxvol01.dialogue: Bones stay silent, but their silence speaks.
caxvol01.speaker: Volun

caxcaa04.dialogue: She has put the Mark on them...
caxcaa04.speaker: caalenfa

caxcax00.dialogue: The Path is the Path, Volun.
caxcax00.speaker: caalenfa

ca4caa02.dialogue: ...Riots. Seven Cult leaders unmasked and killed. Wailing and consternation!
ca4caa02.speaker: Caalenfa
ca4caa02.desc: spoken, he describes what he sees in his bowl, to Volun

ca4vol01.dialogue: Haha! -Ah, Caalenfaire my love, the Veiled Ones are here.
ca4vol01.speaker: Volun

ca4caa03.dialogue: Yes, yes, they muddy my scrying bowl. Tell them, Volun, then send them away!
ca4caa03.speaker: Caalenfa

ca4vol02.dialogue: Your great deed will be celebrated all over Faerun. And Phlan will erect a monument in your honor!
ca4vol02.speaker: Volun
ca4vol02.desc: spoken, to party, relaying official info

ca4vol03.dialogue: But think not of returning to Phlan! For that is not in your future - not yet. Farewell.
ca4vol03.speaker: Volun
ca4vol03.desc: spoken, lowers her voice, whispers secret info

kspdma03.dialogue: You have successfully entered the mighty Castle Cormanthor. The air reeks of smoke and the rank musk of mating dragon-kin.
kspdma03.speaker: DM

xugDMYA.dialogue: This once-stately elven hall is now given over completely to the barrack-rookeries of the dragon-kin.
xugDMYA.speaker: DM

kssdma03.dialogue: History is written by the victors, so there is no epitaph for the nameless thousands who are at rest here - their lives, loves and sacrifices forgotten, their names lost to quiet eternity.
kssdma03.speaker: DM

kvkdmaYA.dialogue: Immediately the Cult Mages begin to dispel their magic Gates.
kvkdmaYA.speaker: DM

vbmdma00.dialogue: Underneath the Cult Overseer's battered body, you find a curious treasure - a jawbone talisman made into a necklace, and electric with the mysterious ensorcellments of the Cult of the Dragon.
vbmdma00.speaker: DM

vbmdma01.dialogue: When you pick it up, it summons a Gate.
vbmdma01.speaker: DM

vbfdma00.dialogue: Lashed to a horn in the Tusk-Lord's forehead, you find a sturdy iron key.
vbfdma00.speaker: DM

kyaDMYA.dialogue: You sense that watchful eyes are upon you...
kyaDMYA.speaker: DM

kyaDMYB.dialogue: ...but they find you lacking, because the drawbridge stays up.
kyaDMYB.speaker: DM

kyaDMYC.dialogue: You sense the presence of a magical guardian.
kyaDMYC.speaker: DM

kyaDMYD.dialogue: It examines you, and then with joy hurries to lower the drawbridge.
kyaDMYD.speaker: DM

vehdma00.dialogue: The aura of evil is strong here. You can sense waves of evil sloshing back and forth - from the orc idol to the dark Spawn Pool, and back again.
vehdma00.speaker: DM

vemdma00.dialogue: When you shatter the orc idol, you break an evil spell.
vemdma00.speaker: DM

vemdma01.dialogue: With its minions destroyed and its token in pieces, the Spawn Pool retreats to the foul place it sprang from - the Pool of Radiance.
vemdma01.speaker: DM

ksvdma03.dialogue: The door is solidly set and well-crafted, obviously by dwarves. It is firmly locked, but you see signs it's been opened recently. Through an unusually large keyhole, you smell the stale air of the dungeons, and the rank odor of orcs.
ksvdma03.speaker: DM

kswdma03.dialogue: The chest once held a  proud silken banner, the centerpiece of the legendary Midsummer Firemeet of Myth Drannor. But now the banner is in decay, pawed and torn by greedy hands.
kswdma03.speaker: DM

kswdma05.dialogue: There is nothing of value inside.
kswdma05.speaker: DM

kszdma03.dialogue: You are in the presence of untold thousands of anguished souls. The pain of their unending death agonies grips your heart and lungs, making each heartbeat painful and each breath a gasp.
kszdma03.speaker: DM

dbgdmaYA.dialogue: You lay the common battleaxe in the basin...
dbgdmaYA.speaker: DM

dbgdmaYB.dialogue: It is gripped by phantom hands, and dragged down into a place beyond the grave.
dbgdmaYB.speaker: DM

dbgdmaYC.dialogue: Again phantom hands rise, eager to accept the token of your respect.
dbgdmaYC.speaker: DM

ddgdmaYA.dialogue: You lay the common dagger in the basin...
ddgdmaYA.speaker: DM

ddgdmaYB.dialogue: It is gripped by phantom hands, and dragged down into a place beyond the grave.
ddgdmaYB.speaker: DM

ddgdmaYC.dialogue: Again unseen hands seize upon your token of respect.
ddgdmaYC.speaker: DM

dwmdma00.dialogue: Congratulations! You defeated Kya Mordrayn, and so she was claimed by her dark masters. And you slew the dracolich Pelendralaar, and used the Gauntlets of Moander to destroy the Pool of Radiance.
dwmdma00.speaker: DM

dwmdma01.dialogue: You have dealt a terrible blow to the mighty Cult of the Dragon, and all the free peoples of the Realms salute you.
dwmdma01.speaker: DM

dhgdmaYA.dialogue: You lay the common warhammer in the basin...
dhgdmaYA.speaker: DM

dhgdmaYB.dialogue: It is gripped by phantom hands, and dragged down into a place beyond the grave.
dhgdmaYB.speaker: DM

dhgdmaYC.dialogue: Again your tribute vanishes, seized eagerly by unseen spirits.
dhgdmaYC.speaker: DM

dlgdmaYA.dialogue: You lay the common long sword in the basin...
dlgdmaYA.speaker: DM

dlgdmaYB.dialogue: It is gripped by phantom hands, and dragged down into a place beyond the grave.
dlgdmaYB.speaker: DM

dlgdmaYC.dialogue: Again the watchful spirits show their approval of your gift.
dlgdmaYC.speaker: DM

dmgdmaYA.dialogue: You lay the common mace in the basin...
dmgdmaYA.speaker: DM

dmgdmaYB.dialogue: It is gripped by phantom hands, and dragged down into a place beyond the grave.
dmgdmaYB.speaker: DM

dmgdmaYC.dialogue: Again the phantom hands spirit away your gift.
dmgdmaYC.speaker: DM

ktidmaYA.dialogue: An inscription reads, 'If friend you be, and in need, these treasures are for thee. Use them as my companions no longer can.  - Jelde Asturien, Priest of Lathander, Knight of Myth Drannor'
ktidmaYA.speaker: DM

ktcdma03.dialogue: The ground gives way beneath your feet...
ktcdma03.speaker: DM

kvmdma03.dialogue: As you approach this door, a chill settles upon your soul.
kvmdma03.speaker: DM

ktedma03.dialogue: You have fallen at least 30 feet. You can see a ragged hole above you, but no way to get back to the surface the way you came.
ktedma03.speaker: DM

ktjDM00.dialogue: Mellen, the Singing Word, unseals the Glyph of Song.
ktjDM00.speaker: DM

ktjdma04.dialogue: You recognize the magic seal in front of the door - it is the Glyph of Song. But you have not learned the glyph's Unsealing Word.
ktjdma04.speaker: DM

vasdma00.dialogue: There is nothing left in this chest.
vasdma00.speaker: DM

vasdma01.dialogue: In the spectre's chest you find a grotesque gargoyle's mouth, carved in stone.
vasdma01.speaker: DM

vasdma02.dialogue: Every time you speak, it repeats what you say in the harsh gargoyle tongue.
vasdma02.speaker: DM

vasdma03.dialogue: And if gargoyles speak, it will translate what they say for you.
vasdma03.speaker: DM

jwjdma00.dialogue: There is nothing left in this chest.
jwjdma00.speaker: DM

selections: Ask why she tells you of your doom
Ask her why you must die
Tell Bergos she will die, not you
Spit on the name of Lolth
Demand that she reveal all her warriors
Taunt her about how few warriors she commands
Show her you have the Staff of Sunlight
Tell her you want to leave in peace

dr1dlr01.speaker: Drwleadr
dr1dlr01.desc: spoken, hissed as a whispered order

dr1dlr02.dialogue: O you trespassers, when the bright angels come for you...
dr1dlr02.speaker: Drwleadr

dr1dlr03.dialogue: ...tell them it was Lolth, Queen of Darkness, who sent your spirits screaming up into the light, and Bergos, of the great House of Freth, who was her instrument.
dr1dlr03.speaker: Drwleadr

dr1dlr04.dialogue: Watch! Your strength will drain away, your vision will fail, and your spells will perish upon your lips, for I have told you true - this is your hour of doom.
dr1dlr04.speaker: Drwleadr

dr1dlr06.dialogue: Lolth smiles on those who pronounce doom in her name, and then execute it.
dr1dlr06.speaker: Drwleadr

dr1dlr07.dialogue: Are you so blind that you don't realize where you are? You are walking the drow ways, ogglin. You are breathing drow air.
dr1dlr07.speaker: Drwleadr

dr1dlr08.dialogue: You have crept close to our stronghold, and now you will perish.
dr1dlr08.speaker: Drwleadr

dr1dlr09.dialogue: She is the Dark Mother of All Drow, the Weaver of Chaos. Those who have never heard of her, she despises most of all.
dr1dlr09.speaker: Drwleadr

dr1dlr10.dialogue: Not so! Behind me, ten warriors stand ready! More than enough to save me from the five of you. Behold!
dr1dlr10.speaker: Drwleadr

dr1dlr11.dialogue: Not so! Behind me, ten warriors stand ready! More than enough to save me from the four of you. Behold!
dr1dlr11.speaker: Drwleadr

dr1dlr12.dialogue: Not so! Behind me, ten warriors stand ready! More than enough to save me from the few of you. Behold!
dr1dlr12.speaker: Drwleadr

dr1dlr13.dialogue: Not so! Behind me, ten warriors stand ready! More than enough to save me from the six of you. Behold!
dr1dlr13.speaker: Drwleadr

dr1dlr14.speaker: Drwleadr
dr1dlr14.desc: spoken, 'Step out of concealment! Be watchful!'

dr1dlr15.dialogue: Lolth did not raise her children to be so foolish.
dr1dlr15.speaker: Drwleadr

dr1dlr16.dialogue: Lolth has given me more than I need to crush the likes of you. Behold!
dr1dlr16.speaker: Drwleadr

dr1dlr17.dialogue: Which makes us more eager to strike the light from your eyes forever.
dr1dlr17.speaker: Drwleadr

dr1dlr18.dialogue: You will leave, yes. In peace? That is up to you and your god.
dr1dlr18.speaker: Drwleadr

dr1pro00.dialogue: Ask why she tells you of your doom
dr1pro00.speaker: Protagonist

dr1pro01.dialogue: Ask her why you must die
dr1pro01.speaker: Protagonist

dr1pro03.dialogue: Tell Bergos she will die, not you
dr1pro03.speaker: Protagonist

dr1pro04.dialogue: Spit on the name of Lolth
dr1pro04.speaker: Protagonist

dr1pro06.dialogue: Demand that she reveal all her warriors
dr1pro06.speaker: Protagonist

dr1pro07.dialogue: Taunt her about how few warriors she commands
dr1pro07.speaker: Protagonist

dr1pro08.dialogue: Show her you have the Staff of Sunlight
dr1pro08.speaker: Protagonist

dr1pro09.dialogue: Tell her you want to leave in peace
dr1pro09.speaker: Protagonist

dwgdwg02.dialogue: Ah. We were wondering who it was, making so much noise out in the hall. Foluben said it was zombies...
dwgdwg02.speaker: Greyanna

dwgdwg03.dialogue: ...and he was right. Your wounds make you clumsier than usual. And look, Kalannar! Blood sloshes out of their boots.
dwgdwg03.speaker: Greyanna

dwgdwg04.dialogue: ...and he was right. Look, Kalannar! Their company is half dead.
dwgdwg04.speaker: Greyanna

dwgdwg05.dialogue: Ah. We were wondering who it was, making so much noise out in the hall. Foluben said it must be rats...
dwgdwg05.speaker: Greyanna

dwgdwg06.dialogue: ...and he was right. You're far from home, little rats. And wounded, too!
dwgdwg06.speaker: Greyanna

dwgdwg07.dialogue: Ah. We were wondering who it was, making so much noise out in the hall. Foluben said it was rats... I said it was some light-loving rivven...
dwgdwg07.speaker: Greyanna

dwgdwg08.dialogue: I will know next time that Foluben is always right.
dwgdwg08.speaker: Greyanna

dwgdwg09.dialogue: I suppose you are here seeking the Bodach Swan. If so, you come in vain.
dwgdwg09.speaker: Greyanna
dwgdwg09.desc: spoken, raises her voice, stern and carefully neutral

dwgdwg11.dialogue: Ibrith! What thick heads you light-lovers have! I told you, you seek it in vain.
dwgdwg11.speaker: Greyanna

dwgdwg12.dialogue: Although, by the Ancient Eye, it would be a powerful ally for you.
dwgdwg12.speaker: Greyanna

dwgdwg13.dialogue: I tell you, forget the Bodach Swan! I am Greyanna Faeurdyn, malla ilharess of Myth Drannor! Focus your wits on me, if you can.
dwgdwg13.speaker: Greyanna

dwgdwg14.dialogue: Very well, I will tell you, although I assure you, you will never meet the Swan.
dwgdwg14.speaker: Greyanna

dwgdwg15.dialogue: Every drow child knows of the Bodach Swan. For it is the one who lurks around the corner, up near the surface, right at the edge of hearing, just out of sight.
dwgdwg15.speaker: Greyanna

dwgdwg16.dialogue: Pale it is, with eyes that flash light into the darkest crevice, and a mouth like the inferno of the cursed Sun.
dwgdwg16.speaker: Greyanna

dwgdwg17.dialogue: Yes, the Bodach Swan is just a story, a child's fable. I only brought it up because my warriors needed a moment to surround you.
dwgdwg17.speaker: Greyanna

dwgdwg19.dialogue: Oh, the Bodach Swan is just a story we tell to scare our children. I only brought it up because my warriors needed a moment to surround you.
dwgdwg19.speaker: Greyanna

dwgdwg20.dialogue: What of them? Do not try to tell me they are your allies!
dwgdwg20.speaker: Greyanna

dwgdwg21.dialogue: Only fools, mindless thralls and the proud in chains ally with the Cult. Which are you?
dwgdwg21.speaker: Greyanna

dwgdwg22.dialogue: Go ahead. Call for help! I doubt the Cult or anyone else will come to aid you.
dwgdwg22.speaker: Greyanna

dwgdwg23.dialogue: What do I care? Kill them all, and welcome. We of the House of Freth have no more use for the Cult.
dwgdwg23.speaker: Greyanna

dwgdwg24.dialogue: They helped us destroy our blood enemies, the drow of the House of Kilsek.
dwgdwg24.speaker: Greyanna

dwgdwg25.dialogue: But soon we will chase the mighty Cult screaming off into the sunlight, where they belong.
dwgdwg25.speaker: Greyanna

dwgdwg26.dialogue: You, however - you will never see the cursed sunlight again.
dwgdwg26.speaker: Greyanna

dwgdwg27.dialogue: Do not concern yourselves about the Cult of the Dragon.
dwgdwg27.speaker: Greyanna

dwgdwg28.dialogue: Worry instead about the drow of the House of Freth.
dwgdwg28.speaker: Greyanna

dwgdwg29.dialogue: Why do you care? In a moment, one or the other of us will be dust! What will a name matter then?
dwgdwg29.speaker: Greyanna

dwgdwg30.dialogue: You seek to put off that moment, when one or the other of us will die. Ah, but I relish it! And that is the difference between us.
dwgdwg30.speaker: Greyanna

dwgdwg31.dialogue: Come, waerogglin! You gain nothing by waiting! The Bodach Swan will not come to save you. Lift your swords! Throw your spells! Act now! Save yourselves, if you can.
dwgdwg31.speaker: Greyanna

dwgdwg32.dialogue: I am Greyanna Faeurdyn, Qu'Daharil of the House of Freth, malla ilharess of the Catacombs of Myth Drannor.
dwgdwg32.speaker: Greyanna
dwgdwg32.desc: Qu'Daharil = noble daughter, malla ilharess = honored mistress

dwgdwg33.dialogue: I tell you this so that, when your gods spit on you for being weak, you will have someone to mewl about.
dwgdwg33.speaker: Greyanna

dwgdwg34.dialogue: Do not dare to threaten me, orbb jivven! The darkness will claim you and your Staff soon enough.
dwgdwg34.speaker: Greyanna

dwgpro00.dialogue: Ask her about the Bodach Swan
dwgpro00.speaker: Protagonist

dwgpro01.dialogue: Insist she tell you about the Bodach Swan
dwgpro01.speaker: Protagonist

dwgpro02.speaker: Protagonist

dwgpro03.dialogue: Tell her you are at war with the Cult
dwgpro03.speaker: Protagonist

dwgpro04.dialogue: Warn her you have the Staff of Sunlight
dwgpro04.speaker: Protagonist

kaqdma03.dialogue: The water has an acrid smell and an unhealthy color.
kaqdma03.speaker: DM

kbqdma03.dialogue: The door was once painted with a rune, but it's now too faint to make out what it was.

kbtdma03.dialogue: The air here is stifling hot, and smells of beast.

kbydma03.speaker: DM

kcadma03.dialogue: A horrible stench assails your nostrils.

kwdDMYC.speaker: DM

kwdDMYD.dialogue: They are brutish creatures, yes, and disgusting to look upon, but they dealt honorably with Beriand and me. Fare thee well!'

kwjDMYC.speaker: DM

vafdma02.dialogue: You put the key into your pack.

keozeo03.speaker: BkGood
keozeo03.desc: spoken, very erudite and scholarly but intense

keozeo04.dialogue: ...toss me into the Pyre of Silence, two floors down from here. And any other books the Pyre will accept, toss them in!

keozeo05.dialogue: For we all have evil writ on our pages, and must not be made to surrender our secrets. Do as I say! Goodbye.
