gn1pro04.speaker: Protagonist

gx2gng02.dialogue: Look, Ethe, our saviors have returned!
gx2gng02.speaker: Gloran

gx2gu200.dialogue: They are hurt! Let us try to heal them.
gx2gu200.speaker: Ethe

gx2gu201.dialogue: And they are unhurt, thank the Lady. We'll save our healing arts for another time.
gx2gu201.speaker: Ethe

gx2gu202.dialogue: And they are unhurt, thank the Lady. Or almost so!
gx2gu202.speaker: Ethe

gx2gng06.dialogue: Their wounds are slight, but let us heal them.
gx2gng06.speaker: Gloran
gx2gng06.desc: spoken, glad to be of service

gx2gu203.dialogue: ...but we will try to heal them.
gx2gu203.speaker: Ethe

gx2gu204.dialogue: Ah - the heroes have come back! Do they need our healing, do you think?
gx2gu204.speaker: Ethe

gx2gng09.dialogue: No! The Hand of the Goddess has preserved them.
gx2gng09.speaker: Gloran

gx2gu205.dialogue: Welcome, travelers, and rest here as long as you like... the Silver Fire will protect you.
gx2gu205.speaker: Ethe

gx2gng10.dialogue: They are not badly hurt.. but let us show them the strength of the Silver Fire.
gx2gng10.speaker: Gloran

gx2gng11.dialogue: Yes! Let us show them the strength of the Silver Fire.
gx2gng11.speaker: Gloran

gx2gng12.dialogue: Welcome back, travelers, to the sanctuary of the Silver Fire.
gx2gng12.speaker: Gloran

gx2gu206.dialogue: Rest here as long as you like.
gx2gu206.speaker: Ethe

gx2gng13.dialogue: Come, Ethe, it is time to summon the healing Fire.
gx2gng13.speaker: Gloran

gx4gng02.dialogue: Ah Ethe, it is them!  The heroes of Myth Drannor!
gx4gng02.speaker: Gloran

gx4gn200.dialogue: See how the flame brightens for them! Welcome heroes! The tales of your deeds precede you!
gx4gn200.speaker: Ethe

gx4gng03.dialogue: Look Ethe, our heroes have returned!
gx4gng03.speaker: Gloran

gx4gn201.dialogue: It is they who slew the dracolich, and crushed the haughty Kya Mordrayn!
gx4gn201.speaker: Ethe

gx4gng04.dialogue: Let us heal those hurts, heroes!  Our shrine is honored by your valor.
gx4gng04.speaker: Gloran
gx4gng04.desc: spoken, administering a blessing, then a goodbye

gx4gng05.dialogue: The Mythal hums in tune again, heroes, thanks to you!
gx4gng05.speaker: Gloran

gx4gn202.dialogue: ...and Mystra rejoices in its song.  Rest here a while and let her blessings flow over you.
gx4gn202.speaker: Ethe

hcyhac02.speaker: Hachaam
hcyhac02.desc: spoken, ghostly wail, 'Faervian', eerie, can't tell what it wants

hcyhac04.dialogue: Faervian. My Baneblade. You have freed it. You can wield it. I am jealous of you.
hcyhac04.speaker: Hachaam

hcyhac05.dialogue: You hold Faervian. You may swing it, and cleave your enemies with it...
hcyhac05.speaker: Hachaam

hcyhac06.dialogue: ...but the Baneblade will never sing as it did when I flashed it before the Armies of Darkness.
hcyhac06.speaker: Hachaam

hcyhac07.dialogue: You may hold it, but it will always be my blade.
hcyhac07.speaker: Hachaam

hcyhac08.dialogue: I am... I was... Hachaam Selorn, Arms-Captain of the armies of Myth Drannor.
hcyhac08.speaker: Hachaam

hcyhac09.dialogue: But I suppose that means nothing to you now.
hcyhac09.speaker: Hachaam

hcydma00.dialogue: You hold out the sword to the ghost, but it cannot grasp it.
hcydma00.speaker: DM

hcyhac12.dialogue: I will go. But I make a deal with you...
hcyhac12.speaker: Hachaam

hcyhac15.dialogue: You will regret that... You must atone... the Rivener...
hcyhac15.speaker: Hachaam

hcyhac16.dialogue: Bring Faervian to my tomb... the tomb of Hachaam Selorn... little good my Baneblade will do you now.
hcyhac16.speaker: Hachaam

hcyhac17.dialogue: My tomb... bring Faervian to my tomb, the tomb of Hachaam Selorn. I will tell you... of the Rivener... the baneblade Morvian.
hcyhac17.speaker: Hachaam

hcyhac18.dialogue: My tomb... bring Faervian to my tomb. I will tell you... of the Rivener... the baneblade Morvian.
hcyhac18.speaker: Hachaam

hcypro00.dialogue: Ask the ghost who it is
hcypro00.speaker: Protagonist

hcypro02.dialogue: Give the sword to the ghost
hcypro02.speaker: Protagonist

hcypro03.dialogue: Tell the ghost the sword is yours
hcypro03.speaker: Protagonist

hcypro04.dialogue: Tell the ghost to go away
hcypro04.speaker: Protagonist

hcxhac04.dialogue: I thank you for Faervian. It brings me peace to have it by my side once again.
hcxhac04.speaker: Hachaam

hcxhac05.dialogue: But hush! In the little time I have left, I must tell you about the Baneblade Morvian.
hcxhac05.speaker: Hachaam

hcxhac06.dialogue: It is a greater blade than Faervian, or so many say. For years after the fall of Myth Drannor, the gold dragons kept it...
hcxhac06.speaker: Hachaam

hcxhac07.dialogue: ...but it was taken by a fell beast, the Demon Rivener. They could not slay the thing, so they sealed it behind the Glyph of Moon, a majuscule first writ by Corellon Larethian himself.
hcxhac07.speaker: Hachaam

hcxhac08.dialogue: But time has weakened the Rivener, or so I believe. And lo! I give you the power to undo the Glyph. Hear now the Rivening Word!
hcxhac08.speaker: Hachaam

hcxhac09.dialogue: The Demon Rivener. A fell beast, who hates all light and love, took a treasure from the gold dragons who had protected it for many years.
hcxhac09.speaker: Hachaam

hcxhac10.dialogue: They chased the Rivener here, but could not defeat it. And so they sealed it deep underneath the Castle, behind the Glyph of Moon, a majuscule first writ by Corellon Larethian himself.
hcxhac10.speaker: Hachaam

hcxhac11.dialogue: The treasure the fiend took? Morvian, which some say is the most powerful of the Baneblades. Ah, it is a thing of beauty, to be sure!
hcxhac11.speaker: Hachaam

hcxhac12.dialogue: And it is time that someone undid the Glyph, and confronted the Rivener, and took Morvian to hand once again. So behold! I teach you the Rivening Word!
hcxhac12.speaker: Hachaam

hcxhac15.dialogue: Ah you fools... beware the Rivener...
hcxhac15.speaker: Hachaam

hcxhac16.dialogue: Behold, I curse you now with the Rivening Word.
hcxhac16.speaker: Hachaam

hcxdma01.dialogue: The ghost opens his mouth, and Ffrakun, a Word of Power, leaps forth.
hcxdma01.speaker: dm

hcxhac18.dialogue: May it serve you as you deserve.
hcxhac18.speaker: Hachaam

hcxhac19.dialogue: Use it with care, when you find the circle surrounded by 4 blades, the Glyph of Moon.
hcxhac19.speaker: Hachaam

hcxhac24.dialogue: Before you go, I will teach you a Word of Power, the Rivening Word.
hcxhac24.speaker: Hachaam

hcxpro00.dialogue: Tell the ghost you returned his sword
hcxpro00.speaker: Protagonist

hcxpro01.speaker: Protagonist

ha1har02.dialogue: Can ya hear me? Can ya? Aye, I see ya can.
ha1har02.speaker: harldain
ha1har02.desc: spoken, disjointed, half to himself, as if awakening from a bad dream

ha1har03.dialogue: Stiff I be, if a ghost can be stiff...
ha1har03.speaker: harldain
ha1har03.desc: spoken, disjointed, half to himself, as if awakening from a bad dream

ha1har04.dialogue: Too long I been sinking into stone, aye, struggling while ma blood turns to tar and ma thoughts to lead.
ha1har04.speaker: harldain
ha1har04.desc: spoken, disjointed, lapsing back into a bad dream

ha1har08.dialogue: I be falling asleep. And so this House be heading for ruin.
ha1har08.speaker: harldain

ha1har09.dialogue: Wait, wait, it comes back to me now. I have seen ya...
ha1har09.speaker: harldain

ha1har10.dialogue: Aye, I know. It be coming back to me now.
ha1har10.speaker: harldain

ha1har11.dialogue: Doing? I be falling asleep. And so this House be heading for ruin.
ha1har11.speaker: harldain

ha1har12.dialogue: I be tied to this place, ya see. Its stone be my bone, its pump, my heart.
ha1har12.speaker: harldain

ha1har13.dialogue: What goes on inside this House, I be aware of - I feel it, aye, just as I once felt air in my lungs and blood in my veins.
ha1har13.speaker: harldain

ha1har14.dialogue: So I have seen ya and know yar tough mettle, with the arraccats, aye, and the orogs, and the glaveens from the Cult of the Dragon. Ya cleansed the water, ya did. And so I know ya be the ones to bring back the City Spires, or none will.
ha1har14.speaker: harldain

ha1har15.dialogue: Aye, I know, ya young ones, so impatient. Well - if ya want to get going aroun' this city, listen up!
ha1har15.speaker: harldain

ha1har16.dialogue: About the only use that tomfool of a mage ever be. Except the Spires. The Spires be the rarest of the rare - magic that be useful!
ha1har16.speaker: harldain

ha1har17.dialogue: Ya seen the tall Spires here and there in the city, have ya not? And the Orrery, the big tickamatock in the Speculum?
ha1har17.speaker: harldain

ha1har18.dialogue: The Orrery, 'twould use the motion of the planets to move ya between Spires in a twinkling. Ah, 'twas easy to move around then - the Orrery spinning like a top, and children chasing each other from Spire to Spire to Spire, crossing the whole city in the shake of a stick.
ha1har18.speaker: harldain

ha1har19.dialogue: We dwarves carved five stones for the Orrery, beautiful stones - green, blue, red, orange, and white, the colors of the planets.
ha1har19.speaker: harldain

ha1har20.dialogue: But during the Dark Days, we stopped the Orrery, and took out the stone Planets, and bound them in metal. Because, if not bound, the Planets fly back to the Orrery, so strong be the life we carved in them.
ha1har20.speaker: harldain

ha1har22.dialogue: But - maybe ya know this. For one of the Planets be set free recently - aye, Dulumbarzul, the green one, the Planet of Trees. Ya be the ones set it loose, maybe.
ha1har22.speaker: harldain

ha1har23.dialogue: But - maybe ya know this. For one of the Planets be set free recently - aye, Tulimatar, the orange one, the Angry Planet. Ya be the ones set it loose, maybe.
ha1har23.speaker: harldain

ha1har24.dialogue: But - maybe ya know this. For one of the Planets be set free recently - aye, Veelaar, the red one, the Planet of Luck. Ya be the ones set it loose, maybe.
ha1har24.speaker: harldain

ha1har25.dialogue: If ya find any more of these stones, free them from their cages, if ya can. Or bring them here to me. So the Spires may live again.
ha1har25.speaker: harldain

ha1har26.dialogue: If ya find any of these stones, free them from their cages, if ya can. Or bring them here to me. So the Spires may live again.
ha1har26.speaker: harldain

ha1har27.dialogue: I have seen ya carry one of the Planets with ya. Here, I call it forth.
ha1har27.speaker: harldain

ha1har29.dialogue: Now, I break its bonds and...
ha1har29.speaker: harldain

ha1har30.dialogue: ...it flies away to the Orrery! Back to the Speculum, where it belongs!
ha1har30.speaker: harldain

ha1har31.dialogue: If ya find any more of these stones, free them from their cages, if ya can. So the Spires may live again.
ha1har31.speaker: harldain

ha1har33.dialogue: Nothing - unless ya be tired of walking. Free the Planets, and the Spires will make it easy for ya to get from anywhar to anywhar.
ha1har33.speaker: harldain

ha1har35.dialogue: But - maybe ya know this. For two of the Planets be set free recently - aye, Dulumbarzul, the green one, and Tulimatar, the orange one. Ya be the ones set them loose, maybe.
ha1har35.speaker: harldain

ha1har36.dialogue: But - maybe ya know this. For two of the Planets be set free recently - aye, Dulumbarzul, the green one, and Veelaar, the red one. Ya be the ones set them loose, maybe.
ha1har36.speaker: harldain

ha1har37.dialogue: But - maybe ya know this. For two of the Planets be set free recently - aye, Tulimatar, the orange one, and Veelaar, the red one. Ya be the ones set them loose, maybe.
ha1har37.speaker: harldain

ha1har38.dialogue: But - maybe ya know this. For three of the Planets be set free recently - aye, Dulumbarzul, the green one, and Tulimatar, the orange one, and Veelaar, the red one. Ya be the ones set them loose, maybe.
ha1har38.speaker: harldain

ha1har39.dialogue: Ah, 'tis selfish, or maybe not so. I be bound to this place, as I said. What goes on outside these walls, I know nothing of it.
ha1har39.speaker: harldain

ha1har40.dialogue: But if the Orrery runs like tops again, and the Gates open, and the Spires return... Maybe my soul will stretch farther... maybe I will live in my City again.
ha1har40.speaker: harldain

ha1har41.dialogue: Maybe then the part of me I gave to this city will remain here forever... and the part that be Harldain Ironbar will at last join his kin in the Long House of the Dwarves.
ha1har41.speaker: harldain

ha1har42.dialogue: For ya, the Spires will be handy, eh? Ya had enough of walking? For me, they would be peace. Truth be, I grow tired. One day follows another, and I long for sleep.
ha1har42.speaker: harldain

ha1har43.dialogue: Wait now, ya ungrateful glaveen. Ya must receive a gift from me first.
ha1har43.speaker: harldain

ha1har45.dialogue: The last Planet be down in the Catacombs, or so I heard from someone who dwells there.
ha1har45.speaker: harldain

ha1har46.dialogue: At least one of the Planets be down in the Catacombs, or so I heard from someone who dwells there.
ha1har46.speaker: harldain

ha1har47.dialogue: Ya know the Catacombs? The elf warrens under the castle? Of course ya don't. No way to get to 'em now - all the common ways blocked up long ago.
ha1har47.speaker: harldain

ha1har48.dialogue: But there be an old way, eh? To use the Wizard's Torc, and pass through the Circle of Ualair. But to make the Torc work for ya, I must give ya the Starstone.
ha1har48.speaker: harldain

ha1har49.dialogue: But there be an old way, eh? To use the Wizard's Torc, and pass through the Circle of Ualair. And I see ya have the Wizard's Torc with ya, that which be lost all these years!
ha1har49.speaker: harldain

ha1har51.dialogue: 'Tis a neckpiece, a great pondering arc of gold.
ha1har51.speaker: harldain

ha1har52.dialogue: It used to have the power to open the Circle of Ualair, 'til its Starstone was wrenched out. Now it's naught but a ringly slibslab of gold.
ha1har52.speaker: harldain

ha1har55.dialogue: Why, 'tis outside the Speculum, the spiraling circle in the amphitheater - if it not be trampled to dust by the long march of years.
ha1har55.speaker: harldain

ha1har57.dialogue: 'Tis one of Myth Drannor's greatest treasures.
ha1har57.speaker: harldain

ha1har58.dialogue: For the Torc be not complete, ya see. Ualair the Silent wrenched the Starstone from it, so that it be useless to the enemy.
ha1har58.speaker: harldain

ha1har60.dialogue: If the Wizard's Torc be mended, a true heart may stand in the Circle of Ualair, and open a Gate to the catacombs under the Castle.
ha1har60.speaker: harldain

ha1har61.dialogue: No one has used that Gate since the fall of Myth Drannor. It be time someone did, to be bringing light to places dark for too long. And that is why I be giving up the Starstone.
ha1har61.speaker: harldain

ha1har63.dialogue: I will give it, aye, so when ya find the Wizard's Torc ya be able to make it complete, and so ya enter the Catacombs.
ha1har63.speaker: harldain

ha1har66.dialogue: Sirra, I know not. Without the Starstone, it be only a pretty bauble for the neck.
ha1har66.speaker: harldain

ha1har67.dialogue: After the Weeping War it disappeared into the dungeons, where it be gathering dust in some forgotten corner or slavering thing's lair.
ha1har67.speaker: harldain

ha1har71.dialogue: Ah, ya people of flesh and blood, such a hurry ya be in. Hurry all ya like, ya'll be like me anyway. -Here's what ya should know.
ha1har71.speaker: harldain

ha1har72.dialogue: Ya can start up the City Spires if ya free the Planets. Then the Spires can move ya across the City in a wink. Ya know the Orrery Planets, don't ya? Five glowing stones, bound up in metal.
ha1har72.speaker: harldain

ha1har73.dialogue: But one of the Planets be in the Catacombs, eh? Under the castle. And to get down there, ya need to put the Starstone back into the Wizard's Torc.
ha1har73.speaker: harldain

ha1har74.dialogue: But one of the Planets be in the Catacombs, eh? Under the castle. And to get down there, ya need me put the Starstone back into yar Wizard's Torc.
ha1har74.speaker: harldain

ha1har75.dialogue: And then ya use the Wizard's Torc at the Circle of Ualair, right? And that be all.
ha1har75.speaker: harldain

ha1har77.dialogue: So let me have yar treasure, so's I can combine it with one of mine - the Starstone.
ha1har77.speaker: harldain

ha1har78.dialogue: For the Torc be not complete, ya see. Ualair the Silent wrenched the Starstone out from it. He knew the Speculum be lost, but he hoped against hope the Army of Darkness would not take Castle Cormanthor, once the Torc be made useless.
ha1har78.speaker: harldain

ha1har79.dialogue: With the Wizard's Torc complete, a true heart may stand in the Circle of Ualair, and open a Gate to the catacombs under the Castle.
ha1har79.speaker: harldain

ha1har80.dialogue: Why, he be the Grand Mage of Myth Drannor in those dark days before the Fall.
ha1har80.speaker: harldain

ha1har81.dialogue: No one has used that Gate since the fall of Myth Drannor. 'Tis time someone did, and brought light to places that been dark for too long.
ha1har81.speaker: harldain

ha1har82.dialogue: In the Dark Days, after Ualair the Silent plucked it from the Wizard's Torc, aye, he gave it into my keeping. And now thankful will I restore it to its place.
ha1har82.speaker: harldain

ha1har84.dialogue: Aya, goodbye, I'll keep ya no longer.
ha1har84.speaker: harldain

ha1har85.dialogue: Aye, goodbye, I'll leave ya in peace.
ha1har85.speaker: harldain

ha1har86.dialogue: Except to say, I have a collection, eh? Excellent weapons, fine armor - prizes plucked from unlucky travelers, or from the stiff hands of robbers who thought our hoard unguarded.
ha1har86.speaker: harldain

ha1har87.dialogue: For ya, I might be persuaded to part with a piece or two - for a price.
ha1har87.speaker: harldain

ha1har88.dialogue: Well, don't leave without the Starstone! Without it, the Wizard's Torc be naught but a pretty necklace.
ha1har88.speaker: harldain

ha1har89.dialogue: And see me also about my collection. Excellent weapons, fine armor... for ya, I be persuaded maybe to let go a piece or two - for a price.
ha1har89.speaker: harldain

ha1har90.dialogue: First, I must tell ya, I have a collection, eh? Excellent weapons, fine armor - prizes plucked from unlucky travelers, or from the stiff hands of robbers who thought our hoard unguarded.
ha1har90.speaker: harldain

ha1har92.dialogue: For ya, I be persuaded maybe to part with a piece or two - for a price.
ha1har92.speaker: harldain

ha1har94.dialogue: Now here be the Starstone. Keep it well, until ya find the Wizard's Torc, so the Starstone can make it whole again.
ha1har94.speaker: harldain

ha1har95.dialogue: Now I take the Wizard's Torc and tap in the Starstone, where it belongs.
ha1har95.speaker: harldain

ha1har96.dialogue: There! With this, ya can enter the Circle of Ualair the Silent, and open the Gate to the Catacombs.
ha1har96.speaker: harldain

ha1hara0.dialogue: Find the slot just inside the doorway, aye, and put the Passkey in. The traps will fall silent, and ya be safe crossing the hall.
ha1hara0.speaker: harldain

ha1hara1.dialogue: When ya want to turn the traps on again, put the Passkey back into the slot. Then beware! Traps be deadly once again.
ha1hara1.speaker: harldain

ha1hara2.dialogue: That pool, that foul cess that erupted by my pumphouse. It be like a fell hand squeezing the life out of my heart.
ha1hara2.speaker: harldain

ha1hara3.dialogue: I thank ya for removing it, and cleansing the city water, aye, I thank ya most warmly.
ha1hara3.speaker: harldain

ha1hara4.dialogue: Aya, there be a Passkey around here somewhere, turns the traps off. There not be a reason to use it for over a hundred years.
ha1hara4.speaker: harldain

ha1hara5.dialogue: Devilish, the traps! Aye! We employed the services of Kilgorash the Cunning, a kobold lord. Yes, even kobolds be living peacefully in Myth Drannor, before the Dark Days came.
ha1hara5.speaker: harldain

ha1hara6.dialogue: This be the Onaglym, the House of Gems. Huge wealth we dwarves held here in our hoard - and one day will hold again. The traps be always standing guard over that wealth.
ha1hara6.speaker: harldain

ha1hara7.dialogue: Sadly depleted, aye, ransack and ruin! But I be building it up, so one day my kin be led back to Myth Drannor - if not by their beards of honor, then by their greedy noses!
ha1hara7.speaker: harldain

ha1hara8.dialogue: Aye, I know it well! I be aware of everything that happens here in the House of Gems. But I be caught, as ya know, by the foul Pool, and could not come to your aid.
ha1hara8.speaker: harldain

ha1hara9.dialogue: Ah - a joke! As if I be telling you where the hoard lay! Ho ho! The fabulous Hoard of the Onaglym Dwarves, which thousands have sought at the cost of their lives! Ho ho ho ho ho!
ha1hara9.speaker: harldain

ha1harb0.dialogue: 'Tis a device that shows how the planets move in the sky. The mages use them to harness celestial motion, or some such fool notion.
ha1harb0.speaker: harldain

ha1harb1.dialogue: Once I knew every stone and slab of this city. But then the wars came, and I died, and helpless I am, cursed ya might say, to watch others tumble my great works into folly, ay, folly and ruin.
ha1harb1.speaker: harldain

ha1harb2.dialogue: Pool of Radiance? I know naught about it, except that 'tis another plague conjured up by tomfool mages, aye, who brew naught but trouble always for the solid folk of the earth.
ha1harb2.speaker: harldain

ha1harb3.dialogue: Ah! Now there be a spell even a dwarf finds beautiful - an ancient protective spell that be woven into stone and spire, rock and road of this city.
ha1harb3.speaker: harldain

ha1harb4.dialogue: We dwarves played a proud part in its creation - for we cut and polished the Gems of the Weave, the huge precious stones that allow mortals to touch the Mythal's mighty magic.
ha1harb4.speaker: harldain

ha1harb5.dialogue: But lately it seems to me that the Mythal falters, aye, or goes astray. Maybe the current Gem be taken, or maybe no guardian be left to guide the Mythal.
ha1harb5.speaker: harldain

ha1harb7.dialogue: Aye, Mystra be a goddess much beloved by the people of this city, at one time. And kind to dwarves, I may add, though few dwarves loved her.
ha1harb7.speaker: harldain

ha1harb8.dialogue: She cries out for her followers, ya say? I know not where her followers may be.
ha1harb8.speaker: harldain

ha1harc0.dialogue: The building ya speak of be a shrine to Mystra. The lady Anorrweyn, a fair elf - she be priestess there when I were alive.
ha1harc0.speaker: harldain

ha1harc1.dialogue: Whatever aid ya can lend her, ya should do.
ha1harc1.speaker: harldain

ha1harc6.dialogue: They entered my House about a fortnight ago. By then, the slowness was upon me, and naught I could do - naught but smile when I felt the traps go off!
ha1harc6.speaker: harldain

ha1harc7.dialogue: But then they be moving into the tower, and sitting longtimes in the Room of Words. Until ya came and taught them what swords and spells be for!
ha1harc7.speaker: harldain

ha1harc8.dialogue: Now I feels the rude boots of orog, trampin' up and down my Round Tower, aye, even as we speak.
ha1harc8.speaker: harldain

ha1harc9.dialogue: I do not know why I linger here, when all my kith and kin entered the Long House years ago. The folly of some wizard, or the cruel whim of some human god, aye, no doubt.
ha1harc9.speaker: harldain

ha1pro39.speaker: Protagonist

ha2har05.dialogue: By the Beard! Ya found one of the Orrery's Planets, and ya carried it here. By yar leave, I call it forth, to ma hand.
ha2har05.speaker: harldain

ha2har07.dialogue: Well! Ya have been busy, or so I have heard.
ha2har07.speaker: harldain

ha2har08.dialogue: Anorrweyn came to visit me. She told me of yar exploits, aye, and our great need for a new Gem of the Weave.
ha2har08.speaker: harldain

ha2har09.dialogue: A Cult Mage fell into one of my traps, ya see, and told me much before he died.
ha2har09.speaker: harldain

ha2har10.dialogue: Well! By the Beard! Ya have been busy!
ha2har10.speaker: harldain

ha2har11.dialogue: I see ya carry an Orrery Planet. And the elf-lady Anorrweyn came to me, aye, and told me ya'd be here, seeking a new Gem of the Weave.
ha2har11.speaker: harldain

ha2har12.dialogue: I see ya carry an Orrery Planet. And a Cult Mage fell into one of my traps, and told me much before he died, aye, about the Baelnorn and his Gem.
ha2har12.speaker: harldain

ha2har13.dialogue: But first, yar Orrery Planet! With yar leave, I call it forth to my hand.
ha2har13.speaker: harldain

ha2har16.dialogue: I break the iron bands and...
ha2har16.speaker: harldain

ha2har18.dialogue: ...it flies away to the Orrery! Back to the Speculum, where it belongs!
ha2har18.speaker: harldain

ha2har19.dialogue: ...it flies away to the Orrery, to join the others ya released.
ha2har19.speaker: harldain

ha2har20.dialogue: Aye, ya done well. By my count, ya but need to free one more, and then the Spires will live again!
ha2har20.speaker: harldain

ha2har21.dialogue: If ya find any more of these stones, free them from their cages, if ya can. So the Spires may live again.
ha2har21.speaker: harldain

ha2har23.dialogue: Why, that stone ya carried be one of the Planets, belongs in the Great Orrery in the Speculum. I be telling you about it earlier.
ha2har23.speaker: harldain

ha2har24.dialogue: We took them from the Orrery back during the Weeping Wars, because the foe be using the Spires to invade the City.
ha2har24.speaker: harldain

ha2har25.dialogue: We bound the Planets in metal, lest they fly back on their own to whar they belong. When I took off the binding, that's what it did, aye - flew back to the Orrery.
ha2har25.speaker: harldain

ha2har27.dialogue: Then there be three others out there somewheres, waiting for ya to release them as well.
ha2har27.speaker: harldain

ha2har28.dialogue: Then there be two others out there somewheres, waiting for ya to release them as well.
ha2har28.speaker: harldain

ha2har29.dialogue: Be ya walking up to any Spire, ya can command it, aye, and so ya travel to any other Spire in the wink of an eye.
ha2har29.speaker: harldain

ha2har30.dialogue: She be a water spirit. She dwelt in this area long before our kind raised a City here, and like as not, when its last spire crumbles, she be here still.
ha2har30.speaker: harldain

ha2har31.dialogue: A frivolous creature, but by the Father! She made beautiful music in our fountains and pools, once upon a time.
ha2har31.speaker: harldain

ha2har33.dialogue: Aye, the Red Planet, Veelaar, it be seen once in a high tower of the Castle - but none can get up there now but flying creatures.
ha2har33.speaker: harldain

ha2har34.dialogue: Aye, Plinshree - ya know Plinshree, the water nymph? She be telling me she saw something like the White Planet, Sash-pulim, down in the catacombs.
ha2har34.speaker: harldain

ha2har35.dialogue: Aye, Plinshree - ya know Plinshree, the water nymph? She be telling me she saw something like the Orange Planet, Tulimatar, in the village of the lizard-men.
ha2har35.speaker: harldain

ha2har36.dialogue: Aye, Plinshree - ya know Plinshree, the water nymph? She be telling me she saw something like the Green Planet, Dulumbarzul, over in the marshes.
ha2har36.speaker: harldain

ha2har38.dialogue: Now ya best be about yar business.
ha2har38.speaker: harldain

ha2har39.dialogue: Farewell, and may your beard grow long.
ha2har39.speaker: harldain

ha2har41.dialogue: I can feel it... the Spires are coming alive. All over this part of the City.
ha2har41.speaker: harldain

ha2har42.dialogue: Ah, glaveens, ya have done it. Now my spirit can travel beyond this old House. And ya can use the Spires to get all around the City in the wink of an eye!
ha2har42.speaker: harldain

ha2har43.dialogue: Aye, 'tis a marvel, such a marvel that I can hardly speak. Thank ya, aye, thank ya most warmly.
ha2har43.speaker: harldain

ha2har44.dialogue: Now must we talk on matters more grave - the new Gem of the Weave.
ha2har44.speaker: harldain

ha2har45.dialogue: From what that Cult Mage said, ya know we need a new Gem of the Weave, and quickly.
ha2har45.speaker: harldain

ha2har46.dialogue: Anorrweyn told me how greatly we need it.
ha2har46.speaker: harldain

ha2har47.dialogue: So I be about to do something I swore I never - giving up one of the keys to the Hoard of the Onaglym Dwarves.
ha2har47.speaker: harldain
ha2har47.desc: spoken, brisk, this is a huge honor

ha2har48.dialogue: You must go out into the open air, into the courtyard of the House of Gems.
ha2har48.speaker: harldain

ha2har49.dialogue: There be a statue out in the middle of the courtyard - or rather I say, the statue be gone, but the pedestal remains...
ha2har49.speaker: harldain

ha2har50.dialogue: There be a hole in that pedestal. That be whar ya use the key I give ya.
ha2har50.speaker: harldain

ha2har53.dialogue: I be giving ya the Emerald of the Weave - a great green gem, aye, flawless and dazzling.
ha2har53.speaker: harldain

ha2har55.dialogue: It be large, eh? This be but one of the keys to the Hoard, aye, and ya shall but glimpse the treasures I have locked away.
ha2har55.speaker: harldain

ha2har56.dialogue: I hoard them so that someday, when my kin return to rebuild this City, they may find them of use.
ha2har56.speaker: harldain

ha2har58.dialogue: Bear it to the top of the Speculum, aye, to the top of the dragon's back, and lay it upon the spines.
ha2har58.speaker: harldain

ha2har59.dialogue: The Emerald must be made into the Gem of the Weave. For that, ya need not only the Gem, but one who will be bound to it. Aye, but who among you can be sacrificed to that spell?
ha2har59.speaker: harldain

ha2har60.dialogue: For the Gem requires a Communicant, one tied forever to the Mythal. A powerful priest or mage, or else the joining will destroy you.
ha2har60.speaker: harldain

ha2har61.dialogue: In the glory days, people would rush to take the honor! A Tyryl Wizard, maybe, or one of the Dweomerkeepers of Mystra. But now, after the Fall... I wonder if anyone suitable be left alive.
ha2har61.speaker: harldain

ha2har63.dialogue: So that is why you must go back to the lady Anorrweyn, and free her. She must be your Communicant - there be no other.
ha2har63.speaker: harldain

ha2har64.dialogue: So that is why you must go back to the lady Anorrweyn, and plead your case. She must be your Communicant - there be no other.
ha2har64.speaker: harldain

ha2har65.dialogue: The key be a device called a Tumblebar. It be shafts of iron linked with bits of chain - aye, a strange and cunning contrivance indeed.
ha2har65.speaker: harldain

ha2har66.dialogue: There be a statue out in the courtyard of this House. Or rather, the statue be gone, but the pedestal remains...
ha2har66.speaker: harldain

ha2har67.dialogue: Put the Tumblebar into the pedestal - ya'll find a hole atween two stones. 'Twill go all the way in - and what was hidden will be revealed.
ha2har67.speaker: harldain

ha2har68.dialogue: Be ya thinking of any more questions for me, afore I give ya the Tumblebar?
ha2har68.speaker: harldain

ha2har70.dialogue: They would do just as you! Their High Mage would attune the Gem to herself, aye! And if she be not killed, she be able to sway the Mythal.
ha2har70.speaker: harldain

ha2har71.dialogue: But she would not restore it to good, eh? She would take its powers and twist them to evil. So hold fast to the Emerald of the Weave!
ha2har71.speaker: harldain

ha2har72.dialogue: I be no a wizard, for which I eternally thank the All-Father, but even I can tell that it be fading - or worse, be falling under someone's sway.
ha2har72.speaker: harldain

ha2har74.dialogue: I know not, aye, I do not truck in talismans of death. It be not in this House, nowhere around here, that's all say I.
ha2har74.speaker: harldain

ha2har76.dialogue: Nay, I have not. The Cult of the Dragon has sent warriors against me, aye, more trap-fodder, but naught of their wizardly kitkob was worthy of the Hoard.
ha2har76.speaker: harldain

ha2har80.dialogue: Hark now, I be forgetting to tell you of Plinshree.
ha2har80.speaker: harldain

ha2har81.dialogue: I know the naiad right well, for 'twas I who built the water system in this city. She be a flighty creature, none worse, but become dear to me even so.
ha2har81.speaker: harldain

ha2har82.dialogue: 'Tis a sorrow ya did not find her waterbells, for by the Bearded Lady! they make a pretty music.
ha2har82.speaker: harldain

ha2har83.dialogue: 'Tis a sorrow ya did not give her the waterbells you found, for by the Bearded Lady! they made a pretty music. Can ya not find a fountain or a well and lighten your load?
ha2har83.speaker: harldain

ha2har84.dialogue: Ah, 'tis joy that ya gave her some of the waterbells back! 'Tis sorrow that she does not have all of them, for by the Bearded Lady, they make a pretty music!
ha2har84.speaker: harldain

ha2har85.dialogue: 'Tis great joy that ya gave her the waterbells back! Did ya hear them? By the Bearded Lady, they make a pretty music!
ha2har85.speaker: harldain

ha2har87.dialogue: Why, Anorrweyn, as I told ya, and the water spirit, Plinshree...
ha2har87.speaker: harldain

ha2har88.dialogue: The water spirit, Plinshree, she talks me from out the water...
ha2har88.speaker: harldain

ha2har89.dialogue: ...and the Cult be sending two or three dozen warriors, aye, but they never stay for long. They be wonderfully stupid about traps!
ha2har89.speaker: harldain

ha2har90.dialogue: Ah! Some times ago, a rogue be creeping through. Ha, he were a shifty one, not a trap sprung on him, no sirrah.
ha2har90.speaker: harldain

ha2har91.dialogue: But neither did he find much treasure, so off he crept again.
ha2har91.speaker: harldain

ha2har93.dialogue: And the pesky gargoyles be flocking in the garden again. I think that be all.
ha2har93.speaker: harldain

ha2har94.dialogue: Aye, ya be ready. The Gem be one of our most precious treasures! Do not let the Cult get ahold it, or the Mythal be lost to us forever!
ha2har94.speaker: harldain

ha2har95.dialogue: But I talk overlong, and of trifles. Ya must be on your way.
ha2har95.speaker: harldain

ha2har97.dialogue: Now here be the Tumblebar. Keep it well, and use it as I told you.
ha2har97.speaker: harldain

ja1jar03.dialogue: Stop! Stop please, all of you, and ponder this riddle...
ja1jar03.speaker: jarial

ja1jar04.dialogue: A quest of love / Ends with me, / Yet I am made / Endlessly. / If I drop, / I say my name, / If I touch rock, / Freedom gain.
ja1jar04.speaker: jarial

ja1jar05.dialogue: What is the answer? Solve it, I beg you, and set me free!
ja1jar05.speaker: jarial

ja1jar06.dialogue: I simply cannot figure it out.
ja1jar06.speaker: jarial
ja1jar06.desc: spoken, at the end of his rope

ja1jar07.dialogue: Hmmm... something must touch the rock. But what?
ja1jar07.speaker: jarial

ja1jar10.dialogue: Free me from this living tomb, and I will fight fearlessly at your side.
ja1jar10.speaker: jarial

ja1jar11.dialogue: Ahhgh! Please! Come back soon! Free me from this living tomb, and I will fight fearlessly at your side.
ja1jar11.speaker: jarial

ja1jar13.dialogue: Oh, you are the ones those scarred mages were talking about.
ja1jar13.speaker: jarial

ja1jar14.dialogue: You've probably seen them - the ones wearing red cloaks?
ja1jar14.speaker: jarial

ja1jar15.dialogue: They mentioned a group of adventurers from New Phlan.
ja1jar15.speaker: jarial

ja1jar16.dialogue: They are newcomers. I'd never seen one until recently.
ja1jar16.speaker: jarial

ja1jar17.dialogue: Exactly how recently, I can't tell you. I have a very poor sense of time.
ja1jar17.speaker: jarial

ja1jar18.dialogue: They asked if I had seen a group of adventurers from Phlan.
ja1jar18.speaker: jarial

ja1jar19.dialogue: But they had been cruel to me earlier, so I told them nothing.
ja1jar19.speaker: jarial

ja1jar20.dialogue: Also, I did not like the look in their eye.
ja1jar20.speaker: jarial

ja1jar21.dialogue: Perhaps the scarred mages found them after all.
ja1jar21.speaker: jarial

ja1jar23.dialogue: Ozama is - was - my lover. We came to Myth Drannor together, adventuring.
ja1jar23.speaker: jarial

ja1jar24.dialogue: Her conjuring was a sight to behold - so fluid and beautiful, with her violet eyes blazing.
ja1jar24.speaker: jarial

ja1jar25.dialogue: But she had a blinding temper. And so did I, at that time.
ja1jar25.speaker: jarial

ja1jar26.dialogue: I was jealous of her skill. I said something very cruel...
ja1jar26.speaker: jarial

ja1jar27.dialogue: ...and in return she spat out a spell and dropped a pebble at my feet. And the boulder grew around me.
ja1jar27.speaker: jarial

ja1jar28.dialogue: Ozama spoke it, before she left me. Perhaps she meant it as a kindness, to give me a chance to free myself, but it has been nothing but torment.
ja1jar28.speaker: jarial

ja1jar29.dialogue: There is little more to tell. She continued adventuring, and I never saw her again.
ja1jar29.speaker: jarial

ja1jar30.dialogue: Before she left, she spoke the riddle to me.
ja1jar30.speaker: jarial

ja1jar31.dialogue: You will say I am crazy, but I believe she intended to come back and release me.
ja1jar31.speaker: jarial

ja1jar32.dialogue: I am afraid she is dead, and I mourn her.
ja1jar32.speaker: jarial

ja1jar33.dialogue: Now, please, let us speak of something else.
ja1jar33.speaker: jarial

ja1jarZA.dialogue: She went off to the northeast part of the Main Halls. We had talked to a friendly voice there, who called himself Preybelish.
ja1jarZA.speaker: jarial

ja1jarZB.dialogue: He had a necklace she thought she might buy.
ja1jarZB.speaker: jarial

ja1jar34.dialogue: If it can be solved, I can be a free man again.
ja1jar34.speaker: jarial

ja1jar35.dialogue: And my sorcery will serve the clever soul who found the answer.
ja1jar35.speaker: jarial

ja1jar36.dialogue: Oh, everything and everybody evil passes by here eventually.
ja1jar36.speaker: jarial

ja1jar37.dialogue: Phaerrim and alhoon, beholders, orcs of course, margoyles and arraccat...
ja1jar37.speaker: jarial

ja1jar38.dialogue: There was a dark naga who was fond of riddles. He and I actually became quite friendly for a while.
ja1jar38.speaker: jarial

ja1jar39.dialogue: The undead are the worst. Sometimes they claw at me for weeks.
ja1jar39.speaker: jarial

ja1jar40.dialogue: Let this stone be a lesson to you - never scorn the love of a mage!
ja1jar40.speaker: jarial

ja1jar41.dialogue: I offended the wizard Ozama, and she gave me this stone prison in reply.
ja1jar41.speaker: jarial

ja1jar42.dialogue: Ten hundred times I have wished Ozama dropped the stone on my head instead.
ja1jar42.speaker: jarial

ja1jar43.dialogue: Yet, Ilmater help me, I love her still.
ja1jar43.speaker: jarial

ja1jar44.dialogue: Oh, this cursed boulder protects me utterly. That's the evil genius of it.
ja1jar44.speaker: jarial

ja1jar45.dialogue: I had a beholder try to kill me once. It threw spells for a week. What patience!
ja1jar45.speaker: jarial

ja1jar46.dialogue: It shed tears when it finally had to give up.
ja1jar46.speaker: jarial

ja1jar47.dialogue: Oh, the answer is not a word. I can assure you of that.
ja1jar47.speaker: jarial

ja1jar48.dialogue: I've been in this rock for many years. I've spoken every word there is, tried every spell I know.
ja1jar48.speaker: jarial

ja1jar49.dialogue: To solve the riddle, speaking isn't enough. You have to DO something, I'm sure of it.
ja1jar49.speaker: jarial

ja1jar50.dialogue: Tell me, travelers, what news from Phlan?
ja1jar50.speaker: jarial

ja1jar51.dialogue: Well, that is dire news, and no mistake. I wish I could help you.
ja1jar51.speaker: jarial

ja1jar52.dialogue: Zhentil Keep is where I grew up, and learned the wizard arts.
ja1jar52.speaker: jarial

ja1jar53.dialogue: But that is a long time ago. Now I think of myself as a citizen of Myth Drannor.
ja1jar53.speaker: jarial

ja1jar54.dialogue: Aaaagh! What is the answer to Ozama's riddle? It's driving me mad.
ja1jar54.speaker: jarial

ja1jar55.dialogue: Friends, I have said enough. Now it is up to you.
ja1jar55.speaker: jarial

ja1jarYA.speaker: jarial

ja2jar02.dialogue: You can't believe how good that feels.
ja2jar02.speaker: jarial

ja2jar03.dialogue: Just to be able to reach the floor - what joy! Thank you ten hundred times.
ja2jar03.speaker: jarial

ja2jar06.dialogue: I am eager to see the world again. May I travel with you? I will gladly take the place of someone in your party.
ja2jar06.speaker: jarial

ja2jar07.dialogue: I am eager to see the world again. May I travel with you?
ja2jar07.speaker: jarial

ja2jar08.dialogue: When you have decided who is to stay behind, I will join you.
ja2jar08.speaker: jarial

ja2jar09.dialogue: Lead on then! Show me the way to this Pool of Radiance!
ja2jar09.speaker: jarial

ja2jar10.dialogue: Ah, to be adventuring once more!
ja2jar10.speaker: jarial

ja2jar11.dialogue: I will obey your wishes. Tell me, do you know a safe place I might go, and maybe meet you again?
ja2jar11.speaker: jarial

ja2jar12.dialogue: But you are few, and the danger is great! Either you are very brave, or very foolish. Will you reconsider?
ja2jar12.speaker: jarial

ja2jar13.dialogue: I think I can get there. Maybe they can use my help.
ja2jar13.speaker: jarial

ja2jar14.dialogue: I have met Nottle before. He will be amazed to see me, ha ha!
ja2jar14.speaker: jarial

ja2jar15.dialogue: I will make my own way, then.
ja2jar15.speaker: jarial

ja2jar16.dialogue: I am a sorcerer of above-average ability. I know a missile spell, an armoring spell, a protection spell - and minor cantrips, of course.
ja2jar16.speaker: jarial

ja2jar17.dialogue: My possessions are meager - a dagger, a crooked staff, a sling, and a thick cloak.
ja2jar17.speaker: jarial

ja2jar18.dialogue: I have a stout heart, my mind is keen, and I will not fail you in courage or in judgment.
ja2jar18.speaker: jarial

ja2jar19.dialogue: Your ambition is great! Azuth help me, I see I am doomed to die young.
ja2jar19.speaker: jarial

ja2jar20.dialogue: But at least I will die in good company, if you will have me.
ja2jar20.speaker: jarial

ja2jar21.dialogue: Walk in Azuth's sight, until we meet again.
ja2jar21.speaker: jarial

ja2pro01.dialogue: Tell him he might join later
ja2pro01.speaker: Protagonist

ja2pro02.speaker: Protagonist

ja2pro04.dialogue: Warn him that you seek a Pool of Radiance
ja2pro04.speaker: Protagonist

ja4jar01.dialogue: I must say - I am worried. Very worried.
ja4jar01.speaker: Jarial

ja4jar02.dialogue: When we defeated Kya Mordrayn, she didn't die. She was - taken. Eaten, if you will.
ja4jar02.speaker: Jarial

ja4jar03.dialogue: When you defeated Kya Mordrayn, she didn't die. She was - taken. Eaten, if you will. The stir of magics was incredible!
ja4jar03.speaker: Jarial

ja4jar04.dialogue: I am afraid something has been fed. Something terrible. Now it sleeps, but - someday - somewhere - the cycle of evil will begin all over again.
ja4jar04.speaker: Jarial

ja4jar05.dialogue: Your numbers are not great. Will you not take me into your company? Then we can face together whatever evil may come!
ja4jar05.speaker: Jarial

ja4jar06.dialogue: But for now, the city is yours! Can you feel it? The Mythal is alive again, with strength it hasn't shown since the fall of Myth Drannor.

ke1kel03.dialogue: Trust me, sister. They are not.
ke1kel03.speaker: kellan

ke1bro01.dialogue: We shall see. Behold the Shrine of the Silver Fire! Let the followers of Sammaster Madfool flee its holy flame!
ke1bro01.speaker: Bronwyn
ke1bro01.desc: spoken, tense, spoken loud as a challenge

ke1kel04.dialogue: See? It is as I told you. If they were Cult, they would not ask!
ke1kel04.speaker: kellan

ke1bro02.dialogue: You are right, Kellan. -Forgive us our wary ways, strangers. Since we came to Myth Drannor, we have met nothing but enemies.
ke1bro02.speaker: Bronwyn

ke1bro03.dialogue: You asked about the Silver Fire. It is a Sisterhood dedicated to the dismay, downfall and destruction of the Cult of the Dragon.
ke1bro03.speaker: Bronwyn

ke1bro04.dialogue: You asked about Sammaster. If you do not know him, you know his work - for it was he that betrayed Mystra's trust and founded the deadly Cult of the Dragon.
ke1bro04.speaker: Bronwyn

ke1bro05.dialogue: You wondered who we are. We are Sisters of the Silver Fire, devoted to the dismay, downfall and destruction of the Cult of the Dragon.
ke1bro05.speaker: Bronwyn

ke1bro06.dialogue: We have reason to believe the Cult is brewing evil in Myth Drannor, and we have come to stop it.
ke1bro06.speaker: Bronwyn

ke1bro07.dialogue: But our party was nearly destroyed, and we found our Shrine abandoned by its guardians -
ke1bro07.speaker: Bronwyn

ke1kel10.dialogue: - so we idle here, struggling to keep its flame alive while our enemy grows stronger by the hour.
ke1kel10.speaker: kellan

ke1kel12.dialogue: If the Cult knew where we were, you would be standing in a smoking ruin.
ke1kel12.speaker: kellan

ke1bro08.dialogue: We were sent to Myth Drannor by the incantrix Fieryat Ildacer, one of the Seven of the Sisterhood of Silver Fire, to destroy a dracolich named Pelendralaar.
ke1bro08.speaker: Bronwyn

ke1kel15.dialogue: There were twelve of us then.
ke1kel15.speaker: kellan

ke1bro09.dialogue: What the Sisterhood did not know is that Pelendralaar had been joined by a Cult mage of great power - I do not know her name.
ke1bro09.speaker: Bronwyn

ke1bro10.dialogue: We found the Cult guarding a creature called the Baelnorn. We attempted to free him...
ke1bro10.speaker: Bronwyn

ke1kel16.dialogue: Thus to make us thirteen in number. That was ill-fated!
ke1kel16.speaker: kellan

ke1bro11.dialogue: Many mages were there to oppose us. Our group was swept apart in a fury of magic, and I fear all the others have been destroyed.
ke1bro11.speaker: Bronwyn

ke1kel19.dialogue: Aye, we know where he is, only too well.
ke1kel19.speaker: kellan

ke1bro12.dialogue: Much deeper in these catacombs, you will find great doors with an elven rune before them. The Baelnorn is somewhere beyond those doors, held in force by the Cult.
ke1bro12.speaker: Bronwyn

ke1bro13.dialogue: But you can't get there now. The way is sealed with a Glyph...
ke1bro13.speaker: Bronwyn

ke1kel21.dialogue: It is the Glyph of Safekeeping. I do not know the Word that unseals it.
ke1kel21.speaker: kellan

ke1bro14.dialogue: Think carefully before you broach those doors! For such an affront is sure to arouse the full fury of the Cult.
ke1bro14.speaker: Bronwyn

ke1bro15.dialogue: It must be a talisman of great power. Such a thing would be in the lair of some creature - if it has not already fallen into the hands of the Cult.
ke1bro15.speaker: Bronwyn

ke1bro16.dialogue: Since it is beloved of Mystra, we would gladly help you look for it - but we must stay here until its guardians return, or the Silver Fire will fail.
ke1bro16.speaker: Bronwyn

ke1bro17.dialogue: We do not know who they may be. They were gone when we stumbled in here, and the Silver Fire nearly dead.
ke1bro17.speaker: Bronwyn

ke1bro18.dialogue: Because the flame was not dead, I think maybe they are still alive.
ke1bro18.speaker: Bronwyn

ke1bro19.dialogue: So we are trapped very nicely! We cannot go and look for the guardians, for fear the Shrine will fail while we are gone!
ke1bro19.speaker: Bronwyn

ke1kel27.dialogue: Yet neither can we stay here! This Shrine will not stand a minute against the black fury of the Cult.
ke1kel27.speaker: kellan

ke1bro20.dialogue: If you meet the guardians, or any of our Sisterhood, bid them return here to us! For we wish to make war on the Cult, as we came here to do...
ke1bro20.speaker: Bronwyn

ke1bro21.dialogue: ...but we cannot, for we dare not leave this Shrine untended.
ke1bro21.speaker: Bronwyn

ke1bro22.dialogue: That would explain how well equipped you are! Spoils from your war on those evildoers.
ke1bro22.speaker: Bronwyn

ke1kel34.dialogue: Would that we could go with you! Rather than languishing here.
ke1kel34.speaker: kellan

ke1kel35.dialogue: If that is true, you will take me into your company!
ke1kel35.speaker: kellan

ke1bro23.dialogue: Kellan! -You must forgive my companion. Her speech can be rough -
ke1bro23.speaker: Bronwyn

ke1kel37.dialogue: Aye, because I grew up in the Cult, and their ways are not gentle -
ke1kel37.speaker: kellan

ke1bro24.dialogue: But that is behind us now. It is true - she languishes here -
ke1bro24.speaker: Bronwyn

ke1kel38.dialogue: Languish! Say rather I am going mad.
ke1kel38.speaker: kellan

ke1kel39.dialogue: Take me into your company, and I will tell you about our enemy. For it is true - I walked with Dragon-love in my heart for years and years, and so I know their ways.
ke1kel39.speaker: kellan

ke1bro25.dialogue: You cannot join their company now, Kellan. You must stay here. Now calm yourself, and let the travelers speak.
ke1bro25.speaker: Bronwyn

ke1bro26.dialogue: You cannot join their company now, Kellan. You must stay here. -Travelers, I think our conversation is at an end.
ke1bro26.speaker: Bronwyn

ke1kel43.dialogue: Aaaagh - I cannot stand it! You who wave your fine weapons and strut in your armor. Take me into your company! For I rot here, waiting.
ke1kel43.speaker: kellan

ke1kel44.dialogue: I do not need your service! I need to become one of your company.
ke1kel44.speaker: kellan

ke1bro27.dialogue: Well, that makes it clear that you are not with the Cult.
ke1bro27.speaker: Bronwyn

ke1kel46.dialogue: Aye - they do not ask for leave, they take what they want.
ke1kel46.speaker: kellan

ke1bro28.dialogue: Farewell, friends. If you meet any of our Sisterhood, bid them return here to us! For we wish to make war on the Cult, as we came here to do...
ke1bro28.speaker: Bronwyn

ke1bro29.dialogue: ...but we cannot, for we dare not leave this Shrine untended.
ke1bro29.speaker: Bronwyn

ke1bro30.dialogue: Farewell, friends. If you meet the guardians, or any of our Sisterhood, bid them return here to us! For we wish to make war on the Cult, as we came here to do...
ke1bro30.speaker: Bronwyn

ke1bro31.dialogue: ...but we cannot, for we dare not leave this Shrine untended.
ke1bro31.speaker: Bronwyn

ke1bro32.dialogue: Farewell. I hope we may meet again!
ke1bro32.speaker: Bronwyn

ke1pro02.speaker: Protagonist

ke1pro04.speaker: Protagonist

ke1pro05.dialogue: Ask who the Shrine's guardians are
ke1pro05.speaker: Protagonist

ke1pro06.dialogue: Ask if the Cult knows about this shrine
ke1pro06.speaker: Protagonist

ke1pro07.dialogue: Ask them how they came to be here
ke1pro07.speaker: Protagonist

ke1pro08.dialogue: Ask them where the Baelnorn is
ke1pro08.speaker: Protagonist

ke1pro09.dialogue: Tell them you seek Anorrweyn's skull
ke1pro09.speaker: Protagonist

ke1pro11.dialogue: Take your leave of the Sisters
ke1pro11.speaker: Protagonist

ke2bro00.dialogue: What do you think, Kellan? They do not look so timid to me.
ke2bro00.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2bro01.dialogue: The trader Nottle was just here, and he said that about you.
ke2bro01.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2kel05.dialogue: He also said he was your friend. But maybe he is everyone's friend - and no one's.
ke2kel05.speaker: kellan

ke2bro02.dialogue: Do not worry! The guardians told us of your bravery.
ke2bro02.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2bro03.dialogue: So we sent old Nottle hurrying on his way.
ke2bro03.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2kel06.dialogue: Yes, his backside is just the right height for kicking.
ke2kel06.speaker: kellan

ke2kel07.dialogue: Hold a moment! Don't you know where you are?
ke2kel07.speaker: kellan

ke2kel08.dialogue: This is the Shrine of the Silver Fire. The nagas are its guardians - you set them free, or so I hear...
ke2kel08.speaker: kellan

ke2bro04.dialogue: And we are Sisters of the Silver Fire, friends to any and all that seek to destroy the Cult of the Dragon. For that is our sworn purpose.
ke2bro04.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2bro05.dialogue: Bide a moment with us - you are among friends.
ke2bro05.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2bro06.dialogue: Why, we are Sisters of the Silver Fire, friends to any and all that seek to destroy the Cult of the Dragon.
ke2bro06.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2kel10.dialogue: And this is the Shrine of the Silver Fire. The nagas are its guardians - you set them free, or so they tell us.
ke2kel10.speaker: kellan

ke2bro07.dialogue: Bide a moment with us - you are among friends.
ke2bro07.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2bro08.dialogue: He came here seeking refuge - and to pitch his wares, of course.
ke2bro08.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2bro09.dialogue: This is the Shrine of the Silver Fire - a sanctuary for all who oppose the Cult of the Dragon.
ke2bro09.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2kel12.dialogue: But Nottle Trinketmaster is no enemy of the Cult! He will sell anything to anyone... the grasping skeesicks...
ke2kel12.speaker: kellan

ke2bro10.dialogue: Foolish halfling! He thought he could fool the Sisters of the Silver Fire.
ke2bro10.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2kel13.dialogue: His backside will remind him of his folly.
ke2kel13.speaker: kellan

ke2bro11.dialogue: Because we revere Mystra, the Lady of Spells.
ke2bro11.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2bro12.dialogue: Long ago the high mage Sammaster deceived her, and used his ill-gotten knowledge to found the Cult of the Dragon.
ke2bro12.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2bro13.dialogue: And so the incantrix Yhelfanna founded our Sisterhood, dedicated to undoing the evil Sammaster had done.
ke2bro13.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2bro14.dialogue: We were sent to Myth Drannor by the incantrix Fieryat Ildacer, one of the Seven of the Sisterhood of Silver Fire, to destroy a dracolich named Pelendralaar.
ke2bro14.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2kel18.dialogue: There were twelve of us then.
ke2kel18.speaker: kellan

ke2bro15.dialogue: What the Sisterhood did not know is that Pelendralaar had been joined by a Cult mage of great power - I do not know her name.
ke2bro15.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2bro16.dialogue: We found the Cult guarding a creature called the Baelnorn. We attempted to free him...
ke2bro16.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2kel19.dialogue: Thus to make us thirteen in number. That was ill-fated!
ke2kel19.speaker: kellan

ke2bro17.dialogue: Cult mages appeared, and our company was swept apart in a fury of magic. I fear all our companions have been destroyed.
ke2bro17.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2kel22.dialogue: Ugh. We know where he is, aye, only too well.
ke2kel22.speaker: kellan

ke2bro18.dialogue: Much deeper in these catacombs, you will find great doors marked with an elven rune. The Baelnorn is somewhere beyond them, held in force by the Cult.
ke2bro18.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2bro19.dialogue: But you can't get there now. The Cult sealed the way with one of their Glyphs...
ke2bro19.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2kel24.dialogue: It is the Glyph of Safekeeping. I do not know the Word that unseals it.
ke2kel24.speaker: kellan

ke2bro20.dialogue: Think carefully before you broach those doors! For such an affront is sure to arouse the full fury of the Cult.
ke2bro20.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2bro21.dialogue: That would be a talisman of great power. Such a thing might be in the lair of some creature - if it has not already fallen into the hands of the Cult.
ke2bro21.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2bro22.dialogue: We were sent to Myth Drannor by the incantrix Fieryat Ildacer, one of the Seven of the Sisterhood of Silver Fire, to destroy a dracolich named Pelendralaar.
ke2bro22.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2kel28.dialogue: There were twelve of us then.
ke2kel28.speaker: kellan

ke2bro23.dialogue: What the Sisterhood did not know is that Pelendralaar had been joined by a Cult mage of great power - I do not know her name.
ke2bro23.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2bro24.dialogue: We found the Cult guarding a creature called the Baelnorn. We attempted to free him...
ke2bro24.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2kel29.dialogue: Thus to make us thirteen in number. That was ill-fated!
ke2kel29.speaker: kellan

ke2bro25.dialogue: Cult mages appeared, and our company was swept apart in a fury of magic. I fear all our companions have been destroyed.
ke2bro25.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2bro26.dialogue: We are of two minds about what to do.
ke2bro26.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2kel31.dialogue: One mind says to strike! The Cult thinks we are dead, and a small company can get far before they realize the truth.
ke2kel31.speaker: kellan

ke2bro27.dialogue: The other mind says that two is too small a company to attack the whole Cult! We may get far, but we would not get far enough.
ke2bro27.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2kel34.dialogue: If your number ever falls short, return here to us, and we will join your ranks.
ke2kel34.speaker: kellan

ke2bro28.dialogue: We will not fail you. Goodbye.
ke2bro28.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2kel35.dialogue: Look - there is room in your party - let me join you! Or, if I am too rough for your company, consider my sister Bronwyn.
ke2kel35.speaker: kellan

ke2bro29.dialogue: We will not fail you. Goodbye.
ke2bro29.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2kel36.dialogue: Look - you number but a few...
ke2kel36.speaker: kellan

ke2bro30.dialogue: ...let us join with you, and march together against the Cult.
ke2bro30.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2kel38.dialogue: You are right. It is the only way.
ke2kel38.speaker: kellan

ke2bro31.dialogue: It is a plan fraught with peril. Still, I would walk with you - in a heartbeat I would - and I know my sister feels the same.
ke2bro31.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2kel39.dialogue: Enough talk! Enough questions! We have the same enemy. If I only had more companions, I would be cleaving Cult necks right now. Will you not take me into your company?
ke2kel39.speaker: kellan

ke2kel40.dialogue: ...or, if I am too rough for you, will you not take my sister Bronwyn? For mark my words, the Silver Fire will not stand by, while the Cult grows in power!
ke2kel40.speaker: kellan

ke2kel41.dialogue: No! You will not walk away! We have the same enemy. I have spells and a mighty arm, and deep hatred for the Cult. Will you not take me into your company?
ke2kel41.speaker: kellan

ke2kel42.dialogue: ...or, if I am too rough for you, will you not take my sister Bronwyn? For mark my words, the Silver Fire will not stand by, while the Cult grows in power!
ke2kel42.speaker: kellan

ke2kel89.dialogue: Hiya, they are back, and they freed the guardians!
ke2kel89.speaker: kellan

ke2bro32.dialogue: We meet again. And look! Our Shrine is restored, thanks to you. The Silver Fire burns bright once more.
ke2bro32.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2bro33.dialogue: Why, it serves all those who oppose the Cult of the Dragon. It is a solace and sanctuary hidden from their eyes.
ke2bro33.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2bro34.dialogue: And now that it is restored, Kellan and I are free to resume our quest...
ke2bro34.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2kel96.dialogue: ...to cleave through the Cult ranks, and banish Pelendralaar to the dead place reserved for his foul kind!
ke2kel96.speaker: kellan

ke2bro35.dialogue: If you will take one or both of us into your company, that is.
ke2bro35.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2bro36.dialogue: Ah, but the guardians have told us the tale already, of the seesawing battle and how you toppled the Skull.
ke2bro36.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2kel99.dialogue: I wish I had been there! To swing a sword with you, and cleave naga necks, and cast the most hurtful spells I know.
ke2kel99.speaker: kellan

ke2bro37.dialogue: In a heartbeat! For our quest is the same as yours...
ke2bro37.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2kela2.dialogue: ...to cleave through the Cult ranks, and banish Pelendralaar to the dead place reserved for his foul kind!
ke2kela2.speaker: kellan

ke2kela3.dialogue: We are Sisters of the Silver Fire! The most canny and fearsome adversaries of the Cult in Faerun! You dare much, to question our abilities!
ke2kela3.speaker: kellan

ke2bro38.dialogue: Calmly, sister! You lash out, but no enemy is there.
ke2bro38.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2bro39.dialogue: Let me tell you about my sister Kellan. She is both fighter and sorcerer. She learned her skills in the Cult...
ke2bro39.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2bro40.dialogue: ...but now, her skills at summoning death and mayhem far exceed theirs. And her spirit I think you know by now.
ke2bro40.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2kela4.dialogue: And Bronwyn! Dear Bronwyn. She is a ranger of great renown, skilled with sword and bow, and priest and healer in the bargain...
ke2kela4.speaker: kellan

ke2kela5.dialogue: ...and I am proud to call her sister, and do whatever she may say.
ke2kela5.speaker: kellan

ke2bro41.dialogue: We thank you. Now our quest will not fail!
ke2bro41.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2dma02.dialogue: Kellan and Bronwyn join your party.
ke2dma02.speaker: DM

ke2kela8.dialogue: You are wise. Greater numbers would draw unwanted attention. But if any of your company should falter...
ke2kela8.speaker: kellan

ke2bro42.dialogue: ...or fall to the enemy, come seek us out here.
ke2bro42.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2bro43.dialogue: Now you best be on your way. Goodbye.
ke2bro43.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2bro44.dialogue: Which of us will you take with you?
ke2bro44.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2kelb2.dialogue: Later! You know not the Cult! There is no 'later'!
ke2kelb2.speaker: kellan

ke2bro45.dialogue: Kellan! -Forgive my sister. Her tongue is harsh, when she has no enemy to face.
ke2bro45.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2bro46.dialogue: It is hard, but we will wait here. If you have need of companions, we are ready! Goodbye.
ke2bro46.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2kelb3.dialogue: Ah! Farewell then, cruel sister. You leave me here to waste away!
ke2kelb3.speaker: kellan

ke2bro47.dialogue: I will see you soon, dear Kellan.
ke2bro47.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2bro48.dialogue: Travelers, I am one of you now. Let us go.
ke2bro48.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2bro49.dialogue: Farewell then, sister - you must take care! For I will not be there to keep you from trouble.
ke2bro49.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2kelb6.dialogue: I will return to you, dear Bronwyn. Come, my new companions, let's go!
ke2kelb6.speaker: kellan

ke2bro50.dialogue: When you make up your mind, you will find us here. Goodbye.
ke2bro50.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2kelb9.dialogue: Yes, but look, one of your company is dead.
ke2kelb9.speaker: kellan

ke2kelc0.dialogue: Yes, but look, some of your company are dead.
ke2kelc0.speaker: kellan

ke2kelc1.dialogue: I mean no insult. But a time comes when those who fall must be laid aside. We face the Cult of the Dragon! Tenderness may be a luxury you can no longer afford.
ke2kelc1.speaker: kellan

ke2kelc2.dialogue: Look at Bronwyn! Look at me! We are strong, and we are alive. We have come through dragonfire and black magic to be here. Will you not take us into your company?
ke2kelc2.speaker: kellan

ke2kelc3.dialogue: Look at Bronwyn! Look at me! We are strong and alive. We have come through dragonfire and black magic to be here. Will you not take one of us into your company?
ke2kelc3.speaker: kellan

ke2bro53.dialogue: Your loyalty to your companion is deep! I respect you for it.
ke2bro53.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2bro54.dialogue: Your loyalty to your companions is deep! I respect you for it.
ke2bro54.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2kelc6.dialogue: I do not! Foolishness it seems to me, to prefer the dead to the living. But it is your choice.
ke2kelc6.speaker: kellan

ke2kelc7.dialogue: Full? If you say so. But your numbers seem low to me.
ke2kelc7.speaker: kellan

ke2kelc8.dialogue: Look at Bronwyn! Look at me! We are strong and able. We have come through dragonfire and black magic to be here. Will you not take us into your company?
ke2kelc8.speaker: kellan

ke2bro55.dialogue: They wish to see it through themselves, Kellan. We must respect their decision.
ke2bro55.speaker: Bronwyn

ke2keld0.dialogue: Tolerate, yes. Respect, no! Foolishness it seems to me, not to accept aid so freely offered. But it is your choice, travelers.
ke2keld0.speaker: kellan

ke5kel02.dialogue: Do you wish to take me into your company? Or do you want to talk about my life in the Cult?
ke5kel02.speaker: kellan

ke5kel03.dialogue: Ask, and I will answer you.
ke5kel03.speaker: kellan
ke5kel03.desc: spoken, reluctantly, she would prefer to act rather than talk

ke5kel05.dialogue: Weaknesses? They keep secrets from each other. When I was in the Cult, I never told anyone what I was doing. When I left the Cult, it took them a year to find out.
ke5kel05.speaker: kellan

ke5kel06.dialogue: So you can nibble at them for a while, if you are careful. Kill a mage here, a band there, and no one will know.
ke5kel06.speaker: kellan

ke5kel07.dialogue: But woe to you when at last they see you as the threat you are. Then you will see the Claw come down quick and hard!
ke5kel07.speaker: kellan

ke5kel10.dialogue: It is hard, if there are too many of them. If you can, cast spells to protect yourselves before the enemy is even in sight. And have wands and staves ready! Do not run short of magic!
ke5kel10.speaker: kellan

ke5kel11.dialogue: Do not waste your time with spells that hold or fuddle the fighters. Their mages may undo them with a counterspell.
ke5kel11.speaker: kellan

ke5kel12.dialogue: Be sure to hit the mages hard - if you let them cast a spell, all may be lost! Once the mages have fallen, then concentrate your fury on each fighter, one by one.
ke5kel12.speaker: kellan

ke5kel15.dialogue: We had many. We were careful to slaughter them every one, so no word would creep back that the Silver Fire was loose among them!
ke5kel15.speaker: kellan

ke5kel16.dialogue: But then we stormed the gates where the Baelnorn was kept. That creature must be important to them, indeed! For many mages came down upon us unawares, and loosed fire and lightning, and so all was lost.
ke5kel16.speaker: kellan

ke5kel20.dialogue: Have you ever seen a dragon? They are mighty! If so, you understand why the Cult would strive to increase the power of dragons, and then harness it for their own use.
ke5kel20.speaker: kellan

ke5kel21.dialogue: I was barely a woman when I first saw one. It killed and devoured most of the caravan I was traveling in, yet it spared me. Why?
ke5kel21.speaker: kellan

ke5kel22.dialogue: The Cult convinced me it was my destiny to serve dragons. And so I believed for many years.
ke5kel22.speaker: kellan

ke5kel23.dialogue: But slowly I came to realize that Sammaster's teachings were mad, and that my destiny was not to bow to them, but to kill them and their evil. And so I left the Cult and become a humble servant of the Silver Fire.
ke5kel23.speaker: kellan

ke5kel27.dialogue: I am willing. You seem to be a good company.
ke5kel27.speaker: kellan

ke5kel28.dialogue: Come back to me with fewer in your company, and I will gladly fill out your number.
ke5kel28.speaker: kellan

ke5kel30.dialogue: I am willing. You are a good company. Let the Cult beware!
ke5kel30.speaker: kellan

ke5kel33.dialogue: I am willing. You are a good company. But your ranks are full now - if we count your dead companion.
ke5kel33.speaker: kellan

ke5kel34.dialogue: If you need me, look for me here.
ke5kel34.speaker: kellan

ke5kel37.dialogue: Enough talk! I am one of you now. Let's go.
ke5kel37.speaker: kellan

ke5kel38.dialogue: I grow weary of talk. If you need me, look for me here.
ke5kel38.speaker: kellan

ke5kel39.dialogue: Well then, look for me here, if you should change your mind.
ke5kel39.speaker: kellan

ke5kel40.dialogue: Yes, but one of your company is dead. Think on that a moment.
ke5kel40.speaker: kellan

ke5kel41.dialogue: Look for me here, if you find room in your company for a rough one such as me.
ke5kel41.speaker: kellan

ke5kel42.dialogue: I grow weary of talk. Will you have me into your company, or no?
ke5kel42.speaker: kellan

ke5kel43.dialogue: If you say so. Your numbers seem not overlarge to me. Look for me here, if you should change your mind.
ke5kel43.speaker: kellan

ke4kel03.dialogue: Ah, aha, Kelemvor, you can come for me now! We would make the Lady blush, haha!
ke4kel03.speaker: Kellan
ke4kel03.desc: spoken, she is just so utterly and unabashedly proud and full of herself, Kelemvor=God of the Dead, Mystra's paramour

ke4kel04.dialogue: The Cult, we broke their backs! And that witch, how she screamed! Ah, forgive me, friends, I am giddy, still giddy with the glory of it.
ke4kel04.speaker: Kellan

ke4bro00.dialogue: What Kellan means to say is, we have fulfilled our quest, thanks to you. The Silver Fire is ever in your debt.
ke4bro00.speaker: Bronwyn

ke4bro01.dialogue: I am of the woodland, and lack skill with words, but I thank you most warmly, and will treasure the time we spent together.
ke4bro01.speaker: Bronwyn

ke4bro02.dialogue: I have told Kellan about our victory.
ke4bro02.speaker: Bronwyn

ke4kel08.dialogue: And you fed the dust to Pelendralaar! Ah, I wish I could have been there!
ke4kel08.speaker: Kellan

ke4kel09.dialogue: Ah, aha, Kelemvor, you can come for me now! We would make the Lady blush, haha!
ke4kel09.speaker: Kellan
ke4kel09.desc: spoken, she is very happy, Kelemvor=God of the Dead, Mystra's paramour

ke4bro03.dialogue: Nottle told us of your victory! Some of his tale is not to be believed!
ke4bro03.speaker: Bronwyn

ke4kel10.dialogue: How you broke them! Their mages, in flames! The witch collected by her masters! Pelendralaar, choking on dust! Ah, how I envy you your glory!
ke4kel10.speaker: Kellan

ke4kel12.dialogue: I welcome you, comrades, and bid you rest and heal here in our Shrine.
ke4kel12.speaker: Kellan

ke4kel13.dialogue: Our victory was great, but Bronwyn is dead, and joy has fled from my heart.
ke4kel13.speaker: Kellan

ke4kel14.dialogue: If you will have me, I will join you, and then let the evil things beware! For a black sorrow is upon me, and I am lost, without Bronwyn's gentle wisdom.
ke4kel14.speaker: Kellan

ke4kel15.dialogue: Welcome, travellers - I bid you rest and heal here in our Shrine.
ke4kel15.speaker: Kellan

ke4kel16.dialogue: I have heard of your victory, and it is great, but Bronwyn is dead, and joy has fled from my heart.
ke4kel16.speaker: Kellan

ke4kel18.dialogue: Ah, aha, Kelemvor, you can come for me now! We would make the Lady blush, haha!
ke4kel18.speaker: Kellan
ke4kel18.desc: spoken, she is just so happy, Kelemvor=God of the Dead, Mystra's paramour

ke4kel19.dialogue: Forgive me, comrades, I am still drunk on our glory. Rest and heal here, in the glow of the Silver Fire.
ke4kel19.speaker: Kellan
ke4kel19.desc: spoken, still a little giddy with glee

ke4kel20.dialogue: Ah, travellers, welcome! Of course we have heard the news - Kya Mordrayn dead, and her dracolich is dust! Hahaa!
ke4kel20.speaker: Kellan

ke4kel21.dialogue: Forgive me, comrades, I am still drunk on the glory of it. Rest and heal here, in the glow of the Silver Fire.
ke4kel21.speaker: Kellan
ke4kel21.desc: spoken, still a little giddy with glee

ke4kelXA.dialogue: Why, we are Sisters of the Silver Fire, devoted to the dismay, downfall and destruction of the Cult of the Dragon.
ke4kelXA.speaker: Kellan

ke4broXB.dialogue: We were sent to Myth Drannor by the incantrix Fieryat Ildacer, one of the Sisterhood's Seven, to destroy a dracolich named Pelendralaar.
ke4broXB.speaker: Bronwyn

ke4kelXC.dialogue: But we are too late, it seems! For you have done that very thing.
ke4kelXC.speaker: Kellan

ke4broXE.dialogue: Rest and heal here, whenever you need it, brave heroes. The Shrine of the Silver Fire will ever be in your debt.
ke4broXE.speaker: Bronwyn

ke4kelXF.dialogue: And if you should need a companion for your company, why, consider one of us!
ke4kelXF.speaker: Kellan

ke4kelXL.dialogue: Oh, it was a mighty deed! All of Faerun will soon be agog over it!
ke4kelXL.speaker: Kellan

ke4broXM.dialogue: And it will be a dagger of fear in the heart of the Cult of the Dragon!
ke4broXM.speaker: Bronwyn

ke4broXO.dialogue: For what you have done, all of Faerun will thank you...
ke4broXO.speaker: Bronwyn

ke4kelXP.dialogue: ...except for those fools in the Cult of the Dragon, ha ha!
ke4kelXP.speaker: Kellan

ke4broXQ.dialogue: But you also were the ones who freed the guardians of our Shrine, Gloran and Ethe. And for this we are most especially grateful.
ke4broXQ.speaker: Bronwyn

lzkogd09.dialogue: So you say, lizard slime. So you say. Bubunuk!

lzklz119.dialogue: We not fear you, orog clods. Or the flap-tongue hotbloods. Shashiki!

mg1mg124.speaker: mrgoyle1

mg1mg125.dialogue: Never mind, it doesn't matter, you won't get a chance to do either. Begone!
mg1mg125.speaker: mrgoyle1

mg1mg126.dialogue: And I suppose you have a message for our master.
mg1mg126.speaker: mrgoyle1

mg1mg127.dialogue: And it must be delivered to him in person.
mg1mg127.speaker: mrgoyle1

mg1mg128.dialogue: Too bad he's not here. So go away!
mg1mg128.speaker: mrgoyle1

mg1mg129.dialogue: You told us before you were messengers!
mg1mg129.speaker: mrgoyle1

mg1mgg09.dialogue: oik oik oik ikk ikk ikk oik oik!
mg1mgg09.speaker: Margroup

mg1mgg10.speaker: Margroup
mg1mgg10.desc: spoken, outburst, loud and rude sniggering

mg1mg132.dialogue: No, no, foolish ones, you are nothing like my master!
mg1mg132.speaker: mrgoyle1

mg1mgg11.dialogue: oik oik oik ikk ikk ikk oik oik!
mg1mgg11.speaker: Margroup

mg1mg134.dialogue: He did? And what did he say to tell us?
mg1mg134.speaker: mrgoyle1

mg1mg135.dialogue: Then why did you take so long to deliver this message? This is the third time you have been here.
mg1mg135.speaker: mrgoyle1

mg1mg136.dialogue: No servant of the master would dare to wait so long. You fool no one. Begone!
mg1mg136.speaker: mrgoyle1

mg1mgg12.dialogue: oik oik oik ikk ikk ikk oik oik!
mg1mgg12.speaker: Margroup

mg1mg137.dialogue: Oh, we will, we will. You can tell the master that, next time you see him.
mg1mg137.speaker: mrgoyle1

mg1mgg13.dialogue: oik oik oik ikk ikk ikk oik oik!
mg1mgg13.speaker: Margroup

mg1mg139.dialogue: If the master commands it... so we will do.
mg1mg139.speaker: mrgoyle1

mg1mgg14.dialogue: oik oik oik ikk ikk ikk oik oik!
mg1mgg14.speaker: Margroup

mg1mg140.dialogue: You can tell the master that, next time you see him. Now, begone!
mg1mg140.speaker: mrgoyle1

mg1mg141.dialogue: Injured, you say? And need help?
mg1mg141.speaker: mrgoyle1

mg1mg142.dialogue: Tell me more. How badly hurt are you?
mg1mg142.speaker: mrgoyle1

mg1mg144.dialogue: I am very sorry to hear that. Drag their corpses somewhere else, and leave us alone. Now go!
mg1mg144.speaker: mrgoyle1

mg1mg145.dialogue: Treasure? We don't need treasure. We have plenty of treasure in here.
mg1mg145.speaker: mrgoyle1

mg1mg146.dialogue: What we care about is how weak and defenseless you are.
mg1mg146.speaker: mrgoyle1

mg1mg148.dialogue: I am very sorry to hear that. That means you won't last long enough to be worth our while.
mg1mg148.speaker: mrgoyle1

mg1mg149.dialogue: Drag yourselves off and die someplace else. Now go!
mg1mg149.speaker: mrgoyle1

mg1mg151.dialogue: Too much to risk. It would've been fun, but... we'll leave the drawbridge up, as the Master commanded. And that is that.
mg1mg151.speaker: mrgoyle1

mg1mgg15.dialogue: Ahhhhh, no! Grumble phooey grumble mumble.
mg1mgg15.speaker: Margroup

mg1mgg16.dialogue: Oh, oho, badly hurt! Help, help! Ah hahaha! Poor broken bits of flesh!
mg1mgg16.speaker: Margroup
mg1mgg16.desc: spoken, trying to muffle their gleeful cackling

mg1mg153.dialogue: Ah, don't worry, we will help you! Wait right there...
mg1mg153.speaker: mrgoyle1

mg1pro00.dialogue: Ask who gave them the order
mg1pro00.speaker: Protagonist

mg1pro03.dialogue: Say that you are the master
mg1pro03.speaker: Protagonist

mg1pro04.dialogue: Say that the master sent you
mg1pro04.speaker: Protagonist

mg1pro06.dialogue: Ask if they'd like something to eat
mg1pro06.speaker: Protagonist

mg1pro07.dialogue: Say you're injured, and need help
mg1pro07.speaker: Protagonist

mg1pro09.dialogue: Tell them he said to lower the drawbridge
mg1pro09.speaker: Protagonist

mg1pro10.dialogue: Tell them he said to kill each other
mg1pro10.speaker: Protagonist

mg1pro11.dialogue: Say he said to watch out for intruders
mg1pro11.speaker: Protagonist

mg1pro12.dialogue: Tell them he said they must go join him
mg1pro12.speaker: Protagonist

mg1pro13.dialogue: Say he said you must replace them as guards
mg1pro13.speaker: Protagonist

mg1pro15.dialogue: Say you are very badly hurt
mg1pro15.speaker: Protagonist

mg1pro16.dialogue: Say most of you are dead
mg1pro16.speaker: Protagonist

mg1pro17.dialogue: Say you're too weak to carry your treasure
mg1pro17.speaker: Protagonist

mdwdma02.dialogue: You touch the stone, and a flash of memory ignites in your mind...
mdwdma02.speaker: DM

mdwdma03.dialogue: ...a silent mass of grieving dwarves, holding torches aloft... an honor guard of dwarves bearing a fallen warrior to this marker...
mdwdma03.speaker: DM

mdwdmaYA.dialogue: The procession leader touches the marker, and a way opens down to the ancient crypts. A great sadness overwhelms you and sweeps you downward. The lights dim and go dark.
mdwdmaYA.speaker: DM

mdwdmaYB.dialogue: You touch the stone, and a flash of memory floods into you...
mdwdmaYB.speaker: DM

mdwdmaYC.dialogue: Visions of ancient ceremonies flood your mind's eye. The bright lights of torches, troops of dwarves moving in a sad procession... but then the vision fades.
mdwdmaYC.speaker: DM

mdwdmaYE.dialogue: Again you get a glimmer of memory from the stone - a flicker of great sadness, nothing more.
mdwdmaYE.speaker: DM

mdwdmaYG.dialogue: You learn nothing new about this ceremonial stone.
mdwdmaYG.speaker: DM

mdwdmaYH.dialogue: You touch the stone, and get a flicker of a vision - a ghostly army of dwarven warriors, silently descending a great stone stairway into the Halls of the Dwarf-Father.
mdwdmaYH.speaker: DM

mdwdmaYI.dialogue: The ceremonial marker now seems quiet and peaceful.
mdwdmaYI.speaker: DM
