mgfDMYA.speaker: DM

mgfDMYB.dialogue: With a giggle of excitement, the ghost of Floribud now disappears off to the east.
mgfDMYB.speaker: DM

mgoDMYA.dialogue: You see signs that this barricade was erected fairly recently.
mgoDMYA.speaker: DM

mgoDMYB.dialogue: But by whom, or why, you cannot tell.
mgoDMYB.speaker: DM

mgoDMYC.dialogue: Your ranger can tell it was the slipshod work of orcs, trying to keep something out of their stronghold.
mgoDMYC.speaker: DM

mgoDMYD.dialogue: Your rangers agree it was the slipshod work of orcs, trying to keep something out of their stronghold.
mgoDMYD.speaker: DM

mgoDMYE.dialogue: Your rogue recognizes the slapdash handiwork of orcs, trying to keep creatures out of their stronghold.
mgoDMYE.speaker: DM

mgoDMYF.dialogue: One of your rogues recognizes the slapdash handiwork: orcs built the barricade, probably to keep creatures out of their stronghold.
mgoDMYF.speaker: DM

mgoDMYG.dialogue: You can tell orcs built this barricade recently, to keep the restless undead out of the orc stronghold.
mgoDMYG.speaker: DM

mmadma04.dialogue: You lick up the last few drops of a sharp-tasting elixir. You feel more fluid and flexible, more dexterous!
mmadma04.speaker: DM

mqadma00.dialogue: When the last orc falls, a bundle falls out from under its belt. The orc has collected the hearts and brains of the fallen, and wrapped them in some paper.
mqadma00.speaker: DM

mqadma01.dialogue: The paper turns out to be pages from the Adventurer's Journal of Athan's band.
mqadma01.speaker: DM

mqadma02.dialogue: Athan had learned that 'the scarred ones' had taken up residence in Castle Cormanthor, and somehow found a way to corrupt Myth Drannor's ancient protective spell, the Mythal.
mqadma02.speaker: DM

mqadma03.dialogue: He sought a way into the Castle, to stop the scarred ones and somehow restore the Mythal.
mqadma03.speaker: DM

mqadma04.dialogue: There is more - he mentions 'allies' and 'City Heights' and 'the Skeletal Arm' - but bloodstains have blotted out everything else.
mqadma04.speaker: DM

mpedmaYA.dialogue: Haashingutak, the Word of Venom, opens the sealed door!
mpedmaYA.speaker: DM

msldmaYA.dialogue: Tam-tamak, the Knocking Word, speaks itself, and opens your way into the hidden shelter.
msldmaYA.speaker: DM

ng1ng102.dialogue: Oh, this is splendid, we welcome you, all six of you!
ng1ng102.speaker: dnaga1

ng1dn200.dialogue: The count is perfect - two for each of us. Kog will be pleased.
ng1dn200.speaker: Dnaga2

ng1ng103.dialogue: Oh, by the Fang! The count is all wrong!
ng1ng103.speaker: dnaga1

ng1dn201.dialogue: Why couldn't there have been three of you, or six, or nine? Kog will be annoyed!
ng1dn201.speaker: Dnaga2
ng1dn201.desc: spoken, disgusted, 'this is all your fault'

ng1ng104.dialogue: Oh, this is splendid, we welcome the three of you!
ng1ng104.speaker: dnaga1

ng1dn202.dialogue: The count is perfect - one for each of us. Kog will be pleased.
ng1dn202.speaker: Dnaga2

ng1dn203.dialogue: Kog is our boss. This is now the shrine of Kog.
ng1dn203.speaker: Dnaga2

ng1ng107.dialogue: It was Kog who pledged our lives to the Pool, and silenced the woman.
ng1ng107.speaker: dnaga1

ng1ng108.dialogue: Oh, never mind about us, let's talk about you.
ng1ng108.speaker: dnaga1

ng1dn204.dialogue: We'd better let Kog take the big ugly one.
ng1dn204.speaker: Dnaga2

ng1dn205.dialogue: We'd better let Kog take at least one of the big ugly ones.
ng1dn205.speaker: Dnaga2

ng1dn206.dialogue: We'd better let Kog take the human.
ng1dn206.speaker: Dnaga2

ng1dn207.dialogue: We'd better let Kog take at least one of the humans.
ng1dn207.speaker: Dnaga2

ng1dn208.dialogue: No humans among you, curse you! Humans are Kog's favorite.
ng1dn208.speaker: Dnaga2

ng1ng115.dialogue: Oh, she is no one anymore, she is long dead. Only her voice was left, crying for her followers...
ng1ng115.speaker: dnaga1

ng1dn209.dialogue: ...but when the Pool came and Kog raised the Sign of Coils, even the voice was gone, ha ha.
ng1dn209.speaker: Dnaga2

ng1ng116.dialogue: 'Mystra this' - 'Mystra that' - all day long. It was more than a body could bear!
ng1ng116.speaker: dnaga1

ng1dn210.dialogue: But enough of that! We need to decide which of you Kog will take.
ng1dn210.speaker: Dnaga2

ng1dn211.dialogue: But enough of that! We need to decide which one of you Kog will take.
ng1dn211.speaker: Dnaga2

ng1ng119.dialogue: The new lords of Myth Drannor fetched the Pool...
ng1ng119.speaker: dnaga1

ng1dn212.dialogue: ...the Spawn Pools subdue anyone who might interfere with their rule...
ng1dn212.speaker: Dnaga2

ng1dn213.dialogue: ...There is a spirit here, a powerful elf-woman, but then the Pool came, ha ha! Kog used it to silence her...
ng1dn213.speaker: Dnaga2

ng1ng120.dialogue: The Spawn Pool gives us the power to silence just about anyone.
ng1ng120.speaker: dnaga1

ng1ng121.dialogue: And exalt those who swear loyalty to them, as Kog has done.
ng1ng121.speaker: dnaga1

ng1ng122.dialogue: You lie! You are a fool, to attempt to deceive a dark naga. This Pool can never be destroyed, believe me...
ng1ng122.speaker: dnaga1

ng1ng123.dialogue: ...and as it grows, so does the power of Kog.
ng1ng123.speaker: dnaga1

ng1ano00.dialogue: Oh Lady, the Servants, the Servants of Mystery, are they here?
ng1ano00.speaker: Anorrwyn
ng1ano00.desc: spoken, plaintive, with an effect to imply that it comes from beyond this world, called out from offscreen

ng1kog01.dialogue: Wrong! I take whoever I please.
ng1kog01.speaker: Kog

ng1kog02.dialogue: Because humans are the juiciest. And their blood runs HOT. So - let's eat.
ng1kog02.speaker: Kog

ng1kog03.dialogue: Ah, but you will not begin to harm this one.
ng1kog03.speaker: Kog

ng1ng130.dialogue: Oh, no no no. You will not escape the coils of Kog.
ng1ng130.speaker: dnaga1

ng1kog04.dialogue: Well said. -Enough of this talk! Let's eat.
ng1kog04.speaker: Kog

ng1pro01.dialogue: Ask about the woman Kog silenced
ng1pro01.speaker: Protagonist

ng1pro04.dialogue: Say Kog will not take any of you
ng1pro04.speaker: Protagonist

ng1pro08.dialogue: Bid them goodbye, and move on
ng1pro08.speaker: Protagonist

na1ane00.speaker: Anesh
na1ane00.desc: spoken, translation from deep drow is: They are here

na1nat03.speaker: Nathlil
na1nat03.desc: spoken, translation from deep drow is: Parley

na1ane01.dialogue: Hold, surface crawlers. Nathlilik, first daughter of the House of Kilsek, commands parley.
na1ane01.speaker: Anesh

na1Nat04.dialogue: You choose well. The way around this chasm is long and perilous. Hear me out, and I will lower the drawbridge.
na1Nat04.speaker: Nathlil

na1Nat05.dialogue: I've been watching you. You kill the Cult filth when you can. We have a common enemy, and that can make us allies. For a time.
na1Nat05.speaker: Nathlil

na1Nat06.dialogue: Ha! And lose your keen attention? Not just yet.
na1Nat06.speaker: Nathlil

na1Nat07.dialogue: I've been watching your progress against the Cult. Your enemy is my enemy, and that can make us allies for a time. Yes?
na1Nat07.speaker: Nathlil

na1Nat09.dialogue: True. You are wise to know it. But at present I have a use for you. And you have need of this bridge.
na1Nat09.speaker: Nathlil

na1Nat11.dialogue: A Cult Mage blocks my path at a stairway far south and west of here. He bears the Staff of Sunlight. It can be of use to you.
na1Nat11.speaker: Nathlil

na1Nat12.dialogue: Kill him. Take the staff. And stay far from me and mine.
na1Nat12.speaker: Nathlil

na1Nat13.dialogue: Ha! I need no traps to rid the underearth of you. You're as like to kill each other, tripping over yourselves in the goddess' sweet darkness.
na1Nat13.speaker: Nathlil

na1Nat14.dialogue: You are nothing to me. Save this: kill the mage and clear my path.
na1Nat14.speaker: Nathlil

na1Nat15.dialogue: This would be trap enough to destroy you, should I wish it so.
na1Nat15.speaker: Nathlil

na1Nat16.dialogue: See for yourself. Take it. Cast its light upon the Freth. Watch them fry in its gaze.
na1Nat16.speaker: Nathlil

na1Nat17.dialogue: My reasons are my own. Agree or refuse. I tire of looking at you.
na1Nat17.speaker: Nathlil

na1Nat18.dialogue: Hate is the song in my blood! It is all that lives in me now, the Freth have seen to that.
na1Nat18.speaker: Nathlil

na1Nat19.dialogue: Because he keeps me from my prey! And from my death. That is the only joy left for me now, the Freth have seen to that.
na1Nat19.speaker: Nathlil

na1Nat20.dialogue: They lured us here with promises of glory. The Cult was to give us dominion over Myth Drannor. Titles. Riches.
na1Nat20.speaker: Nathlil

na1Nat21.dialogue: Lies! We were the price the Freth paid for power! Our blood fed to the Cult's dracolich. Our souls sucked from living bodies!
na1Nat21.speaker: Nathlil

na1Nat22.dialogue: You've seen my people - they're trapped between life and death. Slaves! Only I survive to free them.
na1Nat22.speaker: Nathlil

na1Nat23.dialogue: Speak! Will you kill the mage?
na1Nat23.speaker: Nathlil

na1Nat24.dialogue: What do you know of passion? Heat that drives life? The earth burns with it, and so do the hearts of my people.
na1Nat24.speaker: Nathlil

na1Nat25.dialogue: Two hearts, joined, burn hottest. Is it the same with you in your pale beds? Are your mates of value to you?
na1Nat25.speaker: Nathlil

na1Nat26.dialogue: The Cult has taken my mate. They have enslaved his soul. Darkness is no comfort to me now.
na1Nat26.speaker: Nathlil

na1Nat27.dialogue: I cannot restore his body to life, but I will free his soul to death. And my own soon after.
na1Nat27.speaker: Nathlil

na1Nat28.dialogue: Can you understand this? I care not. Find the mage. Kill him. Agree to this and I will give you the bridge.
na1Nat28.speaker: Nathlil

na1Nat29.dialogue: If I free the souls of the Kilsek drow, their bodies can no longer serve the Cult.
na1Nat29.speaker: Nathlil

na1Nat30.dialogue: Surely it is of use to you if the Cult's guards crumble suddenly to dust.
na1Nat30.speaker: Nathlil

na1Nat31.dialogue: Find the mage. Destroy him. Claim the Staff. Clear my way to the Cult's nest. It is all of use to you.
na1Nat31.speaker: Nathlil

na1Nat32.dialogue: Then go all the way north, then east, then south, then all the way west to find the stair. It is south of an arraccat warren - beware those fierce marauders! The Staff will do the Cult little good against you. Behold! The bridge is yours.
na1Nat32.speaker: Nathlil

na1Nat33.dialogue: But beware, sunwalkers, for the peace between us is brief. And fragile.
na1Nat33.speaker: Nathlil

na1Nat34.dialogue: That is well. I think what pleases you will be to kill this mage, and use his Staff upon the Freth. Have your bridge then.
na1Nat34.speaker: Nathlil

na1Nat35.dialogue: You have lost an opportunity, sunwalkers. Make your own way against the Cult, then.  Anesh. Belar... Z'han!
na1Nat35.speaker: Nathlil
na1Nat35.desc: spoken, impatient, to her men, translation - Anesh, Belar. Come!

na1Nat38.dialogue: You have lost an opportunity, sunwalkers. Make your own way against the Cult, then.  Anesh. Belar... Z'han!
na1Nat38.speaker: Nathlil
na1Nat38.desc: to her men, translation - Anesh, Belar. Come!

na1pro04.dialogue: Tell her to lower the drawbridge now
na1pro04.speaker: Protagonist

na1pro05.dialogue: Ask why she would do that
na1pro05.speaker: Protagonist

na1pro08.dialogue: Tell her she is your enemy
na1pro08.speaker: Protagonist

na1pro11.dialogue: Ask why she hates the Freth
na1pro11.speaker: Protagonist

na1pro12.dialogue: Ask what the Staff of Sunlight can do
na1pro12.speaker: Protagonist

na1pro13.dialogue: Tell her you think it's a trap
na1pro13.speaker: Protagonist

na1pro14.dialogue: Demand to know what's behind her need
na1pro14.speaker: Protagonist

na1pro15.dialogue: Ask why she wants to get past the mage
na1pro15.speaker: Protagonist

na1pro16.dialogue: Agree to kill the Cult mage
na1pro16.speaker: Protagonist

na1pro17.dialogue: Refuse to do ask she asks
na1pro17.speaker: Protagonist

na1pro18.dialogue: Ask why you should help her
na1pro18.speaker: Protagonist

na1pro19.dialogue: Agree to kill the Cult mage
na1pro19.speaker: Protagonist

na1pro20.dialogue: Tell her you will do as you please
na1pro20.speaker: Protagonist

na1pro21.dialogue: Refuse to do as she asks
na1pro21.speaker: Protagonist

na1pro22.dialogue: Ask why you should help her
na1pro22.speaker: Protagonist

na1pro23.dialogue: Agree to kill the Cult mage
na1pro23.speaker: Protagonist

na1pro24.dialogue: Tell her you will do as you please
na1pro24.speaker: Protagonist

na1pro25.dialogue: Refuse to do as she asks
na1pro25.speaker: Protagonist

na2Nat02.dialogue: Well, isn't this pretty. You have me at your mercy now. Kill me if you like. But then what I know will die with me.
na2Nat02.speaker: Nathlil

na2Nat03.dialogue: Release me, and I will teach you what I learned. It is of use to you.
na2Nat03.speaker: Nathlil

na2Nat04.dialogue: Be quick then. Our enemies grow stronger by the second.
na2Nat04.speaker: Nathlil

na2Nat05.dialogue: Prison disagrees with me - I grow forgetful. Release me and my memory may return.
na2Nat05.speaker: Nathlil

na2Nat06.dialogue: Go then. What care I how your tale ends?
na2Nat06.speaker: Nathlil

na2Nat07.dialogue: What I have learned will even the score. Open the door and I'll teach you what the dragonkin taught me.
na2Nat07.speaker: Nathlil

na2Nat08.dialogue: What, do you doubt my resolve? You fear that outside of this cage I'll waste a breath taking your lives? The hate that sings through me is for the enemy we share.
na2Nat08.speaker: Nathlil

na2Nat09.dialogue: Only the weak throw away knowledge for pride's sake.
na2Nat09.speaker: Nathlil

na2Nat10.dialogue: Go then. They will come for me soon. Their dracolich craves the power in my blood. In death or undeath, I will join my mate soon enough.
na2Nat10.speaker: Nathlil

na2Nat11.dialogue: Ah. My pale allies.  Your rescue comes too late to save Anesh and Belar, but still a welcome sight.
na2Nat11.speaker: Nathlil

na2Nat12.dialogue: Release me. I have learned much since last we met.
na2Nat12.speaker: Nathlil

na2Nat14.dialogue: Survived, have you? And in the end you did do me the favor I asked.
na2Nat14.speaker: Nathlil

na2Nat15.dialogue: Little good it did me. Anesh and Belar are dead, their blood fed to the Cult's dracolich. And I am next.
na2Nat15.speaker: Nathlil

na2Nat16.dialogue: But we are allies now, are we not? Release me, and I will teach you what I have learned.
na2Nat16.speaker: Nathlil

na2Nat17.dialogue: You should have killed that mage I told you of. He bore a staff that would have been of use to you.
na2Nat17.speaker: Nathlil

na2Nat18.dialogue: If not for him, Anesh and Belar might live yet. And I might not be a prisoner.
na2Nat18.speaker: Nathlil

na2Nat19.dialogue: But we are allies now, are we not?
na2Nat19.speaker: Nathlil

na2Nat20.dialogue: I was right to wager on you. Though little good it did me.
na2Nat20.speaker: Nathlil

na2Nat21.dialogue: Anesh and Belar are dead, their blood fed to the Cult's dracolich. And I am next if you leave me here.
na2Nat21.speaker: Nathlil

na2Nat22.dialogue: Release me, and I will teach you what I have learned.
na2Nat22.speaker: Nathlil

na2Nat23.dialogue: My people were lured here with promises of glory. The Freth told us that the Cult would give our houses dominion over Myth Drannor. Titles. Riches.
na2Nat23.speaker: Nathlil

na2Nat24.dialogue: Lies! The Kilsek were the price the Freth paid for power! Our blood fed to the Cult's dracolich. Our souls sucked from living bodies!
na2Nat24.speaker: Nathlil

na2Nat25.dialogue: You've seen my people - they're trapped between life and death. Slaves! Only I survive to free them.
na2Nat25.speaker: Nathlil

na2Nat26.dialogue: Release me! Let me fulfill my blood oath. And I will tell you what I've learned.
na2Nat26.speaker: Nathlil

na2Nat27.dialogue: What do you know of passion? Heat that drives life? The earth burns with it, and so do the hearts of my people.
na2Nat27.speaker: Nathlil

na2Nat28.dialogue: Two hearts, joined, burn hottest. Is it the same with you in your pale beds? Are your mates of value to you?
na2Nat28.speaker: Nathlil

na2Nat29.dialogue: The Cult has taken my mate. They have enslaved his soul. Darkness is no comfort to me now.
na2Nat29.speaker: Nathlil

na2Nat30.dialogue: I cannot restore his body to life, but I will free his soul to death. And my own soon after.
na2Nat30.speaker: Nathlil

na2Nat31.dialogue: Can you understand this? I care not. Release me. Let me find my way to him, and I will tell you what I've learned.
na2Nat31.speaker: Nathlil

na2Nat33.dialogue: The air is fresher on this side of the bars.  Don't worry, I'll keep my bargain. This knowledge cost Anesh and Belar their lives. Use it well.
na2Nat33.speaker: Nathlil
na2Nat33.desc: Spoken, with a deep breath, beat

na2Nat34.dialogue: You have seen my people in service to the Cult. Dead but not dead. The Cult have enslaved their souls.
na2Nat34.speaker: Nathlil

na2Nat35.dialogue: Their spirits are trapped in a great urn inside the castle - a Soul Vessel.
na2Nat35.speaker: Nathlil

na2Nat36.dialogue: Destroy the urn, and my kin will be freed to death. Kedar, my mate, will take his place in Lloth's web, and I will make quick to join him. The Kilsek drow will trouble you no more.
na2Nat36.speaker: Nathlil

na2Nat37.dialogue: I heard no particulars, only that it is vulnerable to a smashing weapon.
na2Nat37.speaker: Nathlil

na2Nat38.dialogue: They spoke of it in a great hall at the center of the castle, and laughed that it was guarded by those whose souls it held. I go to find it now.
na2Nat38.speaker: Nathlil

na2Nat39.dialogue: The Pool! Ssussan! I have seen it - in the great cavern beneath the castle. The Cult told us its touch would make us invulnerable to sunlight and give drow dominion over the surface world.
na2Nat39.speaker: Nathlil

na2Nat40.dialogue: Ha! Hope dulls the sharp blade. The Pool's touch brought death, and worse. My mate... My kin... I saw it strip their souls from them.
na2Nat40.speaker: Nathlil

na2Nat41.dialogue: I left them there, at the Cult's mercy. For that I must answer to Lloth. But first, I'll return and end this.
na2Nat41.speaker: Nathlil

na2Nat42.dialogue: You flatter yourselves. I take aid where necessity dictates, but don't imagine I'll soil myself walking sword to sword with surface crawlers.
na2Nat42.speaker: Nathlil

na2Nat43.dialogue: Let us say I must decline your generous offer.
na2Nat43.speaker: Nathlil

na2natYA.dialogue: Oh, it is I who thank you. And all the more so if you will keep far from me from now on.
na2natYA.speaker: nathlil

na2natYB.dialogue: Enough. The souls of my kin call to me. Lloth bless whichever of us lives to free her servants.
na2natYB.speaker: nathlil

na2Nat47.dialogue: If I free the souls of the Kilsek drow, their bodies can no longer serve the Cult.
na2Nat47.speaker: Nathlil

na2Nat48.dialogue: Surely it is of use to you if the Cult's guards crumble suddenly to dust.
na2Nat48.speaker: Nathlil

na2Nat49.dialogue: The dragonkin you slaughtered bear the key that opens this cage. Release me, and I will teach you what I learned.
na2Nat49.speaker: Nathlil

na2Nat51.dialogue: Come now, release me. With a bit more breathing space I could tell you what I've learned. It is of use to both of us.
na2Nat51.speaker: Nathlil

na2Nat52.dialogue: Ssussan! You waste time - and that is precious to us now. Search the dragonkin, they bear the key to this cell.
na2Nat52.speaker: Nathlil

na2Nat54.dialogue: I may leave this life under a Cult blade, but I will not be bored to death by chattering surface dwellers. Release me or leave me to my fate.
na2Nat54.speaker: Nathlil

Na9Nat05.dialogue: May you bring hell and chaos down upon the Cult, lightlings. I go to join my kin, and my mate.
Na9Nat05.speaker: Nathlil

no2not02.dialogue: Eh, now I suppose you'll be begging a reward from old Nottle.
no2not02.speaker: nottle

no2not03.dialogue: Well, if you're looking for a hard bargain, you've come to the right place.
no2not03.speaker: nottle

no2not04.dialogue: Something to aid your fallen comrade, maybe?
no2not04.speaker: nottle

no2not05.dialogue: Something to aid your fallen ones, maybe?
no2not05.speaker: nottle

no2not06.dialogue: Say, looks like you could use a healer.
no2not06.speaker: nottle

no2not07.dialogue: Do I look like a holy man? Bah. I'm a trader!
no2not07.speaker: nottle

no2not08.dialogue: Do I look like a holy man? Bah. I'm a trader! But you do look like you could use some help.
no2not08.speaker: nottle

no2not09.dialogue: Oh no, you must have a reward. Nottle the Trader owes a debt to no one!
no2not09.speaker: nottle

no2not10.dialogue: That would be nice, eh? So would a fire, and a nice warm supper, and an hour's peace.
no2not10.speaker: nottle

no2not11.dialogue: Wake up! You're in Myth Drannor. And I'm a trader, see? I can't be giving things away. Unless...
no2not11.speaker: nottle

no2not12.dialogue: It means I'm a trader, see? I can't afford to get all weepy about so-called good deeds.
no2not12.speaker: nottle

no2not13.dialogue: But I suppose I do owe you a little something.
no2not13.speaker: nottle

no2not14.dialogue: Here, tell you what, I'll tell you a little secret. I know a hidden spot, a safe place to go. Some people are hiding there - customers of mine, heh heh.
no2not14.speaker: nottle

no2not15.dialogue: You help them, they help you - I keep my customers alive - everybody is happy, eh? I think that's fair payment for your good deed.
no2not15.speaker: nottle

no2not17.dialogue: I got a wagon here filled with a bit o' everthing. If'n you got the gold, I'll sell you arrows, swords, whatever you want.
no2not17.speaker: nottle

no2not18.dialogue: But let's settle this account first. I don't like to be owing anybody anything.
no2not18.speaker: nottle

no2not19.dialogue: Ah, but if I tell you my secret, you're as good as healed.
no2not19.speaker: nottle

no2not20.dialogue: Let me put it this way - one of 'ums a good healer.
no2not20.speaker: nottle

no2not22.dialogue: Hey! I'm trying to give you something! Hard enough for me to do, without you asking a bunch of fool questions! So just be quiet a minute.
no2not22.speaker: nottle

no2not23.dialogue: But let's settle accounts first - I don't like to be owing anybody anything. So - listen carefully...
no2not23.speaker: nottle

no2not24.dialogue: Hey, just let me tell you my secret, all right? Then I'm outta debt to you, and you're as good as healed. So - listen carefully...
no2not24.speaker: nottle

no2not25.dialogue: It's a deal then? I tell you the secret, and we're even? Arh, that's good. Now listen carefully. I'm gonna teach you a Word of Power.
no2not25.speaker: nottle

no2not26.dialogue: Ahhh, no you don't. Let's settle this first - I don't like to be owing anybody anything. So listen carefully...
no2not26.speaker: nottle

no2not27.dialogue: Now you know a Word of Power - the Knocking Word. Go to the big tree stump to the west, across the river from here. The Word will speak itself, and get you into the secret place.
no2not27.speaker: nottle

no2not28.dialogue: Now get on your way. Come back and see me if you got any gold to spend. I'll help lighten your load, heh heh.
no2not28.speaker: nottle

no2not29.dialogue: I just taught you the Knocking Word. Words like it unseal glyphs. Very handy thing to know how to do, heh heh.
no2not29.speaker: nottle

no2not30.dialogue: I just taught you a Word of Power - the Knocking Word. These Words unseal glyphs. Very handy thing to know how to do, heh heh.
no2not30.speaker: nottle

no2not31.dialogue: Now that you know the Word, go find the big tree stump. It's got a glyph set next to it - the Glyph of the Hidden. Walk up to it, and the Word will speak itself! That will get you into the secret place.
no2not31.speaker: nottle

no2not32.dialogue: There. That's done. Don't be askin' me to repeat it. Arh, you're gettin' a bargain - don't get used to it - it'll never happen again.
no2not32.speaker: nottle

no2not33.dialogue: Bah, don't thank me. You can't fatten my purse if you're dead.
no2not33.speaker: nottle

no2not34.dialogue: Plumb west of here, across the river. Just follow the orcs, heh heh.
no2not34.speaker: nottle

no2not35.dialogue: Well now, you figured out the way to my heart, didn't you?
no2not35.speaker: nottle

no2not36.dialogue: But you can't just GIVE it to me - where's the sport in that?
no2not36.speaker: nottle

no2not37.dialogue: I'll get your money soon enough, heh heh. Come visit my shop later.
no2not37.speaker: nottle

no2not38.dialogue: Ah yes. Sooner or later, everyone trades with Nottle, heh heh.
no2not38.speaker: nottle

no2not40.dialogue: Ahhh, it's a tough life but a good one. Meet all kinds of creatures.
no2not40.speaker: nottle

no2not41.dialogue: I've got my wits to live on, and my wagon - it's got so many blarsted spells on it, I'm amazed it don't just burst into flames someday.
no2not41.speaker: nottle

no2not42.dialogue: I trade with anybody and everbody. Steal what I can. Cheat everyone just a little. That's the secret to success, heh heh!
no2not42.speaker: nottle

no2not44.dialogue: ...you better go use that Word I taught you. Come back if you want to see my shop.
no2not44.speaker: nottle

no2not45.dialogue: Ah, Myth Drannor - like they say, it's a glorious city. Treasure everywhere!
no2not45.speaker: nottle

no2not47.dialogue: That's enough about Myth Drannor. You want anything else?
no2not47.speaker: nottle

no2not48.dialogue: Alhoon are mindflaying beasties. Disgusting. Phaerrim are - uh - just be glad they're gone.
no2not48.speaker: nottle

no2not49.dialogue: It comes up from under, out of the dungeon lairs of alhoon and phaerrim.
no2not49.speaker: nottle

no2not50.dialogue: Something's been killing them off! Free treasure for everyone, heh heh.
no2not50.speaker: nottle

no2not51.dialogue: Enemies? I don't have any. Everyone likes Nottle the Trader, heh heh.
no2not51.speaker: nottle

no2not52.dialogue: But you... Watch out for orcs and orog. I've even met a few drow.
no2not52.speaker: nottle

no2not53.dialogue: Your worst enemy, of course, is whoever chirped those fellows from Phlan.
no2not53.speaker: nottle

no2not54.dialogue: I heard they was dead. Sorry to hear it. Athan was a good trader - sharp, you know? He brought me some good stuff.
no2not54.speaker: nottle

no2not55.dialogue: I'll try to find out who killed them, but... that kind of information don't come cheap.
no2not55.speaker: nottle

no2not56.dialogue: Orcs didn't chirp 'em, I'll tell you that for free.
no2not56.speaker: nottle

no2not57.dialogue: Pool of Radiance? Don't know anything about that.
no2not57.speaker: nottle

no2not59.dialogue: Yeah, time for me to open up shop.
no2not59.speaker: nottle

no2not60.dialogue: I told you already - no more bargains from me. See me again when you're ready to lighten your moneybags.
no2not60.speaker: nottle

no2not61.dialogue: Hey, that's enough talk. Go use that Word I taught you. See me again when you're ready to spend some gold.
no2not61.speaker: nottle

no2dmaYB.speaker: dm

no4not02.dialogue: Ha, now there's a sight more welcome than hot vittles.
no4not02.speaker: nottle

no4not03.dialogue: Do you have the Key of Dumathoin? You'll need it to barst this box open.
no4not03.speaker: nottle

no4not04.dialogue: By Halberin's beard, you're witless. Key - it's a key! You use it to open locked doors such as this one.
no4not04.speaker: nottle

no4not05.dialogue: Find it, and quick now, or I'll be on the Field of the Dead, cheating the damned out of their skulls!
no4not05.speaker: nottle

no4not06.dialogue: One of those Scarred Mages took it. He left here with a surly squad of orog.
no4not06.speaker: nottle

no4not07.dialogue: They're rough, but you could get that key off them if you wanted to, heh heh.
no4not07.speaker: nottle

no4not08.dialogue: They were on their way to the Room of Words. That's in the House of Gems - up, up, up from here.
no4not08.speaker: nottle

no4not09.dialogue: Come on now, show mercy on old Nottle. Unlock the door.
no4not09.speaker: nottle

no4not11.dialogue: The Key of Dumathoin. Could you hurry? Prison makes me jumpy.
no4not11.speaker: nottle

no4not12.dialogue: Oh, it's like that, is it? You're offering me the hard bargain?
no4not12.speaker: nottle

no4not13.dialogue: Well, I won't do it. Shame on you.
no4not13.speaker: nottle

no4not14.dialogue: Quite sure. You put a price on my freedom, and you'll regret it.
no4not14.speaker: nottle

no4not15.dialogue: I accept your apology. Now, by the rage of the Broken God, open that door.
no4not15.speaker: nottle

no4not16.dialogue: My freedom in exchange for information? Sure, heh heh. Just open the door.
no4not16.speaker: nottle

no4not17.dialogue: I say, shame. To take advantage of someone who's in a bad spot.
no4not17.speaker: nottle

no4not19.dialogue: Bah! You're trying to scare me into making a bad deal. That'll never work.
no4not19.speaker: nottle

no4not20.dialogue: All right! You win, curse you! Open the door, and I'll give you something you urgently need.
no4not20.speaker: nottle

no4not21.dialogue: Goodbye. You'll be back, key in hand.
no4not21.speaker: nottle

no4not22.dialogue: Aaah - can you smell it? The air is fresher out here. The smell of freedom!
no4not22.speaker: nottle
no4not22.desc: spoken - he's just been released from prison

no4not23.dialogue: Did I tell you how much I hate cages? And only a fiend's cage can keep hold of me, heh heh.
no4not23.speaker: nottle

no4not24.dialogue: Again I find myself in your debt! Bah! If I tell you something interesting, that will make us even, eh?
no4not24.speaker: nottle

no4not25.dialogue: Here, as I promised, I give you something you urgently need: a lesson in manners.
no4not25.speaker: nottle

no4not26.speaker: Nottle
no4not26.desc: spoken, LOCALIZERS please put a 3 second silent pause before the start of this line

no4not28.dialogue: Now I keep my promise - I'll tell you something I learned from the mages.
no4not28.speaker: nottle

no4not29.dialogue: I gotta get back to my wagon, so I'll rattle through this quick. If I told you I heard rumors of a treasure, a great treasure, are you interested?
no4not29.speaker: nottle

no4not30.dialogue: Well then, you'll want to seek out the Hoard of the Onaglym Dwarves. One of the most fabulous treasures in all Faerun!
no4not30.speaker: nottle

no4not31.dialogue: And it's probably less than a thousand steps from where we are right now - as the worm crawls, heh heh.
no4not31.speaker: nottle

no4not32.dialogue: 'Course, lots o' people been searching for it ever since the Wars. Nobody found even a single gem. But maybe you'll get lucky, eh?
no4not32.speaker: nottle

no4not33.dialogue: Those mages talked about something called the Helm Cleaver. It sounds powerful, eh?
no4not33.speaker: nottle

no4not34.dialogue: They said they had to show it to some orogs, and so it was being brought to the Dragon Room. Wherever that is. House o' Gems, maybe?
no4not34.speaker: nottle

no4not36.dialogue: Those mages whispered in fear about a black room, haunted by shadows. Somewheres nearby, I think.
no4not36.speaker: nottle

no4not37.dialogue: Which is interesting, because a long time ago I hears that something called the Mountain Fist was lost to a murder of shadows.
no4not37.speaker: nottle

no4not39.dialogue: Those mages lost a few of their pals to a den of arraccat nearby. They hate arraccat, and by the Black Hand, so do I! Hiding in shadows is no good with those bug-eyed beasts.
no4not39.speaker: nottle

no4not40.dialogue: You run into arraccat? Big, ugly, spider-looking beasts? You will, heh heh.
no4not40.speaker: nottle

no4not41.dialogue: The mages were whining about all the treasure their friends were carrying. Many jewels and much gold, and magic items too, I believe they said.
no4not41.speaker: nottle

no4not42.dialogue: And if you should find a pair of Gauntlets there, bring them to me at my wagon! I'll give you a fair price for them, oh yes, heh heh.
no4not42.speaker: nottle

no4not43.dialogue: Right-o. Now, if I told you I heard rumors of an ally for you, someone who might join your party and fight by your side, are you interested?
no4not43.speaker: nottle

no4not44.dialogue: I heard tell of a rogue around these parts - a thief of great skill, if somewhat lacking in judgment, heh heh. I'll find out what it takes to acquire his services.
no4not44.speaker: nottle

no4not45.dialogue: The mages gabbled about some intruders they caught - people they called the Silver Fire. But I guess not all of them got killed. Some are still loose, causing trouble, heh heh.
no4not45.speaker: nottle

no4not46.dialogue: A long time ago, someone told me about a man in a wight's barrow. But he wasn't dead - cold and stiff, but not dead.
no4not46.speaker: nottle

no4not47.dialogue: I believe the mages might have another prisoner!
no4not47.speaker: nottle

no4not48.dialogue: They said he had to go up to the upper floors of this dungeon. Something about a skeleton's arm? Didn't make much sense.
no4not48.speaker: nottle

no4not50.dialogue: Finally - if I told you about some barstly strong magic things, such as the Inferno Knife and the Spell Chain of Sarg, are you interested?
no4not50.speaker: nottle

no4not51.dialogue: Good! Because I'm hopin' you'll find 'em and sell 'em to me at my wagon. I'll be seeing you...
no4not51.speaker: nottle

no4not52.dialogue: Farewell. Hope you find lots of treasure, heh heh. See you at my wagon!
no4not52.speaker: nottle

kvqnot03.speaker: Nottle

nx4not01.dialogue: Ah, I always knew you could do it, to wreck the Cult and tumble the dracolich down to the Forgotten Place.
nx4not01.speaker: Nottle

nx4not02.speaker: Nottle

jzwozxYA.dialogue: Huluk! Go away! This loot ours!
jzwozxYA.speaker: orcgnt15

jzwnob03.dialogue: Huk, huluk, we take loot from orcs, weakling orcs of Mol. We orcs of Zud! Zud orcs be strong! You go away now.
jzwnob03.speaker: nobody

jzwnob05.dialogue: 'Surr-enn-dur.' We orcs of Zud! We not know what that word means! You make us angry.
jzwnob05.speaker: nobody

jzwnob07.dialogue: You not go away fast enough.
jzwnob07.speaker: nobody

jzwnob09.dialogue: Hammer, yes, ring, yes. Strong things for Zud, we hide them. We orcs of Zud! Zud orcs be strong! You go away now.
jzwnob09.speaker: nobody

jzwnob11.dialogue: Mol! Mol is weakling, weaklings speak of Mol. You make us angry.
jzwnob11.speaker: nobody

jzwnob13.dialogue: Zud! Zud! We orcs of Zud. Zud lord of the Great Hall. Zud makes orcs strong. Strong orcs get loot! You go away now.
jzwnob13.speaker: nobody

jzwpro02.dialogue: Ask them what the loot is
jzwpro02.speaker: Protagonist

jzwpro03.dialogue: Ask them where they got the loot
jzwpro03.speaker: Protagonist

jzwpro05.dialogue: Take your leave of the orcs
jzwpro05.speaker: Protagonist

zjgDMYA.dialogue: It seems this platform once connected with the raised walkway to the south.
zjgDMYA.speaker: DM

zjgDMYB.dialogue: Today, however, the magic is lost.
zjgDMYB.speaker: DM

vaadma00.dialogue: When the last orc falls, something clatters out of his grasp - a round blue stone bound in bands of iron.
vaadma00.speaker: DM

vaadma01.dialogue: Try as you might, you can't figure out a use for the thing - or break the bands that encircle it.
vaadma01.speaker: DM

vagdma00.dialogue: Even in his death throes, one of the lizardfolk tries to keep something concealed...
vagdma00.speaker: DM

vagdma01.dialogue: You find a short stabbing spear tucked behind his back. It is cruelly sharp, excellently made, and obviously ensorcelled with powerful spells of destruction.
vagdma01.speaker: DM

vagdma02.dialogue: Even as his life ebbs, one of the orog tries to hide something...
vagdma02.speaker: DM

vagdma03.dialogue: You find a short stabbing spear wrapped in skins. It is cruelly sharp, excellently made, and obviously ensorcelled with powerful spells of destruction.
vagdma03.speaker: DM

nrtdma02.dialogue: In this cave, a dense mortar of sand and clay has been used to cement together a wall of odd-shaped stones.
nrtdma02.speaker: DM

nrtdma03.dialogue: It is set back from the entrance, and doesn't quite reach all the way to the ceiling.  An old, earthy odor flows down from the small opening at the top.
nrtdma03.speaker: DM

nrtdma04.dialogue: The wall is unyielding to pressure, but appears designed to be pushed out from the other side.
nrtdma04.speaker: DM

nrtdma06.dialogue: Your dwarf nods at the crude, but sturdy, stonework, commenting that pushing against the wall would be fruitless, since it is well supported from the other side.
nrtdma06.speaker: DM

nrtdma08.dialogue: Your ranger inspects the patterns of the deep tracks in the dried mud at the base of the structure, and concludes that large, booted humanoids built the wall within the last few seasons.
nrtdma08.speaker: DM

nrtdma11.dialogue: This cave entrance is blocked by a rock wall which cannot be pushed in or smashed from this side.
nrtdma11.speaker: DM

nrtdma13.dialogue: You step over the rubble of the stone-and-mortar wall, and see a single clear passage leading away into the darkness.
nrtdma13.speaker: DM

nrtdma15.dialogue: Peering into the cave, you see two clear ways, each heading a different direction into darkness.
nrtdma15.speaker: DM

nrtdma17.dialogue: You can make out a few blocked or overgrown passageways leading from the back of the cave.
nrtdma17.speaker: DM

nrtdma18.dialogue: But only three of them are clear and easily usable.
nrtdma18.speaker: DM

nrtdma20.dialogue: A network of tunnels and halls leads out of the cave, but several are choked with debris and rubble.
nrtdma20.speaker: DM

nrtdma21.dialogue: A handful of them are fit to use.
nrtdma21.speaker: DM

nrtdma23.dialogue: Stairways and tunnels seems to lead out of the cave in every direction, but the entrances to a few have collapsed.
nrtdma23.speaker: DM

nrtdma26.dialogue: A branching network of passages begins in this cave.
nrtdma26.speaker: DM

nrtdma27.dialogue: All entrances are clear and open for use.
nrtdma27.speaker: DM

nrtdma29.dialogue: You see a single clear passage leading away into the darkness.
nrtdma29.speaker: DM

nrtpro00.dialogue: Return to the Halls of Light
nrtpro00.speaker: Protagonist

nrtdma30.dialogue: You climb a short tunnel, returning to the Halls of Light.
nrtdma30.speaker: DM

nrtpro01.dialogue: Return to the Halls of Stone
nrtpro01.speaker: Protagonist

nrtdma31.dialogue: You climb up through a hallway to the Halls of Stone.
nrtdma31.speaker: DM

nrtpro02.dialogue: Return to the tombs of the Main Halls
nrtpro02.speaker: Protagonist

nrtdma32.dialogue: You follow a winding passage back to the tombs of the Main Halls.
nrtdma32.speaker: DM

nrtpro03.dialogue: Return to the mines of the Main Halls
nrtpro03.speaker: Protagonist

nrtdma33.dialogue: You follow the rocky tunnel back to the mines of the Main Halls.
nrtdma33.speaker: DM

nrtpro04.dialogue: Return to the Lizardfolk Camp in the Deep Halls
nrtpro04.speaker: Protagonist

nrtdma34.dialogue: You climb down the stone ladder, returning to the Lizardfolk Camp in the Deep Halls.
nrtdma34.speaker: DM

nrtpro05.dialogue: Return to the Ceremonial Court in the Deep Halls
nrtpro05.speaker: Protagonist

nrtdma35.dialogue: You descend several short flights of stairs to the Ceremonial Court in the Deep Halls.
nrtdma35.speaker: DM

nrtpro06.dialogue: Return to the Naga's Lair in the First Cellar
nrtpro06.speaker: Protagonist

nrtdma36.dialogue: You walk down the dirt-floored tunnel to the Dark Naga's Lair in the First Cellar of the Catacombs.
nrtdma36.speaker: DM

nrtpro07.dialogue: Return to the Margolye Chasm in the Second Cellar
nrtpro07.speaker: Protagonist

nrtdma37.dialogue: You descend several short ramps to the Margoyle Chasm in the Second Cellar of the Catacombs.
nrtdma37.speaker: DM

nrtpro08.dialogue: Return to the Cult Stronghold in the Second Cellar
nrtpro08.speaker: Protagonist

nrtdma38.dialogue: You climb down a cobwebbed stair, returning to the southern edge of the Second Cellar of the Catacombs.
nrtdma38.speaker: DM

nrtpro09.dialogue: Return to the prison cells of the Lower Keep
nrtpro09.speaker: Protagonist

nrtdma39.dialogue: You decsend a long sprial stair, returning to the prison cells of the Lower Keep of the Catacombs.
nrtdma39.speaker: DM

nrtpro10.dialogue: Return to the far northeast of the Lower Keep
nrtpro10.speaker: Protagonist

nrtdma40.dialogue: You ascend a long, narrow stair which ends in the northeast corner of the Lower Keep of the Catacombs.
nrtdma40.speaker: DM

nrtdma41.dialogue: You climb down several hundered steps, returning to the Catacomb Prisons.
nrtdma41.speaker: DM

nrtdma42.dialogue: You make your way back to the tunnel of the Lizardfolk.
nrtdma42.speaker: DM

nrtpro13.dialogue: Return to the Passage to Castle Cormanthor
nrtpro13.speaker: Protagonist

nrtdma43.dialogue: You slither back down through the narrow stone channel, returning to the Passage to Castle Cormanthor.
nrtdma43.speaker: DM

od5ode03.dialogue: Tarry a moment, favored of Shaundakul! Speak to me, and I will tell you of the places I have seen in Myth Drannor...
od5ode03.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode04.dialogue: ...and tales I have heard of the City Heights, and the dungeons underneath it, and of the Hall of Wizards, and the Catacombs deep below that famous ruin.
od5ode04.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode05.dialogue: Welcome back, Wind Riders! Ask me more about our city.
od5ode05.speaker: Odelinde
od5ode05.desc: spoken, proud to be of service

od5ode06.dialogue: I am glad you have returned. I heard a rumor, and feared greatly for your safety.
od5ode06.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode07.dialogue: Welcome back! The whispering winds told me you were returning, and other things besides.
od5ode07.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode08.dialogue: I am glad to see that Beshaba has not yet kissed you. I pray she ever fails!
od5ode08.speaker: Odelinde
od5ode08.desc: spoken, concerned; Beshaba is the goddess of ill fortune

od5ode09.dialogue: Travellers - I welcome you back. I have had some work to do - defending my shrine!
od5ode09.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode10.dialogue: Tymora be praised - for if we survive this, it will be luck indeed - by luck and by grace of the Wind Rider.
od5ode10.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode12.dialogue: That the Cult of the Dragon had learned of you, and realized their peril, and laid a deadly trap for you.
od5ode12.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode13.dialogue: Thank the gods that rumor was false!
od5ode13.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode14.dialogue: Beshaba is the Maid of Misfortune! How fortunate you are, never to have received a kiss from Tyche's Unpleasant Daughter.
od5ode14.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode15.dialogue: For those that feel her kiss regret it to the end of their days.
od5ode15.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode16.dialogue: Some dragon-like creatures, ugly beasts, with spellflingers of the Cult behind them. But the Wind Rider taught them how to fly, ha ha ha!
od5ode16.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode23.dialogue: Travellers, I have news for you! I met someone who roams about the city - one of your kind.
od5ode23.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode24.dialogue: Travellers! I have heard a voice, crying on the wind.
od5ode24.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode25.dialogue: Welcome back! The breeze blows strong - yet tales of your victories outfly it.
od5ode25.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode26.dialogue: Travellers! What know you of the Silver Fire? A tale has come to me about them.
od5ode26.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode27.dialogue: I tell you true - it has been hard, these last hours. Never before has the Helping Hand been so hard pressed.
od5ode27.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode30.dialogue: He was a trifle, little more than a gutter thief, but yet - he had a quick wit and a steady eye. He said his name was Tudo.
od5ode30.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode31.dialogue: It was a woman's voice, gentle yet strong - an elf high-born of a noble House, or I have never met one.
od5ode31.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode32.dialogue: 'The Mythal shall be free,' she said, and I believed her.
od5ode32.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode33.dialogue: 'My skull,' she said, 'where have they taken my skull?' And I wept to hear the pain in her voice.
od5ode33.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode34.dialogue: 'Mystra,' she cried, 'where are your children? I call, but none come.' And I wept to hear the pain in her voice.
od5ode34.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode35.dialogue: She sobbed for Mystra, the goddess of magic! I felt my heart would break, and called to her, but she did not answer, and went away wailing to the southwest.
od5ode35.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode36.dialogue: An eblis I know told me that twelve beings came into Myth Drannor from the South. He said they were 'Silver Fire,' but I do not know what that means.
od5ode36.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode37.dialogue: Not that it matters. For the eblis also told me that a dead dragon found them and breathed upon them, and they all died.
od5ode37.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode39.dialogue: The Cult of the Dragon. They came in force, and I tell you true, I would have perished, but they heard some dark call and vanished again, as suddenly as they came.
od5ode39.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode40.dialogue: Dark nagas - four of them. They harried me, but their puny god is no match for the Wind Rider! They slunk away to the south.
od5ode40.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode44.dialogue: Travellers! Far and wide, the wind gloats over your sharp victories against the Cult of the Dragon.
od5ode44.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode45.dialogue: Talk with me, travellers! I may know a tale or two of great use to you.
od5ode45.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode46.dialogue: I will tell you what I know of the city, and where helpful treasures might be found.
od5ode46.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode48.dialogue: Ask me what you will, O Favored of the Wind Rider. For evil yet lives in dark corners of our city, and it scoffs at your great victory.
od5ode48.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode49.dialogue: Well, travellers! Every breeze whispers new tales of your exploits!
od5ode49.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode50.dialogue: Favored Ones - welcome back to the Shrine of Shaundakul.
od5ode50.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode51.dialogue: I see the Winds of Fortune have blown you back to me.
od5ode51.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode52.dialogue: What tale may I tell you this time?
od5ode52.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode53.dialogue: The mistral winds told me you would return.
od5ode53.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode54.dialogue: Do you seek more tales, travellers?
od5ode54.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode55.dialogue: See, you return, with the Helpful Hand ever at your back.
od5ode55.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode57.dialogue: Ill news, travellers! I have no more tales for you... until the mistral winds brings me more.
od5ode57.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode58.dialogue: I can think of no more tales to tell you right now.
od5ode58.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode59.dialogue: Now, travellers, no more tales. You must be on your way.
od5ode59.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode60.dialogue: I have told you every tale I know.
od5ode60.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode64.dialogue: I was down in the Dungeons a fortnight ago, and I heard something strange - the sound of a jailer on his rounds, jingling his keys.
od5ode64.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode65.dialogue: I tried to locate him, but in vain! He was behind a wall, and I could not find a crack in it big enough to slip through.
od5ode65.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode66.dialogue: Down in the Main Halls it was, south of the round room where the Ormyrr keeps his orc prisoners.
od5ode66.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode69.dialogue: Here is a story. A mongrelman came through here, laden with a knapsack, and rested a time at this shrine.
od5ode69.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode70.dialogue: His kind often say little, and he was no different. But he did mention he was on his way into the Dungeons, to the Main Halls.
od5ode70.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode71.dialogue: When he took up his knapsack, I saw what was inside. Necklaces - dozens of them.
od5ode71.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode73.dialogue: O travelers, on your journeys, have you ever found the Man in the Stone?
od5ode73.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode74.dialogue: I have never seen him, but many who stay at my shrine swear he exists, somewhere in the Dungeons.
od5ode74.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode75.dialogue: From the waist up, he is a man. But from the waist down, he is a boulder! How he lives, how he eats - that is a riddle no one has been able to solve.
od5ode75.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode78.dialogue: Here is a tale that concerns the Dungeons. It happened to me many years ago.
od5ode78.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode79.dialogue: Some servants of a phaerrim came to molest Lord Shaundakul's shrine. Human they had been once, although they were no longer. And the leader of them wore a great golden arc around its neck - a magnificent Torc.
od5ode79.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode80.dialogue: I killed that human, and many of the others. But when I came to reclaim the Torc, it was gone. I can only think that someone took it back down into the Dungeons.
od5ode80.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode91.dialogue: I heard a tale from one of the lizardfolk, just before I killed him.
od5ode91.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode92.dialogue: He spoke of a magical Gate, which dropped foul-tasting undead creatures into the Dungeons as steadily as rainwater drips off a sattern leaf.
od5ode92.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode93.dialogue: The lizard swore that the humans of the Cult of the Dragon created this Gate. But I believe his master, Malgi Hi, actually brought it forth.
od5ode93.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode94.dialogue: I am wondering if, in your travels, you have come upon any talking books?
od5ode94.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode95.dialogue: I heard some orogs talking about some books such as that. Apparently these books wield such power that the orogs could not open them!
od5ode95.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode96.dialogue: But I also heard the orogs say they were evil books, and so I fear they must be destroyed somehow.
od5ode96.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode98.dialogue: When I was banished from my shrine, some of the lizardfolk were taunting me - from a safe distance, you may be sure.
od5ode98.speaker: Odelinde

od5ode99.dialogue: They claimed they held 'the secret waters of life.' And when I struck the arm from one of them, he ran back into the Dungeons, bawling for the Waters to restore him.
od5ode99.speaker: Odelinde

od5odea3.dialogue: I warn you, beware the arraccat! Especially down in the lowest levels of the Dungeons...
od5odea3.speaker: Odelinde

od5odea4.dialogue: ...many a cocksure traveler has been taken by them, and his possessions added to the growing heap of treasures that feather the arraccat nest.
od5odea4.speaker: Odelinde

od5odea6.dialogue: Here is a tale my mother told me. Once a mighty warrior strode into our city, wielding a mighty club - the Mountain Fist!
od5odea6.speaker: Odelinde

od5odea7.dialogue: He cast fear into the hearts of all, for he did not care whom he killed. If there was a challenge, or treasure that we wanted, he pursued and won it.
od5odea7.speaker: Odelinde

od5odea8.dialogue: But such arrogance rarely lives for long, and he was no exception. Deep underground, a chill of spirits overtook him, and drained his life, and now his name is forgotten even to himself.
od5odea8.speaker: Odelinde

od5odeb1.dialogue: Shall I tell you of the Earthborn Wind? It was a gift of Shaundakul to the dwarves of Myth Drannor...
od5odeb1.speaker: Odelinde

od5odeb2.dialogue: ...mysterious breezes to keep the city's underground air fresh and healthful. A Rillstone Ruby was at its heart, and Juliban Genshihir its last caretaker.
od5odeb2.speaker: Odelinde

od5odeb3.dialogue: Alas for us! The breezes stopped centuries ago, when Juliban died, and the Dungeons became an unhealthy place.
od5odeb3.speaker: Odelinde

od5odeb8.dialogue: Several orogs came to me, seeking refuge. I was sorry to send them away, but they were brought here by the Cult, and I did not trust them.
od5odeb8.speaker: Odelinde

od5odeb9.dialogue: They told me they had been driven out of the Catacombs by the drow, who also took from them all their treasures - weapons, armor, and an old bone relic or two.
od5odeb9.speaker: Odelinde

od5odec1.dialogue: I have been into the Catacombs many times - through cracks and crawl-holes. I do not know of a way in for those of your kind.
od5odec1.speaker: Odelinde

od5odec2.dialogue: Adventurers do get in somehow, from time to time... but when they do, the evil denizens of the Catacombs are quick to seal the entrances behind them. In particular, watch out for the dark nagas, the margoyles, and the plentiful undead.
od5odec2.speaker: Odelinde

od5odec4.dialogue: O travelers, you have probably seen for yourselves the many once-splendid wells and fountains which the dwarves crafted throughout Myth Drannor...
od5odec4.speaker: Odelinde

od5odec5.dialogue: I have seen for myself that not all of them are destroyed - in the deeper Catacombs especially, there are those that still brim with blessing waters.
od5odec5.speaker: Odelinde

od5odec6.dialogue: But beware! For some seem fair, yet are foul beneath the surface, and trap the unwary.
od5odec6.speaker: Odelinde

od5oded8.dialogue: Why, surely you know of the Baelnorn, the protector of old, who dwells deep in the Catacombs?
od5oded8.speaker: Odelinde

od5oded9.dialogue: He has been here since the city's Fall. But he comes forth less and less often. My grandmother saw him, but my mother has not, nor have I.
od5oded9.speaker: Odelinde

od5odee3.dialogue: Ah! The Hall of Wizards is one of the great buildings of Myth Drannor. Surely you have seen it, revered of Shaundakul? It is in the shape of a great dragon, embracing a great Egg.
od5odee3.speaker: Odelinde

od5odee4.dialogue: Even today it is the center of magic for Myth Drannor, although that magic has lost its purpose and drifted away from the wishes of those who summoned it.
od5odee4.speaker: Odelinde

od5odee5.dialogue: Much magic lives in the Hall of Wizards still, and I am reluctant to enter - although I have grown attached to Caalenfaire, and his companion Volun, who sometimes appear there.
od5odee5.speaker: Odelinde

od5odee7.dialogue: Have you seen the Orrery in the Hall of Wizards? An orrery is a device to track the positions of the planets...
od5odee7.speaker: Odelinde

od5odee8.dialogue: ...although it always seemed strange to me, to build such a grand device to do something so simple. If you wish to know the positions of the planets, why not look up into the sky?
od5odee8.speaker: Odelinde

od5odee9.dialogue: Sadly, the Orrery no longer functions. Some of the Stones that were its planets have long been missing, although I saw the Blue Planet not long ago, in the hands of other travelers of your kind.
od5odee9.speaker: Odelinde

od5odef1.dialogue: There are many passages near the Hall of Wizards. Is it true that wizards of your kind are not fond of walking?
od5odef1.speaker: Odelinde

od5odef2.dialogue: Inside the Hall of Wizards is the Rhonglyn, a device that moves from floor to floor in the Dungeons. Right outside is the Spire of Mythanthor, which now opens the way again into the Dungeons, thanks to you.
od5odef2.speaker: Odelinde

od5odef3.dialogue: In the amphitheatre is the Circle of Ualair, which I see has been opened! I suppose that is also your doing? The Wind Rider thanks you for that - he loves to open what was shut, and let the wind do its work.
od5odef3.speaker: Odelinde

od5odef4.dialogue: In the center of the amphitheatre is the Circle of Ualair, which led into the Catacombs under the castle, once upon a time. Those were more peaceful days.
od5odef4.speaker: Odelinde

od5odef8.dialogue: Ah, the Castle, do not go there! For years after the city fell, the Castle repelled evil invaders. Dwarf, elf and gnome had conspired to create many a trap for them... barricades... silent guardians...
od5odef8.speaker: Odelinde

od5odef9.dialogue: But over the centuries, these ancient defenses wore out. I do not know if any remain. Now dark things nest in the aeries and strongrooms of Castle Cormanthor.
od5odef9.speaker: Odelinde

od5odeg1.dialogue: Favored ones! Shaundakul's bright wind has swirled all around Castle Cormanthor. In vain has it looked for a way for you to enter there.
od5odeg1.speaker: Odelinde

od5odeg2.dialogue: The ones who hold it have closed up every entrance, save the one in the aerie where the dragon-kin come in and out.
od5odeg2.speaker: Odelinde

od5odeg5.dialogue: Oh, Hand of Beshaba! I have dire news about that place. For once again the great dracolich Pelendralaar has been seen to leave the Castle, and go to hunt again among the ruins of Myth Drannor.
od5odeg5.speaker: Odelinde

od5odeg6.dialogue: He and his minions have already searched out all the powerful creatures of the city. Phaerrim, alhoon, clutch of baatezu - it mattered not, he drove them all from the city, or sent them smoking to their deaths...
od5odeg6.speaker: Odelinde

od5odeg7.dialogue: But now it seems he searches for someone else. If you approach the Castle in the open air, beware!
od5odeg7.speaker: Odelinde

od5odeh0.dialogue: Listen! For I heard a tale from a passing Ormyrr. She said she has seen all manner of creatures come up from deep underground - driven out into the light by the Cult.
od5odeh0.speaker: Odelinde

od5odeh1.dialogue: The creatures told the Ormyrr that the Cult has sealed the underground approaches to the Castle. They do not use passageways, you see - they create magical gates, and use those to get from stronghold to stronghold.
od5odeh1.speaker: Odelinde

od5odeh9.dialogue: Here is an alarming thing - something has tainted the city's water!
od5odeh9.speaker: Odelinde

od5odei0.dialogue: Ever since I have lived here, the water has been pure and wonderful to drink. I think maybe a guardian of some kind watches over it - I imagined sometimes I heard someone singing.
od5odei0.speaker: Odelinde

od5odei1.dialogue: But of late the water has been foul, and the city fountains burble no more. Woe to the dwarves, that their great waterworks should fail at last after so long a service.
od5odei1.speaker: Odelinde

od5odeYB.dialogue: Now here is a thing. Orogs approached me - respectful of my fangs, you may be sure!
od5odeYB.speaker: Odelinde

od5odeYC.dialogue: They wished me to help them recover a thing called the Helm Cleaver. But what use is such a thing for me? I snapped at them and sent them running, back into the House of Gems.
od5odeYC.speaker: Odelinde

od5odei4.dialogue: As you walk near the Hall of Wizards, beware of gargoyles! They delight in ambushes here, flying low and swooping up to appear without warning.
od5odei4.speaker: Odelinde

od5odei5.dialogue: I wish I still had the Stone Mouth. Have you heard of it? It is a stone that enables you to understand the speech of gargoyles and margoyles.
od5odei5.speaker: Odelinde

od5odei6.dialogue: It was helpful in dealing with them and frustrating their attacks. But the Stone Mouth was stolen from my shrine many years ago.
od5odei6.speaker: Odelinde

od5odej0.dialogue: To the east of here, you might find a barrow, if it has not collapsed or been sealed.
od5odej0.speaker: Odelinde

od5odej1.dialogue: There is a weapon there, such as your kind like to use, enchanted with a warrior's voice. Pay heed to its warning! That is all I can tell you.
od5odej1.speaker: Odelinde

od5odej4.dialogue: East of here, there is a garden, with a patch of dark-stained earth. Approach it carefully, travelers! For that is Thirsty Ground.
od5odej4.speaker: Odelinde

od5odej5.dialogue: Once it was a beautiful garden that gave comfort to those who watered it with their tears. But the Weeping Wars changed it forever, as wars do.
od5odej5.speaker: Odelinde

od5odej6.dialogue: It may aid you if your need is dire - if you have been touched by wraiths, or kissed by spectres, or fallen under a curse, or if there are many dead among you.
od5odej6.speaker: Odelinde

od5odej7.dialogue: But beware! For the payment it seeks is your bloodlife itself, and it does not sip daintily.
od5odej7.speaker: Odelinde

od5odej8.dialogue: East of here, you will find the great Ear of the City. It is a Pillar beloved of Shaundakul, that listens to the voices on the wind, and remembers what they say.
od5odej8.speaker: Odelinde

od5odej9.dialogue: But it is hard to get to, for beasts surround the Pillar, and strive to drown it out with their grumbling voices and shrieking cries. And of late they have grown very strong.
od5odej9.speaker: Odelinde

od5odek3.dialogue: Have you looked in the Scrying Mirror, there in the Hall of Wizards?
od5odek3.speaker: Odelinde

od5odek4.dialogue: If you do, it will show you things far away, things that are close to your heart or hanging like a sword over your life, even if you know it not.
od5odek4.speaker: Odelinde

od5odek7.dialogue: Away to the southwest, you will find the lizardfolk village. Beware! They relish all humankind as food. Yet they themselves are not very good eating.
od5odek7.speaker: Odelinde

od5odek8.dialogue: Once they were a friendly people - or at least not openly enemies of good. But they have a leader now, strong in magic, who styles himself Malgi Hi.
od5odek8.speaker: Odelinde

od5odek9.dialogue: Malgi Hi has raised a great idol, and put a stone, bound in iron, in place as its one fiery eye. And under its influence the lizards seem to grow in cruelty and cunning.
od5odek9.speaker: Odelinde

od5odel1.dialogue: Here is a sad story! Not so long ago, pilgrims of Mystra flocked to the area to the southwest, where the beautiful Shrine to Mystra stood, once upon a time.
od5odel1.speaker: Odelinde

od5odel2.dialogue: They came here because a ghost of the shrine would sometimes appear where the building once stood. So the splendor of the shrine was not totally lost!
od5odel2.speaker: Odelinde

od5odel3.dialogue: But the area grew more dangerous, and the pilgrims stopped coming. So the shrine faded. Now a foul Spawn Pool has risen on the spot, guarded by my dark brethren.
od5odel3.speaker: Odelinde

od5odel5.dialogue: There is little I can tell you about the stone idol, abandoned in the ruins to the southwest. Whatever purpose it may hold is of no use to nagas.
od5odel5.speaker: Odelinde

od5odel6.dialogue: Maybe you can ask the ormyrrs about that area. I have seen them linger at the idol, and Nottle as well. They may know more about it.
od5odel6.speaker: Odelinde

od5odem7.dialogue: I am worried about the Ormyrrs. Have you met them? They live away in the marshes to the southeast.
od5odem7.speaker: Odelinde

od5odem8.dialogue: They have been friendly to travelers - and Shaundakul smiles on such creatures, and blesses them, even if they worship him not.
od5odem8.speaker: Odelinde

od5odem9.dialogue: But lately I heard a rumor that they no longer follow this path - indeed, that they took up arms against some sojourning alaghi, and killed them. And friendly breezes no longer blow to me from the southeast.
od5odem9.speaker: Odelinde

od5oden4.dialogue: Listen, travelers! Turn your hearts toward the House of Gems to the east. Too long has it been silent and neglected, the gathering-place of dust and cobwebs.
od5oden4.speaker: Odelinde

od5oden6.dialogue: Travelers, enough talk about this place and that. The Guiding Wind blows eastward. Let your feet follow the breath of Shaundakul.
od5oden6.speaker: Odelinde

od5oden8.dialogue: Enough, Favored of the Wind Rider! I have talked with you long enough. You seek the Wizard's Torc, or so the winds have whispered to me...
od5oden8.speaker: Odelinde

od5oden9.dialogue: ...but you will not find it by trading tales with me. Be on your way!
od5oden9.speaker: Odelinde

od5odeo1.dialogue: I know no more about that area. But I do know that your steps need to lead into the Catacombs. Go now - with the Wind Rider ever at your back.
od5odeo1.speaker: Odelinde

od5odeo3.dialogue: That is enough talk! I have places to go. And you - your steps lead again to the Catacombs, or I am a fool. Now, be on your way!
od5odeo3.speaker: Odelinde

od5odeo5.dialogue: Travelers, I should not say more. These matters are deep, beyond my simple devotion. Go talk to the ghost of Anorrweyn Evensong! She can help you when I cannot.
od5odeo5.speaker: Odelinde

od5odeo9.dialogue: Beloved ones! Suddenly I realize where you should go. To the roof of the Speculum! There is a gate at the dragon's foot, it should not be hard to get there. Now, off with you!
od5odeo9.speaker: Odelinde

od5odep2.dialogue: Now, enough talk! You must find the Pool, and destroy it... you have a long way to go. May Shaunakul's blessing go with you.
od5odep2.speaker: Odelinde

od5odep4.dialogue: That is all I know about the Dungeons, O Favored Ones.
od5odep4.speaker: Odelinde

od5odep5.dialogue: That is all I can tell you for now, about city places up on the surface.
od5odep5.speaker: Odelinde

od5odep6.dialogue: But travelers, that is all I know about the Wizards' Hall.
od5odep6.speaker: Odelinde

od5odep7.dialogue: I can tell you no more about the Catacombs. Maybe later, I will know more.
od5odep7.speaker: Odelinde

od5odep8.dialogue: I have told you all I know about the upper reaches of the Catacombs.
od5odep8.speaker: Odelinde

od5odep9.dialogue: There is little more to say about the deep Catacombs - except that it is a mysterious place, and dangerous.
od5odep9.speaker: Odelinde

od5odeq0.dialogue: I have nothing more to tell you about the Castle - but I will try to find out more.
od5odeq0.speaker: Odelinde

od5odeq1.dialogue: I have told you everything I know about the other places of Myth Drannor.
od5odeq1.speaker: Odelinde

od5odeq2.dialogue: You need not worry about the Dungeons. Your thoughts must go back to Castle Cormanthor, and your destiny.
od5odeq2.speaker: Odelinde

od5odeq3.dialogue: Worry not about the Catacombs! Your path winds back to Castle Cormanthor.
od5odeq3.speaker: Odelinde

od5odeq4.dialogue: No more talk about the Castle! The enemy awaits you there - what else do you need to know?
od5odeq4.speaker: Odelinde

od5odeq5.dialogue: Travelers, enough tales! You must be on your way, back to the Castle.
od5odeq5.speaker: Odelinde

od5odeq6.dialogue: I have told you all the dungeon tales I know.
od5odeq6.speaker: Odelinde

od5odeq7.dialogue: Favored Ones, I have already told you all the catacomb tales I know.
od5odeq7.speaker: Odelinde

od5odeq8.dialogue: Wind Travelers, you've heard all I know about the City Heights.
od5odeq8.speaker: Odelinde

od5odeq9.dialogue: You've heard every tale I know about them.
od5odeq9.speaker: Odelinde

od5oder0.dialogue: Journey with care, travellers. Come back, if ever you need the Helping Hand.
od5oder0.speaker: Odelinde

od5oder1.dialogue: Fare you well, until again I may trade tales with you, in the name of the Wind Rider.
od5oder1.speaker: Odelinde

od5oder4.dialogue: Walk with his Hand on you, until we meet again.
od5oder4.speaker: Odelinde

od5oder5.dialogue: Goodbye, Favored of the Wind Rider!
od5oder5.speaker: Odelinde

Od1Ode02.dialogue: Hold! In the name of all that is light! My need is dire. Will you rise to aid me?
Od1Ode02.speaker: Odelinde

Od1Ode03.dialogue: You who wear the blood of the dark naga, I beg you - help me drive out evil from my home!
Od1Ode03.speaker: Odelinde

Od1Ode04.dialogue: Orcs despoil my home, the temple of Lord Shaundakul.
Od1Ode04.speaker: Odelinde

Od1Ode05.dialogue: I was hunting in the ruins - the lizardfolk are fat this time of year. When I returned, the orc filth had overrun my shrine. They raised an idol to Gruumsh on my Lord's altar and frolicked before it!
Od1Ode05.speaker: Odelinde

Od1Ode06.dialogue: Sssss! My fangs dripped at the sight! I coiled to strike, but a pool of ichor bubbled up out of the ground before me. Its scent is pure evil. Hungry. Unslakable. It drew my strength from me like water from a well.
Od1Ode06.speaker: Odelinde

Od1Ode07.dialogue: The pool basks in the orcs' foulness. While it thrives there, I am helpless to destroy them!
Od1Ode07.speaker: Odelinde

Od1Ode08.dialogue: The orcs' sacrilege spawned the pool. It feeds on the abomination that their idol brings to that sacred place.
Od1Ode08.speaker: Odelinde

Od1Ode09.dialogue: If the idol is destroyed, the balance of good will be restored. The spawning pool must seep back from whence it came.
Od1Ode09.speaker: Odelinde

Od1Ode10.dialogue: I am Odelinde, guardian naga and priestess of Shaundakul the Wind Rider. My family has watched over his temple for generations.
Od1Ode10.speaker: Odelinde

Od1Ode11.dialogue: My mother, her mother before her, and so on down the centuries, all of us dedicated to the Helping Hand. And I am the last. I cannot fail them!
Od1Ode11.speaker: Odelinde

Od1Ode12.dialogue: Shaundakul is He who reaches out to adventurers in need. But now it is He who is in need, and I who must reach out to you.
Od1Ode12.speaker: Odelinde

Od1Ode14.dialogue: Orc corpses are like to yield some plunder, but when his temple is restored, Shaundakul's gifts will be more use to travelers than mere gold.
Od1Ode14.speaker: Odelinde

Od1Ode15.dialogue: To the north and west, in a circle of columns that lies open to the wind. Hurry, I implore you!
Od1Ode15.speaker: Odelinde

Od1Ode16.dialogue: To the west, in a circle of columns that lies open to the wind. Hurry, I implore you!
Od1Ode16.speaker: Odelinde

Od1Ode17.dialogue: My fangs only strike at the enemies of good. It is the way of my kind.
Od1Ode17.speaker: Odelinde

Od1Ode18.dialogue: Caalenfaire is known to me. If he looked up from his divinations to speak my name to you, your cause must be great indeed.
Od1Ode18.speaker: Odelinde

Od1Ode19.dialogue: But it is my Lord who aids, I am only his Hand. And aid is lost to us while his temple is fouled.
Od1Ode19.speaker: Odelinde

Od1Ode20.dialogue: My mother told me tales of this dwarf lord, when I was wet from the egg.
Od1Ode20.speaker: Odelinde

Od1Ode21.dialogue: But what use are ghosts now? My Lord needs flesh, bone, and steel to rid his temple of this desecration!
Od1Ode21.speaker: Odelinde

Od1Ode22.dialogue: I reach out to you in need, travelers.
Od1Ode22.speaker: Odelinde

Od1Ode23.dialogue: Help me to cleanse my home of Gruumsh's filth and the hand of the Wind Rider will be opened to you. His gifts are great aid to adventurers in this harsh place.
Od1Ode23.speaker: Odelinde

Od1Ode24.dialogue: While the orc idol squats on my Lord's altar, the spawn pool keeps me at bay.
Od1Ode24.speaker: Odelinde

Od1Ode25.dialogue: Go where the wind takes you, then. If it brings you this way again, look for me at Lord Shaundakul's shrine.
Od1Ode25.speaker: Odelinde

Od1Ode26.dialogue: There I will strive to destroy the abomination that fouls it, so I can return to His work once again.
Od1Ode26.speaker: Odelinde

Od2Ode03.dialogue: Your courage has restored my Lord's temple. May you be refreshed and replenished, Favored of Shaundakul.
Od2Ode03.speaker: Odelinde
Od2Ode03.desc: Spoken, grateful for your help, she casts a spell

Od2DM00.dialogue: The naga's spell rests and heals the party.
Od2DM00.speaker: DM

Od2Ode05.dialogue: The spawn pool has retreated for now, but I must stay vigilant against its return. I have seen its kind in the ruins to the south: once they have broken ground, they seek to rise again.
Od2Ode05.speaker: Odelinde

Od2Ode06.dialogue: The Mythal once helped to keep such things at bay. But our guardian spell is changed of late. Even the blueglow moss sickens and dies.
Od2Ode06.speaker: Odelinde

Od2Ode07.dialogue: I am Odelinde, guardian naga and priestess of Shaundakul the Wind Rider. My family has watched over his temple for generations.
Od2Ode07.speaker: Odelinde

Od2Ode08.dialogue: Caalenfaire! If he has looked up from his divinations to speak with you, your fate must be quickwoven indeed. Only the most powerful of destinies command his interest. Where I can aid you I will.
Od2Ode08.speaker: Odelinde

Od2Ode09.dialogue: Can it be? When I was a hatchling, my grandmother sang a song about a Pool of Radiance. The Pool that promises eternal life... But these spawn pools bring only death.
Od2Ode09.speaker: Odelinde

Od2Ode10.dialogue: There's an old entrance to the dwarven dungeons just west of here. They must have crawled up from there.
Od2Ode10.speaker: Odelinde

Od2Ode11.dialogue: I was off hunting when they infested my shrine.  By the time I returned, they had raised their idol and the spawn pool had bubbled up to bask in the sacrilege. Its loathsome emanations kept me from slaughtering the orcs.
Od2Ode11.speaker: Odelinde

Od2Ode12.dialogue: Be assured I'll be waiting if they come this way again. Orc gut is not so sweet as lizard flesh, but it suffices.
Od2Ode12.speaker: Odelinde

Od2Ode13.dialogue: Harldain has been dead for centuries. But even now, he is not free to abandon his caretaking. Some curse or misfortune binds him to this city.
Od2Ode13.speaker: Odelinde

Od2Ode14.dialogue: His spirit still haunts the House of Gems, to the east and north of here. Be wary if you seek him there. Its traps and secret perils keep most living creatures from venturing inside.
Od2Ode14.speaker: Odelinde

Od2Ode15.dialogue: It is an ancient benison from the Mythal. When it thrives, the blueglow moss has healing properties. Gather it wherever you may find it and use it like a balm on your wounds.
Od2Ode15.speaker: Odelinde

Od2Ode16.dialogue: Abomination and newly hatched evil draws them like a seedling to sunlight. Destroy the evil and the pool retreats.
Od2Ode16.speaker: Odelinde

Od2Ode17.dialogue: But the pools are just symptoms of a greater ill. Like the orc incursions and the withering of the blue glow moss. Something has taken hold of the Mythal, or none of these evils would be possible.
Od2Ode17.speaker: Odelinde

Od2Ode18.dialogue: If the Mythal could be restored, it would shield us again. But that lore is beyond me.
Od2Ode18.speaker: Odelinde

Od2Ode19.dialogue: In my great-great-grandmother's time, the Mythal was a shield over the city. But its guardianship deteriorates as the centuries pass.
Od2Ode19.speaker: Odelinde

Od2Ode20.dialogue: Of late its powers seem reversed. Harming where once it helped. As if a dark hand shapes it.
Od2Ode20.speaker: Odelinde

Od2Ode21.dialogue: The great mage Mythanthor cast the Mythal in the Year of the Soaring Stars, with the mages of the Coronal's high court.
Od2Ode21.speaker: Odelinde

Od2Ode22.dialogue: The songs say that he gave his life in the casting of it, sacrificing himself so that elf, dwarf, and human might live together in peace under its protective shield.
Od2Ode22.speaker: Odelinde

Od2Ode23.dialogue: Its blessings were wondrous then, if you believe the tales - flight, everlight, near immortality. But its powers have faded since the city fell to ruin.
Od2Ode23.speaker: Odelinde

Od2Ode24.dialogue: The guardian spell had its own protectors once, souls dedicated to its upkeep and lore. In my mother's time, one still roamed the city as a spirit.
Od2Ode24.speaker: Odelinde

Od2Ode25.dialogue: She was elven, clad in the robes of the devotees of Mystra. My mother called her Anorrweyn Evensong.
Od2Ode25.speaker: Odelinde

Od2Ode26.dialogue: Anorrweyn lost her life in the Weeping Wars, defending her shrine when the nycaloths sent walls of living fire through the city.
Od2Ode26.speaker: Odelinde

Od2Ode27.dialogue: The shrine and she both fell, but through her will - or Mystra's - both returned as ghost-selves to haunt the site in the Nightingale Court where they once stood.
Od2Ode27.speaker: Odelinde

Od2Ode28.dialogue: Servants of Mystery visited her there in decades past, but I have not seen her for many moltings. She may have faded. Spirits sometimes do.
Od2Ode28.speaker: Odelinde

Od2Ode29.dialogue: Myth Drannor is as full of riches as it is of danger.
Od2Ode29.speaker: Odelinde

Od2Ode30.dialogue: They say the House of Gems, to the east and north of here, holds wealth beyond imagining. Although none have survived its perils long enough to confirm the tale.
Od2Ode30.speaker: Odelinde

Od2Ode31.dialogue: It is rumored that to the east of here, in the Dwarven ruins, riches lies hidden beneath the earth, awaiting the right footfall.
Od2Ode31.speaker: Odelinde

Od2Ode32.dialogue: There is a column to the east and south of here that whispers secrets carried on the wind. I used to go there often, for as Shaundakul knows, it tells marvelous tales!
Od2Ode32.speaker: Odelinde

Od2Ode33.dialogue: The private garden of Fiona Casilltenirra, the elven vampiress, lies fallow to the east. If you are willing to pay a dark price, the very earth there can grant powerful boons.
Od2Ode33.speaker: Odelinde

Od2Ode34.dialogue: Beyond the stronghold of the lizardfolk in the Nightingale Court, you may find a silent stone oracle, awaiting offerings. They say its potions and the ink of its scrolls were made from crushed ioun stones, in the desperate times of the Weeping Wars.
Od2Ode34.speaker: Odelinde

Od2Ode35.dialogue: The gargoyles hide much in their skytop aeries. But who can understand their gibberish? The mages of the Speculum once had a perverse amulet, called the Stone Mouth, with which they could decipher the gargoyle tongue.
Od2Ode35.speaker: Odelinde

Od2Ode39.dialogue: But plunder enriches only the pocket. It is noble deeds and service that enrich the heart.
Od2Ode39.speaker: Odelinde

Od2Ode40.dialogue: May the wind be at your back, Favored of Shaundakul. I shall guard this temple while I can.
Od2Ode40.speaker: Odelinde

Od2Ode41.dialogue: Return here whenever you like. I have tales for you, and Shaundakul's blessings if you are in need.
Od2Ode41.speaker: Odelinde

Od2Ode42.dialogue: But we have talked overlong. Adventure calls you. Answer it.
Od2Ode42.speaker: Odelinde

od4ode02.dialogue: You are the Favored!  The heroes who have rescued Myth Drannor!  My lord Shaundakul sings your deeds upon the wind!
od4ode02.speaker: Odelinde

od4ode03.dialogue: Favored of Shaundakul!  The wind sings with the tales of your victory!  The Mage Mordrayn is fallen, Pelendralaar is dust.  SSSsssssssss!  You have brought triumph to the city once again.
od4ode03.speaker: Odelinde

od4ode04.dialogue: May you be refreshed and restored, heroes of Myth Drannor.  The Wind Rider's blessing is upon you.
od4ode04.speaker: Odelinde
od4ode04.desc: spoken, administering a blessing, then a goodbye

od4ode05.dialogue: The Wind Rider's blessing is upon you, heroes.  When you need healing, return to his shrine and let his servant refresh you.
od4ode05.speaker: Odelinde
