pr1dmaYA.dialogue: The room beyond the barred window seems unnaturally dark. Out of the blackness, a voice speaks to you.
pr1dmaYA.speaker: DM

pr1pre02.dialogue: Who's there? What do you want? -Beware, I warn you, I am not defenseless!
pr1pre02.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre03.dialogue: Goodbye. But say, in your travels, if you ever come upon any neckpieces - necklaces, amulets, torcs, chokers, collars and so on - show them to me.
pr1pre03.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre04.dialogue: I am a collector, you might say, of such things. Now, farewell.
pr1pre04.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre05.dialogue: Ah, you have good in your hearts, not evil! I have seen adventurers like you before. Human, or something like it.
pr1pre05.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre06.dialogue: No, even I can see you are not defenseless. Human, aren't you? Or something like it?
pr1pre06.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre07.dialogue: I like humans - most of them, anyway.
pr1pre07.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre08.dialogue: Ah, you have good in your hearts, not evil! I am relieved to know this - I have seen adventurers like you before.
pr1pre08.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre09.dialogue: Good ones. Very, very good ones.
pr1pre09.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre10.dialogue: Prisoner? Oh yes, indeed I am, prisoner of my desires...
pr1pre10.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre11.dialogue: Good travels to you. But say, before you go, do you have any fine neckpieces? Necklaces, amulets, torcs, chokers, neck rings, pendants, collars, of very high quality?
pr1pre11.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre12.dialogue: I am a collector, you might say, of just about anything that goes on one's neck.
pr1pre12.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre14.dialogue: Strange - at least one of you seems to be wearing one. A very nice one, too. Goodbye.
pr1pre14.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre15.dialogue: Ah, maybe when you get to know me better - and I get to know you - that will be revealed. Until then - goodbye.
pr1pre15.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre16.dialogue: I am Preybelish. Don't ask me to talk about myself - it's a sad story - my name is all you need to know.
pr1pre16.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre17.dialogue: My door has the Glyph of Gobtadan emblazoned on the floor before it - as evil a sign as you will find - and the door will stay shut until the Word of Venom is uttered aloud.
pr1pre17.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre18.dialogue: I sit in the darkness and contemplate my mistakes - and every once in a while I receive a glimmer of joy from travelers such as you.
pr1pre18.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre19.dialogue: Oh, I've done things - terrible things! But I don't want to talk about myself.
pr1pre19.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre20.dialogue: I dare not tell you the name - but he is a pinnacle of evil, believe me! But I don't want to talk about my problems.
pr1pre20.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre21.dialogue: Well, everybody needs to oppose somebody - except for me. But I don't want to talk about myself.
pr1pre21.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre22.dialogue: Oh, you don't want to do that. You don't want to get tangled up with me.
pr1pre22.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre24.dialogue: Let's talk about you. You don't have any necklaces, do you? Any of you? Pity.
pr1pre24.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre25.dialogue: Let's talk about you. You're not wearing a necklace, are you? Any of you? Pity.
pr1pre25.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre26.dialogue: Oh, I don't mean common trinkets like amulets of protection. I mean rare and wonderful neckpieces, like the Collar of Nefridina or Cegilune's Blessed Necklace.
pr1pre26.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre27.dialogue: I am a collector of such things, you see. But now, tell me more of yourselves.
pr1pre27.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre28.dialogue: Goodbye. If you find any fine necklaces out there, think of me!
pr1pre28.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre29.dialogue: Never been there myself. It has been nice talking with you...
pr1pre29.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre30.dialogue: If you find any fine necklaces out there, think of me!
pr1pre30.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre31.dialogue: In Myth Drannor? Unlikely place for anyone to raise one of those.
pr1pre31.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre32.dialogue: Maybe you should seek out rare treasures instead. Many of the old ones are still around.
pr1pre32.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre33.dialogue: And if you find any fine necklaces out there, think of me! Goodbye.
pr1pre33.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre34.dialogue: Ah, I quite agree with you there. The Cult of the Dragon helps nobody but itself.
pr1pre34.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre35.dialogue: Still, you have to admire how much power they've scraped together. Very powerful, the Cult. Very, very powerful.
pr1pre35.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre36.dialogue: Maybe you should seek out rare treasures instead. Much less dangerous, and more profitable too, or so I hear.
pr1pre36.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre37.dialogue: Ah, I quite agree with you there. They help nobody but themselves.
pr1pre37.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre38.dialogue: Still, you have to admire how much power they've scraped together. Very powerful, those mages are. Very, very powerful.
pr1pre38.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre39.dialogue: Maybe you should seek out rare treasures instead. Much less dangerous, and more profitable too, or so I hear.
pr1pre39.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre40.dialogue: I want to talk about you now. And that marvelous neckpiece I see you wearing. What is it, may I ask? And do you have any others?
pr1pre40.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre41.dialogue: Do you now? Then tell me about one or two of them.
pr1pre41.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre43.dialogue: I am a collector of neckpieces. They fascinate me.
pr1pre43.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre44.dialogue: I don't mean common trinkets like amulets of protection. I mean rare and wonderful neckpieces, like the Collar of Nefridina or Cegilune's Blessed Necklace.
pr1pre44.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre45.dialogue: So tell me about the necklaces you own. I am dying to hear about them!
pr1pre45.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre46.dialogue: Well, now you know. And I am curious too, about the necklaces you own.
pr1pre46.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre47.dialogue: Yes, I thought that's what it was. Nothing else has its color, its vibrancy!
pr1pre47.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre48.dialogue: Yes, that explains it. Quite a rare treasure, is Theodore's Token of Luck!
pr1pre48.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre49.dialogue: I - I am amazed. I had heard tales but - I didn't think they were true! Tyr's Locket of Justice... very effective against the plentiful undead!
pr1pre49.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre50.dialogue: Onglore's Amulet of War, you say. Well, that is rare and wonderful.
pr1pre50.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre51.dialogue: Well, that is a rare and wonderful neckpiece!
pr1pre51.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre52.dialogue: Not as rare as the masterpieces in my collection, of course, but still...
pr1pre52.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre53.dialogue: It's too bad I'm, ah, indisposed at the moment. Come and see me later - I may be able to persuade you to let go of it.
pr1pre53.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre54.dialogue: Oh yes, you must come by later. Until then, goodbye!
pr1pre54.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre55.dialogue: Maybe we can discuss your neckpieces some other time. Goodbye.
pr1pre55.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre57.dialogue: Ah, but those are common trinkets, barely worth a glance. I was hoping you'd have a truly wonderful neckpiece, like the Torc of Torm.
pr1pre57.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre58.dialogue: If you find something like that, come and see me. Until then, goodbye.
pr1pre58.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre59.dialogue: Quite all right. I understand. You are probably quite attached to them.
pr1pre59.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre60.dialogue: And won't let them go without a fight.
pr1pre60.speaker: preybeli

pr1dma00.dialogue: Haashingutak, the Word of Venom, opens the sealed door!
pr1dma00.speaker: dm

pr1pre62.dialogue: Aaaah - but you see - I can't let a neckpiece like that simply walk away...
pr1pre62.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre64.dialogue: You have the Starstone?! Not for long.
pr1pre64.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre65.dialogue: Ah, wait, I can guess. I sensed it when you approached. You have its Starstone, although the mighty Gobtadan alone can explain how you came by it...
pr1pre65.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre66.dialogue: No matter. It will not be yours much longer.
pr1pre66.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre67.dialogue: And I simply must have it.
pr1pre67.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre69.dialogue: The Wizard's Torc? Why, yes, I own it. Of course I own it. Why do you ask?
pr1pre69.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre77.dialogue: What did I tell you when we met? I collect fine neckpieces. Yet did you bring me any? Do I see any adorning your bony necks? No.
pr1pre77.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre78.dialogue: It's enough to send a body deep into dark despair - or off into a spitting rage.
pr1pre78.speaker: preybeli
pr1pre78.desc: spoken, hurt and then with malice

pr1pre80.dialogue: No offense, but the neckpieces you have are very common. What I seek are the rare pieces - personal masterworks such as Athraxi's Amulet or the Gorget of Purgelum.
pr1pre80.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre81.dialogue: No offense, but the neckpiece you have is very common. What I seek are the rare pieces - personal masterworks such as Athraxi's Amulet or the Gorget of Purgelum.
pr1pre81.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre82.dialogue: I can see out, but you can't see in. That's the beauty of the spell.
pr1pre82.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre83.dialogue: I cast it because, when you see someone, you learn a lot about them. Take you for instance. I can see you're human-shaped, and are probably adventurers of some kind.
pr1pre83.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre84.dialogue: But what you can't learn by seeing is whether or not someone is trustworthy. If they will help you - or plunder your fortune - when you are down on your luck.
pr1pre84.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre85.dialogue: Which is what you really want to know, isn't it? If someone can be trusted. Or not.
pr1pre85.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre87.dialogue: Trusted to live and let live? Usually.
pr1pre87.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre88.dialogue: Trusted to not be a fool? Maybe.
pr1pre88.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre89.dialogue: Trusted to see a fine necklace and not desire it of all things? Never.
pr1pre89.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre90.dialogue: Oh, I have necklaces, and amulets, and lockets, and torcs, and collars, and gorgets, and even a neck ring and some chokers. All of exquisite beauty!
pr1pre90.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre91.dialogue: Ah, they would shock and amaze you! I enjoy putting them all on. Such a sight! But as for what they are exactly, we are not friends enough for me to say.
pr1pre91.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre92.dialogue: What must I do to persuade you to part with it?
pr1pre92.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre93.dialogue: Well, now you've really tickled my fangs. What could it be?
pr1pre93.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre94.dialogue: I'm too curious to continue asking politely.
pr1pre94.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre95.dialogue: Dare I tell you? Oh, very well. You know about nagas, don't you? Serpentine creatures, very wise and powerful, but also very fierce-looking?
pr1pre95.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre96.dialogue: Not all nagas are evil. Some are peace-loving and loyal to those who are friendly to them.
pr1pre96.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre97.dialogue: Fortunately, I do not have that problem.
pr1pre97.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre98.dialogue: Ah! Tell me about it. Show it to me!
pr1pre98.speaker: preybeli

pr1pre99.dialogue: Where is it? What have you done? Aaaagh, you imbeciles, I should just kill you all now!
pr1pre99.speaker: preybeli
pr1pre99.desc: spoken, outburst in shock and horror

pr1prea2.dialogue: The necklace! That fabulous neckpiece! You're not wearing it, any of you! You pawned it for some trifle, or fumbled it into some abyss!
pr1prea2.speaker: preybeli

pr1prea3.dialogue: If it is lost to me, I will kill you all slowly, one by one!
pr1prea3.speaker: preybeli

pr1prea4.dialogue: You will barely live long enough to regret your mistake!
pr1prea4.speaker: preybeli

pr1prea5.dialogue: Ah - you're right - I am overwrought.
pr1prea5.speaker: preybeli

pr1prea6.dialogue: You have the neckpiece in a pocket somewhere, that's it. Safe in a pocket, that's right, isn't it?
pr1prea6.speaker: preybeli

pr1prea7.dialogue: No, no, I can see it in your faces - you don't have it! You pawned it for some trifle, or fumbled it into an abyss!
pr1prea7.speaker: preybeli

pr1prea8.dialogue: Ah! Excellent!  And now you must give Kluusar's Bloodstone Amulet to me.
pr1prea8.speaker: preybeli

pr1prea9.dialogue: Ah! Excellent! And now you must give Theodore's Token of Luck to me.
pr1prea9.speaker: preybeli

pr1preb0.dialogue: Ah! Excellent! And now you must give Tyr's Locket of Justice to me.
pr1preb0.speaker: preybeli

pr1preb1.dialogue: Ah! Excellent! And now you must give Onglore's Amulet of War to me.
pr1preb1.speaker: preybeli

pr1preb3.dialogue: Ah - ah - ah - it's you, the do-gooders, come to talk to me again. To ease my loneliness.
pr1preb3.speaker: preybeli

pr1preb4.dialogue: You remember me, don't you? Preybelish? The voice out of the darkness - the collector of neckpieces.
pr1preb4.speaker: preybeli

pr1preb5.dialogue: But looking at what you've got around your necks - it seems you've disappointed me. No truly fine neckpieces.
pr1preb5.speaker: preybeli

pr1preb6.dialogue: The Wizard's Torc? Why, yes, I own it. Of course I own it. Why do you ask?
pr1preb6.speaker: preybeli

pr1preb8.dialogue: Ah, I see you still have Kluusar's Bloodstone Amulet! Since you mentioned it, I have thought of nothing else.
pr1preb8.speaker: preybeli

pr1preb9.dialogue: Ah, I see you still have Theodore's Token of Luck! Since you mentioned it, I have thought of nothing else.
pr1preb9.speaker: preybeli

pr1prec0.dialogue: Ah, I see you still have Tyr's Locket of Justice! Since you mentioned it, I have thought of nothing else.
pr1prec0.speaker: preybeli

pr1prec1.dialogue: Ah, I see you still have Onglore's Amulet of War! Since you mentioned it, I have thought of nothing else.
pr1prec1.speaker: preybeli

pr1prec2.dialogue: What will it take to persuade you to part with it?
pr1prec2.speaker: preybeli

pr1prec3.dialogue: Ah, I am glad to see you again! Since you told me about Kluusar's Bloodstone Amulet, I have thought of nothing else.
pr1prec3.speaker: preybeli

pr1prec4.dialogue: Ah, I am glad to see you again! Since you told me about Theodore's Token of Luck, I have thought of nothing else.
pr1prec4.speaker: preybeli

pr1prec5.dialogue: Ah, I am glad to see you again! Since you told me about Tyr's Locket of Justice, I have thought of nothing else.
pr1prec5.speaker: preybeli

pr1prec6.dialogue: Ah, I am glad to see you again! Since you told me about Onglore's Amulet of War, I have thought of nothing else.
pr1prec6.speaker: preybeli

pr1prec8.dialogue: Ah, I see you still have Kluusar's Bloodstone Amulet! I saw you wearing it when we met, and since then I have thought of nothing else.
pr1prec8.speaker: preybeli

pr1prec9.dialogue: Ah, I see you still have Theodore's Token of Luck! I saw you wearing it when we met, and since then I have thought of nothing else.
pr1prec9.speaker: preybeli

pr1pred0.dialogue: Ah, I see you still have Tyr's Locket of Justice! I saw you wearing it when we met, and since then I have thought of nothing else.
pr1pred0.speaker: preybeli

pr1pred1.dialogue: Ah, I see you still have Onglore's Amulet of War! I saw you wearing it when we met, and since then I have thought of nothing else.
pr1pred1.speaker: preybeli

pr1pred3.dialogue: Ah, I am glad to see you again! I saw you wearing Kluusar's Bloodstone Amulet when we met, and since then I have thought of nothing else.
pr1pred3.speaker: preybeli

pr1pred4.dialogue: Ah, I am glad to see you again! I saw you wearing Theodore's Token of Luck when we met, and since then I have thought of nothing else.
pr1pred4.speaker: preybeli

pr1pred5.dialogue: Ah, I am glad to see you again! I saw you wearing Tyr's Locket of Justice when we met, and since then I have thought of nothing else.
pr1pred5.speaker: preybeli

pr1pred6.dialogue: Ah, I am glad to see you again! I saw you wearing Onglore's Amulet of War when we met, and since then I have thought of nothing else.
pr1pred6.speaker: preybeli

pr1pred8.dialogue: Ah, what do I see here? One of you is wearing Kluusar's Bloodstone Amulet!
pr1pred8.speaker: preybeli

pr1pred9.dialogue: Ah, what do I see here? One of you is wearing Theodore's Token of Luck!
pr1pred9.speaker: preybeli

pr1pree0.dialogue: Ah, what do I see here? One of you is wearing Tyr's Locket of Justice!
pr1pree0.speaker: preybeli

pr1pree1.dialogue: Ah, what do I see here? One of you is wearing Onglore's Amulet of War!
pr1pree1.speaker: preybeli

pr1pree2.dialogue: Ah, I am disappointed of course. Even a little bit angry! I still want that neckpiece! What do you suggest?
pr1pree2.speaker: preybeli

pr1pree3.dialogue: For free? That is a mighty gift! Are you sure?
pr1pree3.speaker: preybeli

pr1dma01.dialogue: You toss Kluusar's Bloodstone Amulet through the window. It is swallowed up by the blackness beyond.
pr1dma01.speaker: DM

pr1dma02.dialogue: You toss Theodore's Token of Luck through the window. It is swallowed up by the blackness beyond.
pr1dma02.speaker: DM

pr1dma03.dialogue: You toss Tyr's Locket of Justice through the window. It is swallowed up by the blackness beyond.
pr1dma03.speaker: DM

pr1dma04.dialogue: You toss Onglore's Amulet of War through the window. It is swallowed up by the blackness beyond.
pr1dma04.speaker: DM

pr1pree8.dialogue: Thank you for your generous gift. I realize that you expect me to give you something in return - if not now, maybe later.
pr1pree8.speaker: preybeli

pr1pree9.dialogue: Fortunately, that's not the kind of creature I am.
pr1pree9.speaker: preybeli

pr1pref0.dialogue: Now I must admire this wonderful neckpiece for a while. It really is magnificent! Goodbye.
pr1pref0.speaker: preybeli

pr1pref1.dialogue: Trade? Ah, but I am afraid I couldn't bear to part with anything in my collection. No, I'm afraid a trade is out of the question... unless...
pr1pref1.speaker: preybeli

pr1pref2.dialogue: ...you give me the necklace, and I give you the sweet kiss of oblivion.
pr1pref2.speaker: preybeli

pr1pref3.dialogue: Ah. I was afraid of that. I am disappointed of course - even a little bit angry!
pr1pref3.speaker: preybeli

pr1pref5.dialogue: You know how much I crave the neckpiece! And yet you deny me of it. You hold it out - you flaunt it - then snatch it away! Doesn't that seem cruel to you? Heartless?
pr1pref5.speaker: preybeli

pr1pref6.dialogue: But - you know how much I crave the neckpiece! And yet you deny me of it. You hold it out - you flaunt it - then snatch it away! Doesn't that seem cruel to you? Heartless?
pr1pref6.speaker: preybeli

pr1pref7.dialogue: The more I think about it, the more I think someone needs to teach you a lesson.
pr1pref7.speaker: preybeli

pr1pref8.dialogue: Very well. I'll bide my time. What would you like to talk about? Are you looking for something, maybe?
pr1pref8.speaker: preybeli

pr1pref9.dialogue: Rings! What use have I for rings? Rings and swords and wands, I pitch them down the nearest crack.
pr1pref9.speaker: preybeli

pr1preg0.dialogue: So you seek Oblivion, do you? Ah me, that is funny.
pr1preg0.speaker: preybeli

pr1preg1.dialogue: Because I want nothing more than to give it to you.
pr1preg1.speaker: preybeli

pr1preg2.dialogue: Ah, that is up from here, way up, near the surface.
pr1preg2.speaker: preybeli

pr1preg3.dialogue: I hear there may be a fine necklace up there as well. If you find it, bring it back to show me, will you?
pr1preg3.speaker: preybeli

pr1preg4.dialogue: Ah, you are kind, you are my friends, to bring me neckpieces like this. I will try to be patient, until you return. Goodbye.
pr1preg4.speaker: preybeli

pr1preg6.dialogue: That old thing? It is not here. It was taken into the Catacombs long ago, and no one gets into the Catacombs these days.
pr1preg6.speaker: preybeli

pr1preg7.dialogue: Take my advice, forget that old bone. There's still plenty of treasure right here in the dungeons. Necklaces, for example. Plenty of necklaces still to be found.
pr1preg7.speaker: preybeli

pr1preg8.dialogue: And if you do find any, you will show them to me, won't you? I will try to be patient until you return. Goodbye.
pr1preg8.speaker: preybeli

pr1preh1.dialogue: Well then, at last my Wizard's Torc can be made complete!
pr1preh1.speaker: preybeli

pr1preh3.dialogue: Well, we have that in common.
pr1preh3.speaker: preybeli

pr1preh4.dialogue: Take my advice - there's plenty of useful treasure right here in the dungeons. Necklaces, for example. Plenty of necklaces still to be found.
pr1preh4.speaker: preybeli

pr1preh6.dialogue: Ah, no, my frail two-legged friends, don't do that! You'll be killed, and that marvelous neckpiece will be lost to me forever!
pr1preh6.speaker: preybeli

pr1preh7.dialogue: No, no, no, I cannot allow that to happen...
pr1preh7.speaker: preybeli

pr1preh9.dialogue: Ah, the Glyph of Gobtadan, very powerful, very evil! Until it is unwritten by the Word of Venom, no living being will pass my door.
pr1preh9.speaker: preybeli

pr1prei0.dialogue: You're leaving? Good travels to you. And if you find any fine neckpieces -  necklaces, amulets, torcs, chokers, neck rings, gorgets, pendants, collars - think of me.
pr1prei0.speaker: preybeli

pr1prei1.dialogue: Goodbye. Show me a new neckpiece, next time you come!
pr1prei1.speaker: preybeli

pr1preYB.dialogue: Very well then.  I'll bide my time. Goodbye - show me a new neckpiece, next time you come!
pr1preYB.speaker: preybeli

pr1prei4.dialogue: Your neckwear does not impress me. Next time, show me something new.
pr1prei4.speaker: preybeli

pr1prei5.dialogue: I'm bored with Kluusar's Bloodstone Amulet. Bring me something else, and I might let you have it back.
pr1prei5.speaker: preybeli

pr1prei6.dialogue: I'm bored with Theodore's Token of Luck. Bring me something else, and I might let you have it back.
pr1prei6.speaker: preybeli

pr1prei7.dialogue: I'm bored with Tyr's Locket of Justice. Bring me something else, and I might let you have it back.
pr1prei7.speaker: preybeli

pr1prei8.dialogue: I'm bored with Onglore's Amulet of War you gave me. Bring me something else, and I might let you have it back.
pr1prei8.speaker: preybeli

pr1prej1.dialogue: Ah - I can see it in your faces - you've come to offer me a rare neckpiece.
pr1prej1.speaker: preybeli

pr1prej2.dialogue: Ah - I can see it in your faces - you've found a neckpiece for me.
pr1prej2.speaker: preybeli

pr1prej4.dialogue: Ah, that is marvelous. Marvelous! I simply must have them, all of them, right now.
pr1prej4.speaker: preybeli

pr1prej5.dialogue: No, no, we must talk about your neckpiece - I hope to own it, you see. Won't you tell me something about it?
pr1prej5.speaker: preybeli

pr1prej6.dialogue: No, no, you must stay, we must talk about your rare neckpiece - I hope to own it, you see. Won't you tell me something about it?
pr1prej6.speaker: preybeli

pr1prej7.dialogue: Ah, that is marvelous. Marvelous! I simply must have it, right now.
pr1prej7.speaker: preybeli

pr1prej8.dialogue: Ah, that is marvelous. Marvelous! I simply must have them, all of them, right now.
pr1prej8.speaker: preybeli

pr1prej9.dialogue: Ah, I know what you're thinking - 'this necklace will lure the old lizard out of his hidey-hole, and then we can kill him.'
pr1prej9.speaker: preybeli

pr1prek0.dialogue: You think I'm not really a helpless prisoner, that I know the Word of Venom, and can open my door at any time.
pr1prek0.speaker: preybeli

pr1prek1.dialogue: Well, if that's what you're thinking, you're right.
pr1prek1.speaker: preybeli

pr1dma05.dialogue: Haashingutak, the Word of Venom, opens the sealed door!
pr1dma05.speaker: dm

pr1prek3.dialogue: Wait! I will not stop you from leaving. But I assure you that if you return, all you will find is stony silence and the powerful Glyph of Gobtadan guarding my door.
pr1prek3.speaker: preybeli

pr1prek4.dialogue: You have Kluusar's Bloodstone Amulet. Give it to me!
pr1prek4.speaker: preybeli

pr1prek5.dialogue: You have Theodore's Token of Luck. Give it to me!
pr1prek5.speaker: preybeli

pr1prek6.dialogue: You have Tyr's Locket of Justice. Give it to me!
pr1prek6.speaker: preybeli

pr1prek7.dialogue: You have Onglore's Amulet of War. Give it to me!
pr1prek7.speaker: preybeli

pr1prek8.dialogue: Your offer is heartfelt, and genuine, and very very attractive...
pr1prek8.speaker: preybeli

pr1prek9.dialogue: ...but I will decline it. Come in and get me, if you dare. I will bandy words with you no more.
pr1prek9.speaker: preybeli

pr1prel0.dialogue: That is not true. All your neckpieces will be mine, and your necks with them!
pr1prel0.speaker: preybeli

pr1prel1.dialogue: I believe this is farewell forever. Enjoy your loss.
pr1prel1.speaker: preybeli

pr1prel2.dialogue: Ah, I think you will find that all who knew the Word are dead. Very, very dead.
pr1prel2.speaker: preybeli

pr1prel4.dialogue: I will not stop you from leaving. Just be warned - if you return, all you will find is stony silence and the powerful Glyph of Gobtadan guarding my door.
pr1prel4.speaker: preybeli

prpdmaYA.dialogue: Far away, you hear the sound of distant magic coming to life!
prpdmaYA.speaker: DM

prudma00.dialogue: You have cleared the Sharpstick Room of orcs. The ormyrrs you met in the Halls of Light are now free to move back into this room.
prudma00.speaker: DM

pwcdmaYA.dialogue: The scroll is blank - but from its blankness, you hear Ogramirad, the Word of Constriction.
pwcdmaYA.speaker: DM

pwcdmaYB.dialogue: The sound of it briefly chokes shut every throat in the room.
pwcdmaYB.speaker: DM

pwddmaYA.dialogue: The hide contains the Word of Dragon, but you have already learned it.
pwddmaYA.speaker: DM

pwsdma00.dialogue: The scroll turns to liquid, and dribbles away between your fingers. When it drips to the ground, it teaches you Shashakiro, the Splashing Word.
pwsdma00.speaker: dm

pwzdma00.dialogue: The scroll flies to dust as you open it, and when you breathe the dust, it teaches you Mellen, the Singing Word.
pwzdma00.speaker: dm

pwvdma00.dialogue: The scroll rips itself into pieces! And the sound it makes teaches you Haashingutak, the Word of Venom.
pwvdma00.speaker: dm

pwpdmaYA.dialogue: Far away, you hear the sound of distant magic coming to life!
pwpdmaYA.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYA.dialogue: You earned a good bargain by helping Nottle the Scavenger.
qlgdmaYA.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYB.dialogue: He helped you to gain healing and wisdom from elves sheltering in the Stillwater ruins.
qlgdmaYB.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYC.dialogue: They enabled you to unseal the way into the dwarven Dungeons of Myth Drannor.
qlgdmaYC.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYD.dialogue: You defeated the orc chieftain Zud.
qlgdmaYD.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYE.dialogue: You recovered the staff Deathbane from the orc hoard, and returned it to Beriand, the blind priest of Mystra.
qlgdmaYE.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYF.dialogue: You freed the sorcerer Jarial from his rocky prison.
qlgdmaYF.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYG.dialogue: You defeated the dark naga Preybelish, and won for yourself the Wizard's Torc.
qlgdmaYG.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYH.dialogue: You defeated the spectral Jailer of Bedlam Prison.
qlgdmaYH.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYI.dialogue: You learned the identity of your foe: they are of the Cult of the Dragon, and have taken control of the Mythal, the city's ancient protective spell.
qlgdmaYI.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYJ.dialogue: You sealed the Nightmare Gate to Mungoth, a land of eternal undeath.
qlgdmaYJ.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYK.dialogue: You helped Emmeric, one of Athan's band, escape his Cult captors.
qlgdmaYK.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYL.dialogue: You found the Onyx of the Richest Wort.
qlgdmaYL.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYM.dialogue: You recovered the Gauntlets of Ogre Power from an arraccat treasure pile.
qlgdmaYM.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYN.dialogue: You found the Mountain Fist, long lost to shadows.
qlgdmaYN.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYO.dialogue: You returned the Ruby of Earthborn Wind to its proper place, and restored the Channels of Earthborn Wind.
qlgdmaYO.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYP.dialogue: You found the Waters of Life in a well guarded by lizardfolk.
qlgdmaYP.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYQ.dialogue: You found and destroyed three tomes of great evil.
qlgdmaYQ.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYR.dialogue: You freed the Sharpstick Room, sacred to ormyrrs, from orc squatters.
qlgdmaYR.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYS.dialogue: You rescued Nottle from a Cult cage.
qlgdmaYS.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYT.dialogue: You put the Lifespring Guardian to rest and restored the waters of wisdom to the Lifespring Wells.
qlgdmaYT.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYU.dialogue: You freed the Rhonglyn from Borea's icy grip, and used the ancient device to reach the Speculum.
qlgdmaYU.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYV.dialogue: You were declared to be talibund, to be Veiled Ones, by the ghost of the legendary soothsayer Caalenfaire.
qlgdmaYV.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYW.dialogue: You found and freed the ancient Ring of Calling from the Skeletal Arm.
qlgdmaYW.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYX.dialogue: You used the Ring of Calling to open the ancient Seal of Mythanthor, and thus to reach the fabled City Heights.
qlgdmaYX.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYY.dialogue: You destroyed a Spawn Pool in the Shrine of Shaundakul, and restored Odelinde, the Shrine's guardian, to her place of power.
qlgdmaYY.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYZ.dialogue: You destroyed a Spawn Pool in the House of Gems, and removed its paralyzing curse from the ghost of the dwarf lord, Harldain Ironbar.
qlgdmaYZ.speaker: DM

qlgdmaY[.dialogue: You recovered the Helm Cleaver, a weapon sacred to orogs, from a Cult stronghold.
qlgdmaY[.speaker: DM

qlgdmaY\\.dialogue: You gathered rumors borne on the wind from the ear of the city, the Column of the Whispering Wind.
qlgdmaY\\.speaker: DM

qlgdmaY].dialogue: You found the Thirsty Ground, an ancient garden with a dark gift.
qlgdmaY].speaker: DM

qlgdmaY^.dialogue: You entered the Tomb of Eternal Sleep, and brought forth Eadred, the warrior of old trapped in the tomb.
qlgdmaY^.speaker: DM

qlgdmaY_.dialogue: You returned idolons to a great stone idol, and gained its Fading Rings.
qlgdmaY_.speaker: DM

qlgdmaY`.dialogue: You destroyed the dark naga Kog and his servants and dispelled the Spawn Pool in the ghostly Temple of Mystra.
qlgdmaY`.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYa.dialogue: You brought back the ghost of Anorrweyn Evensong from exile in the dark places of her past.
qlgdmaYa.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYb.dialogue: You defeated the evil sorcerer Malgi Hi and his fanatic lizardfolk minions.
qlgdmaYb.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYc.dialogue: You killed Pujik, the self-appointed King of the Ormyrrs, and dispelled the Spawn Pool in the Ormyrr meeting-place.
qlgdmaYc.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYd.dialogue: You opened a portal to a hidden Cult stronghold, and learned the Splashing Word.
qlgdmaYd.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYe.dialogue: You gave back the Waterbells taken from the naiad Plinshree, and restored the Music of the Waters to the city's fountains.
qlgdmaYe.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYf.dialogue: You stood in the Circle drawn by Ualair the Silent, and opened up the ancient portal into the elven Catacombs.
qlgdmaYf.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYg.dialogue: You raided the chambers of the Freth drow, defeated the drow mage Greyanna, and recovered the skull of Anorrweyn Evensong.
qlgdmaYg.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYh.dialogue: You returned Anorrweyn's skull to her shrine, bringing her spirit more fully into this time and place.
qlgdmaYh.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYi.dialogue: You freed all the Orrery Planets, and renewed the Spires that allow travel from place to place in the city.
qlgdmaYi.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYj.dialogue: You located the Shrine to the Silver Fire hidden in the elven Catacombs.
qlgdmaYj.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYk.dialogue: You freed the Shrine's guardians, and met Kellan and Bronwyn, survivors of a Silver Fire sortie against Kya Mordrayn and Pelendralaar.
qlgdmaYk.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYl.dialogue: You invaded the Cult Stronghold deep in the Catacombs, and freed the baelnorn Miroden Silverblade, the Protector of the Mythal.
qlgdmaYl.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYm.dialogue: You encountered the drow warrior Nathlilik, and agreed to collaborate against your common enemy, the Cult.
qlgdmaYm.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYo.dialogue: You killed the drow warrior Nathlilik.
qlgdmaYo.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYq.dialogue: You rescued Beriand, who had been pulled from his hidden shelter by the Cult.
qlgdmaYq.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYs.dialogue: You rescued Beriand and Faeril, who had been pulled from their hidden shelter by the Cult.
qlgdmaYs.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYu.dialogue: With the Stone Mouth, you lured gargoyles and margoyles to their doom and gained their treasures.
qlgdmaYu.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYw.dialogue: You destroyed the spectral revenant of Thyaast Ammath, an ancient spellsummoner tragically undone by her own greatspells.
qlgdmaYw.speaker: DM

qlgqlo48.dialogue: To destroy the Pool of Radiance, you should explore this ruined area, looking for allies.
qlgqlo48.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo49.dialogue: To destroy the Pool of Radiance, you must find and enter the elven shelter. Nottle mentioned that it was hidden in a tree stump.
qlgqlo49.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo50.dialogue: To destroy the Pool of Radiance, you must learn the Word of Power from the elven book.
qlgqlo50.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo51.dialogue: To destroy the Pool of Radiance, open a way up from the Dungeons to the city Heights.
qlgqlo51.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo52.dialogue: First, find the Tumbledown Door, which leads into the Dungeons.
qlgqlo52.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo53.dialogue: To do that, explore the Dungeons to find the Skeletal Arm taken from Athan's band.
qlgqlo53.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo54.dialogue: To do that, explore more of the Dungeons to find a way to release the magic Ring from the Skeletal Arm.
qlgqlo54.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo55.dialogue: To do that, unfreeze the Rhonglyn, the magical transportation device of the elves.
qlgqlo55.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo56.dialogue: To do that, explore the places the Rhonglyn can take you.
qlgqlo56.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo57.dialogue: To do that, wear the Ring of Calling, and find the Seal of Mythanthor.
qlgqlo57.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo58.dialogue: To destroy the Pool of Radiance, you should explore the city Heights, looking for the allies Caalenfaire mentioned: Odelinde the golden serpent, and the ghost of the dwarf lord Harldain Ironbar.
qlgqlo58.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo59.dialogue: To destroy the Pool of Radiance, you should talk to a servant of Mystra about the forlorn woman's cry you heard.
qlgqlo59.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo60.dialogue: To destroy the Pool of Radiance, you must destroy whatever has paralyzed the spirit of Harldain Ironbar.
qlgqlo60.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo61.dialogue: To destroy the Pool of Radiance, open up the Circle of Ualair, and enter the Catacombs.
qlgqlo61.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo62.dialogue: To do that, find the great neckpiece of Ualair, the Wizard's Torc, and return to it the Starstone that Harldain gave you.
qlgqlo62.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo63.dialogue: To do that, check the lair of Preybelish for the great neckpiece of Ualair, the Wizard's Torc.
qlgqlo63.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo64.dialogue: To do that, wear the Wizard's Torc, and find the Circle of Ualair.
qlgqlo64.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo65.dialogue: To destroy the Pool of Radiance, you should bring a Token of Mystra - or a Servant of Mystery herself - to the ghost shrine of Anorrweyn Evensong.
qlgqlo65.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo66.dialogue: To destroy the Pool of Radiance, you must explore more of the aboveground ruins.
qlgqlo66.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo67.dialogue: To destroy the Pool of Radiance, seek the baelnorn, Miroden Silverblade, deep in the Catacombs.
qlgqlo67.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo68.dialogue: To destroy the Pool of Radiance, free the baelnorn Miroden Silverblade. He is imprisoned in the Cult stronghold deep in the Catacombs.
qlgqlo68.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo70.dialogue: To destroy the Pool of Radiance, you must find another great Gem of the Weave, which the dwarves crafted in times of old.
qlgqlo70.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo71.dialogue: To destroy the Pool of Radiance, take the Tumblebar to the pedestal in the courtyard of the House of Gems. Use the Tumblebar to open the Hoard of the Onaglym Dwarves, and retrieve the Gem of the Weave.
qlgqlo71.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo73.dialogue: To destroy the Pool of Radiance, you must find a Communicant to attune the Gem of the Weave.
qlgqlo73.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo74.dialogue: Anorrweyn cannot help you until you retrieve her skull from the Catacombs, and return it to her grave in the ghost shrine of Mystra.
qlgqlo74.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo75.dialogue: Anorrweyn cannot help you until you return her skull to her grave in the ghost shrine of Mystra.
qlgqlo75.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo76.dialogue: You must convince Anorrweyn Evensong to be the Communicant.
qlgqlo76.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo77.dialogue: To destroy the Pool of Radiance, you must take the Gem of the Weave to the Dragon Spires atop the Speculum. There, Anorrweyn Evensong can attune the Gem to the Mythal.
qlgqlo77.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo78.dialogue: Anorrweyn waits for you to destroy the Sapphire of the Weave, so she can wrest control of the Mythal from Kya Mordrayn, and render the Cult sorceress vulnerable to your attack.
qlgqlo78.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo79.dialogue: To destroy the Sapphire, you must make your way through the underground passage into Castle Cormanthor.
qlgqlo79.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo80.dialogue: To destroy the Sapphire, you must descend to the deepest chambers of Castle Cormanthor.
qlgqlo80.speaker: questlog

qlgqloYy.dialogue: In the Scrying Mirror, you saw Kya Mordrayn and Pelendralaar, a dracolich, basking in the terrible power of the Pool of Radiance.
qlgqloYy.speaker: questlog

qlgqloZA.dialogue: The Whispering Wind told you she heard two elves praying to Mystra in Stillwater.
qlgqloZA.speaker: questlog

qlgqloZB.dialogue: The Whispering Wind told you she heard a voice crying for help in the Nightingale Court.
qlgqloZB.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo82.dialogue: To find the hidden shelter, you must get the Knocking Word from the halfling Nottle. Then go to the big tree stump, and walk close to its Glyph.
qlgqlo82.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo83.dialogue: To find the hidden shelter, walk up to the Glyph on the big tree stump. The Knocking Word you learned will speak itself to open up the secret place.
qlgqlo83.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo85.dialogue: To get the Ring of Calling for yourself, you must find the Skeletal Arm that Athan had. First, learn the Word of Mystra from the elves' book - it will unseal the Glyph of Mystra in front of the door leading down into the Dungeons.
qlgqlo85.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo86.dialogue: To get the Ring of Calling for yourself, explore the Upper Halls of the Dungeons to find the Skeletal Arm that Athan had. Or find the Room of Words, where you might learn the Word of Oblivion that will shatter the arm and release the Ring to you.
qlgqlo86.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo87.dialogue: To get the Ring of Calling for yourself, explore the Dungeons further, to find someone or something that can teach you the Word of Oblivion. This Word of Power should release the Ring of Calling from the Skeletal Arm.
qlgqlo87.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo88.dialogue: To get the Ring of Calling for yourself, explore the Upper Halls of the Dungeons further, to find the Skeletal Arm that Athan had. If you find the Skeletal Arm, the Word of Oblivion you learned should release the Ring of Calling from its grip.
qlgqlo88.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo90.dialogue: To restore Beriand's power to resurrect the dead, bring back his staff Deathbane, which orcs seized and carried off into the Dungeons.
qlgqlo90.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo91.dialogue: To begin this quest, read the Word of Power in the elves' book. Once you learn the Word of Mystra, you can unseal the Tumbledown door that leads to the Dungeons.
qlgqlo91.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo92.dialogue: In an orc's chest, you found an elven staff which its owner named 'Deathbane.' You should return it to its owner.
qlgqlo92.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo93.dialogue: A Scarred Mage controls the room where stairs lead to the Upper Halls. To move beyond the Dungeon's Main Halls, you must defeat him and his cohort of undead.
qlgqlo93.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo95.dialogue: Someone dwells beyond the door marked with the Glyph of Gobtadan. Locating some fine neckpieces will help you find out more about him.
qlgqlo95.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo96.dialogue: If you want to learn more about Preybelish and his treasures, you must find some fine neckpieces - or learn the Word of Venom.
qlgqlo96.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo97.dialogue: If you want to learn more about Preybelish and his treasures, you must find more fine neckpieces - or learn the Word of Venom.
qlgqlo97.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo99.dialogue: If you want to get Preybelish's treasures for yourself, explore the City until you learn the Word of Venom, which will unseal the Glyph of Gobtadan. Then you must defeat him in combat.
qlgqlo99.speaker: questlog

qlgqloa0.dialogue: Beriand told you he met a helpful fellow, locked away in a dark cell. If you want to learn more about him, explore the northeast part of the Dungeon's Main Halls.
qlgqloa0.speaker: questlog

qlgqloYz.dialogue: Jarial told you his lover, Ozama, left him to investigate a friendly voice she heard in the northeast part of the Dungeon's Main Halls.
qlgqloYz.speaker: questlog

qlgqloa2.dialogue: You heard about a magical Gate which brings undead into the Dungeons. To destroy the Nightmare Gate, explore the Dungeons until you locate it.
qlgqloa2.speaker: questlog

qlgqloa3.dialogue: You found a magical Gate which brings undead into the Dungeons. Explore the Dungeons to find a way to destroy it.
qlgqloa3.speaker: questlog

qlgqloa4.dialogue: You found a Cult letter, asking permission to use the Constricting Word to dispel the Gate that brings undead into the Dungeons. Explore the Cult strongholds in the area to find the Word and the Gate.
qlgqloa4.speaker: questlog

qlgqloa5.dialogue: You learned the Cult's powerful Word of Constriction. To find where they use this Word of Power, explore more of the Dungeons.
qlgqloa5.speaker: questlog

qlgqloa6.dialogue: You found a letter that revealed the Cult could close the Gate that brings undead into the Dungeons. You also learned the Cult's Word of Constriction. To use the Word on the Gate, you need only approach the Nightmare Gate.
qlgqloa6.speaker: questlog

qlgqloZC.dialogue: You saw a Gate that brings undead into the Dungeons. You also learned the Cult's Word of Constriction. To use the Word on the Gate, you need only approach the Nightmare Gate.
qlgqloZC.speaker: questlog

qlgqloZD.dialogue: You saw a Gate that brings undead into the Dungeons. You also found a letter that revealed the Cult could close the Gate with a Word of Power. To close the Gate, find a way to learn the Word.
qlgqloZD.speaker: questlog

qlgqloa8.dialogue: You took the Key of Dumathoin off a Cult Mage. Explore the Dungeons, to find where the Key might be used.
qlgqloa8.speaker: questlog

qlgqloa9.dialogue: Beriand is worried because Nottle seems to be missing. Watch for signs of Nottle as you explore the Dungeons.
qlgqloa9.speaker: questlog

qlgqlob0.dialogue: Orogs told you that the Cult holds Nottle prisoner. To free Nottle, seek out the Cult outpost where he is being held.
qlgqlob0.speaker: questlog

qlgqlob1.dialogue: Orogs told you that the Key of Dumathoin can be used in a room in the Deep Halls.
qlgqlob1.speaker: questlog

qlgqlob2.dialogue: You need to free Nottle, who is being held in a cage deep in the Dungeons.
qlgqlob2.speaker: questlog

qlgqlob4.dialogue: Beriand told you of the Laughing Man, who dwells in the Dungeons and is friends with the creatures there. To learn more about him, explore the Main Halls.
qlgqlob4.speaker: questlog

qlgqlob5.dialogue: From a distance you heard what sounded like a crazy man, down in the Dungeon's Main Halls.
qlgqlob5.speaker: questlog

qlgqlob6.dialogue: To free the sorcerer Jarial from the stone, you must solve his riddle.
qlgqlob6.speaker: questlog

qlgqloY{.dialogue: The riddle is: 'A quest of love ends with me, yet I am made endlessly. If I drop, I say my name, if I touch rock, freedom gain.'
qlgqloY{.speaker: questlog

qlgqlob7.dialogue: Athan told you the Cult of the Dragon holds Castle Cormanthor, and has raised a Pool of Radiance beneath it. The Pool drains life from New Phlan and other cities, and if it is not destroyed, all of Faerun will fall under its thrall.
qlgqlob7.speaker: questlog

qlgqlob8.dialogue: You must continue along the underground approach, and infiltrate Castle Cormanthor.
qlgqlob8.speaker: questlog

qlgqlob9.dialogue: To enter the castle, you must try scaling its walls.
qlgqlob9.speaker: questlog

qlgqloc0.dialogue: He warned you that, to enter the castle, you may have to scale its walls and enter through the aerie of the dragon-kin.
qlgqloc0.speaker: questlog

qlgqloc2.dialogue: Beriand told you of a group of Ormyrrs, wandering within the Dungeons. To learn what brings them underground, find them and talk to them.
qlgqloc2.speaker: questlog

qlgqloc3.dialogue: Geb, the Ormyrr you met, told you of his tribe, the Sharpstick clan. He said they are somewhere else in the Dungeons.
qlgqloc3.speaker: questlog

qlgqloc4.dialogue: The Ormyrrs are superstitious and won't go near the orcs in the Sharpstick Room. To be able to trade with the Ormyrrs, you need to clear the Sharpstick Room of orcs.
qlgqloc4.speaker: questlog

qlgqloc6.dialogue: You heard the great wizard Mythanthor created portals that lead from one place to another. Many of these portals have been shut with his Seal.
qlgqloc6.speaker: questlog

qlgqloc7.dialogue: You saw the Great Seal of Mythanthor, a purple crescent arc, but you do not have the device that unseals it.
qlgqloc7.speaker: questlog

qlgqloc9.dialogue: To open the Way of Mythanthor and ascend to the City Heights, bring the Ring of Calling before the Seal of Mythanthor.
qlgqloc9.speaker: questlog

qlgqlod0.dialogue: To open the Way of Mythanthor and ascend to the City Heights, find the Skeletal Arm, release its Ring of Calling, and bring the Ring before the Seal of Mythanthor.
qlgqlod0.speaker: questlog

qlgqlod2.dialogue: Faeril told you how Borea, a mage of ice from the deep North, came to Myth Drannor many years ago, intending to unlock its secrets. She vanished without trace. Look for signs of her passing as you explore the Dungeons.
qlgqlod2.speaker: questlog

qlgqlod3.dialogue: In the Dungeons, you saw a frozen door. To explore more of the Dungeons, shatter the ice that seals this door.
qlgqlod3.speaker: questlog

qlgqlod4.dialogue: In the Dungeons, you entered a frozen chamber of mysterious purpose. To explore more of the Dungeons, you should investigate this chamber.
qlgqlod4.speaker: questlog

qlgqlod5.dialogue: In the Deep Halls, you unfroze the Rhonglyn, the magical transportation device of the elves. To explore more of the Dungeons, use its pillars to send your company to different places in the Dungeons.
qlgqlod5.speaker: questlog

qlgqloY|.dialogue: Emmeric said that rooms containing rings of colored stones could be the key to escaping the Dungeons.
qlgqloY|.speaker: questlog

qlgqloY}.dialogue: You found the Rhonglyn, a transportation device electric with the magic of old Myth Drannor. To explore more of the Dungeons, you must find and remove whatever has frozen one of its rooms.
qlgqloY}.speaker: questlog

qlgqlod7.dialogue: You have heard rumors that books of great power - and possibly great evil - exist somewhere in the Dungeons.
qlgqlod7.speaker: questlog

qlgqlod8.dialogue: To destroy evil books, you must feed them all to the Pyre of Silence.
qlgqlod8.speaker: questlog

qlgqloe0.dialogue: Rumors tell that a swarm of arraccat have made a nest in the Deep Halls of the Dungeons, and arraccat hatchlings play with the glittering treasures of many a hapless passerby.
qlgqloe0.speaker: questlog

qlgqloe1.dialogue: In the Deep Halls of the Dungeons, you came upon a swarm of arraccat guarding a nest laden with treasure.
qlgqloe1.speaker: questlog

qlgqloe3.dialogue: Legends tell that something called the 'Mountain Fist' was lost to fell spirits deep in the Dungeons.
qlgqloe3.speaker: questlog

qlgqloe4.dialogue: You defeated a murder of shadows and skeletons deep in the Dungeons, but haven't yet claimed their treasure.
qlgqloe4.speaker: questlog

qlgqloe6.dialogue: Somewhere in the Upper Dungeon, lizardfolk guard a well. The waters of this well are rumored to have great healing powers.
qlgqloe6.speaker: questlog

qlgqloe7.dialogue: In the Dungeon's Halls of Light, lizardfolk guard a well, the waters of which heal their wounds and refresh their spirits.
qlgqloe7.speaker: questlog

qlgqloe8.dialogue: At the Dwarven Brewers' Shrine, a voice told you that the Brewer's Onyx had been hidden 'in the throat of one of our children.' To find the Onyx, solve the riddle.
qlgqloe8.speaker: questlog

qlgqlof0.dialogue: You heard a rumor that the orcs are led by a great orc named Zud, who holds court in a vast hall in the northwest part of the Dungeon's Main Halls.
qlgqlof0.speaker: questlog

qlgqlof1.dialogue: In the Main Halls of the Dungeons, you were challenged by orcs guarding Zud's great hall. To clear the halls of orcs, you will have to defeat the one they revere as leader.
qlgqlof1.speaker: questlog

qlgqloY~.dialogue: You met some orcs who bragged about their leader, Zud, who lives in one of the Dungeon's Great Halls.
qlgqloY~.speaker: questlog

qlgqlof3.dialogue: Odelinde told you she heard a jailer walking his rounds, down in the Main Halls of the Dungeons. She said he jangled with every step.
qlgqlof3.speaker: questlog

qlgqlof4.dialogue: You heard tell that, down in the south part of the Main Halls of the Dungeons, a creature stalks the stairs there, jingling hundreds of keys on a chain.
qlgqlof4.speaker: questlog

qlgqlof5.dialogue: Down in the Main Halls of the Dungeons, past a secret door, you found the sign pointing to Bedlam Prison.
qlgqlof5.speaker: questlog

qlgqlof7.dialogue: Beriand had a dream about a mysterious wind which arose deep underground, when he threw something into a deep well.
qlgqlof7.speaker: questlog

qlgqlof8.dialogue: Odelinde told you of the Earthborn Wind, a gift of Shaundakul to Myth Drannor. A great Ruby initiates the blessing wind, and Juliban Genshihir was the Ruby's last caretaker.
qlgqlof8.speaker: questlog

qlgqlof9.dialogue: When you found the great Rillstone Ruby, a ghostly voice told you to 'Find the Well. Release the Ruby. Restore the Wind.'
qlgqlof9.speaker: questlog

qlgqlog0.dialogue: You restored the Earthborn Wind when you put the Rillstone Ruby into the Well of Earthborn Wind. You heard the blessing wind begin to flow again in the three ancient channels that wind up to the Halls of Stone.
qlgqlog0.speaker: questlog

qlgqlog1.dialogue: You have begun to reap the blessings of the Channels of Earthborn Wind, scattered through the Halls of Stone in the Dungeons.
qlgqlog1.speaker: questlog

qlgqloY.dialogue: You found ancient Channels in the Halls of Stone in the Dungeons, but they are dry and lifeless. Nothing flows up from below.
qlgqloY.speaker: questlog

qlgqloYÄ.dialogue: In the Deep Halls, you found the tomb of Juliban Genshihir, last Keeper of the Earthborn Wind.
qlgqloYÄ.speaker: questlog

qlgqloYÅ.dialogue: In the Deep Halls, you found a marker near the Well of the Earthborn Wind.
qlgqloYÅ.speaker: questlog

qlgqloYÇ.dialogue: You learned that blessed winds are supposed to flow up from the Well and emerge in the Channels above.
qlgqloYÇ.speaker: questlog

qlgqlog3.dialogue: When you get out of the Dungeons and reach the City Heights, remember to seek out Odelinde, the Golden Serpent, as Caalenfaire predicted you should.
qlgqlog3.speaker: questlog

qlgqlog4.dialogue: Caalenfaire told you that Odelinde, the Golden Serpent, could be a valuable ally, and predicted that you would find her somewhere on the City Heights.
qlgqlog4.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo~8.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo~9.dialogue: When you laid the baneblade Faervian back in Hachaam Selorn's grave, the ghost of the bladesinger told you of a long-lost prize - the baneblade Morvian, seized by the Demon Rivener and lost to sight centuries ago. He taught you the Rivening Word, which you are to use when you see the wall sealed with the Crescent Moon of Corellon Larethian, the Protector of Elves.
qlgqlo~9.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo0.dialogue: You have unsealed the Glyph of Moon that has contained the Demon Rivener since the time of Myth Drannor's fall. Now you must defeat the demon mage if you are to win the greatest of baneblades, Morvian.
qlgqlo0.speaker: questlog

qlgqlo1.dialogue: You saw the tomb of the hero Hachaam Selorn in the Dungeon's Halls of Light.
qlgqlo1.speaker: questlog

qlgdmaYë.dialogue: You brought forth the Emerald of the Weave from the Hoard of the Onaglym Dwarves, and helped Anorrweyn attune it to the Mythal.
qlgdmaYë.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYì.dialogue: You found and freed the hero Athan from his dank Cult prison cell.
qlgdmaYì.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYï.dialogue: You restored the baneblade Faervian to the tomb of Haacham Selorn, and defeated the Demon Rivener to bring the greatest of baneblades, Morvian, back into the light.
qlgdmaYï.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYó.dialogue: You used the Stone of Fate to bring ancient dwarven defenses to life, sealing the doom of the Cult forces defending the underground approach to Castle Cormanthor.
qlgdmaYó.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYô.dialogue: You brought doom upon the Cult forces defending the underground approach to Castle Cormanthor.
qlgdmaYô.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYõ.dialogue: You negotiated the underground approach to Castle Cormanthor, scaled the castle walls, and entered the Cult stronghold from above.
qlgdmaYõ.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYù.dialogue: With Nathlilik's help, you smashed the Vessel of Souls, sending into oblivion the souls of drow enslaved by the Cult.
qlgdmaYù.speaker: DM

qlgdmaYü.dialogue: Against great odds, you smashed the Vessel of Souls, sending into oblivion the souls of drow enslaved by the Cult.
qlgdmaYü.speaker: DM

qlgdmaY°.dialogue: You spoke the Word of Redemption, allowing Miroden Silverblade to destroy the Sapphire of the Weave. Now Anorrweyn Evensong controls the Mythal.
qlgdmaY°.speaker: DM

qlgdmaY£.dialogue: In open combat, you defeated Kya Mordrayn, allowing her soul to be claimed by her dark masters.
qlgdmaY£.speaker: DM

qlgdmaY•.dialogue: Finally, you slew the great dracolich Pelendralaar, and used the Gauntlets of Moander to destroy the Pool of Radiance, ending the Cult's threat to all the free peoples of the Realms.
qlgdmaY•.speaker: DM

vacdma00.dialogue: One of the nagas has a neck pouch. Inside it, you find a scrimbone - a bone that nagas write on, by holding the bone with their tongue and chiseling into it with a sharp fang.
vacdma00.speaker: DM

vacdma01.dialogue: On the bone, you can make out a name - 'Preybelish' - and a strange word. As you look at the word...
vacdma01.speaker: DM

vacdma02.dialogue: The naga's scrimbone teaches you the Word of Venom.
vacdma02.speaker: DM

kuydma03.dialogue: Among all the residue of old magics, you sense new power emanating from this ancient mirror.
kuydma03.speaker: DM

jjfdma02.dialogue: This door appears to be barred from the inside.
jjfdma02.speaker: DM

kuxdma03.dialogue: You know where you are - even after hundreds of years, the powerful aura of magics is unmistakable.
kuxdma03.speaker: DM

kuxdma04.dialogue: You have entered the Speculum - Myth Drannor's celebrated Hall of Wizards - abandoned ever since the city fell.
kuxdma04.speaker: DM

kvedma00.dialogue: An unseen presence haunts the shade of this tree...
kvedma00.speaker: DM

kvezve03.dialogue: Woe, woe to Myth Drannor! Hachaam Selorn is no more, and his baneblade Faervian - dark elves caress it deep in the Catacombs....
kvezve03.speaker: knghost

kvedmaYA.dialogue: You feel the presence sink back down out of the light.
kvedmaYA.speaker: DM

vekdma00.dialogue: After Pujik dies, the axe he bears shatters to pieces! And you sense a spell has been broken.
vekdma00.speaker: DM

vekdma01.dialogue: With its talisman gone and its minions destroyed, the Spawn Pool retreats underground, back to the deadly Pool of Radiance that spawned it.
vekdma01.speaker: DM

kvadma03.dialogue: The sturdy door is barred on this side. With some difficulty, you lift the bar.
kvadma03.speaker: DM

kvadma04.dialogue: Chill air pours out - you recognize the stale odor of the deep dungeons.
kvadma04.speaker: DM

kvddma03.dialogue: You recognize this bridge! A famous ballad sings of how Hachaam Selorn and a handful of heroes held this little bridge...
kvddma03.speaker: DM

kvddma04.dialogue: ...against companies of flinds, gnolls and ogre-kin, blocking the way with a mountain of burning bodies.
kvddma04.speaker: DM

kvddma05.dialogue: Of those great deeds, nothing remains.
kvddma05.speaker: DM

kvhdmaYA.dialogue: A human voice calls out to you from somewhere out of sight.
kvhdmaYA.speaker: DM

kvhdmaYB.dialogue: The one speaking is the human sorcerer Malgi Hi.
kvhdmaYB.speaker: DM

vejdma00.dialogue: Both the naga's totem and the Spawn Pool radiate malice. Hate flows out at you in buffeting waves.
vejdma00.speaker: DM

vendma00.dialogue: Your blow shatters the naga's totem, and breaks the aura of protection it gave to the Spawn Pool.
vendma00.speaker: DM

vendma01.dialogue: Seething, the Spawn Pool retreats into the deeps, back to the Pool of Radiance that sent it forth.
vendma01.speaker: DM

kvizvi02.dialogue: Wok ubukuk, gubgub? Oik ik ik!
kvizvi02.speaker: marg7
kvizvi02.desc: spoken, gleefully torturing someone; 'Ooh, aah, does that hurt, idiot?'

kvizvi03.dialogue: Ooh, aah, does that hurt? Oik ik ik!
kvizvi03.speaker: marg7

kvjdma03.dialogue: The sturdy door is barred on this side. With some difficulty, you lift the bar.
kvjdma03.speaker: DM

kvjdma04.dialogue: Chill dungeon air pours out - flavored with the rank smell of the lizardfolk.
kvjdma04.speaker: DM

jtqdma03.dialogue: The sturdy door is firmly blocked on the other side.
jtqdma03.speaker: DM

jtqdma05.dialogue: The grass around it is overgrown and it appears no one has opened this door in a long time.
jtqdma05.speaker: DM

jtrdma03.dialogue: You peer in the keyhole of this door and notice it's blocked with something - possibly the key.
jtrdma03.speaker: DM

jtrdma05.dialogue: It is useless trying to open the door from this side.
jtrdma05.speaker: DM

kzcDMYA.dialogue: The runes carved into these sturdy doors are ancient, but they seem to be wards that protect against evil.
kzcDMYA.speaker: DM

kzcDMYB.dialogue: You suspect that this was once a cache-hold of the legendary Knights of Myth Drannor.
kzcDMYB.speaker: DM

stndma02.dialogue: A small chamber lies behind the door. A well-made, cut-stone, dusty crawlway leads up out of the chamber.
stndma02.speaker: DM

stndma04.dialogue: You crawl through the stone passage to the surface.
stndma04.speaker: DM

stadma02.dialogue: You enter a short, steeply-descending tunnel. A slight, but steady stream of fresh air flows up from below.
stadma02.speaker: DM

stadma04.dialogue: You descend a short tunnel to the surface.
stadma04.speaker: DM

stbdma02.dialogue: You enter a short, gradually descending hallway. The air inside is stale.
stbdma02.speaker: DM

stbdma04.dialogue: You descend a hallway to the surface.
stbdma04.speaker: DM

stcdma02.dialogue: The door opens into a winding lateral passageway. The way is unlittered, but dusty from years of disuse.
stcdma02.speaker: DM

stcdma04.dialogue: You follow a winding passage to the surface.
stcdma04.speaker: DM

stddma02.dialogue: Behind the door is a level, rocky mining tunnel. All is quiet; the digging and production ceased years ago.
stddma02.speaker: DM

stddma04.dialogue: You scramble the length of the rocky tunnel to reach the surface.
stddma04.speaker: DM

stedma02.dialogue: You enter a narrow chamber, out of which climbs a ladder cut into the stone. You ascend carefully, as the rungs are worn from repeated use in years past.
stedma02.speaker: DM

stedma04.dialogue: You climb the stone ladder to the surface.
stedma04.speaker: DM

stfdma02.dialogue: The door opens onto a very steep stairway. After several switchbacking flights, you reach the surface.
stfdma02.speaker: DM

stfdma04.dialogue: You climb several short flights of stairs to the surface.
stfdma04.speaker: DM

stgdma02.dialogue: Behind the door is a steadily climbing, dirt-floored tunnel. The many sets of tracks you see were made long ago.
stgdma02.speaker: DM

stgdma04.dialogue: You ascend the dirt-floored tunnel to the surface.
stgdma04.speaker: DM

sthdma02.dialogue: Several short ramps climb back and forth to the surface. As you ascend, your armor and weapons clang-echo off the old stone walls.
sthdma02.speaker: DM

sthdma04.dialogue: You climb several short ramps to the surface.
sthdma04.speaker: DM

stidma02.dialogue: A cobwebbed stair climbs up immediately beyond the door. After many flights, you reach the surface.
stidma02.speaker: DM

stidma04.dialogue: You climb a cobwebbed stair to the surface.
stidma04.speaker: DM

stjdma02.dialogue: Behind the door is a lengthy, spiral stair, climbing up into the blackness. The air is cold, but stagnant, and you reach the surface without incident.
stjdma02.speaker: DM

stjdma04.dialogue: You ascend a long sprial stair.
stjdma04.speaker: DM

stkdma02.dialogue: Beyond the door a narrow stair rises up, up, up out of sight. After a long climb, you reach the surface.
stkdma02.speaker: DM

stkdma04.dialogue: You ascend a long, narrow stair.
stkdma04.speaker: DM

stldma02.dialogue: Before you lies a well-made stone stair. You ascend several hundered steps to the surface.
stldma02.speaker: DM

stmdma02.dialogue: The door opens onto a partially caved-in tunnel, littered with bones and debris.  The stench is heavy and the going slow, but you reach the surface safely.
stmdma02.speaker: DM

stmdma04.dialogue: You pick your way through the length of the partially caved-in tunnel.
stmdma04.speaker: DM

swodma03.dialogue: When you reach the top, you find a makeshift scaffold of immense beams supporting a rock-and-mortar wall.
swodma03.speaker: DM

swodma04.dialogue: Your dwarf quickly sizes up the structure, kicks aside one of the beams, and jumps back.  The wall wobbles for a second, then tumbles down.
swodma04.speaker: DM

swodma06.dialogue: The dwarves in your party talk amongst themselves, and reach a quick consensus. They lift a single beam out of the structure, and the wall crashes down.
swodma06.speaker: DM

swodma08.dialogue: Several heavy blows smashes one of the beams, and the wall collapses under its own weight.
swodma08.speaker: DM

swodma10.dialogue: You climb over the stones and lumps of sand-and-clay and emerge in the fresh air of Stillwater.
swodma10.speaker: DM

swodma12.dialogue: You emerge in the fresh air of Stillwater.
swodma12.speaker: DM

th1thi04.dialogue: Why have you come? The Blood Lesson? The Blood Blessing? Fiona's Kiss of Life? Speak.
th1thi04.speaker: Thirsty

th1thi05.dialogue: You stand on thirsty ground. Why have you come?
th1thi05.speaker: Thirsty

th1thi06.dialogue: If the spectre has caressed you, or the wraith kissed you, I can give back the life they stole from you...
th1thi06.speaker: Thirsty

th1thi07.dialogue: If someone has laid a curse upon you, I can remove it...
th1thi07.speaker: Thirsty

th1thi08.dialogue: If someone in your company is dead, I can restore them to life...
th1thi08.speaker: Thirsty

th1thi09.dialogue: I think you know what I want.
th1thi09.speaker: Thirsty

th1thi10.dialogue: Be assured I try not to take it all. Oh yes, I try VERY hard.
th1thi10.speaker: Thirsty

th1thi12.dialogue: Just let me slake my thirst.
th1thi12.speaker: Thirsty

th1thi14.dialogue: You do not need the Blood Lesson. You have not been drained of life.
th1thi14.speaker: Thirsty

th1thi15.dialogue: But since you asked for it, I will give you a lesson.
th1thi15.speaker: Thirsty

th1thi17.dialogue: Here, I give you back the life you lost...
th1thi17.speaker: Thirsty

th1thi18.dialogue: In return I take what I need.
th1thi18.speaker: Thirsty

th1thi27.dialogue: You do not need the Blood Blessing, for no one has laid a curse on you.
th1thi27.speaker: Thirsty

th1thi28.dialogue: But since you asked for it, I can hardly refuse.
th1thi28.speaker: Thirsty

th1thi30.dialogue: Behold! I lift all curses laid upon you...
th1thi30.speaker: Thirsty

th1thi31.dialogue: And take only a little of what I need.
th1thi31.speaker: Thirsty

th1thi39.dialogue: You do not need my Kiss of Life, for you have no dead people in your company.
th1thi39.speaker: Thirsty

th1thi40.dialogue: But since you offered me a kiss, it would be rude of me to refuse it.
th1thi40.speaker: Thirsty

th1thi41.dialogue: As you wish. Look! One touch from my lips restores life to your dead comrade...
th1thi41.speaker: Thirsty

th1thi42.dialogue: As you wish. Look! A touch from my lips restores life to your dead comrades...
th1thi42.speaker: Thirsty

th1thi43.dialogue: In return I steal from you just a little kiss...
th1thi43.speaker: Thirsty

th1thi44.dialogue: It is a kiss you may not soon forget.
th1thi44.speaker: Thirsty

th1pro00.dialogue: Ask what the ground is thirsty for
th1pro00.speaker: Protagonist

th1pro05.dialogue: Ask about Fiona's Kiss of Life
th1pro05.speaker: Protagonist

tzzDMYA.dialogue: You destroy the phylactery of the lich Thyaast Ammath, and scatter her life force to the winds of oblivion.
tzzDMYA.speaker: DM

tzzDMYB.dialogue: You destroy the lich's phylactery, the sanctum for her life force. Destroying Thyaast Ammath will now end her existence permanently.
tzzDMYB.speaker: DM
