tudtdo02.dialogue: Say, what is this? Friends of yours? If you've sold me out, Nottle, I swear by the Lord of Shadows, you'll pay. The treasure's mine!
tudtdo02.speaker: Tudo

tudntl00.dialogue: Ahhh - now it's YOUR treasure, is it? Yar crockin' our deal, Tudo, ya blarsted hothead.
tudntl00.speaker: Nottle

tudtdo03.dialogue: None of your business. It's mine and it'll stay mine.
tudtdo03.speaker: Tudo

tudntl01.dialogue: Hoho! We'll see about that, ya younking natterjack of a rogue.
tudntl01.speaker: Nottle

tudntl02.dialogue: What do you think? We killed them, heh heh.
tudntl02.speaker: Nottle

tudtdo05.dialogue: WE? I killed them, more like. Which is why the scroll belongs to me. So tell your bunch of strongarms here to get lost, or else.
tudtdo05.speaker: Tudo

tudntl03.dialogue: If I wanted that scroll, I'da have it now. I don't need no bunch o' strongarms to pluck a plum off a baby like you.
tudntl03.speaker: Nottle

tudntl04.dialogue: If'n you don't believe me, ask them.
tudntl04.speaker: Nottle

tudtdo07.dialogue: All right, strangers, what are you doing here, jinxing up our racket? Did Nottle put you up to this? Speak up, and be quick about it!
tudtdo07.speaker: Tudo

tudntl05.dialogue: Ahh, that's right, these are the ones I told you about, Tudo. The Pool of Radiance and all.
tudntl05.speaker: Nottle

tudntl06.dialogue: Ahh, no, don't believe them, they're lying!
tudntl06.speaker: Nottle

tudntl07.dialogue: These are the ones I told you about, Tudo. The Pool of Radiance and all.
tudntl07.speaker: Nottle

tudntl08.dialogue: You best listen to them, Tudo! These are the ones I told you about - the Pool of Radiance and all.
tudntl08.speaker: Nottle

tudtdo12.dialogue: Now nobody gets the scroll. You happy now?
tudtdo12.speaker: Tudo

tudntl09.dialogue: Agh, Tudo, you hotheaded clummitoad! These are the ones I told you about - the Pool of Radiance and all.
tudntl09.speaker: Nottle

tudtdo13.dialogue: Yeah, well, thanks for that. But you still ain't getting my treasure without a fight! Look at the dead mages! I can take care of myself!
tudtdo13.speaker: Tudo

tudntl10.dialogue: Ahhh now - hold on, Tudo, don't you recognize these folks? This is the 'small band' in the Song of Faerun!
tudntl10.speaker: Nottle

tudtdo14.dialogue: Ah, right - here you are in Myth Drannor, prizes dripping off you, and you don't want treasure.
tudtdo14.speaker: Tudo

tudntl11.dialogue: Ahhh now - hold on, Tudo, don't you recognize these folks? They're not after treasure, heh heh. They are the 'small band' in the Song of Faerun!
tudntl11.speaker: Nottle

tudtdo15.dialogue: Ah - ah - you are the ones the Bard of Kara-Tur sings about! Tell me, what is your secret? By Oghma's Beard, I wish the Bard would place MY deeds in the Song of Faerun!
tudtdo15.speaker: Tudo

tudtdo17.dialogue: Why, the Song of Faerun is the great tale of the world - as the Bard writes it, so it comes to be. To be in it is to breathe the air of immortality!
tudtdo17.speaker: Tudo

tudtdo18.dialogue: Ah, great things! Your exploits fire the blood! Listen...
tudtdo18.speaker: Tudo

tudtdo19.dialogue: 'The Pool! The Pool! It grows, and yet...'
tudtdo19.speaker: Tudo

tudntl13.dialogue: Ahh, 'tis marvelous. You have heard it? We heard it in the ruins of the Nightingale Court, at the column of the Whispering Wind!
tudntl13.speaker: Nottle

tudtdo20.dialogue: Ah, great things! Your exploits fire the blood! Listen...
tudtdo20.speaker: Tudo

tudtdo21.dialogue: 'From out the blackness, up to light...'
tudtdo21.speaker: Tudo

tudntl14.dialogue: '...Came one small band of growing might.
tudntl14.speaker: Nottle

tudntl15.dialogue: Ahh, 'tis marvelous. You have heard both verses? We heard them in the ruins of the Nightingale Court, at the column of the Whispering Wind!
tudntl15.speaker: Nottle

tudtdo22.dialogue: Will you merit a third verse? No one knows. But if you do - by Ibrandul's tongue, I would like to help you earn it!
tudtdo22.speaker: Tudo

tudntl16.dialogue: Him? Great deeds? Aha ha ha.
tudntl16.speaker: Nottle

tudntl17.dialogue: Then filchin' purses is a great deed, and coobilking maids, and muggling marks for coppers!
tudntl17.speaker: Nottle

tudtdo24.dialogue: I've been held down by the low company I've kept. Until now! This is my moment! Take me into your ranks, and no trap will sting you! No lock will keep you back!
tudtdo24.speaker: Tudo

tudntl18.dialogue: Well now, here's your chance at glory, Tudo. Hahar! A chance to roast in a Cult firestorm, more likely, heh heh.
tudntl18.speaker: Nottle

tudtdo27.dialogue: Shows what you know, you hardhead skinnuck, and why you'll always be a miserable old trader, carping for coppers. Glory and the firestorm, it's all the same.
tudtdo27.speaker: Tudo

tudtdo28.dialogue: Travelers! This is my moment! Take me into your ranks, and no trap will sting you! No lock will keep you from your destiny!
tudtdo28.speaker: Tudo

tudtdo30.dialogue: Yes! Together, we'll make the Cult cough up some rubies! Our deeds will be worth a song, and then some! So long, Nottle, you old boot.
tudtdo30.speaker: Tudo

tudntl19.dialogue: Hahar! That's a polite way of sayin' to get lost, Tudo.
tudntl19.speaker: Nottle

tudtdo33.dialogue: Shut up, you old boot. I know what it means. But they'll come around, mark my words! Hit a trap, or bump a lock, they'll reconsider.
tudtdo33.speaker: Tudo

tudtdo34.dialogue: When you do, look me up! You'll find me at Nottle's wagon. Until then, fare thee well!
tudtdo34.speaker: Tudo

tudntl20.dialogue: Well, you got no rogue in your company. And the lad does know how to tickle a lock and fuddle a trap.
tudntl20.speaker: Nottle

tudntlXA.dialogue: Just make him promise to shut his yap, and he might do you well.
tudntlXA.speaker: Nottle

tudntl21.dialogue: Well, you got a rogue already. But why not give the lad a chance? He tickles locks and fuddles traps better'n many.
tudntl21.speaker: Nottle

tudntl22.dialogue: Ahh, forget it, Tudo, their company is big enough already. Gets way too much of the wrong kind o' attention, heh heh.
tudntl22.speaker: Nottle

tudtdo40.dialogue: Then it is simple. One of them must stand aside, and I will take their place.
tudtdo40.speaker: Tudo

tudtdo41.dialogue: Yes! Together, we'll make the Cult cough up some rubies! We'll do deeds worth a song, and then some!
tudtdo41.speaker: Tudo

tudtdo42.dialogue: Let me know when you have decided who is to remain behind.
tudtdo42.speaker: Tudo

tudtdo43.dialogue: Brave words - but you'll come around, mark my words! Hit a trap, or meet a lock, you'll reconsider, and quickly.
tudtdo43.speaker: Tudo

tudntl23.dialogue: Well, you got rogues among ya already. But this lad tickles locks and fuddles traps better'n many...
tudntl23.speaker: Nottle

tudntl24.dialogue: ...and he's got spirit, I'll give him that! Why not give one o' your company a breather, a rogue maybe, and give him a chance instead?
tudntl24.speaker: Nottle

tudntl25.dialogue: You'd be doing me a big favor, heh heh. Think on it, eh?
tudntl25.speaker: Nottle

tudtdo47.dialogue: Then come find me at Nottle's wagon! Together, we'll make the Cult cough up some rubies! Now, fare thee well.
tudtdo47.speaker: Tudo

tudntl26.dialogue: Well, you got no rogue among you, and this lad tickles locks and fuddles traps better'n many...
tudntl26.speaker: Nottle

tudntl27.dialogue: ...and he's got spirit, I'll give him that! Why not give one o' your company a breather, and give him a chance?
tudntl27.speaker: Nottle

tudntl28.dialogue: You'd be doing me a big favor, heh heh. Think on it, eh?
tudntl28.speaker: Nottle

tudtdo51.dialogue: Then come find me at Nottle's wagon! Together, we'll make the Cult cough up some rubies! Our deeds will be worth a song, and then some! Now, fare thee well.
tudtdo51.speaker: Tudo

tudntl29.dialogue: Well, you got rogues among ya already. But this lad tickles locks and fuddles traps better'n many...
tudntl29.speaker: Nottle

tudntl30.dialogue: ...and he's got spirit, I'll give him that! Why not give one o' your company a breather, and give him a chance instead?
tudntl30.speaker: Nottle

tudtdo53.dialogue: Meaning no disrespect, maybe your dead should make room for the living... for one who is keen to avenge them!
tudtdo53.speaker: Tudo

tudtdo54.dialogue: Make room for me in your company! And then we'll make the Cult cough up some rubies! That is all I have to say.
tudtdo54.speaker: Tudo

tudntl31.dialogue: You see! They're not here to strongarm you, Tudo. They're the ones I told you about - seeking the Pool of Radiance.
tudntl31.speaker: Nottle

tudtdo56.dialogue: Ah - you are the ones in the Song of Faerun! By Oghma's Beard, I wish the Bard of Kara-Tur would sing about me!
tudtdo56.speaker: Tudo

tudtdo57.dialogue: If you have need of a rogue, think of me! After we leave here, look for me at Nottle's wagon. Fare thee well!
tudtdo57.speaker: Tudo

tudtdo58.dialogue: Wait! Wait! Don't you think you could take me with you? You'll need a skilled rogue, where you're going!
tudtdo58.speaker: Tudo

tudntl32.dialogue: Ahh, forget it, Tudo, their company is big enough already. Gets way too much of the wrong kind o' attention, heh heh.
tudntl32.speaker: Nottle

tudtdo60.dialogue: Well, if any of your company should stand aside, think of me. After we leave here, look for me at Nottle's wagon. Fare thee well!
tudtdo60.speaker: Tudo

tudtdo61.dialogue: Think on it! This is my moment! Take me into your party, and I will not fail you.
tudtdo61.speaker: Tudo

tudpro01.dialogue: Ask Tudo what the treasure is
tudpro01.speaker: Protagonist

tudpro02.dialogue: Demand that Tudo give you the treasure
tudpro02.speaker: Protagonist

tudpro03.dialogue: Assure Tudo you don't want his treasure
tudpro03.speaker: Protagonist

tudpro04.dialogue: Ask what happened to the Cult mages
tudpro04.speaker: Protagonist

tudpro06.dialogue: Tell him you were just passing by
tudpro06.speaker: Protagonist

tudpro07.dialogue: Tell him Nottle asked you to come
tudpro07.speaker: Protagonist

tudpro08.dialogue: Warn him about trying to boss you around
tudpro08.speaker: Protagonist

tudpro10.dialogue: Tell them they deserve each other, and move on
tudpro10.speaker: Protagonist

tudpro11.dialogue: Ask about the Bard and Song of Faerun
tudpro11.speaker: Protagonist

tudpro12.dialogue: Ask what the Song says about you
tudpro12.speaker: Protagonist

tudpro13.dialogue: Ask Tudo what great deeds he's done
tudpro13.speaker: Protagonist

tudpro14.dialogue: Hint that maybe Tudo could join you
tudpro14.speaker: Protagonist

tudpro15.dialogue: Tell Tudo your party is full
tudpro15.speaker: Protagonist

tudpro18.dialogue: Tell him your ranks are full
tudpro18.speaker: Protagonist

tudpro20.dialogue: Ask Nottle what you should do
tudpro20.speaker: Protagonist

tudpro22.dialogue: Take your leave of Nottle and Tudo
tudpro22.speaker: Protagonist

tudpro23.dialogue: Tell Tudo you might make room for him
tudpro23.speaker: Protagonist

tudpro24.dialogue: Tell Tudo he'll never join your party
tudpro24.speaker: Protagonist

tudpro26.dialogue: Ask Nottle what you should do
tudpro26.speaker: Protagonist

tu4tud02.dialogue: Heyya, brave heroes, my name is Tudo, I am a rogue of no little renown! You need someone of my skill if you're going to uncover all this fabulous city has to offer.
tu4tud02.speaker: Tudo
tu4tud02.desc: spoken, slick and smooth (text change) 5-2-01, lines combined

tu4tud04.dialogue: Let the clumsy one of your company stand aside! I am ready to join with you, and let the good times begin!
tu4tud04.speaker: Tudo

tu4tud05.dialogue: Take me into your ranks, and no trap will sting you! No lock will keep you from the treasures you so richly deserve.
tu4tud05.speaker: Tudo

tu4tud06.dialogue: Ah, heroes! I am so glad to see you again!
tu4tud06.speaker: Tudo

tu4not00.dialogue: You big liar. You lost a gross of gold pieces to me when they beat the Cult, heh heh.
tu4not00.speaker: Nottle

tu4tud07.dialogue: A bet I'm glad I lost, Nottle!
tu4tud07.speaker: Tudo

tu4not01.dialogue: Without him among you, he was sure you were doomed, the lordy strutabout!
tu4not01.speaker: Nottle

tu4tud08.dialogue: But now, the Cult is no more! And all the treasures of Myth Drannor lie at your feet - if you have a shrewd enough rogue with you, that is, ahem.
tu4tud08.speaker: Tudo

tu4tud09.dialogue: Ah, friends-in-arms, you have returned, huzzah! To take me away from this stinging gnat of a trader, I have no doubt.
tu4tud09.speaker: Tudo

tu4not02.dialogue: Argh, I hope so! For if I hear once more how you single-hand slew the dracolich...
tu4not02.speaker: Nottle

tu4tud10.dialogue: Single-handed! No! I used both hands. Oh, how I hope I can be one of you once again!
tu4tud10.speaker: Tudo

ttadma02.dialogue: You are deep below New Phlan, in the cavern where the Pool of Radiance has reawakened, threatening the city. The four people here are a sample adventuring party. Use them to explore this area, and you'll learn how to master this game. (click the left mouse button or press the space bar to continue.)
ttadma02.speaker: DM

ttadma03.dialogue: I am the Dungeon Master, the DM. Whenever you see lines like these, explaining game events or mechanics, the DM is telling you what is happening with your characters.
ttadma03.speaker: DM

ttadma04.dialogue: How do you get a character to do something? Look in the lower right corner of the screen. There are four colored bars - blue, green, purple, and yellow. Each character has been assigned one of these colors.
ttadma04.speaker: DM

ttadma05.dialogue: Let's tell your 'green' character to walk to a certain spot, and continue the tutorial from there.
ttadma05.speaker: DM

ttadma06.dialogue: To do that, try this: left-click on the green bar to select the green character. Then click on the ground near the opening at the end of the fence. Click the left mouse button or press the space bar when you're ready to begin.
ttadma06.speaker: DM

ttbdma02.dialogue: You don't have to move characters one at a time. To move your party as a group, use the round button in the lower right corner of the screen.
ttbdma02.speaker: DM

ttbdma03.dialogue: Click the button so that three people appear on it. When you do that, the characters will group themselves together, ready to travel as a party...
ttbdma03.speaker: DM

ttbdma04.dialogue: ...and if you click on the ground, the party leader will move there, and your other characters will follow.
ttbdma04.speaker: DM

ttbdma05.dialogue: Try it out. As a party, go through the opening at the end of the fence, then head east, over to the purple signpost. We'll continue the tutorial from there.
ttbdma05.speaker: DM

ttcdma02.dialogue: Now let me tell you about the icons that appear along the bottom of the game screen - you've probably figured out most of them already.
ttcdma02.speaker: DM

ttcdma03.dialogue: From left to right: the Game Options and Quest Log buttons, the Time of Day display, and the Map button, and, on the right side, the Party-At-A-Glance bars, the little Party Formation and Rest buttons, and the big Group/Ungroup Party button.
ttcdma03.speaker: DM

ttcdma04.dialogue: If you want a full explanation of each feature, you can get it at any time from this signpost, Playing the Game. The sign can also tell you how to take some common game actions.
ttcdma04.speaker: DM

ttcdma05.dialogue: To read what is posted, just click on the sign. When you are finished, select the last item in the talk menu. Now, I will display the information on the signpost.
ttcdma05.speaker: DM

ttddma02.dialogue: It's time to learn about the characters -- who are these people, anyway?
ttddma02.speaker: DM

ttddma03.dialogue: Just like what you learned at the Playing the Game signpost, most of what is here you can figure out by experimenting with the game yourself.
ttddma03.speaker: DM

ttddma04.dialogue: Except for the most important part:
ttddma04.speaker: DM

ttddma05.dialogue: To learn about a character or an object in the game, right click on him, her, or it.  This will bring up a small menu, which includes a name, a few statistics (HP means Hit Points, AC means Armor Class), and some menu choices.
ttddma05.speaker: DM

ttddma06.dialogue: But before we go on: after you are done reading, right click on a character or object.  Notice the sort of information you get.
ttddma06.speaker: DM

ttddma07.dialogue: Then, after you've looked around the interface some, left click on the signpost, All about Characters, to bring up a list of choices to learn more.
ttddma07.speaker: DM

tuadma02.dialogue: An icy draft penetrates your armor, and a chill creeps into your heart. You're in the dungeons now.
tuadma02.speaker: DM

tuadma03.dialogue: But it's only a single room, and not a very threatening one at that.
tuadma03.speaker: DM

tuadma04.dialogue: Notice the objects in this room: some barrels to the west and a couple of treasure chests to the east.
tuadma04.speaker: DM
tuadma04.desc: (text change) MAB, 04-27-01: removed ', a table north of you'

tuadma05.dialogue: To investigate an object, first approach it with one of your characters. This is stealthy work, so you may want to choose your rogue...
tuadma05.speaker: DM

tuadma06.dialogue: ...after all, when's the last time YOU saw a barbarian pick a lock?
tuadma06.speaker: DM

tuadma07.dialogue: Choose a character, and approach each object in turn. To get out of here, move down into the bottom corner of the room.
tuadma07.speaker: DM

tucdma02.dialogue: Here are three barrels. One of them has a key in it - the key to one of the chests on the other side of the room. Your job is to get that key. There are a couple of ways to do it...
tucdma02.speaker: DM

tucdma03.dialogue: You could just reach your hand in. To do that, you'll move the mouse cursor over a barrel and, when the hand icon appears, click. For barrels, or other open containers, a click means you search for and grab whatever's inside.
tucdma03.speaker: DM

tucdma04.dialogue: But maybe you're too cautious to grab. In that case, you could right-click on the barrel. This would bring up a menu of everything you can do with that object - options such as 'search' and 'smash.'
tucdma04.speaker: DM
tucdma04.desc: (text change) MAB, 04-27-01, edited out reference to 'move.'

tucdma05.dialogue: 'Search' would be the same as grabbing. If you choose 'Smash,' however, your character tries to break open the container. If it breaks, anything inside will spill out, and appear as a pile of treasure on the ground...
tucdma05.speaker: DM

tucdma06.dialogue: To get treasure out of a pile, click on it - and then drag whatever you want off the grid onto whichever character you want to have it.
tucdma06.speaker: DM

tucdma07.dialogue: In short, all objects in the game work this way: if you move the mouse cursor over something, and it turns into a hand, a left click means 'do the most common thing'; a right click means 'give me a list of everything I can do.'
tucdma07.speaker: DM

tucdma08.dialogue: Now, go ahead and check out those barrels!
tucdma08.speaker: DM

tucdma10.dialogue: Looks like you didn't get the key you need.
tucdma10.speaker: DM

tucdma11.dialogue: Did you investigate the barrel in the back?  Did you click-drag the key off the grid into a character's inventory? Is there a treasure pile lying around that you haven't gone through?
tucdma11.speaker: DM

tucdma13.dialogue: Looks like you've done everything there is to do here.  Head down into the bottom corner of the room to be transported back to the cavern under New Phlan.
tucdma13.speaker: DM

tucdma14.dialogue: Now it's time to use that key you found. Head across the room to the two chests.
tucdma14.speaker: DM

tucdma15.dialogue: You've already found the key. Why don't you head across the room to the chest on the right?
tucdma15.speaker: DM

uuddma02.dialogue: There are two chests here. You'll find one opens (with some difficulty) and one doesn't.
uuddma02.speaker: DM

uuddma03.dialogue: But don't let that stop you - click on each one anyway, just to see what happens.
uuddma03.speaker: DM

uuddma04.dialogue: Then head across the room to the barrels. They hold something you need.
uuddma04.speaker: DM

uuddma05.dialogue: You'll need a key to open the chest on the left.  It's hidden in one of the barrels on the other side of the room.
uuddma05.speaker: DM

uuddma07.dialogue: Oops, you forgot to pick up the key.  The barrel in the back has a key in it; you won't be able to open one of the chests without it.
uuddma07.speaker: DM

uuddma09.dialogue: Now let's clean out some treasure chests!
uuddma09.speaker: DM

uuddma10.dialogue: To do that, you'll click on each one, and see what happens. Don't forget to put anything you find into inventory - click-drag it off the treasure grid and onto one of your characters.
uuddma10.speaker: DM

uuddma11.dialogue: If you really want to do this right, use rogue skills on the chests. To do that, right-click on your rogue character, and select (S)kills. 'Search,' 'Open Lock,' and 'Disable Device' can be lifesavers in situations like this.
uuddma11.speaker: DM

uuddma13.dialogue: Before opening that chest on the right, you might want to try out some of your rogue's skills on it.
uuddma13.speaker: DM

uuddma14.dialogue: Right click on your rogue, then select (S)kills.  Search, Open Lock, and Disable Device can all be particularly useful.
uuddma14.speaker: DM

uuddma17.dialogue: You've done everything there is to do in here.  Go down into the bottom corner of the room, and you'll be transported back to the cavern under New Phlan.
uuddma17.speaker: DM

tvadma02.dialogue: Monsters.  Deep in the dungeons of Myth Drannor, there are monsters everywhere, eager to take your treasure and your lives.
tvadma02.speaker: DM

tvadma03.dialogue: Of course, this is only the tutorial, so the threat is very small. Only a single orc, unaware as yet of your presence.
tvadma03.speaker: DM

tvadma04.dialogue: Let's learn about combat - starting with what happens before the fighting starts. Sometimes you spot the enemy before he sees you. This gives you a few options...
tvadma04.speaker: DM

tvadma05.dialogue: You can try to move away before you are noticed - very advisable if the monsters look too strong for you.
tvadma05.speaker: DM

tvadma06.dialogue: You can try to sneak past the creature. It might not notice you. Of course, the closer you get, the greater the chance you will be detected.
tvadma06.speaker: DM

tvadma07.dialogue: You can approach the creature. Not all creatures you meet are enemies - and even some enemies will talk rather than fight.
tvadma07.speaker: DM

tvadma08.dialogue: Or you can attack. If, when you put the cursor over a creature, it turns into a sword, a click will begin combat.
tvadma08.speaker: DM

tvadma09.dialogue: Go ahead and deal with this orc - walk up to it, or click on it to start a fight.
tvadma09.speaker: DM

tvbdma01.dialogue: Okay! You've triggered combat. Now each character and adversary take their actions one at a time, in order from fastest to slowest.
tvbdma01.speaker: DM

tvbdma02.dialogue: In the upper left corner of the screen, a row of colored icons will appear - the initiative bar. This bar graphically displays the order in which the combatants will take their actions.
tvbdma02.speaker: DM

tvbdma03.dialogue: In the initiative bar, each character is represented by a gem of his or her color, and the monsters are represented by red creature faces. But let's get on with how to fight!
tvbdma03.speaker: DM

tvbdma04.dialogue: A pulsing circle underneath one of your characters means it's his or her turn to act. To attack the orc, click on it. Your character will approach the orc and strike it - or, if holding a missile weapon, will fire it at the orc.
tvbdma04.speaker: DM

tvbdma05.dialogue: To cast a spell, right-click on your character, choose 'arcane spells' or 'divine spells,' then pick a spell and a target. Now go to it!
tvbdma05.speaker: DM

tvcdma01.dialogue: Now that the orc is dead, you may want to loot its body. Once the monsters are dead, if they have treasure, it's all gathered into one treasure-pile object; click on it to get the loot.
tvcdma01.speaker: DM

tvcdma02.dialogue: You also may want to rest. Rest heals your characters and restores the spells they used up during the fight. To rest, click on the tent in the lower right corner of the screen. But be careful...
tvcdma02.speaker: DM

tvcdma03.dialogue: If the tent is green, you are in a place where resting is safe. If it is yellow, monsters may interrupt your rest. And if it's red, it's not safe for rest at all.
tvcdma03.speaker: DM

tvcdma04.dialogue: Go ahead and rest here. Then move the table (or smash it), and click on the door to open it... although you may want to right-click on it and (L)ook through its barred window first.
tvcdma04.speaker: DM

tvddma01.dialogue: One orc down, a few more to go!  Don't forget to collect the booty.  Click on the treasure pile.  When the grid pops up, click and drag the items you want to the characters you want to have them.
tvddma01.speaker: DM

tvedma02.dialogue: Now, as you clash with these orcs, pay attention to the cursor. The icons on it can help you plan your movement.
tvedma02.speaker: DM

tvedma03.dialogue: Each character's combat turn is divided into two halves. During the first half, you can move, or attack, or cast a spell. During the second half, you can move - and attack, unless you've attacked already.
tvedma03.speaker: DM

tvedma04.dialogue: As you move the cursor around to potential destinations, if there is a '+' sign, you know it will take only half a move to get there - leaving some time to attack. If there is no '+', it will take your entire turn to get there.
tvedma04.speaker: DM

tvedma05.dialogue: When you are done with a character's turn, and want to move on to the next one, hit the space bar.
tvedma05.speaker: DM

tvedma06.dialogue: One more thing: from time to time your party catch the monsters off guard, surprising them.
tvedma06.speaker: DM

tvedma07.dialogue: When this happens, the initiative bar -- the colored gems in the upper left corner of the screen -- will appear for only your characters: there will be no red monster icons.
tvedma07.speaker: DM

tvedma08.dialogue: This means that for the the first round of combat, each character in your party may take a single action before the any monster can react.
tvedma08.speaker: DM

tvedma09.dialogue: But be careful: a SINGLE action is NOT a full combat turn, it is only a half turn.  A character may either move OR attack, but not both.
tvedma09.speaker: DM

tvedma10.dialogue: So, you can make a ranged attack (with a bow, sling, or spell) OR move, but not fire AND THEN move.
tvedma10.speaker: DM

tvedma11.dialogue: Lastly, the monsters also sometimes surprise your party.  If you see a single red monster icon in the upper left hand corner, that's what happened.  They all get to take an action, before you can do anything.
tvedma11.speaker: DM

tvedma12.dialogue: Sometime you beat them to the punch, and sometimes they get the jump on you.
tvedma12.speaker: DM

tvfdma01.dialogue: Three more orcs down. Don't forget to take their treasure - find the treasure pile and click on it.
tvfdma01.speaker: DM

tvfdma02.dialogue: Your next combat is off to the southwest. But you will notice that there doesn't seem to be any way into that chamber.
tvfdma02.speaker: DM

tvfdma03.dialogue: That's because the way in is hidden -- a secret door. To find it, select your rogue, and move him near the wall dividing these rooms.
tvfdma03.speaker: DM

tvfdma04.dialogue: He will apply his powers of observation automatically, and look for the door.  If he doesn't find it right away, you may have to use his search skill.
tvfdma04.speaker: DM

tvfdma05.dialogue: When he does find the door, it will become visible.  Open it and go into the next chamber.
tvfdma05.speaker: DM

tvgdma01.dialogue: By now you know the basics of moving and attacking. When you fight your next adversary, try some more advanced combat options.
tvgdma01.speaker: DM

tvgdma02.dialogue: When it's your character's combat turn, right-click on him or her, and choose 'combat options.'
tvgdma02.speaker: DM

tvgdma03.dialogue: You can probably figure out each option by its name, or by using it a few times. To learn more, click on the Combat Commands signpost in front of you, or read the full description in the manual.
tvgdma03.speaker: DM

tvgdma04.dialogue: To fight your last adversary, go past the signpost. After you defeat him, move down to the south corner of this room to exit.
tvgdma04.speaker: DM

txzdma01.dialogue: You have defeated everyone here in the tutorial dungeon. To go back to the main cavern, walk into the corner south of here.
txzdma01.speaker: DM

txadma02.dialogue: Don't forget: you can return here any time to practice manipulating objects. Just go through the door that brought you here the first time.
txadma02.speaker: DM

txbdma02.dialogue: Don't forget: you can return here any time to practice combat. Just go through the portal that brought you here the first time.
txbdma02.speaker: DM

tttdma02.dialogue: Please move the party closer to the signpost to continue the tutorial.
tttdma02.speaker: DM

tttdma03.dialogue: To learn about a character or object in the game, right click on him, her, or it.  This will bring up a small menu, which includes name, a few statistics (HP means Hit Points, AC means Armor Class), and some menu choices.
tttdma03.speaker: DM

tttdma04.dialogue: The options below discuss each of those menu choices.
tttdma04.speaker: DM

tttdma05.dialogue: When you right click on one of your characters, the first menu option (underneath the HP and AC line) is Character Sheet.
tttdma05.speaker: DM

tttdma06.dialogue: This selection brings up a graphical information page for the individual you clicked on.
tttdma06.speaker: DM

tttdma07.dialogue: One of the features of this page is a grid containing the character's equipment.  To equip or swap weapons, armor, rings, amulets, gauntlets, or boots, click-drag and then drop.
tttdma07.speaker: DM

tttdma08.dialogue: Also on the Character Sheet are tabs for spells, skills & feats, and stats.  Click on a tab to see the associated list for the character.
tttdma08.speaker: DM

tttdma09.dialogue: Unlike the inventory display, these lists are not interactive: they only display information about the character.
tttdma09.speaker: DM

tttdma10.dialogue: Also: You may not cast spells from the Character Sheet; that can only be done from the pop-up menus (see casting arcane or divine spells).
tttdma10.speaker: DM

tttdma11.dialogue: There are number of non-player characters (NPCs) in Pool of Radiance II.  You may wish to add some of them to your party.
tttdma11.speaker: DM

tttdma12.dialogue: However, the party may not have more than six characters in it at any one time.
tttdma12.speaker: DM

tttdma13.dialogue: If your party is full, and you want to add an NPC, you will have to 'make room.' To do this, right click on the character you want to kick out, and...
tttdma13.speaker: DM

tttdma14.dialogue: ...then select 'Remove from Party.' This will free up a slot in your party, and leave the removed character behind.
tttdma14.speaker: DM

tttdma15.dialogue: But take care: Although single characters have been known to turn up at various places in Myth Drannor, not everyone you leave behind will find his or her way to safety.
tttdma15.speaker: DM

tttdma16.dialogue: When you select '(I)nventory' after right clicking on a character, a second menu appears: Magic / Weapons / Armor)
tttdma16.speaker: DM

tttdma17.dialogue: Select one of these to see a list of this character's items for that category.  For example, choosing 'Weapons' will display a menu of all swords, axes, daggers, hammers, and so on.
tttdma17.speaker: DM

tttdma18.dialogue: To equip a weapon, select it. It appears in the character's hand, and any other weapon he or she was using is put back into inventory.
tttdma18.speaker: DM

tttdma19.dialogue: Some of the items under the 'Magic' heading don't equip -- such as potions and scrolls. When you select one these, the character uses it: drinks the potion, or reads the scroll.
tttdma19.speaker: DM

tttdma20.dialogue: One more thing: if one of the selections -- Magic / Weapons / Armor -- is gray, that means you cannot select it.
tttdma20.speaker: DM

tttdma21.dialogue: Either the character has no items of that category, or equipping or using items of that type cannot be performed at that time during the game.  For example, armor may not be taken off or put on during combat.
tttdma21.speaker: DM

tttdma22.dialogue: Lastly, notice that this menu choice is '(I)nventory.'  The 'I' is in parentheses, because you can press the 'i' key to bring up the inventory directly, without going through the right click menu.
tttdma22.speaker: DM

tttdma23.dialogue: A click on the '(S)kills' selection lists the character's special skills.
tttdma23.speaker: DM

tttdma24.dialogue: To direct the character to apply one of these, select it.  The DM will explain whether the skill was successfully executed or not.
tttdma24.speaker: DM

tttdma25.dialogue: There are two sets of spells in Pool of Radiance II: arcane and divine.  Sorcerers can cast only (A)rcane Spells.
tttdma25.speaker: DM

tttdma26.dialogue: When you select 'arcane spells,' a spell level menu will appear.  It looks something like this: 'Cantrips / 1st Level / 2nd Level' and so on.
tttdma26.speaker: DM

tttdma27.dialogue: If a level is gray, that means the character has no spells of that level, or has already cast all he or she can, and must rest to regain them, or may not cast any of the spells of that level outside of combat.
tttdma27.speaker: DM

tttdma28.dialogue: To cast a spell, you must know what level it is.  Select the appropriate level; a list of spells will appear.
tttdma28.speaker: DM

tttdma29.dialogue: Select the spell you want to cast.  The menu will vanish.  Next select a target, and the character will animate and launch the spell.
tttdma29.speaker: DM

tttdma30.dialogue: Final note: to help with spells which can affect multiple targets, as you move the cursor to target the spell, the characters and monsters that will be hit by the spell turn red.
tttdma30.speaker: DM

tttdma31.dialogue: There are two sets of spells in Pool of Radiance II: arcane and divine.  Clerics (and Paladins and Rangers) can cast only (D)ivine Spells.
tttdma31.speaker: DM
tttdma31.desc: (Text Change)MAB, 06-08-01: added '(and Paladins and Rangers)' to list of characters who can cast divine spells

tttdma32.dialogue: When you select 'divine spells,' a spell level menu will appear.  It looks something like this: 'Orisons / 1st Level / 2nd Level' and so on.
tttdma32.speaker: DM

tttdma33.dialogue: If a level is gray, that means the character has no spells of that level, or has already cast all he or she can, and must rest to regain them, or may not cast any of the spells of that level outside of combat.
tttdma33.speaker: DM

tttdma34.dialogue: To cast a spell, you must know what level it is.  Select the appropriate level; a list of spells will appear.
tttdma34.speaker: DM

tttdma35.dialogue: Select the spell you want to cast.  The menu will vanish.  Next select a target, and the character will animate and launch the spell.
tttdma35.speaker: DM

tttdma36.dialogue: Final note: to help with spells which can effect multiple targets, as you move the cursor to target the spell, the characters and monsters that will be hit by the spell turn red.
tttdma36.speaker: DM

tttdma37.dialogue: The final choice on the character right-click menu is (C)ombat Options.  These will be gray and unavailable, unless the party is in combat.
tttdma37.speaker: DM

tttdma38.dialogue: The combat options will be discussed in the Chamber of the Sword, later in the tutorial.
tttdma38.speaker: DM

tttdma40.dialogue: When you are ready, continue onward to the right, past the signpost, and up the screen a little.  Continue moving right until you see a portcullis in the wall.
tttdma40.speaker: DM

tttdma41.dialogue: When you get close enough to the opening, the cursor will change when you move the mouse cursor over it.
tttdma41.speaker: DM

tttdma42.dialogue: Left click to be transported into a room.
tttdma42.speaker: DM

tttpro01.dialogue: Removing a character from the party
tttpro01.speaker: Protagonist

tvhdma01.dialogue: When it's a character's turn, right click on him or her to pop up a menu, then choose 'combat options' to bring up a list of different attacks or actions this character may perform this turn.
tvhdma01.speaker: DM

tvhdma02.dialogue: When reviewing the list below, keep in mind that different character classes have different combat options, and not every character will have available every option.  Also, characters gain more options as they go up in levels.
tvhdma02.speaker: DM

tvhdma04.dialogue: Choose 'Full Attack' when you want your character to focus this turn entirely on attacking an enemy.
tvhdma04.speaker: DM

tvhdma05.dialogue: A full attack uses up both halves of the combat turn in an effort to execute the maximum number of attacks against an opponent.
tvhdma05.speaker: DM

tvhdma06.dialogue: The 'power attack' trades accuracy for damage.  You character will focus all his or her energy on damaging the opponent, but will also miss the target more often.
tvhdma06.speaker: DM

tvhdma07.dialogue: Select 'defend' when you want your character to stand ready, but take no other action this turn.
tvhdma07.speaker: DM

tvhdma08.dialogue: Delay alters the initiative order for this entire combat by delaying the character's combat turn until after all other characters and monsters have acted.
tvhdma08.speaker: DM

tvhdma09.dialogue: This can be useful, if you want to wait to see what action a monster takes or how much damage another character does before deciding what to do.
tvhdma09.speaker: DM

tvhdma10.dialogue: When you choose 'delay,' the character's diamond in the intiative bar moves to the from its current position to the right end.
tvhdma10.speaker: DM

tvhdma11.dialogue: If you rest when the rest indicator is yellow, wandering monsters may interupt your recovery.
tvhdma11.speaker: DM

tvhdma12.dialogue: When this happens, one character will be on watch, but the others in the party will still be asleep.
tvhdma12.speaker: DM

tvhdma13.dialogue: Choose 'awaken party member' to wake up everyone else.  This will use up your character's entire combat turn, but it will likely be worth to get others to help you fend off the wandering monsters.
tvhdma13.speaker: DM

tvhdma14.dialogue: Clerics have the power to repell or even destroy undead monsters.  To attempt this action, choose 'turn undead.'
tvhdma14.speaker: DM

tvhdma15.dialogue: Keep in mind that turning undead is not a sure thing, and that powerful monsters are more difficult to turn than weaker ones.
tvhdma15.speaker: DM

tvhdma16.dialogue: Barbarians can turn themselves into extra-powerful fighters for a short duration during a combat.  Choose 'rage' to do this.
tvhdma16.speaker: DM

tvhdma17.dialogue: Your character will hit his or her target more frequently, and will do more damage on each hit, but at the cost of his or her own defensive capability.
tvhdma17.speaker: DM

tvhdma18.dialogue: Use rage selectively.  A barbarian can only rage once per combat.
tvhdma18.speaker: DM

tutkel02.dialogue: Approach certain characters, and look what happens. They speak to you.
tutkel02.speaker: Kellan

tutkel03.dialogue: After they speak, you choose a response. Careful! What you choose matters.
tutkel03.speaker: Kellan

tutkel05.dialogue: For now, my business is my own. You will find out who I serve soon enough.
tutkel05.speaker: Kellan

tutkel06.dialogue: I admire your persistence. But do not expect the people you meet to tell you everything you want to know - unless it serves their interests.
tutkel06.speaker: Kellan

tutkel07.dialogue: If you take the time to talk to people, you'll learn things to help you on your journey. Secrets may be divulged. Enemies may become friends.
tutkel07.speaker: Kellan

tutkel08.dialogue: If you parley with your enemies, you may gain the advantage of surprise. But be watchful! Or else they may surprise you instead.
tutkel08.speaker: Kellan

tutkel09.dialogue: Merely approach the person. Usually they speak up, if they have something to say.
tutkel09.speaker: Kellan

tutkel10.dialogue: Some characters may also be storytellers. The cursor will change to a PROFILE SPEAKING icon when it passes over them. Click to hear some of the rumors and legends they know now, and visit them again to learn more.
tutkel10.speaker: Kellan

tutkel11.dialogue: Over other characters, the cursor will change to TWO HANDS. If the hands are one above the other, click to buy or sell items. If the hands are side by side, click if you wish to have that character join your party.
tutkel11.speaker: Kellan

tutkel13.dialogue: You will meet people who believe in your quest. If you ask them, they may be willing to join your ranks. After you talk to them, TWO HANDS side-by-side will appear when you move the mouse cursor over them.
tutkel13.speaker: Kellan

tutkel14.dialogue: In time, I may be one of these people - if you prove yourselves worthy.
tutkel14.speaker: Kellan

tutkel15.dialogue: Doors closed to you will be opened. That which was lost will be found. Friends unexpectedly appear. And everywhere you will hear of the thread of evil, undoing all your hopes.
tutkel15.speaker: Kellan

tutkel16.dialogue: Enough of your questions! Instead, a test. Let's see if you've been paying attention.
tutkel16.speaker: Kellan

tutkel17.dialogue: Now, no more talk! Do not expect people to stand around and jaw with you all day. Here's a little test - to see if you've been paying attention.
tutkel17.speaker: Kellan

tutkel18.dialogue: You did not ask how your responses can shape your progress in the game! Ah, you will find out soon enough.
tutkel18.speaker: Kellan

tutkel19.dialogue: Remember, just approach a person, or click on them, if you want to talk to them.
tutkel19.speaker: Kellan

tutkel20.dialogue: Goodbye? You think so? I don't think you can get rid of me that easily.
tutkel20.speaker: Kellan

tutkelYA.dialogue: To show you a mild example, I'll stop talking - let's see if you can figure out what to do next.
tutkelYA.speaker: Kellan

tutkelYB.dialogue: Have you been paying attention? Let's find out.
tutkelYB.speaker: Kellan

tu5kel02.dialogue: Ah, yes. You saw the PROFILE SPEAKING cursor on me, and you clicked. Very good.
tu5kel02.speaker: Kellan
tu5kel02.desc: spoken, only the 'Aah yes' part of ke2kel45; (text change) KE 6-4-01, and MAB 06-12-01, changed 'TWO HANDS' to 'PROFILE SPEAKING'

tu5kel03.dialogue: Now, what shall we talk about? Choose carefully! Do not expect people to stand around and jaw with you all day.
tu5kel03.speaker: Kellan

tu5kel04.dialogue: Aya, they are back! Not the sharpest arrows in the quiver, are you?
tu5kel04.speaker: Kellan
tu5kel04.desc: spoken, only the 'Aya, they are back!' part of ke2kel89; (text change)KE 6-4-01

tu5kel05.dialogue: You may call me Kellan... I am a fighting sorcerer for the group called the Silver Fire.
tu5kel05.speaker: Kellan

tu5kel06.dialogue: But I used to wield sword and spell for someone else. My name was different then... it would have killed you to hear it.
tu5kel06.speaker: Kellan

tu5kel07.dialogue: If we meet, we will meet in Myth Drannor. I might be friend to you when friends are rare indeed.
tu5kel07.speaker: Kellan

tu5kel08.dialogue: We are here in New Phlan. Enjoy its peaceful streets while you can!
tu5kel08.speaker: Kellan

tu5kel09.dialogue: Soon you will join me in Myth Drannor, the City of Song - a magnificent ruin that is anything but peaceful.
tu5kel09.speaker: Kellan

tu5kel10.dialogue: I am under the orders of the incantrix Fieryat Ildacer. There is someone in Myth Drannor she bids me to destroy...
tu5kel10.speaker: Kellan

tu5kel11.dialogue: You will have your own quests, many of them - but I know not what they are.
tu5kel11.speaker: Kellan

tu5kel12.dialogue: When you meet characters, approach them closely. Often they will speak to you, if they have something to say.
tu5kel12.speaker: Kellan

tu5kel13.dialogue: Also, roll your cursor over them, even after you've talked with them. A PROFILE SPEAKING cursor means 'click to learn more,' or 'to hear stories and legends'...
tu5kel13.speaker: Kellan

tu5kel14.dialogue: The TWO HANDS side-by-side cursor means 'click if you want me to join your party' and TWO HANDS one over another means 'click if you want me to buy or sell items.'
tu5kel14.speaker: Kellan

tu5kel15.dialogue: Do not be too quick to attack characters that don't attack you! If you approach them, they may parley with you, and you might learn something valuable.
tu5kel15.speaker: Kellan

tu5kel16.dialogue: Ah, you do not waste time jawboning! I like that. I hope we meet again, and raise swords together...
tu5kel16.speaker: Kellan

tu5kel17.dialogue: Goodbye. I hope we meet again, and raise swords together...
tu5kel17.speaker: Kellan

tu5kel18.dialogue: And now I must go. Goodbye - or maybe, until we meet again.
tu5kel18.speaker: Kellan

txxdma02.dialogue: These are keyboard shortcuts you may find handy. The first five are general game functions; the next four pertain to the highlighted (active) character.
txxdma02.speaker: DM
txxdma02.desc: (Text Change) There are two text changes here, one on 4-24-01, and one on 06-08-01: 'five' to 'four'

txxdma04.dialogue: Press the ESCape key to bring up the Game Menu, to load or save a game, change the game settings, or quit back to Windows.
txxdma04.speaker: DM

txxdma05.dialogue: It's the same as clicking on the round blue button in the lower left corner of the screen.
txxdma05.speaker: DM

txxdma07.dialogue: Press the RIGHT SHIFT key to switch your characters from walking to running mode. Press it again to switch back.
txxdma07.speaker: DM

txxdma08.dialogue: When walking, your characters move slowly and carefully; they are quicker to notice enemies or things hidden in the environment. When running, they concentrate on getting from here to there as fast as they can, not on noticing things.
txxdma08.speaker: DM

txxdma10.dialogue: Underneath each character and monster are one to three colored circles.  These tell you at a glance how healthy that character is: the more circles, the healthier.
txxdma10.speaker: DM

txxdma11.dialogue: Normally, only the active character (the one whose turn it is) has his or her circles visible. To see all character and monster circles, press the LEFT ALT key; to see only the active character's circles, press LEFT ALT again.
txxdma11.speaker: DM

txxdma13.dialogue: To group or ungroup your party, press the ENTER key on the lower right corner of the keyboard, near the number keypad. This is the same as clicking on the round button in the lower right corner of the screen.
txxdma13.speaker: DM

txxdma14.dialogue: When grouped, you click to move or act with the party leader, and the party's other characters follow your leader. When ungrouped, you click to move or act with only the active character.
txxdma14.speaker: DM

txxdma16.dialogue: Press the BACKSLASH (' \ ') key to call up the Character Sheet for the active character.
txxdma16.speaker: DM

txxdma17.dialogue: It's the same as right-clicking on the character and selecting 'Character Sheet.'
txxdma17.speaker: DM

txxdma19.dialogue: Press the 'i' key to bring up an inventory menu for the active character. The menu has dropdown lists of the character's Magic items, Weapons and Armor. Your character can choose which items to equip from these lists.
txxdma19.speaker: DM

txxdma20.dialogue: It's the same as right-clicking on the character and selecting  'Inventory'.
txxdma20.speaker: DM

txxdma22.dialogue: Press the 'a' or 'd' key to call up a spellcasting menu - 'a' for 'arcane' spells (for sorcerers) and 'd' for 'divine' spells (for clerics).
txxdma22.speaker: DM

txxdma23.dialogue: It's the same as right-clicking on the character and selecting either 'arcane spells'  or 'divine spells'.
txxdma23.speaker: DM

txxdma25.dialogue: Press the 's' key to use one of the active character's skills. It's the same as right-clicking on the character and selecting 'skills'.
txxdma25.speaker: DM

txxdma26.dialogue: Press the 'c' key to select one of the active character's combat options. It's the same as right-clicking on the character and selecting 'combat options'.  Remember, these options are only available during combat.
txxdma26.speaker: DM

txxdma28.dialogue: One last tip: you may want to save your game right here. That way, you can easily return and review these keyboard shortcuts.
txxdma28.speaker: DM

txxdma29.dialogue: To save your game, press ESCape to bring up the Game Menu, and select Save Game. Label it something like 'keyboard shortcuts.' Then press Resume Game.
txxdma29.speaker: DM

txxdma31.dialogue: Press the 'F1' key to bring up a list of the game's hotkeys.
txxdma31.speaker: DM

txydma02.dialogue: Here's a tip: to learn some keyboard shortcuts, head over to the signpost to your left and down.
txydma02.speaker: DM

ttxdma02.dialogue: Okay, I'll let you in on a secret. Danger awaits if you follow this walkway. If you want to learn a little more about the game first, head on East, and go through the door.
ttxdma02.speaker: DM

ttxdma03.dialogue: There is danger this way.  If you want to learn a little more about the game first, head South: look for the blue signpost, 'All about Characters.'
ttxdma03.speaker: DM

ttwinf03.dialogue: This signpost, Playing the Game, can teach you about elements of the interface, or you can ask about things you want to learn how to do.
ttwinf03.speaker: infowell

ttwinf05.dialogue: The round button in the lower left corner breaks away from the game action to mundane bookkeeping functions.
ttwinf05.speaker: infowell

ttwinf06.dialogue: Click on the Game Options button to bring up a menu, from which you can load or save games, quit the game, and change the game settings.
ttwinf06.speaker: infowell

ttwinf07.dialogue: When you are done talking to me, try saving your game. Then, whenever you want to ask me a question, all you have to do is load that saved game.
ttwinf07.speaker: infowell

ttwinf08.dialogue: In the box at the lower left corner of the screen, you'll find a book, a sun, and a map icon. These are the Quest Log, Time of Day, and Map functions, respectively.
ttwinf08.speaker: infowell

ttwinf09.dialogue: Click on the Quest Log book to remind yourself about quests you've heard of, but haven't yet fulfilled.
ttwinf09.speaker: infowell

ttwinf10.dialogue: Check the Sun display for time of day. As night falls, a full sun will wane to dark. Be more careful then, because some creatures only come out at night.
ttwinf10.speaker: infowell

ttwinf11.dialogue: Click on the map to see an overhead view of the area you are exploring. You can drag flags from the right to label areas of the map to remind you where certain things are.
ttwinf11.speaker: infowell

ttwinf12.dialogue: In the box at the lower right corner of the screen, you'll find some colored bars, one for each character in the party.
ttwinf12.speaker: infowell

ttwinf13.dialogue: Clicking on a bar selects a character, just as if you had clicked on the character directly. You'll see the highlight box jump to the character you've selected.
ttwinf13.speaker: infowell

ttwinf14.dialogue: The height of the bar indicates the health of the character. When you are in combat, keep your eye on those bars, so you can heal wounded characters or pull them out of danger.
ttwinf14.speaker: infowell

ttwinf15.dialogue: The colored rings underneath a character match that person's colored bar, both in appearance and in function.
ttwinf15.speaker: infowell

ttwinf16.dialogue: Three rings means the character is healthy; with two, they're damaged; if there is only one, the character is hurting.
ttwinf16.speaker: infowell

ttwinf17.dialogue: Red rings appear under enemies, and follow the same system: three means the monster is healthy, two damaged, and one in bad shape.  Watching the red rings under opponents can help guide your combat strategy.
ttwinf17.speaker: infowell

ttwinf18.dialogue: One more thing: the small triangle points to your current party leader. If you want to change leaders, click-drag the triangle to point at a new character.
ttwinf18.speaker: infowell

ttwinf19.dialogue: In the box at the lower right corner of the screen, you'll find two square buttons, one on top of the other. The top one is the Party Formation button; the bottom is the Rest button.
ttwinf19.speaker: infowell

ttwinf20.dialogue: To set your party's marching formation, first arrange the characters the way you'd like them. Then click the Party Formation button.
ttwinf20.speaker: infowell

ttwinf21.dialogue: Tip: it's generally a good idea to have your party leader at the front of your formation.
ttwinf21.speaker: infowell

ttwinf22.dialogue: Click the bottom button when you want your party to rest and relearn their spells. You can learn more about resting elsewhere in the tutorial.
ttwinf22.speaker: infowell

ttwinf23.dialogue: The round button in the lower right corner of the screen is the Group/Ungroup button. To group all your characters together, and move them in formation, click the button so that it displays three little figures.
ttwinf23.speaker: infowell

ttwinf24.dialogue: If you click on a character or its colored bar, this button will change to a single large figure. You can now move that character independently of the others, to scout for traps or secret doors, smash objects, and so on.
ttwinf24.speaker: infowell

ttwinf25.dialogue: To move again as a group, click on the Group/Ungroup button so that it again displays three little figures. But heed this: you can't group your characters when you are in combat.
ttwinf25.speaker: infowell

ttwinf26.dialogue: When you move your characters as a group, everyone follows the 'party leader.' You select your leader using the small triangle below the colored bars in the box in the lower right corner of the screen.
ttwinf26.speaker: infowell

ttwinf27.dialogue: The leader not only heads up the party, but speaks for the party to characters you meet, and interacts with objects when the party is acting as a group.
ttwinf27.speaker: infowell

ttwinf28.dialogue: To change the party leader, click on the triangle and, while holding down the mouse button, slide the triangle underneath another colored bar.
ttwinf28.speaker: infowell

ttwinf29.dialogue: Sometimes you may find that one of the icon boxes covers up a part of the screen you would like to see.
ttwinf29.speaker: infowell

ttwinf30.dialogue: To make the icon box pop down out of the way, click on the small diamond at the bottom center of the icon box. To bring it back up, click on the small diamond at the top center, the only part still showing.
ttwinf30.speaker: infowell

ttwdma00.dialogue: Goodbye. To review this information, come back here and click on this signpost.
ttwdma00.speaker: DM

kwvDMYL.dialogue: A stair winds up through her temple, so that all might bow to the Lady on their way to the House of Gems, which your half-elves can see looms at the top of the stair.
kwvDMYL.speaker: DM

kwyDMYA.speaker: DM

kwwDMYB.dialogue: This is the Glim-Garden of House Ammath, once one of Myth Drannor's most beautiful greenswards.
kwwDMYB.speaker: DM

kwwDMYC.dialogue: The stair south of you winds down the slope to the Glim-Garden, through a ruined dwarf-made temple.

kwxDMYA.speaker: DM

kwxDMYB.dialogue: With some effort you can spot the place where it emerges at the top, and disappears into the delicate trees of the Glim-Garden.
kwxDMYB.speaker: DM

kwxDMYC.dialogue: This stair leads to a rough footpath, which winds and disappears among the crags and crevices of the cliff face overhead.
kwxDMYC.speaker: DM

kwxDMYD.dialogue: You can't see where it leads, but it seems to climb up to the Glim-Garden. You can barely make out the silhouette of the Garden's trees at the top of the cliff.

kwxDMYF.dialogue: With some effort your elf can trace the path, and spots the place where it emerges at the top, and disappears into the darkness under the trees of the Glim-Garden.

kwsDMYA.dialogue: Along the arch is written, in the languages of elves, dwarves, humans and wizards, 'Speculum - Great Hall of Wizards.'
kwsDMYA.speaker: DM

kwsDMYB.dialogue: Through the arch, you see the Spire of Mythanthor, where you first came up from the Dungeons. And, rising behind it, you see the Speculum, which once was the seat of power for Myth Drannor's magical elite.
kwsDMYB.speaker: DM

kwnDMYA.dialogue: To the north, a narrow path switchbacks its way up a steep cliff.
kwnDMYA.speaker: DM

kwnDMYB.dialogue: Up at the top, you see the trees and elevated walkways of the Windrider Glade.
kwnDMYB.speaker: DM

kwrDMYA.dialogue: Faint runes run across the arch, announcing the entrance to the 'Noble House of Omberdawn.'
kwrDMYA.speaker: DM

kwrDMYB.dialogue: But the runes no longer tell the truth. Instead, beyond the archway, you see the expanse of soggy ground known as Sullymarsh.
kwrDMYB.speaker: DM

kwtDMYA.dialogue: The stone path continues to the west. At its end, you can make out one of Myth Drannor's great city squares, the Nightingale Court.
kwtDMYA.speaker: DM

kwtDMYB.dialogue: The proud buildings and public spaces are still elegant, even in ruin.
kwtDMYB.speaker: DM

kwtDMYC.dialogue: The stone path continues to the west. At its end, even in the gloom of night, you can make out the silhouettes of buildings.
kwtDMYC.speaker: DM
